Format/argument type mismatch at line 73 (%d with u64 expression obu_size - size) is undefined behavior but no security mechanism is derivable within the fragment.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds write in AssignOp::Compute: when old_lhs.dtype() and rhs.dtype() have different element sizes, the destination buffer is sized with old_lhs.dtype() (allocate_temp at L69) while Copy (L76/L86) writes rhs's bytes, whose volume is num_elements(rhs.shape()) * sizeof(rhs.dtype()). No shown statement constrains dtype equality, so an attacker-chosen pair (e.g., DT_FLOAT lhs shape [1], DT_DOUBLE rhs shape [2], validate_shape_=false, forward_input=nullptr, use_exclusive_lock_ inherited) overflows the 8-byte copy_tensor by 8 bytes.

evidence.reason: copy_tensor's capacity is fixed by `context->allocate_temp(old_lhs.dtype(), rhs.shape(), &copy_tensor, attr)` at L69 as num_elements(rhs.shape()) * sizeof(old_lhs.dtype()). rhs, an entry-point input (L2), carries its own dtype; no statement in the fragment (L20/L22 constrain only shape, L39 only element count) constrains old_lhs.dtype() relative to rhs.dtype(). Witness passing every guard (validate_shape_=false at L21 skipped; L38-39 false since initialized lhs shape [1] vs rhs shape [2]; forward_input nullptr at L59; use_exclusive_lock_=true at L75): L69 allocates 2*4=8 bytes for DT_FLOAT lhs / DT_DOUBLE rhs, and Copy writes 2*8=16 bytes into that 8-byte buffer -> 8-byte heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

Same mechanism with use_exclusive_lock_=false: after L74 replaced the ref with copy_tensor (8 bytes from the L69 allocation), L85 re-reads that buffer unlocked and Copy writes rhs's 16 bytes (DT_DOUBLE, shape [2]) into the 8-byte capacity fixed by `allocate_temp(old_lhs.dtype(), rhs.shape(), ...)` at L69 -> 8-byte heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The dtype mismatch is unconstrained by any shown check between the inputs (L2/L19) and this sink.

assumptions: allocate_temp(dtype, shape, ...) (L69) sizes the buffer as shape.num_elements() * sizeof(dtype) — the allocation API contract named in the shown call.
Tensor element sizes differ across dtypes (e.g., DT_INT8/DT_FLOAT vs DT_DOUBLE); exact byte sizes are not printed in the fragment but belong to the Tensor type system used by the shown declarations.
Copy(context, &dst, src) writes src's data into dst's storage — per the helper name and the fragment's own comments (L40-41 'can fit in the underlying buffer', L65-66 'copy the rhs into it').
forward_input may return nullptr (explicitly handled at L59).
validate_shape_, use_exclusive_lock_, relax_constraints_ are unconstrained bool members in the fragment; the witness sets validate_shape_=false and uses both allowed values of use_exclusive_lock_.
limitations: The CHECK at L46 is protected by guard L38-39: with equal element counts, Tensor::CopyFrom's name-implied contract returns true for every admitted input, so CWE-617 is not confirmable.

The L51 copy into old_lhs's buffer has the same root cause, but old_lhs's buffer capacity is not declared or allocated inside the shown code, so the boundary claim there is unconfirmable per the capacity rule.
Copy's internal status (if any) is discarded at L51/L76/L86, but no shown security-relevant operation runs on a failure state, so CWE-754 is not confirmable.
A race between the shape check under the mutex (L20) and the unlocked copy (L86) is not confirmable: the fragment shows no concurrent writer of the ref.
If an out-of-scope framework registration enforced lhs.dtype() == rhs.dtype(), it would absorb this finding; that invariant is not visible in the fragment and is not assumed.
Dtype element sizes (4 vs 8 bytes) are external constants, so the concrete byte excess depends on them; the confirmation uses the smallest such pair.

verdict.summary: Attacker-controlled PCL MediaBox/CropBox coordinates parsed by %lf (lines 142-146) are cast with (size_t) floor(...) at lines 153-154 with no range check; negative, NaN, inf, or >=SIZE_MAX doubles make the conversion undefined and yield a huge corrupted page size that is formatted into geometry/options (168-169, 196-197) and forwarded in the GhostPCL delegate command (216-223), enabling out-of-domain rendered geometry and delegate-side resource exhaustion.

evidence.reason: bounds.x1..y2 are attacker-controlled doubles from %lf at lines 142-146 (no range/NaN/inf constraint in the fragment). Witness file line "MediaBox [100 0 0 0\n" parses x1=100.0,x2=0.0 -> count=4 (guard at 148 admits), and width=(size_t)floor(-99.5)=(size_t)(-100.0) is an out-of-range float-to-size_t conversion (UB per C11 6.3.1.4; 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFF9C on x86-64/AArch64). The corrupted size passes guard 155 (huge > page.width=0) and is consumed as a formatted size in geometry/options at 168-169 and 196-197 and placed into the delegate command executed at 216-223, which is the phase-1 formatted-size sink. Primary mechanism: CWE-681 incorrect numeric-type conversion of attacker input into a huge size.

assumptions: Line numbers refer to the fragment as pasted, enumerated from line 1.

MaxTextExtent is the element capacity of command/filename/geometry as declared at lines 9, 11, 12; the code at 115-119 never writes past index MaxTextExtent-1 (the guard at 116-117 is evaluated after the increment, so *p++ max index is MaxTextExtent-2 and the NUL at 119 max index is MaxTextExtent-1, both in bounds).

The out-of-range double-to-size_t UB at 153-154/192-193 yields the huge value 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFF9C/0x8000000000000000 on mainstream x86-64/AArch64 conversion instructions (cvttsd2si-style), which is the magnitude used for the witness.
image_info and exception are non-NULL per the asserts at lines 53-59.
ReadBlobByte returns EOF at end of the blob, giving the loop at 108 a guaranteed sentinel.
limitations: Command/argument injection into the delegate (216-223) is unconfirmed: GetDelegateCommands' template and AcquireUniqueSymbolicLink's name construction are not in the fragment, and the attacker's original filename is not among the format arguments at 218-220.
Discarded ExternalDelegateCommand return (223): a delegate failure is caught downstream by the image==NULL check at 229, so no unguarded security-relevant operation runs on the failure state.

Unchecked AcquireImage (63), CloneImageInfo (199), AcquireUniqueFilename (215), and AcquireString (186-187) can only return NULL on OOM; dereferences at 64/200 are OOM-dependent, not provable from the fragment.
Stale reuse of count across iterations (148 with lines matching neither CropBox nor MediaBox) is idempotent because 155-158 re-max against unchanged bounds; no impact.
FormatLocaleString into command (216) may truncate if the delegate template plus long temp names exceed MaxTextExtent; silent truncation, no demonstrated security impact.

The delegate-side page-raster allocation triggered by the corrupted geometry is a standard callee-side consequence of this fragment's command construction, not a memory safety issue inside the shown code.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read in the RTCP XR report-block parser: block pointers (rb_stats, rb_rr_time, rb_dlrr, rb_voip_mtc) are recorded at lines 31/34/37/40 from headers whose only admission bound is the loop guard at line 23 (header word h < pkt_len); the attacker-controlled block length rb_len (line 25) is never validated against the packet end established by the size check at line 19, and the post-loop field reads (e.g., pj_ntohl(rb_stats->lost) at line 155, jitter/toh fields at 163-175) have no containment check. A crafted 12-byte RTCP XR packet (common.length=2) with a BT_STATS header at word 1, rb_len=1 and specific=0xFF passes lines 14/19/23/28 and causes reads of bytes >=12..15 of the 12-byte packet buffer, i.e., a 4+ byte out-of-bounds read past the pkt buffer (capacity size), remotely triggerable.

evidence.reason: rb_stats is recorded at line 37 from a block header whose only admission bound is the loop guard at line 23 (h < pkt_len), which bounds the 4-byte header word, never the block content. rb_len comes from pj_ntohs((pj_uint16_t)rb_hdr->length) (line 25, domain [0,65535]) and is only filtered for zero (line 28), never checked against the remaining packet. The packet region is bounded by line 19 to 4*(pkt_len+1) <= size bytes (capacity = size, parameter line 3). Witness: size=12, common.length=2, block header at word 1 with bt=BT_STATS, length=1, specific=0xFF; guards 14, 19, 23, 28, 36, 138, 148 are all passed; 'lost' is a distinct member after the header word and begin_seq/end_seq, i.e., byte offset >=8 from the header, so the 4-byte read at line 155 starts at byte >=12 of the 12-byte buffer (index == capacity) and reads bytes 12..15 out of bounds. Primary CWE-125 (OOB read).

Same unvalidated-block mechanism as the line 155 sink. With the same 12-byte witness packet (bt=BT_STATS, rb_len=1) and specific=0xFF setting the j-flag (line 150), the read of jitter_min at line 163 targets a distinct member >=16 bytes past the block header, i.e., bytes >=20..23, fully outside the 4*(pkt_len+1)=12-byte region the parser itself established at line 19; out-of-bounds read past the pkt buffer of capacity size. Confirms the OOB extent is not a one-byte edge case. Primary CWE-125.

assumptions: size (line 3) is the exact byte capacity of the buffer pointed to by pkt; the fragment's own guard at line 19 (4*(pkt_len+1) <= size) relies on this.
sess and its fields (rtcp_session, name, stat) are valid non-NULL pointers; the fragment contains no NULL producer for them.
pj_ntohs/pj_ntohl perform 16-bit/32-bit big-endian reads, as implied by their names and by the 16-bit cast at line 25.

Done report-block structs begin with a 4-byte header word (per the word-advance at lines 46-47) and place distinct content members at increasing, non-overlapping byte offsets; the reads at lines 144-145 and 155 imply begin_seq/end_seq occupy >=2 bytes each and 'lost' lies at offset >=8 from the header.
RTCP length semantics used by the fragment itself (line 19: pkt_len+1 words; lines 25/46-47: block length rb_len+1 words) are taken from the shown arithmetic.
limitations: The exact number of out-of-bounds bytes depends on the layouts of pjmedia_rtcp_xr_rb_stats / rb_dlrr / rb_rr_time / rb_voip_mtc, whose definitions are not shown in the fragment; the confirmed defect is that no shown check bounds any block-content read inside the 4*(pkt_len+1)-byte region established at line 19.

The header reads at lines 14 and 17 occur before the size guard at line 19; for callers passing size<4 they can read bytes 2-3 (and byte 0 for size==0) out of bounds, but this depends on unshown struct offsets and an out-of-contract caller minimum, so it is not confirmed.

TRACE_/PJ_LOG calls at lines 59-61, 96-99, 124, 128-133 pass pj_uint32_t/unsigned values to %p, which is C undefined behavior (type mismatch), but formats are constant (no format-string injection) and no security impact is shown; not reported as a finding.
Pointer formation beyond the packet at lines 46-47 is technically undefined behavior, but the loop guard at line 23 prevents any dereference of the out-of-range pointer; no impact.
Discarded return values of pj_get_timestamp (57), pjmedia_rtcp_get_ntp_time (79), and pj_gettimeofday (178, 213) have no shown failure state feeding a security-relevant operation.

verdict.summary: FractionalAvgPoolGrad Compute writes to an Eigen-mapped heap buffer (allocated at lines 81-83, mapped at lines 86-88) using in_index derived verbatim from unvalidated pooling-sequence tensor values: with row_seq=[-1,2] and in_rows=2, line 115 yields in_index=-2 and line 121 coeffRef(0,-2) writes 16 bytes before the buffer start (OOB heap write, CWE-787). The witness passes every shown guard (lines 24-28, 38, 44, 60-70, 101). A second driver of the same sink is that out_depth (line 36) is never compared with in_depth (line 58), so the d-loop (line 117) can reach rows past the in_depth-row map.

evidence.reason: row_seq_tensor (context->input(2)) values are unvalidated: line 38 bounds only NumElements() > out_rows, never element values, so in_row_start (line 98) retains the full int64_t domain. It becomes the in_r loop counter (line 113) and in_index = (b*in_rows + in_r)*in_cols + in_c (line 115). Witness: orig shape [1,2,2,1], out_backprop [1,1,1,1], row_seq=[-1,2], col_seq=[0,1]; guards at 24-28, 60-70, 38, 44 all pass; at b=r=c=0, in_row_start=-1, in_row_end=min(2-1, in_rows-1)=1 (both overlapping branches), so line 113 admits in_r=-1 and line 115 gives in_index=-2. The temp buffer is allocated at lines 81-83 with in_shape {in_batch,in_rows,in_cols,in_depth} and mapped at lines 86-88 as in_depth x (in_cols*in_rows*in_batch), valid element offsets [0, in_depth*in_cols*in_rows*in_batch)=[0,4). coeffRef(0,-2) for the column-major map computes offset -2*1+0=-2 elements (16 bytes before the 32-byte buffer), an out-of-bounds heap write (CWE-787).

out_depth = out_backprop.dim_size(3) (line 36) and in_depth = orig_input_tensor_shape_flat(3) (line 58) are independent input-derived int64_t values and no shown statement relates them. The d-loop (line 117) admits every d in [0, out_depth), while the map at lines 86-88 has only in_depth rows. Witness: orig shape [1,2,2,1] (in_depth=1, buffer capacity 4 doubles), out_backprop [1,1,1,2] (out_depth=2), row/col_seq=[0,2] (guards 38/44 pass, 2>1); at the last inner iteration in_index=3 (line 115) with d=1 accepted by line 117, coeffRef(1,3) computes offset 3*1+1=4 == capacity, an out-of-bounds heap write past the 4-double buffer at line 121 (CWE-787, same sink statement as the primary finding).

assumptions: Eigen::Map<Eigen::Matrix<double, Dynamic, Dynamic>> (lines 86-88) is column-major by default and coeffRef(row,col) indexes data()[col*rows+row] with no bounds checking in release builds (Eigen's standard semantics); out-of-domain (row,col) performs out-of-bounds memory access.

overlapping_ (lines 99-100, 104-105) is an internal OpKernel attribute whose value is not shown; the primary witness yields in_row_end=1 and in_col_end=0 identically in both ternary branches, so the finding is branch-independent.

context->input(0..3) return valid Tensors per the OpKernelContext contract, and OP_REQUIRES_OK at lines 81-83 and 133-134 abort the kernel on allocation failure, so on the executed path the temp buffer exists with exactly in_shape = {in_batch,in_rows,in_cols,in_depth}.
dim_size() returns non-negative dimension sizes for an existing Tensor (TensorShape type invariant); out_batch/out_rows/out_cols/out_depth are therefore >= 0.

orig_input_tensor_shape, out_backprop, row_seq_tensor, and col_seq_tensor are op-input tensors whose contents/shapes are supplied by the graph; the fragment never constrains the int64 VALUES of the pooling sequences or the relationship between out_depth and in_depth.
limitations: Negative orig-shape dimensions (e.g., in_rows=-3) pass the !=0 guards (lines 60-70) and reach TensorShape::AddDim at line 76; the abort/validation behavior of TensorShape::AddDim is not visible in this fragment, so the consequence cannot be demonstrated and no CWE is assigned.

Integer overflow in in_index (line 115) or in the map column products (lines 88, 91) would require dimension magnitudes that the shown allocation path (lines 81-83, 133-134) could not satisfy, so an overflow-driven OOB is not separately demonstrated.

num_elements_in_pooling_cell (lines 108-109) can be <= 0 on adversarial sequences, but loops 113-114 execute zero iterations when start > end, and double division by zero at line 123 yields NaN/inf rather than a memory-safety failure; not a finding.

The depth-mismatch vector (evidence item 2) is confirmed under fragment-only analysis; if graph construction or op registration elsewhere pins out_depth == in_depth, it would be unreachable in practice, but no such validation appears in the shown code.
Reads at line 119 are in-domain for a rank-4 out_backprop given out_index (line 110); TensorShape behavior for dim_size() with rank < 4 is outside the fragment and is not relied on for any finding.
No command injection, SQL/NoSQL/XPath, log/header injection, SSRF, open redirect, XSS, crypto/entropy, file/access-control, or authn/authz sinks exist in this fragment.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable from the fragment. The only potentially dangerous sink is lsqpack_enc_init (L19-21): its buffer-size argument is set at L16 to sizeof(qeh->qeh_tsu_buf) - the exact capacity of the passed object - and the three unsigned settings are forwarded either verbatim (max_table_size, max_risked_streams) or after a downward-only clamp to 0 (dyn_table_size, L17-18), so no out-of-domain size or index derivation occurs in the shown code. Init failure is fully handled by returning -1 (L19-24). Demoted concerns: NULL qeh is assert-only-guarded (L6) and caller-supplied, callee-side TSU overflow depends on an unshown library contract, and the qeh_begin_out return (L33) is discarded with unshown semantics.

assumptions: sizeof(qeh->qeh_tsu_buf) at L16 equals the byte capacity of the object passed at L21 (language-defined if qeh_tsu_buf is an array member; the member declaration is not in the fragment).
lsqpack_enc_init treats *tsu_buf_sz as a capacity-in / bytes-written-out argument, implied by the assignment at L16 and the 'post-init TSU' debug at L26.
LSQ_WARN/LSQ_INFO/LSQ_DEBUG take printf-style constant format strings.
QENC_MIN_DYN_TABLE_SIZE is a positive named constant, but its value is not visible in the fragment.
limitations: NULL dereference of qeh (CWE-476): no runtime NULL check exists (only the NDEBUG-elided assert at L6), but NULL can only be supplied by an out-of-scope caller; the fragment produces no NULL.

TSU buffer overflow (CWE-787/122): the numeric capacity of qeh->qeh_tsu_buf is not identifiable because its declaration is absent, and the size passed at L21 equals sizeof of the buffer from L16 (in-domain), so an overflow would require unshown callee behavior.

The bodies of lsqpack_enc_init, lsqpack_enc_header_block_prefix_size, and qeh_begin_out are not shown; in particular qeh_begin_out's discarded return value (L33) has unshown status semantics, so no error/status-handling flaw (CWE-754/390) is confirmable.
The declared types of qeh_tsu_sz and qeh_max_prefix_size are unshown; a hypothetical narrowing store of sizeof at L16 cannot be demonstrated as lossy or security-relevant from the fragment.

The value of QENC_MIN_DYN_TABLE_SIZE (L17) is unknown, so the exact lower bound of the non-clamped dyn_table_size range is not quotable; this affects only the clamp's admitted set, not any dangerous enlargement.

verdict.summary: Tensor::FromProto passes the shape-derived element count N to Helper<T>::Decode (line 12) and FromProtoField<T> (line 15) without validating proto.tensor_content()'s byte length (or the repeated field's entry count) against N * sizeof(T), enabling an attacker-controlled heap over-read from a crafted TensorProto (CWE-125). The only shown length constraint is the non-empty check at line 10.

evidence.reason: N = shape.num_elements() (line 7) is derived from the attacker-supplied TensorShapeProto and admitted with N >= 1 by the guard at line 8; content = proto.tensor_content() (line 11) is admitted with only size() >= 1 by the guard at line 10. No shown statement constrains content.size() against N * sizeof(T), so the count argument N is out of domain for a decode of N elements from content: witness N=2 (DT_FLOAT, needs 8 bytes) with content='x' (1 byte) passes lines 4, 5, 8, and 10 and yields a 7-byte heap over-read inside Decode, scaling with N — CWE-125 out-of-bounds read. Line 18 cannot catch an over-read occurring during the callee call, and the callee body is not shown, so confidence is capped accordingly.

Same mechanism as the Decode sink: the shape-derived count N (line 7, admitted N >= 1 at line 8) is passed to FromProtoField without any shown check that proto's repeated value field holds N entries; a shape admitting N=2 with a 1-entry field list passes lines 4, 5, 8, and 10 and reads past the field data — CWE-125 out-of-bounds read, anchored at this call site.

assumptions: TensorShape::IsValid(proto.tensor_shape()) (line 4) is a real validation gate whose internals are not shown; the witness assumes it accepts shapes with non-negative dims such as {2} and {1000}.
std::string's readable byte range is [0, size()); size() >= 1 is established on the decode path only by the non-empty check at line 10.
CASES_WITH_DEFAULT dispatches on proto.dtype() (switch-like macro); known dtypes execute the expression argument, and DT_INVALID/unknown types set dtype_error.
limitations: The actual read happens inside Helper<T>::Decode and FromProtoField<T>, whose bodies are not in the fragment; if either callee re-validates the source length/field count (e.g., returns nullptr on mismatch, which line 18 would then handle), the over-read does not occur. The positive verdict rests on name-implied decode semantics, which caps confidence at 0.6.

shape.num_elements() product overflow producing negative values other than -1 is not derivable inside the fragment (the multiplication is inside TensorShape); the else branch (lines 19-28) would accept such a shape with buf_ == nullptr, but no security-relevant operation on that state is visible (lines 29-32 only store it; line 35 null-checks before dereferencing).
CHECK_NOTNULL(a) (line 2) macro semantics (abort vs. return) are not shown; no null-deref finding is based on it.
No loops exist in the fragment, so loop-termination and parser-position analysis is not applicable.
The byte-level excess (7 bytes in the witness, 3994 in the second example) uses sizeof(float)=4 illustratively; the general excess is N * sizeof(T) - content.size() for any T with sizeof(T) >= 1.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable from the statements visible in this fragment. The only substantive candidates (signed-int overflow of len and of len*2/len*2+1 feeding pop_n(...) at the stated lines, and NULL dereference of tree->car->car->car at the KW_REST test) all fail the witness/reachability requirement: the only shown cap on len is the conditional flush at the `cursp() >= slimit` guard, whose firing depends on an unshown stack-cursor trajectory; the required 2^30+ node input is not constructible from shown constraints; the operand widths of genop_2/pop_n and the values of GEN_VAL_STACK_MAX/GEN_LIT_ARY_MAX are not declared in the fragment; and no NULL-producing path for a malformed tree exists inside the fragment. The code contains no direct memory, injection, crypto, file, or authz sinks. The not-vulnerable verdict rests on absence of evidence rather than a located protective check, hence the low confidence.

assumptions: INT16_MAX is the C standard constant 32767 (the fragment names it at the `if (cursp() >= GEN_LIT_ARY_MAX) slimit = INT16_MAX;` statement).
pop_n(n) consumes n, by its name and by its use in the fragment, as a count of codegen-stack values to pop; pop()/push() adjust the codegen stack by one slot.
genop_1/genop_2 consume the stack-position and count operands passed at the call sites.
The `while (tree)` loop terminates for a NULL-terminated node list via `tree = tree->cdr`; codegen pushes/pops the stack slots implied by the fragment's own pop_n(len*2) accounting.
limitations: Signed-int overflow of len / len*2 / len*2+1 (potential CWE-190/CWE-195/CWE-787 stack underflow via pop_n at `pop_n(len*2)` and `pop_n(len*2+1)`): demoted. The witness needs >= 2^30 consecutive non-KW_REST nodes while the `cursp() >= slimit` flush guard fails to fire on every one; the guard is the only shown len-cap and its firing depends on cursp() behavior, which the fragment neither constrains nor guarantees, so the witness can be neither constructed nor demonstrated to bypass the guard.
Possible truncation of the len operand in genop_2(s, OP_HASH/OP_HASHADD, cursp(), len): the instruction operand width is not identifiable from the fragment; unconfirmable in both directions.
NULL dereference of tree->car->car->car at the KW_REST test: the fragment contains no producer of a NULL car/car->car; the well-formedness of the hash tree is a parser invariant outside the fragment.

Stack-balance assumptions around the two pop() after codegen(s, tree->car->cdr, val) and the pops at the flushes: the push behavior of codegen is not shown; balances are exact only under the fragment's own pair accounting.
Unbounded len accumulation with val == 0 and its return to the caller: no in-fragment sink consumes it on that path.
Non-termination of `while (tree)` on a cyclic tree: no in-fragment producer of a cyclic list.
Values of GEN_VAL_STACK_MAX and GEN_LIT_ARY_MAX are not declared in the fragment, so slimit is treated symbolically and no capacity claim is made from either macro.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The only candidate memory sink is the flat-view read a_shape_flat(i) at lines 23/27, which is fully protected: the rank-equality guard at line 16 (a_shape->NumElements() != b->dims()) admits only NumElements == dims, and the loop condition i < b->dims() at line 22 bounds i to [0, NumElements-1], so no reachable index equals or exceeds the view's NumElements-element capacity. Unconfirmed concerns (NULL pointers, flat<Index>() dtype semantics) are outside what the fragment establishes.

assumptions: a_shape is guaranteed 1-D by the IsVector check at line 9, so flat<Index>() spans exactly a_shape->NumElements() elements.
TensorShapeUtils::IsMatrix/IsVector semantics follow their names: matrix = exactly 2-D, vector = exactly 1-D.
errors::InvalidArgument returns a non-OK Status rather than aborting; no reachable abort exists in the fragment.
The four Tensor* parameters are framework/caller-provided and non-NULL; the fragment contains no statement or call that can produce NULL for them.
limitations: The Tensor* parameters are dereferenced without NULL checks (lines 3, 8-9, 16, 21-23); NULL dereference cannot be produced by the shown code or by framework invariants visible in the fragment, so it is out of scope.

flat<Index>()'s callee behavior (dtype matching or bit-reinterpretation and the resulting byte-level reads) is not shown; a dtype-mismatched a_shape causing reads past tensor storage cannot be confirmed from this fragment.
Contents of a_indices and a_values are not validated beyond their shapes; any downstream consumption of their data is outside this fragment.

a_shape flat-view element values and b's dim_size(i) values are comparable only through the equality at line 23; no test here establishes constraints on those values themselves, which is not security-relevant to any sink in the fragment.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read in MakeDataset: the ordering loop indexes the indices matrix at column 0, while the only shape guard on that tensor (IsMatrix at line 11) checks rank 2 exclusively, so a matrix of shape [N, 0] with N >= 1 passes every guard and the element access at line 32 computes linear index 0 in a zero-element buffer — an 8-byte OOB read (or null dereference if the empty buffer's data pointer is null), crashing or invoking UB on attacker-chosen input.

evidence.reason: indices is entry-point input (ctx->input at line 5); the only guard before this read, IsMatrix(indices->shape()) at line 11, admits every rank-2 shape and nowhere in the fragment is dim_size(1) >= 1 established. Witness: indices shape {1, 0}, values shape {0}, dense_shape shape {0} — all admitted by lines 11, 15, 19; the loop guard at line 31 admits i = 0 (0 < dim_size(0) = 1); matrix<int64>()(0, 0) at line 32 computes row-major linear index 0*0 + 0 = 0 in a matrix view with 1*0 = 0 elements, so the valid index domain [0, 0) is empty and the 8-byte int64 read at element 0 is index == capacity overrun of the empty indices buffer (CWE-125), or a null dereference if that buffer's pointer is null. The ordering OP_REQUIRES at lines 33-37 executes only after the failing dereference, and SparseTensor::Create at line 43, which could reject the shape, also runs after the read, so no shown check protects the sink.

assumptions: TensorShapeUtils::IsMatrix(indices->shape()) at line 11 enforces rank == 2 only (no positive-dimension minimum), so zero-column matrices are admitted; this is the standard TensorFlow contract of IsMatrix and is the only visible effect of that guard.

Tensor::matrix<int64>() yields a row-major matrix view whose element (i, j) exists only for i < dim_size(0) and j < dim_size(1); its capacity (dim_size(0) * dim_size(1) elements) is derived from the same shape object that lines 11 and 31 read.
The op's dtype/shape-inference registration (not shown) is not used in this analysis; only guards visible in the fragment bound the inputs.
limitations: Whether the zero-column access manifests as a null-pointer dereference (CWE-476) depends on the empty tensor's buffer being null; the allocation is not shown, so CWE-125 (OOB read) is the primary classification and the CWE-476 alternative remains unconfirmed.

TensorShape(dense_shape->vec<int64>()) at line 44 inside SparseTensor::Create consumes attacker-controlled dims; negative/inconsistent values could be rejected or CHECK-fail inside callees whose bodies are not shown, so any CWE-617/CWE-20 concern there is unconfirmable.

gtl::InlinedVector<int64, 8> std_order(dense_shape->NumElements(), 0) at line 40 sizes an allocation directly from entry-point input with no cap; a huge dense_shape could exhaust memory, but the failure requires an unchecked allocation to fail with no shown security-relevant operation running on the failure state, so it is not a confirmed finding.
new Dataset<T>(ctx, std::move(tensor)) at line 46 can throw on allocation failure; not treated as a finding for the same reason.
values/indices length consistency and indices-columns == dense_shape rank are not validated in the fragment; any such protections live inside SparseTensor::Create (lines 43-45), which is not shown.
No dtype checks appear in the fragment even though indices are dereferenced as int64 via matrix<int64>(); dtype enforcement by op registration is outside the fragment and not used in the verdict.

verdict.summary: Signed integer overflow of the entry counter len in gen_hash: no shown statement bounds the tree/list length or len, so len can reach 2^30; line 11 then computes len*2 = 2147483648, which wraps to -2147483648 in 32-bit int and is passed to pop_n() as a negative stack-adjustment count, corrupting the stack cursor used by all subsequent bytecode emission (CWE-190). Reachable when val==0 disables the line-36 spill guard; requires an adversarial AST with ~2^30 hash entries.

evidence.reason: len is incremented once per non-kw-rest tree entry at line 33 and, with val==0, the only spill cap (line 36, which requires val!=0) never resets it; the cdr chain length is not bounded by any shown statement, so len retains the full int domain. For an admitted finite chain of 2^30 plain pairs followed by a kw-rest pair, guard line 10 (len > 0) admits len = 1073741824, and line 11 evaluates len*2 = 2147483648, which overflows signed 32-bit int to -2147483648 (CWE-190, integer overflow corrupting a security-relevant count). The negative value is consumed at this call site as the stack-slot count for pop_n — an index/size argument out of its required non-negative domain — corrupting the stack cursor used by subsequent push/pop/genop_* emissions; the downstream byte-level effect is inside unshown callees, so no memory-safety secondary CWE is asserted.

assumptions: int is 32-bit two's complement, so len*2 overflows for len >= 2^30; on a wider int the same overflow occurs at len >= 2^(width-1).
INT16_MAX (line 4) has its standard value 32767.
cursp() reflects the stack depth maintained by this fragment's push/pop/pop_n calls.
The witness tree is a finite, non-cyclic cons list so while(tree) at line 8 terminates.
val == 0 is admitted by every shown guard (line 36 and line 51 require val != 0 but never reject val == 0); the fragment never shows a caller, so this is a range-admitted mode, not an evidenced call.
limitations: Actual out-of-bounds bytes written/read reside inside pop_n/genop_2/codegen whose bodies are not shown; only the out-of-domain negative count at the line-11 call site is confirmable.

The arithmetic demonstrable for the line 37 / line 52 pop_n(len*2) and pop_n(len*2+1) paths is not confirmed here: both are guarded by val != 0 (lines 36 and 51) under which the spill mechanism limits len unless unshown GEN_VAL_STACK_MAX / GEN_LIT_ARY_MAX values or codegen push behavior say otherwise.
tree->car->car->car at line 9 could NULL-deref on a malformed AST, but no shown statement produces NULL on any admitted path; unconfirmed.
Return values of codegen at lines 21, 31, 32 are discarded; whether codegen reports errors by return status is not visible in the fragment, so an error/status-handling flaw cannot be confirmed.
Truncation of len into a 16-bit genop_2 operand depends on the instruction encoder, not shown; unconfirmed.
The unused limit parameter (a would-be depth bound) is not enforced anywhere in the fragment; impact unconfirmable.
Loop non-termination on a cyclic cdr chain is a caller-side AST invariant, not established in the fragment.

The overflow witness requires ~2^30 hash entries (multi-GB source in practice); the fragment shows no input-size cap, so the range is retained per the analysis rules, but this marks the issue as a large-input robustness/DoS concern rather than a small-input bug.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable within the shown fragment. The dbuf reads at L12, L15, L18, L21-L22, L25-L28, L39, L42, and L45 take offsets derived from the unconstrained i64 parameter `pos`, but the capacity of `f` and the bounds behavior of dbuf_getu16be/dbuf_getu32be/pict_read_fixed are not visible in the fragment, so neither negative offsets (pos=-100) nor wrapped offsets (pos=0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, e.g., pos+28 at L42 becomes negative in the shown i64 arithmetic) can be confirmed to reach memory. The only arithmetic sink, `(bi->rowbytes*8)/bi->pixelsize` at L33, is guarded against zero divisors by L32 (admitted set 1..65535), while `rowbytes`' type and provenance are not shown. Truncating (int) debug casts and discarded getter statuses have no security-relevant downstream effect in the shown code.

assumptions: pos (L2) is an internal-helper parameter with no constraint in the fragment, so its residual range is the full i64 domain [-2^63, 2^63-1].

dbuf_getu16be and dbuf_getu32be read 2 and 4 bytes respectively at their offset argument, and pict_read_fixed reads a fixed-point value (name-implied semantics); their values are 16-bit and 32-bit unsigned ranges.
bi->pixelsize (L26) is sourced from a 16-bit getter, so its value domain is 0..65535; the guard at L32 admits 1..65535 and excludes 0.
The division at L33 is therefore never by zero for the guard's admitted set.
limitations: OOB read via unvalidated pos offsets (sinks L12, L15, L18, L21, L22, L25-L28, L39, L42, L45): the capacity of `f` is not declared in the fragment and the getters' bounds behavior is not shown, so negative or wrapped offsets (witnesses pos=-100 and pos=0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF yielding wrapped negatives) are unconfirmable as memory-corrupting reads; no CWE attached.

i64 wrap in pos+k at L42 (pos=9223372036854775807 -> pos+28 = -9223372036854775781): the wrap occurs in the shown types and is consumed as an offset, but the downstream read's capacity and behavior are outside the fragment, so impact cannot be confirmed.
Possible integer overflow in (bi->rowbytes*8) at L33: type, provenance, and magnitude of bi->rowbytes are not shown, and the downstream use of pdwidth is not security-relevant within the fragment.

bi->pdwidth is only assigned when pixelsize>0 (L33/L36); when pixelsize==0 the comparison at L35 reads caller-supplied state whose initialization is not visible — potential stale/uninitialized use is a robustness concern, not a demonstrated vulnerability.
Discarded return statuses of the read helpers: in the shown code a failure value only feeds debug logging and a guarded division, so no security-relevant operation runs on a failure state.

Narrowing (int) casts for debug output (L9, L13, L16, L19, L29-L30, L40) are implementation-defined but affect only log text; formats are literal and arguments numeric, so no log or format-string injection is possible.

verdict.summary: BiasAndClamp never rejects negative bias_size: line 4 only excludes 0, and the line-10 divisibility check passes negative divisors (array_size % -1 == 0). In both build branches the outer loop's step moves the progress variable away from the exit condition (array_ptr += bias_size at line 16; array_offset += bias_size at line 59), so inputs such as bias_size=-1 with a positive array_size never terminate, causing an unbounded hang / denial of service (CWE-835).

evidence.reason: bias_size is int with residual range int\{0} (line 4 excludes only 0; line 10 admits negative divisors such as -1). With bias_size=-1 and array_size=1, array_end_ptr = array_data + 1 (line 13) while each iteration moves array_ptr backward by -1 (line 16), and the inner loops (lines 18/44/52) never execute, so array_ptr never equals array_end_ptr and the loop never reaches its exit condition: CWE-835 non-termination.

evidence.snippet:
for (int array_offset = 0; array_offset < array_size;
       array_offset += bias_size) {
evidence.reason: Same admitted residual range for bias_size: -1 passes line 4 and line 10 (1 % -1 == 0). array_offset starts at 0 and strictly decreases at line 59 while the exit test requires array_offset >= array_size (>0); the loop can never satisfy its exit condition and hangs: CWE-835 non-termination.

assumptions: TFLITE_DCHECK_EQ (line 10) is treated as a debug-only assertion by its name; the confirmed witness passes it even when active because array_size % -1 == 0 for every array_size, so the non-termination finding does not depend on the macro's runtime state.
The walk region of array_data is taken from the code's own bounds at lines 13 and 58 (array_size elements); no declaration or allocation of array_data/bias_data appears in the fragment.
limitations: Out-of-region write candidates were demoted: (a) NEON with positive sizes violating divisibility (e.g., array_size=5, bias_size=2) writes beyond the array_size-element walk region at lines 39-42/50/53 and also never terminates, but reaching the sink requires line 10 to be compiled out, which the fragment cannot verify; (b) NEON with bias_size=4, array_size=-8 passes line 10 even when active and writes array_data[0..3], [4..7], ... at lines 39-42, but the object capacity of array_data is not declared, so CWE-787 cannot be capacity-grounded; (c) non-NEON with non-divisible sizes writes up to index array_size+bias_size-1 at line 61, also contingent on line 10 being inactive.

Whether any real caller can supply negative or non-divisible sizes (provenance of these internal-helper parameters) is outside the fragment; the residual ranges admitted by the shown guards are used as required.
Signed-overflow UB for bias_size near INT_MAX via i += 16 / i += 4 (lines 18, 44) was not pursued: no visible capacity and an unrealistic regime.
No NULL-dereference candidate: the fragment contains no path that produces NULL, and the confirmed witness never dereferences array_data/bias_data.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the fragment. The only vulnerable-looking hand-off, the TSU buffer size passed by pointer to lsqpack_enc_init (lines 16-19), is provably in-domain because the size is set to the buffer's own sizeof and the init return status is fully checked (lines 17-23) before any flag is set or output starts. The three unsigned QPACK settings are unvalidated in the fragment but are consumed only inside the unseen callee, with no shown index/size/allocation derivation, so DoS/memory-safety concerns there are unconfirmable limitations rather than findings.

assumptions: The capacity of qeh->qeh_tsu_buf is sizeof(qeh->qeh_tsu_buf) at line 16, and the size handed to lsqpack_enc_init at line 19 enters at exactly that value, so size-in equals capacity for the TSU buffer by construction.
The (qeh->qeh_tsu_buf, &qeh->qeh_tsu_sz) argument pair at lines 17-19 follows the name-implied in/out size convention: the callee may update the size but is bounded by its entry value.
qeh->qeh_flags carries QEH_INITIALIZED when the function runs (assert precondition at line 6), established by the caller's lifecycle rather than by the fragment.
limitations: Semantic bounds on max_table_size, dyn_table_size, and max_risked_streams (e.g., a maximum table capacity, or a minimum of one risked stream) are not imposed anywhere in the shown code; any resource-exhaustion (CWE-400) or memory-corruption claim would require lsqpack_enc_init's body, which is not shown, so it is unconfirmable from this fragment.

A buffer overrun of qeh->qeh_tsu_buf would require lsqpack_enc_init to write past its supplied size, contradicting the in/out size contract; the callee body is not visible, so this cannot be confirmed.

assert(qeh->qeh_flags & QEH_INITIALIZED) at line 6 is attacker-unreachable in the fragment (flag set by internal lifecycle); if asserts are compiled out (NDEBUG) no attacker-directed sink runs on a hypothetical uninitialized state.
Whether lsqpack_enc_init cleans up partial internal state when it returns nonzero is not shown; a leak or double-init on caller retry is unconfirmable.
The declared type of qeh->qeh_tsu_sz is not shown; a %zu format mismatch at line 24 is unconfirmable and has no demonstrated security impact.
A NULL qeh would be dereferenced at line 6, but no shown path produces NULL, so this is a caller-contract limitation, not a NULL-dereference finding.

verdict.summary: In diST_box_read, the unconstrained entry-point value s->size feeds the allocation at line 5 (sizeof(char)*(s->size+1)), the copy length at line 7, and the array index at line 8. At the type maximum, s->size+1 wraps to 0, so line 5 allocates a 0-byte buffer; the only guard, the line-6 malloc NULL test, admits the path when gf_malloc(0) returns non-NULL, and lines 7 and 8 then perform heap OOB writes (CWE-787) rooted in the allocation-size integer overflow (CWE-190).

evidence.reason: Heap OOB write (CWE-787): s->size is an entry-point input with full declared domain — the fragment imposes no constraint on it, and the only conditional (line 6) tests the malloc result, not s->size. When s->size equals its type maximum, s->size+1 in the allocation expression at line 5 wraps to 0, making the destination capacity (line 5: sizeof(char)*(s->size+1)) 0 bytes. The line-6 guard admits the path when gf_malloc(0) returns non-NULL, after which the line-7 length argument s->size makes gf_bs_read_data write s->size bytes, all out of bounds (excess = s->size over capacity 0). The wrap corrupting the allocation size is the CWE-190 root cause.

Heap OOB write (CWE-787): on the same wrapped path, the sink object's capacity from line 5 (sizeof(char)*(s->size+1)) is 0 bytes, and the array subscript uses the unconstrained s->size (full domain; only the line-6 malloc NULL guard precedes it, which admits this path). The NUL write therefore lands at index s->size in a 0-byte heap buffer, i.e., s->size bytes past the end of the allocated object.

assumptions: sizeof(char) == 1 as it appears in the line-5 allocation expression, so the capacity is s->size+1 bytes whenever no wrap occurs.
gf_bs_read_data(bs, dst, n) consumes its third argument as the number of bytes it writes into dst (name/role semantics).
p->content_script_types is a writable char buffer member of GF_DIMSScriptTypesBox, implied by the malloc assignment and char-array indexing/NUL assignment at lines 5-8.
limitations: The declared type and width of s->size are not visible in the fragment, so the exact wrap value (e.g., 0xFFFFFFFF vs 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF) and signedness cannot be pinned down; the witness is the type maximum for any unsigned width, making this a range-based rather than single-value confirmation.

The overflow path requires gf_malloc(0) to return non-NULL, which is implementation-defined (true on mainstream allocators); if it returned NULL, line 6 would return GF_OUT_OF_MEM and no overflow would occur.
For non-wrapping large s->size, line 5 either allocates a matching s->size+1-byte buffer (lines 7-8 are then an exact fit) or fails and line 6 returns, so no overflow occurs on that branch.

The return value of gf_bs_read_data at line 7 is discarded; whether a short read/exhaustion leaves a partial buffer whose later use is security-relevant cannot be established without the callee contract (demoted candidate).
The fragment contains no loops, injection sinks, crypto/entropy use, path/file operations, or authz checks, so those vulnerability classes are out of scope here.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable from the shown fragment. Every path that reaches a Copy sink (lines 57, 82, 92) ends with a destination whose element count equals rhs.shape().num_elements(): the guard at lines 44-45 admits only equal element counts for the in-place path, the branch-2 paths allocate or forward a destination sized exactly rhs.shape() (lines 62-64, 74-76) and replace the ref (lines 67, 80) before any copy, and the only early-return paths (lines 59, 68, 83) never reach the unlocked fall-through copy. Uninitialized rhs is excluded at lines 9-11 and uninitialized old_lhs at line 44. The sole reachable abort (CHECK at line 52) protects an element-count invariant the fragment itself establishes at line 45, so it is not an attacker-directed reachable abort. Residual concerns (absence of a visible dtype-equality check between rhs and old_lhs, Copy's unshown body, and the non-exclusive-lock race) cannot be confirmed from the fragment and are recorded in limitations.

assumptions: context->input(1), context->mutable_input(0), and context->input_ref_mutex(0) return non-NULL framework-provided objects (the fragment dereferences them at lines 2, 23-24 with no NULL-producing path).

old_lhs.shape().num_elements() and rhs.shape().num_elements() are the tensor element counts, and Copy(context, &lhs, rhs) performs an element-wise copy of rhs into lhs of the same element count (name-implied semantics; body not shown).
Tensor buffer capacities equal their declared shape element counts; absolute byte capacities of old_lhs/copy_tensor/forwarded buffers are framework invariants, not declared in this fragment.
replace_ref_input(0, tensor, lock_held=true) makes a later mutable_input(0, ...) return the replacement tensor object (lines 53-54, 67, 80, 91).
forward_input(1, ...) returns non-null only with the requested rhs.dtype()/rhs.shape(); its result is dereferenced only under the non-null check at line 65.
limitations: CWE-617 (CHECK at line 52): the guard at lines 44-45 establishes element-count equality, which is the precondition under which CopyFrom(old_lhs, rhs.shape()) succeeds; a witness that passes the guard yet fails is not expressible from fragment values, so this is an abort protecting a fragment-established invariant.

Dtype mismatch between rhs and old_lhs is not checked visibly in the fragment and could reach allocate_temp (lines 75-76) and the Copy sinks; however, Copy's body is not shown and the shown code derives no out-of-domain size/index argument at those call sites, making any OOB unconfirmable.

Use-after-free/race on the unlocked fall-through copy (lines 91-92) when use_exclusive_lock_ is false requires a concurrent-execution interleaving and a failure mechanism inside Copy's unshown body; the fragment does not establish that precondition.
No visible check prevents rhs from aliasing the lhs buffer (e.g., Assign(x, x)); consequences depend on Copy's callee body, which is outside the fragment.
Absolute byte capacities of tensor buffers are not declared in the fragment, so any byte-level boundary claim beyond the element-count equality established at line 45 is unconfirmable.
allocate_temp failure at lines 74-76 is handled by OP_REQUIRES_OK (graceful error status); no security-relevant operation runs on the failure state.

verdict.summary: digest_generic_verify compares the caller-supplied expected digest (md) against the computed digest (tmp) with memcmp at line 13. memcmp's standard contract stops at the first differing byte, so its runtime reveals the length of the matching prefix. Since md is read from the caller on every call and no guard or countermeasure modifies the comparison, repeated adaptive queries create a timing oracle that leaks the digest/MAC contents byte by byte, enabling forgery or authentication bypass when tmp is a keyed value.

evidence.reason: Line 13 feeds the unconstrained caller-supplied buffer md (line 1) and the computed digest tmp (line 9) into memcmp as the two compared buffers. memcmp's standard, name-implied contract compares byte-by-byte and returns at the first differing byte, so execution time is proportional to the common leading prefix length. The only guard on the path, `if (ret) goto end;` at lines 10-11, admits ret == 0 (digest_final success) and places no constraint on md or the comparison method, so the timing oracle is reachable for every caller-supplied md. Primary mechanism: CWE-208 observable timing discrepancy in a verification comparison; the weak comparison choice is made entirely in the shown code and no constant-time or blinded comparison exists.

assumptions: memcmp is assumed to compare byte-by-byte and stop at the first differing byte (standard C library documented behavior, used for the call-site confirmation).
digest_final(d, tmp) is assumed, by its name and use, to write the computed digest into tmp and return nonzero on failure; lines 10-11 handle that status.
len (line 4) retains the full signed int domain INT_MIN..INT_MAX because no shown statement constrains the return of digest_length(d); this drives the residual ranges used in Phase 3.
limitations: Negative len causing a huge size_t at memcmp (line 13) and xmalloc (line 7) is not a confirmed finding: digest_length(d)'s contract is not shown (no shown path produces a negative return), md's capacity is not identifiable from the fragment, and the xmalloc path depends on unchecked allocation-failure semantics (CWE-195/CWE-125 hypothesis only).
tmp is not NULL-checked after xmalloc(len) (line 7); whether xmalloc can fail or abort is outside the fragment, so an unchecked-allocation robustness concern only.

The fragment establishes no relationship between md's backing capacity and len, and does not state whether the digest is keyed (MAC) or unkeyed; the timing channel is confirmed, but severity scales with keyed usage.
Timing exploitation requires an attacker able to invoke the verifier repeatedly with chosen md values in a security-sensitive context, which is caller context not shown in the fragment.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the fragment. All candidates were demoted or excluded: the assert at line 15 protects an invariant the fragment itself establishes (lines 26/440), the 4-byte unknown-box read at line 397 is gated by the dataSize==4 check on the same line, the u64 accumulations (totSize, main_sidx_end_pos) are never consumed by any downstream operation, the NULL-dereference candidates cannot be produced by any statement in the fragment, the root_ssix/seg_ssix mismatch (lines 380-383) is unreachable from fragment-written state, and loop termination depends on the unshown bitstream/parser contract. Remaining items are robustness issues (constant-format-string %d/u64 mismatch at line 27) and unconfirmable hypotheses, recorded in limitations.

gf_list_count/get/add/del_item/insert/enum obey standard list semantics: index k in [0, count-1] is valid, strict comparison k < count excludes k == count, and enum returns NULL at exhaustion.
mov->movieFileMap->bs is a valid, non-NULL GF_BitStream supplied by the framework (lines 18, 23, 26, 30, 159, 268, 440 dereference it unconditionally).
The dataSize==4 check at line 397 is the fragment's own capacity statement for box->data; indices 0-3 are within it.
mov->moov is assigned only at line 57 in this fragment, immediately before the mvhd presence check at line 76, so the later dereference at line 470 is protected on the fragment's own path.

Format-specifier mismatch at line 27 (%d with u64 current_top_box_start): the format string is a literal so no format-string injection exists; this is wrong-vararg UB in a log call with no security-relevant downstream decision.

NULL-dereference candidates at lines 100, 332, 344, 365 (trak->Media->information->sampleTable, mov->moof->mfhd): no statement in the fragment produces NULL for these fields; their non-NULL invariant is the (unshown) parser's contract, and deep-deref of NULL here is unconfirmable.

u64 wraps in totSize (lines 74, 125, 135, 189, 204, 230, 258, 307, 427, 432) and main_sidx_end_pos (line 286): neither value is read again in the fragment, so no allocation, index, comparison, or formatting sink consumes a wrapped value.

assumptions: njs_array_alloc(vm, 0, delete, 0) at line 54 yields an array whose storage holds at least `delete` elements, so loop writes at line 62 (i in [0, delete-1], strict i < delete) are in-domain.
args contains exactly nargs entries, so &args[3] and &args[i] with i up to nargs-1 (items = nargs-3, line 35; loop lines 139-140) are in-domain.

limitations: Capacity of array->start is not declared or allocated in the fragment; OOB read at line 62 (n <= length-1) and OOB write at line 116 (region within new length) cannot be grounded in a quoted capacity, so they are unconfirmable in either direction.

Value of NJS_MAX_LENGTH (line 47) is unknown; boundary claims involving it cannot be grounded.
Fast-array invariant that storage capacity >= array->length is maintained outside this function; raw-buffer reads/writes at lines 62 and 116 depend on it.

Delta-driven allocation via njs_array_expand (line 98) is bounded by argument count through items/nargs; failure paths are checked, and a denial-of-service via allocation volume is not demonstrated from the shown code.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable within the fragment. All memcpy operations copy a compile-time sizeof(AVCSliceInfo) between identically-typed objects (lines 13, 37, 40, 159) and derive no size from input; no loop, format string, injection, file, or allocation sink exists. The slice path dereferences avc->s_info.sps->poc_type and n_state.sps->poc_type at line 79 with only assert(avc->s_info.sps) (line 77) as a guard — which does not test n_state.sps and is compiled out under NDEBUG — but no statement in the shown code ever produces a NULL sps pointer (caller state and the unshown callee avc_parse_slice are the only sources), so the NULL-deref/abort candidate fails the required in-fragment producer test and is recorded in limitations rather than as a finding.

assumptions: gf_bs_read_u8 (line 10) returns a u8 in [0,255]; the masks at lines 14 and 15 bound nal_unit_type to [0,31] and nal_ref_idc to [0,3].

On every path reaching lines 148/159, the local ret has been assigned (lines 23, 54–56ff, 136–143); no uninitialized ret read occurs.

Any OOB or capacity claim would require a sink deriving an index/size from input; none exists in the fragment — there are no loops, no pointers with attacker-derived offsets, and no attacker-controlled length arguments.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The only buffer write, X509_digest into hash_buffer at line 11, is bounded to SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH by the fixed EVP_sha256() algorithm and pinned by the length assert at lines 13-14 against the declared capacity uint8_t hash_buffer[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE] at line 2. All EVP_DigestUpdate return codes are asserted (lines 12, 17, 24, 31), and the loop length arguments at lines 22-23 and 29-30 have no demonstrated out-of-domain derivation in the shown code.

assumptions: EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE (line 2) and SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH (line 13) are the standard OpenSSL constants, with EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE >= SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH; the buffer is declared to hold the maximum digest for any EVP_MD.

X509_digest with EVP_sha256() writes exactly the digest length of the selected EVP_MD and sets the out length; EVP_DigestUpdate reads exactly the given byte length from the given pointer (standard OpenSSL contract).
verify_certificate_hash_list_ (line 20) and verify_certificate_spki_list_ (line 27) are standard containers, so range-for termination and data()/size() follow the container contract.
unsigned and unsigned int are interchangeable at the &hash_length call (line 11) on the target platform.
limitations: The element type of verify_certificate_hash_list_ / verify_certificate_spki_list_ is not visible in the fragment, so hash.size() * sizeof(value_type) (lines 22-23, 29-30) cannot be confirmed to overflow or to be mis-scaled; a 1-byte element type makes the byte length exact, and CWE-190/CWE-468 remain unconfirmed.

No shown bound limits the size of either hash list or its element lengths; a config-supplied huge list would only elongate the digest computation (resource-exhaustion concern with attacker control not shown in the fragment).

Empty-container iteration is admitted (no minimum-size check shown) but yields a zero-length EVP_DigestUpdate with no security-relevant effect; a NULL from hash.data() is not produced by any shown statement.
RELEASE_ASSERT aborts on library return codes (lines 12, 17, 24, 31); failure is library/internal-state driven, not attacker-directed through the shown code, so CWE-617 is not confirmed.
The resulting session-id digest is consumed outside this fragment, so any session-resumption or auth-bypass impact cannot be assessed from the shown code.

verdict.summary: Stack buffer overflow in njs_module_path: when dir != NULL, the length check `length > NJS_MAX_PATH` only bounds `dir->length` (plus optional separator) while `info->name.length` is copied unconstrained into `char src[NJS_MAX_PATH + 1]`, allowing an out-of-bounds write via njs_cpymem and the trailing NUL.

evidence.reason: `info->name.length` (size_t) is unconstrained on the dir != NULL path: line 9's assignment is overwritten at line 12, and line 25's guard tests only `length = dir->length + trail`, excluding the name term. With dir->length = NJS_MAX_PATH (trail=0) and info->name.length = 2, the guard at line 25 admits `length = NJS_MAX_PATH`, and this copy writes 'b' at index NJS_MAX_PATH+1 into `char src[NJS_MAX_PATH + 1]` (capacity line 6, last valid index NJS_MAX_PATH) — a 1-byte out-of-bounds write (CWE-121); any larger name.length extends the overflow proportionally.

Same unconstrained `info->name.length` reaches the NUL termination: after the line 39 copy advances p past the in-bounds region (e.g., to index NJS_MAX_PATH+2 in the witness above), this store writes the NUL at index NJS_MAX_PATH+2, exceeding the `NJS_MAX_PATH + 1` capacity declared at line 6 — an additional out-of-bounds write of the same CWE-121 stack overflow.

assumptions: `NJS_MAX_PATH` is a single named constant shared by the capacity declaration `char src[NJS_MAX_PATH + 1]` (line 6) and the guard `length > NJS_MAX_PATH` (line 25), making the boundary arithmetic exact.
`njs_cpymem(p, src, n)` copies n bytes and returns the advanced destination pointer (standard/name-implied copy semantics).
When `dir != NULL`, `dir->length >= 1` (enforced at line 14) so `dir->start[dir->length - 1]` (line 18) indexes at least element 0.
limitations: The capacity of `info->path` is not declared in the fragment, and `realpath` (line 42) returns NULL on length failure, so an overlong resolved path into `info->path` is an unconfirmable boundary claim.

Whether `dir->start`/`info->name.start` point to buffers of at least their stated lengths depends on a framework invariant not shown; the line-18 read and the exact size of the heap/provenance of the overrun contents are not confirmable from the fragment.

Potential path-traversal or symlink-following semantics of `open(&info->path[0], O_RDONLY)` (line 47) depend on the intended module-loader policy, which is outside the fragment; not reported as a separate vulnerability.
The theoretical `length++` wrap at line 21 when `dir->length == SIZE_MAX` is not needed to trigger the confirmed overflow and is not reported as an independent integer-overflow finding.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable from the fragment alone. Every dangerous-looking dereference either sits behind a visible protective check (the unconditional `!mov->moov->mvhd` check at lines 77-80 protecting the `mvhd->timeScale` use at line 476, the `!a` guard at line 34 protecting `a->type` at line 50, the `dataSize==4` guard at line 399) or depends on a callee-side invariant absent from the fragment (mfhd presence at line 366, the byte capacity of `box->data` at line 399, deep track/sample-table pointers at lines 101-102 and 320). The `root_ssix`/`seg_ssix` mismatch at lines 381-384 is a genuine logic anomaly but is not triggerable or consumable inside the fragment.

assumptions: Standard list semantics: for a list with count N, `gf_list_get(L, k)` is valid for k in 0..N-1; loops `for (k=0; k<gf_list_count(...); k++)` reach max index count-1, never count.

`gf_bs_get_position` returns the current bitstream position (u64), so the fragment-produced value at lines 26 and 446 satisfies `current_top_box_start >= bytes_removed`, keeping the line-15 assert and subtraction in-domain for fragment-derived values.

`GF_4CC(a,b,c,d)` consumes exactly the four named byte arguments (macro semantics).
limitations: C1: `mov->moof->mfhd->sequence_number` at line 366 has no visible NULL check, but the fragment contains no statement that produces or guarantees `mfhd`; the NULL producer is callee-side, so the NULL deref (CWE-476) is unconfirmable.
C2: reads `c[0..3]` at line 399 guarded only by `box->dataSize==4`; the byte capacity of `box->data` is not declared in the fragment, so neither an OOB read nor an in-domain read is confirmable.

C3: lines 381-384 guard on `root_ssix` but delete and fail to NULL `seg_ssix`; `root_ssix` is never assigned in the fragment and no consumer of the dangling `seg_ssix` exists here, so the potential use-after-free cannot be triggered or demonstrated.

C8: unchecked `gf_list_add` at lines 154, 328, and 425 fails only on allocation failure with no security-relevant operation on the failure state.
Loop termination at line 23 depends on the callee advancing the bitstream; a non-advancing parse (CWE-835) is not verifiable from the fragment.
Writes through `bytesMissing` (line 24) and `boxType` (line 30) assume caller-provided non-NULL pointers; a NULL contract violation is outside the fragment.

verdict.summary: No security vulnerability is confirmable from the shown fragment. All attacker-relevant logic (seccomp rule installation, socket-family allowlist, arch selection) operates on compile-time constants or on parameters that only influence bit-test comparisons, and every indexed loop is bounded by G_N_ELEMENTS over arrays declared in the fragment. The remaining concerns — silently ignored libseccomp rule-add failures other than -EFAULT (lines 217/235), discarded seccomp_rule_add_exact and lseek return values (256/261/269), sentinel arrays defined outside the fragment (191), and the fixed /tmp directory (263) — each depend on library contracts or externally-defined invariants that are not visible in the fragment, so they are recorded as limitations without CWE assignments.

assumptions: Loop capacities are derivable from the fragment: G_N_ELEMENTS(syscall_blocklist), G_N_ELEMENTS(syscall_nondevel_blocklist), and G_N_ELEMENTS(socket_family_allowlist) at lines 206/223/244 size the loops to the arrays declared at lines 50-111, 113-126, and 128-141 respectively.

arch is used via strcmp (lines 155/159/164/169), which fixes its C contract as a NUL-terminated string; NULL is separately handled at line 150.

After the check at lines 147-148, seccomp is non-NULL for all subsequent uses; after the check at lines 263-264, seccomp_tmpf.fd is a valid open fd, and glnx_steal_fd at line 272 transfers its ownership.
errnum in both blocklists is a compile-time EPERM or ENOSYS constant (visible in the initializers), so g_return_val_if_fail at lines 211/228 is unsatisfiable.
limitations: C1 (no CWE): seccomp_rule_add failures other than -EFAULT are silently treated as success at lines 217/235, so a failed rule add would proceed to export and use the possibly incomplete filter (266, 271). This cannot be confirmed because the fragment does not establish that libseccomp can return a negative other than -EFAULT for these compile-time arguments; the return-value contract is external to the fragment.

C2 (no CWE): seccomp_rule_add_exact return values are discarded at lines 256/261; a failed add would leave a socket family unblocked, but the visible comment (240-242) declares such failures expected and ignored, and no attacker-controlled input can force them within the fragment.

C3 (no CWE): the lseek return at line 269 is discarded; a failure would hand an fd at the wrong offset to bubblewrap, but the fd is a freshly created O_RDWR regular temp file whose creation was checked, and the fragment shows no producer of lseek failure.
