verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read in ParseEquation when the equation yields zero input subscripts: input_label_counts is resized to num_inputs (line 27) with no shown lower bound, and line 51 unconditionally evaluates (*input_label_counts)[0][label] whenever num_inputs != 1 (short-circuit), so num_inputs == 0 reads element 0 of an empty container (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: Input-derived num_inputs (line 16: int num_inputs = input_str.size(), residual range [0, INT_MAX] because the fragment imposes no minimum on ParseEinsumEquation's output) sets the outer capacity at line 27 (input_label_counts->resize(num_inputs)). At line 51, the short-circuit guard num_inputs == 1 admits num_inputs == 0 (0 == 1 is false), so (*input_label_counts)[0][label] is evaluated with container size 0; outer index 0 is outside the valid domain [0, 0), yielding an out-of-bounds read on the line-27 capacity when the loop body executes with num_labels >= 1 and label != kEllipsisLabel (lines 48-49). Primary mechanism: CWE-125 OOB read.

assumptions: kEllipsisLabel is a sentinel outside the mapped label range (real TensorFlow value -1), so the guards at lines 32, 40, and 49 correctly exclude it from label-indexed accesses.

MapToLabels numbers labels consistently with label_mapping (so non-ellipsis labels lie in [0, num_labels)); the shown code does not display MapToLabels' body, so lines 33 and 41 are analyzed only under this invariant.
The output pointer parameters are non-NULL per caller contract; no NULL check is shown and NULL can only originate outside the fragment.
limitations: The OOB at line 51 requires ParseEinsumEquation to accept a zero-input equation (e.g., "->a"); its acceptance set is not shown. If it guaranteed at least one input, the witness would be unreachable, but that guarantee cannot be used because it is not derivable from the fragment.

The return value of MapToLabels (lines 21, 23) is discarded; if it returns a failure status, malformed subscripts could be processed on a partial mapping, but its signature is unshown so the failure state is unconfirmable.

The label-indexed accesses at lines 33 and 41 are only in bounds if MapToLabels emits dense labels in [0, num_labels) and kEllipsisLabel is excluded; both depend on unshown code/constants, so a finding there is unconfirmable in either direction.
For num_inputs > 2, the unique computation only inspects operands 0 and 1 (lines 51-52), producing an incorrect DimensionType; this is a logic flaw with no memory impact inside the fragment.

The size_t-to-int conversions at lines 16 and 26 could in principle wrap for sizes above INT_MAX, but num_labels is bounded by the char key domain (≤ 256) and num_inputs derives from a parsed subscript string; no realistic wrap is demonstrated.

verdict.summary: BM_ParseGlobalQuantizer does not check the return of gf_sg_command_field_new() (line 30) before dereferencing it at line 31 (inf->new_node = node). If the constructor fails and returns NULL, the shown code performs a NULL-pointer write, crashing the decoder (CWE-476, low-severity DoS).

evidence.reason: `inf` is the unchecked return of `gf_sg_command_field_new(com)` at line 30; no shown statement constrains it, so per Phase 1 its residual range is the full `GF_CommandField *` domain including NULL (allocation-failure return, the name-implied contract of a constructor). The only guards on the path (line 7 `if (!node)`, line 10 `if (codec->scenegraph->global_qp)`, line 16 tag equality) constrain `node`, `scenegraph->global_qp`, and the node tag respectively, and none admits or excludes anything about `inf`. When line 30 yields NULL, the write `inf->new_node = node;` at line 31 dereferences a NULL pointer — NULL-pointer dereference, primary CWE-476 (crash/denial of service).

assumptions: The guard at line 7 reduces `node`'s residual range to non-NULL pointers, and the guard at line 16 further reduces it to nodes whose tag equals TAG_MPEG4_QuantizationParameter, making the cast at line 22 type-safe for the admitted set.

`gf_sg_command_field_new` (line 30) and `gf_sg_command_new` (line 29) are treated as allocation-style constructors whose failure yields NULL; this is inferred from their names and usage because their bodies are not shown.
limitations: The NULL dereference at line 31 requires `gf_sg_command_field_new` to fail (e.g., allocation failure); attacker control of that failure is not derivable from the fragment, so the impact is a robustness/DoS concern rated low.

`com == NULL` at line 30 (`gf_sg_command_field_new(com)`) and line 34 (`gf_list_add(com_list, com)`) would fail inside unshown callee code; it is subsumed by the line-31 finding and not independently confirmed.

NULL dereferences of `codec`, `codec->scenegraph`, `bs`, `com_list`, and `node->sgprivate` (lines 10-14, 22-24, 27) cannot be produced by any statement in the fragment; they are caller/framework-dependent and unconfirmed.

The reset of the previous global QP at lines 10-14 occurs before the new node's tag validation at line 16, so a tag-check failure leaves the prior quantizer state lost (lines 10-18); this is a logic/robustness concern with no security-relevant sink in the fragment.

The direct write `node->sgprivate->num_instances = 2` (line 27) and the double registration (global_qp plus command field) are refcount-sensitive, but the decrement/lifecycle code is not shown, so no use-after-free or double-free can be confirmed.

verdict.summary: RestoreTensor uses the int parameter restore_index, which the shown code never constrains (the only NumElements check is on input(0) at lines 6-8), to index tensor flat arrays and the framework dtype list. A negative or out-of-range restore_index (e.g., -1, a member of the admitted set of every guard on the path) reaches the array subscript at line 16 and line 53 and the framework index at line 42, producing an out-of-bounds read of tstring objects before the tensor buffer (CWE-125); the read value is then used in HasTensor and error output.

evidence.reason: restore_index is declared int at line 3 and no shown statement constrains it (the size==1 guard at lines 6-8 applies only to input(0); input(1) has no NumElements check), so its residual range is the full int domain. The sink is an array subscript on the flat<tstring>() array of tensor_name_t, whose valid domain is [0, NumElements()); witness restore_index = -1 passes the only preceding guard (line 8) and reads one tstring object before the array base regardless of the unstated NumElements() value — an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The resulting tensor_name flows into HasTensor (line 38) and error text (lines 39, 46).

Same unconstrained restore_index (declared line 3, no shown bounds) is used as a subscript into input(2)'s flat<tstring>() array; the !shape_spec.empty() guard at line 54 executes after this subscript and does not protect it. Witness restore_index = -1 passes all guards on the path (lines 8, 23, 27, 51) and performs an out-of-bounds read before the array base for every possible element count (CWE-125).

restore_index (int, full domain, unconstrained by any shown check) is passed as an index argument to expected_output_dtype; the callee consumes it as an index, whose required domain is [0, num_outputs), and the shown derivation can produce -1, i.e., an out-of-domain index on every path admitted by the preceding guards (CWE-125). This is the same root cause (missing bounds validation of restore_index) as the sink at line 16.

assumptions: OP_REQUIRES/OP_REQUIRES_OK abort kernel execution with an error status when their condition is false (the error-handling idiom used throughout the fragment).
flat<T>() returns a contiguous array of NumElements() elements with valid subscripts 0 <= i < NumElements() (the indexing contract under which flat<tstring>()(i) is a subscript).
CHECK_NOTNULL(p) returns p when p is non-null; reader is non-null on both branches (lines 23-26 and 27-31), so the CHECK at line 32 cannot fire.
context->input(i) and context->expected_output_dtype(i) provide the op-declared inputs/outputs per the framework API contract (inputs 0..2 exist when the op declares three inputs).
limitations: The exact element count N of input(1)/input(2) is not stated in the fragment, so the non-negative out-of-range case restore_index >= NumElements() is only a residual-range claim; the confirmed excess is the negative-index case (-1), which violates the subscript lower bound [0, N) for every N >= 0.

Attacker control of restore_index is not established inside the fragment (internal-helper parameter; typical kernel callers pass in-range loop indices), which bounds severity and supports confidence 0.7 rather than higher.

ParseShapeAndSlice (line 56) and CopySliceData (line 78) callee bodies are not shown, so slice-validation and copy-bound consistency (potential OOB write into t->flat<T>().data() whose capacity is output_shape per line 71) cannot be confirmed.
The dtype-mismatch error message at line 44 uses expected_output_dtype(0) instead of expected_output_dtype(restore_index) - a misleading-diagnostics bug with no demonstrated security impact.
file_pattern is used to open a user-selected checkpoint file (lines 24, 28, 40), which is the op's intended function; arbitrary-file/path behavior is not assessed as a flaw in this fragment.

A degenerate empty input(1)/input(2) tensor (NumElements() == 0) would make even restore_index == 0 out of bounds, but the fragment neither establishes nor refutes a minimum element count, so this is a range claim, not a demonstrated witness.

verdict.summary: In the tiled branch, DecodeChunk dereferences exr_image->tiles[tile_idx] without checking the calloc result, so an allocation failure (amplifiable via attacker-controlled offsets.size()) causes a NULL-pointer crash (CWE-476), and it discards DecodeTiledPixelData's return status so failed tile decodes are still reported as TINYEXR_SUCCESS (CWE-754).

evidence.reason: CWE-476: exr_image->tiles is assigned the unchecked calloc result at lines 82-83 (allocation of num_tiles elements, where num_tiles = offsets.size() at line 80 is entry-point-derived and unbounded in the fragment). With offsets.size() == 1, loop guard 85 (tile_idx < num_tiles) admits tile_idx == 0 and the dereference at line 87 executes before any other guard (the buffer-bound check at line 94 runs after it). On calloc failure the dereference is of NULL; no NULL check exists between lines 83 and 87, so the failure state is dereferenced and the process crashes (DoS).

evidence.snippet:
tinyexr::DecodeTiledPixelData(
          exr_image->tiles[tile_idx].images,
          &(exr_image->tiles[tile_idx].width),
          &(exr_image->tiles[tile_idx].height),
          exr_header->requested_pixel_types, data_ptr,
          static_cast<size_t>(data_len), exr_header->compression_type,
          exr_header->line_order, data_width, data_height, tile_coordinates[0],
          tile_coordinates[1], exr_header->tile_size_x, exr_header->tile_size_y,
          static_cast<size_t>(pixel_data_size),
          static_cast<size_t>(exr_header->num_custom_attributes),
          exr_header->custom_attributes,
          static_cast<size_t>(exr_header->num_channels), exr_header->channels,
          channel_offset_list);
evidence.reason: CWE-754: the return status of DecodeTiledPixelData is discarded, unlike the checked DecodePixelData call at lines 243-254. For any admitted chunk (data_len in [4, data_size] per guard 125), a decode failure leaves invalid_data (initialized false at line 58) untouched in the tiled branch, so checks at lines 262-268 never fire and the function returns TINYEXR_SUCCESS at line 284, reporting an invalid/undecoded tile as valid image data.

assumptions: head/size describe a readable buffer of exactly size bytes; guards at lines 94 and 185 bound offsets against it.
sizeof(int) == 4 and 64-bit size_t for the byte accounting (the code itself uses sizeof(int)*5 = 20 and sizeof(int)*2 = 8).
offsets is the block table with size() entries, each indexing a block start; its count is unconstrained by the fragment.
AllocateImage allocates an image matching the width/height arguments passed (name-implied); no finding depends on its internals.
limitations: The scanline line_no/num_lines span is not an OOB write: guards 220 (num_lines > 0 => data_window[3] >= line_no) and 240 (line_no_adj >= 0) jointly bound the decoded span to [0, data_height-1] via lines 16-17, 215-216, 229-238.

data_window[3] + 1 at line 216 can overflow int when data_window[3] == INT_MAX, but the wrapped result makes num_lines <= 0 and is rejected by guard 220; UB with no reachable security impact in the fragment.

data_width/data_height at lines 16-17 can overflow int for extreme windows; any wrapped small value admitted by guards 19/32 leaves allocations keyed to the same wrapped dimensions, so no OOB is provable from the shown arithmetic.
static_cast<int>(num_blocks) at line 182 truncates counts above INT_MAX, silently skipping blocks and still returning success, but produces no out-of-bounds index.

The OpenMP loop (line 180) races on the shared invalid_data bool (line 58; TODO comment acknowledges it); a lost failure could return success, but this is a formal data race/robustness concern rather than a demonstrated memory-safety failure.

num_channels is unbounded in the fragment, so total_data_len wrap at lines 160-161 and the pixel_types copy loop at lines 272-274 (array capacities not declared in the fragment) cannot be confirmed as OOB.
The scanline path admits data_len in {1,2,3} (only data_len == 0 rejected at line 209); decoding such small chunks is entirely inside DecodeTiledPixelData/DecodePixelData, whose bodies are not shown.
tile_coordinates[0..1] are unvalidated (only LoD entries checked at lines 113/117); their handling is callee-internal and not anchored in the fragment.
AllocateImage failures (lines 87-89, 175-177) would pass NULL images into the decode helpers; any resultant dereference is in unshown callee code.
A NULL result from calloc is the sole trigger of CWE-476; the finding is OOM-dependent and confidence is capped accordingly.

verdict.summary: Signed int overflow in memory_size * num_filters at line 50: both operands are model-supplied tensor dims with no magnitude bound in the shown code, so e.g. 65536 * 65536 wraps to 0 and the state-shape equality check (lines 49-50) accepts a state tensor of shape (1,0) instead of requiring dim1 == memory_size*num_filters, corrupting the validation that gates tensor geometry.

evidence.reason: memory_size (line 30, from weights_time->dims->data[1]) and num_filters (line 26, from weights_feature->dims->data[0]) are entry-point model data with residual range = full int: the only shown guards are rank != 0 (line 27), num_filters % rank == 0 (line 28), and the equalities at lines 31-33, none of which bounds magnitude or sign. The int*int product at line 50 overflows for the admitted values memory_size = 65536, num_filters = 65536 (both admitted: rank=1 passes line 27; 65536 % 1 == 0 passes line 28; dim equalities pass lines 31-33), wrapping 2^32 to 0 in 32-bit int. The wrapped 0 is consumed directly by the TF_LITE_ENSURE_EQ at lines 49-50, so a state tensor with dims (1,0) passes the shape validation that is supposed to establish dim1 == memory_size*num_filters = 2^32 elements; primary CWE-190 (signed integer overflow corrupting a security-relevant validation comparison).

assumptions: int is 32-bit with two's-complement wraparound (TFLite target convention); the overflow itself does not depend on a fragile boundary since 65536*65536 = 2^32 far exceeds INT_MAX.
Tensor dims, TfLiteSVDFParams, quantization fields, and node->inputs/outputs metadata originate from the untrusted model file and are consumed as entry-point input by this function.
TF_LITE_ENSURE/TF_LITE_ENSURE_OK abort the Prepare call on failure, so later operations only run when all prior checks pass.
TfLiteIntArray data arrays hold size elements per their size field; GetTemporarySafe validates the index against node->temporaries->size.
IsHybridOp (line 60) is a framework helper whose exact predicate is not shown; mutual exclusivity with is_full_integer is assumed but not established in the fragment.
limitations: Downstream heap out-of-bounds in the SVDF Eval kernel (state stride memory_size*num_filters over a state allocated from the wrapped dim1) is outside this fragment and not confirmed here.

1-D input/weights tensors reading input->dims->data[1] (line 31), weights_feature->dims->data[1] (line 32), weights_time->dims->data[1] (line 30), and bias->dims->data[0] (line 37) are OOB-read candidates whose capacity (dims->size) is not identifiable from the shown code (CWE-125 left unconfirmed).

Negative rank (admitted by line 27) yields negative num_units (line 29) stored as a dimension (lines 55, 172) passed to ResizeTensor; the callee's handling of negative dims is not shown, so impact is unconfirmable.
scale->data[0] reads at lines 201-206 are guarded only by quantization.type != kTfLiteNoQuantization (lines 184-200), but the scale array capacity is not visible in the fragment.

TfLiteIntArrayCreate results (lines 53, 66, 68, 70, 74, 104, 118, 134, 149, 163, 171) are dereferenced without NULL checks; this is an unchecked-allocation concern (CWE-476 on OOM), not a confirmed finding because no security-relevant operation runs on the failure state and no attacker-controlled volume is shown.
Zero or negative dims (e.g., memory_size = 0) yield zero-sized tensors; robustness concern only, no in-fragment memory error demonstrated.

verdict.summary: The signature-input lengths (rpid_hash_len, credential_id_len, cert_x_len, cert_y_len) are unconstrained in the shown code and are summed in size_t at line 98 to size the data_signed heap buffer; an admitted value such as rpid_hash_len=2^64-1 wraps the sum to 33 bytes, and the subsequent memcpy at line 108 writes 2^64-1 bytes into that 33-byte allocation, producing a heap buffer overflow (CWE-787, root cause CWE-190).

evidence.reason: rpid_hash_len has no shown constraint in the fragment (its residual range is the full size_t domain), and the allocation at line 98 computes rpid_hash_len+32+credential_id_len+cert_x_len+cert_y_len+2 in size_t, which wraps: with rpid_hash_len=2^64-1 and the other lengths 0, the sum becomes 33. The malloc-NULL guard at line 98 admits this result, so memcpy at line 108 writes 2^64-1 bytes into the 33-byte heap block declared only by the line-98 allocation, a confirmed heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

The allocation-size expression sums four unconstrained size_t inputs plus the constant 2; for the admitted value rpid_hash_len=2^64-1 (other lengths 0) the sum wraps modulo 2^64 to 33 bytes, undersizing the allocation that the memcpy sinks at lines 108-123 then overflow (CWE-190 as the independent root cause of the CWE-787 write).

assumptions: size_t is at least 32 bits, so the modulo-wrap witness (2^64-1 + 32 + 2 -> 33) occurs in the shown unsigned arithmetic.
o_malloc behaves like malloc and returns a usable pointer for a 33-byte request when the NULL branch at line 98 is not taken.

client_data_hash_len remains 32 after generate_digest_raw at line 87 (it is initialized to 32 at line 10 and the digest is SHA-256), so the same value participates symmetric in the line-98 size and the line-111 write.
gnutls_x509_crt_get_key_id with GNUTLS_KEYID_USE_SHA256 writes at most the 32 bytes of cert_export declared at line 9, and o_base64_encode fits in the 64-byte cert_export_b64 declared at line 9.
limitations: cbor_bytestring_handle/cbor_bytestring_length at lines 53-54 are applied to att_cert without a shown cbor_isa_bytestring check; whether the callee returns NULL safely or aborts is not visible in the fragment, so it is unconfirmed.

The msprintf calls at lines 36 and 63 pass a size_t precision to '%.*s' where int is required (varargs type mismatch); turning this into an OOB read needs a length >= 2^31 and non-NUL-terminated data, neither established in the fragment.
o_strlen((char *)client_data) at line 87 assumes NUL termination that no shown statement guarantees.
An empty-string map key compares equal to "x5c"/"sig" via o_strncmp with n=0 (lines 31, 33); identified as a validation weakness without demonstrated security impact.

The confirmed wrap requires the caller to supply near-SIZE_MAX lengths; if the real system derives these lengths from finite buffers, the overflow is unreachable, but that invariant is outside the shown fragment and cannot shrink the admitted domain here.

verdict.summary: The PORT command handler parses six unconstrained %d values and formats four of them with sprintf into a fixed stack array addr[INET_ADDRSTRLEN] (16 bytes). A full parse of values like 2147483647,2147483647,2147483647,2147483647 makes sprintf write 43 characters plus NUL (44 bytes), overflowing the buffer by 28 bytes before the inet_aton validation at line 18 executes — a stack-based buffer overflow (CWE-121) triggered by an attacker-supplied PORT argument.

evidence.reason: Entry-point input str flows through sscanf at line 14 into ints a..d with the full int domain (no magnitude cap is shown between lines 14 and 15). A witness of a=b=c=d=2147483647 (parsed from "2147483647,2147483647,2147483647,2147483647,1,1") makes this sprintf write 43 formatted characters plus NUL = 44 bytes into addr, whose capacity is declared at line 4 as char addr[INET_ADDRSTRLEN] (16 bytes per the POSIX documented constant), an excess of 28 bytes. The only downstream guard (inet_aton at line 18) executes after the write and cannot protect it. Primary mechanism: stack-based buffer overflow (CWE-121) with attacker-controlled content overwriting adjacent stack data.

assumptions: INET_ADDRSTRLEN is the POSIX-documented IPv4 text-buffer size of 16 bytes; the constant appears by name in the declaration at line 4, which is the quoted capacity line.
str is the externally supplied FTP PORT-command argument and no length or content constraint on it appears anywhere in the fragment.
int is 32-bit, so sscanf %d can yield 2147483647 (10 digits).
limitations: The discarded sscanf return (line 14) can leave a..f uninitialized when fewer than six conversions match; the indeterminate values are used at lines 15 and 25 (CWE-457 as a robustness concern), but the resulting values are not deterministically attacker-chosen, so no concrete security impact could be confirmed.
The int arithmetic e * 256 + f at line 25 can overflow, but the client already directly supplies the desired PORT data-port value, so a wrapped result does not grant any additional capability.
The ERR %s read of the overrun addr at line 19 is a consequence of the same line-15 overflow, not an independent root cause.
Any length caps imposed on the PORT command outside this fragment are not shown and therefore not used.

verdict.summary: OP_JMPUW (and the OP_JMP/JMPIF/JMPNOT/JMPNIL family) relocate the program counter without any bounds check against irep->ilen before the next instruction fetch. Line 310 computes a = (uint32_t)((pc - irep->iseq) + (int16_t)a) and line 330 stores pc = irep->iseq + a; the only in-domain statement, the assert 'a < irep->ilen' at line 316, sits in the CHECKPOINT_RESTORE branch only. A witness irep whose 3-unit iseq holds OP_JMPUW with operand +5 (and no catch handler so the guard at line 320 admits) yields a = 5 >= ilen = 3, and the fetch at JUMP reads 2 units past the buffer (operand -1 yields index 0xFFFFFFFF). This is a confirmed OOB instruction-buffer read (CWE-125) gated only by the unshown premise that untrusted bytecode can reach this helper; all other unguarded index sites (pool/syms/reps/regs) lack an identifiable capacity and are recorded as limitations.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) of irep->iseq: operand a is decoded from the instruction stream (declared uint32_t at line 11) with residual range [-32768,32767] after the (int16_t) cast at line 310, and no shown statement bounds it between line 310 and line 330; the only valid-index statement is the debug assert `mrb_assert(a >= 0 && a < irep->ilen)` at line 316, which sits inside CHECKPOINT_RESTORE (lines 311-317) and does not gate this path. The guard at line 320 (`if (ch)`) admits the witness: an irep with a 3-code-unit iseq holding OP_JMPUW operand +5 and no ensure handler gives ch==NULL, a = (uint32_t)(0+5) = 5 >= ilen = 3, so `pc = irep->iseq + 5` (or 0xFFFFFFFF for operand -1) and the JUMP at line 331 fetches 2 units (or ~4GiB) past the 3-unit buffer.

Same CWE-125 class: OP_JMP (and OP_JMPIF/JMPNOT/JMPNIL at lines 289/296/303) adjust pc by a decoded 16-bit operand with no comparison against irep->ilen (the fragment's only iseq bound, line 316). A witness offset: executing the first instruction of any iseq with operand -1 yields pc = irep->iseq - 1, and the subsequent instruction fetch reads before the buffer; operand +32767 likewise lands past the end for any shorter iseq. No guard of any kind sits between the operand and this sink (lines 283-286 contain no conditional).

assumptions: irep->ilen (line 316) is the code-unit length of irep->iseq and is used by the fragment itself as the sole validity bound for instruction indices; it is the only capacity for the iseq identifiable in the shown code.
S-format jump operands are consumed as signed 16-bit values via the explicit (int16_t) casts at lines 284, 289, 296, 303 and 310.
catch_handler_find returning NULL means 'no handler covers pc', as the fragment treats NULL with plain fall-through at lines 319-323 and 931-932.
regs = mrb->c->ci->stack (line 40); pool (line 5), syms (line 6) and irep->reps are pointers whose backing array sizes are not declared anywhere in the fragment.
limitations: The positive verdict for OP_JMPUW/OP_JMP depends on the unshown premise that the VM can be driven by bytecode not validated by a compiler/loader; no attacker-controlled entry point is visible in this fragment, which caps confidence at 0.6. A trust invariant 'bytecode is compiler-validated' is stated nowhere in the fragment and per the rules may not be used to convert the verdict to safe.

Unguarded indices into pool (lines 53, 74-75, 1544-1547, 1560-1563, 1774), syms (lines 128..., 1782?), and irep->reps (lines 1617, 1697) cannot be confirmed: the pool/syms/reps capacities are not identifiable from the fragment, so the required byte-level boundary claim is unconfirmable.

Register-window accesses without an identifiable regs capacity (OP_GETIDX line 197, OP_SETIDX line 230, L_SEND_SYM line 409, OP_ARGARY lv==0 path, OP_ENTER lines 689-757 incl. the argc==15 packed path, OP_APOST lines 1495-1533, OP_HASH/OP_HASHADD/OP_ARYPUSH lines 1573-1595, 1451-1457, and regs[irep->nlocals] at lines 1005, 1829) are demoted: the ci-stack capacity never appears in the fragment.

L_CATCH target pc = irep->iseq + mrb_irep_catch_handler_unpack(ch->target) (line 942) is also unchecked against irep->ilen, but ch->target is decoded from handler-table data not shown in the fragment, so a confirmed derivation cannot be traced.

OP_DEBUG -> abort() (line 1767) is gated by preprocessor configuration (MRB_USE_DEBUG_HOOK/MRB_NO_STDIO) whose values are not fixed by the fragment; and mrb_assert(!"bad mrb_type") (line 334) requires an mrb->exc->tt value not producible on a path shown here — both are unconfirmed reachable-assert/abort candidates.

NULL dereferences of proc (line 4) or of cipush results (lines 441, 577, 1706) would require a NULL parameter or unchecked allocation failure originating outside what the fragment can produce; per rules these are out-of-scope limitations, not findings.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. Every fragment-visible indexed access is provably in-domain: `flat<float>()(0)` is protected by the singleton checks (L42/L47, or L15/L21 with num_slices==1), and the sliced-path reads/writes (L94-L97) are bounded by capacities exactly equal to num_slices (L21/L34/L54/L74-L77) while the loop admits only i in [0, num_slices) (L92). Remaining risk is confined to unshown callee contracts: `flat_inner_outer_dims(axis_ - 1)` receives -1 for axis_==0 (L80), and empty-slice/degenerate-range behavior inside QuantizeSlice/QuantizeTensor is not visible; these are limitations, not confirmed findings.

assumptions: axis_ and mode_ are integer op attributes whose declarations are outside the fragment; axis_ retains its full integer domain except for the constraints shown at L7 and L9.

Tensor framework invariants used by the guards: dims() >= 0 and dim_size(d) >= 0 for a valid index, and NumElements() = product of dim sizes (L15-L21, L34-L40 rely on dims()==1 so NumElements() == dim_size(0)).
OP_REQUIRES_OK aborts Compute with the error status on failure, so allocate_output failures (L56, L62-L63, L74-L77) never leave nullptr outputs dereferenced.

output is allocated with input.shape() (L56), so output->dim_size(i) values and NumElements equal input's, making {pre_dim, num_slices, post_dim} (L88-L89) an exact factorization of output->NumElements() absent int64 overflow.
limitations: flat_inner_outer_dims<float, 3>(axis_ - 1) at L80 receives -1 when axis_ == 0 (admitted by L9); whether the callee rejects, clamps, or rebases that argument, and whether its middle dim equals num_slices, is unshown (not standard-name-implied semantics), so no OOB read or reachable CHECK/abort can be confirmed at this call site.

int64 -> int narrowing at L14 (num_slices = input.dim_size(axis_)) if a dimension exceeded INT_MAX; no fragment statement caps tensor dim sizes, and the narrowed value's downstream effect (loop bound, reshape dim) is not tied to a confirmed sink with a visible capacity.

num_slices == 0 is admitted by L21/L34 and falls through L61 into the slice path with the L92 loop skipped; this is a correctness/semantics observation for empty axis dimensions, not a memory-safety finding.

verdict.summary: Integer overflow in `size * 8` at line 8: the entry-point `int size` is unconstrained by any shown check (residual range INT_MIN..INT_MAX), so for size >= 2^28 the product wraps negative, init_get_bits voids the GetBitContext per its standard contract, and the discarded return lets skip_bits_long/get_bits dereference the NULL-buffered reader (crash) — a reachable DoS on crafted large extradata.

evidence.reason: `size` (signed int, entry-point, residual range INT_MIN..INT_MAX with no shown constraint) is multiplied by 8 in int arithmetic; for the admitted value size = 268435456 the product 2^31 overflows and wraps negative. The standard init_get_bits contract requires bit_size in [0, INT_MAX-7] and on violation voids the reader (buffer=NULL) while returning -1, which the shown code discards. The corrupted length is thus consumed by a memory-reading API (sink line 8), and the failure state is used downstream at line 12 — primary mechanism CWE-190 signed integer overflow corrupting a security-relevant length.

When the line-8 overflow invalidated gb (witness: size = 268435456, buf = valid AAC config), the guard at lines 10-11 (`if (off < 0) return off;`) admits off >= 0, so this skip always executes with n >= 0 against a reader whose buffer is NULL; the standard skip_bits_long macro then performs a multi-byte read from `gb.buffer + (off >> 3)` = NULL + offset, causing a NULL-pointer read crash. No shown statement bounds off above by the remaining bit count, and none revalidates gb after the discarded init failure — CWE-190's corrupted length reaches a memory read here.

init_get_bits/skip_bits_long/get_bits/put_bits/flush_put_bits and the MPEG-4 config parser follow their standard FFmpeg API semantics: init_get_bits rejects bit_size < 0 or > INT_MAX-7 by voiding the context (buffer = NULL, bit_size = 0) and returning -1, and the reader macros perform unchecked buffer reads via pointer arithmetic.

verdict.summary: handle_PORT discards the return value of sscanf and never initializes a..f, so a short PORT argument leaves some of them indeterminate; the indeterminate ints are read in snprintf (addr construction) and in ctrl->data_port = e * 256 + f, steering active-mode connection metadata and leaking stack residue into logs (CWE-457, root cause CWE-252).

evidence.snippet: snprintf(addr, sizeof(addr), "%d.%d.%d.%d", a, b, c, d);
evidence.reason: sscanf at line 14 assigns a prefix of a..f from attacker-controlled str and its return is discarded (no count check, no initialization at line 3). For PORT argument "1,2,3", only a,b,c are assigned and d is indeterminate, yet snprintf at line 15 reads d into the %d argument, an uninitialized int consumed by a standard formatting operation — CWE-457 (primary) caused by the unchecked sscanf return (CWE-252). No guard precedes this read; the inet_aton check at line 18 runs after it and cannot protect it.

For PORT argument "1,2,3,4,5", sscanf (line 14) assigns a..e=5 but leaves f indeterminate (no trailing ','+integer to match); addr becomes "1.2.3.4" which passes the inet_aton guard at line 18, so execution reaches line 25 and reads indeterminate f in signed int arithmetic, storing the result into ctrl->data_port (CWE-457; unchecked sscanf return at line 14 is the CWE-252 root cause). The attacker-controlled e and full-range %d values also make e*256+f overflow, but the downstream port consumer is outside the fragment, so that part is only a noted limitation.

assumptions: str is a NUL-terminated C string, the contract required by sscanf at line 14.
ctrl is non-NULL (internal-helper parameter; NULL is not producible in the fragment).

INET_ADDRSTRLEN in the declaration at line 4 is the standard named constant; its numeric value is not visible in the fragment and is not needed for the confirmed finding because snprintf bounds its own output.
limitations: Integer overflow of e*256+f and the missing 0..65535 port-range validation (line 25) cannot be confirmed as security-relevant because the consumer of ctrl->data_port (the data-connection connect) is not shown in the fragment; no CWE attached.

Truncation of addr by snprintf at line 15 is bounded by sizeof(addr) and cannot overflow; a truncated or short-form address accepted by inet_aton is consumed consistently at lines 24/27, so no injection is confirmed.
Log injection via data_address is not a finding: inet_aton at line 18 rejects non-IP characters, so control characters cannot survive into lines 19/24/27.
Discarded return values of close (line 9) and send_msg (lines 20, 28) are not findings: no security-relevant operation runs on a failure state.

verdict.summary: BD_DecMFFieldVec reads the MF field count nbFields directly from the untrusted BIFS bitstream (line 20, up to 2^31-1) and passes it unvalidated as the element count to gf_sg_vrml_mf_alloc (line 29), forcing a multi-gigabyte allocation request (>= 2 GiB at the maximal admitted count) from a few bytes of input, enabling memory-exhaustion denial of service (CWE-770).

evidence.reason: The allocation-count argument nbFields is derived at line 20 from entry-point bitstream input bs: NbBits=gf_bs_read_int(bs,5) at line 19 admits [0,31], so nbFields=gf_bs_read_int(bs,NbBits) admits [0,2^31-1] with no shown constraint between line 20 and this sink (line 22 and line 28 are value-preserving/type-only guards). Witness: NbBits=31 and a 31-bit count field all-ones gives nbFields=2147483647, which passes every guard and reaches this sink. The name-implied semantics of gf_sg_vrml_mf_alloc is allocation of an array of nbFields elements, i.e. nbFields*sizeof(element) bytes; with sizeof(element)>=1 the maximal admitted count requests >= 2,147,483,647 bytes from a few bytes of stream, an out-of-domain request for the operation (uncontrolled allocation, CWE-770) whose success causes memory-exhaustion DoS; an allocator failure would be handled by the checked return at line 30, so the confirmed mechanism is resource exhaustion, not memory corruption.

assumptions: gf_bs_read_int(bs, n) returns a value in [0, 2^n - 1] for bit counts n <= 31, per the name-implied semantics of the bitstream reader used at lines 19-20.
Each element of an MF array occupies sizeof(element) >= 1 byte (C object-size rule), so the maximal count 2^31-1 yields an allocation request of at least 2 GiB.
field->fieldType values other than GF_SG_VRML_MFNODE all reach the line-29 branch via the line-28 complement test, and the count is passed identically for all of them.
limitations: Integer overflow of count * element-size inside gf_sg_vrml_mf_alloc is not confirmable because the callee body is not shown.

Whether the oversized allocation succeeds depends on the allocator/overcommit; a clean failure would only take the checked error return at line 30, so the confirmed impact is memory-exhaustion on success, not memory corruption.

gf_bifs_dec_qp14_set_length(codec, nbFields) at line 25 and the MFNODE-branch loop at line 40 consume the same tainted count, but their internal limits are not visible in the fragment, so no additional finding is confirmed from them.
No NULL-dereference finding: field/codec are framework-provided with no shown NULL producer, and new_node is NULL-checked at line 42.
The double gf_node_register (lines 43, 63) / gf_node_unregister (line 64) refcount behavior is not confirmable without the callee bodies.
The MFNODE-branch loop at line 40 is bounded by the encoded node data present in the bitstream and terminates early via line 78; no amplification beyond input volume is confirmable.

verdict.summary: Integer overflow in the constant-folding size guard: out_shape.num_elements() * DataTypeSize(n->output_type(i)) (lines 29-30) is computed with no overflow check, so a fully defined shape whose element count times element size reaches 2^64 wraps to 0 (or negative) and fails the '> max_constant_size_in_bytes' comparison. The oversized-output skip at line 31 is bypassed and the node is reported foldable despite a true materialized size far beyond int64_t, gating a decision that leads to resource-exhaustion/DoS during downstream constant folding (CWE-190).

evidence.reason: The size product feeding the security-relevant cap comparison overflows. out_shape derives from shape_map entry shape_it->second[i] (L27); the only guard, IsFullyDefined() (L28), admits any fully defined shape and imposes no magnitude bound, and L22-L35 contain no overflow check or dimension cap. A fully defined shape [2^31,2^31] gives num_elements()=2^62; multiplied by a 4-byte element size the 64-bit product 2^64 wraps to 0, and 0 > max_constant_size_in_bytes (int64_t, L6) is false, so the 'skip oversized output' return false at L31 is bypassed and the function returns true at L70 for a tensor whose true size is 2^64 bytes. Overflow is CWE-190: the corrupted value is consumed by the comparison that gates the oversized-output security decision, changing control flow toward a huge downstream constant-fold allocation.

assumptions: The product out_shape.num_elements() * DataTypeSize(...) is a 64-bit integer expression because it is compared directly against the int64_t parameter max_constant_size_in_bytes (L6, L29-L30); the wrap to 0 holds under both signed and unsigned 64-bit products for the 2^62-by-4 witness.
DataTypeSize returns the per-element size in bytes (name-implied contract); value 4 for a float/int32 element is a TensorFlow API constant not visible in the fragment.
IsFullyDefined() admits shapes with all dimensions known and non-negative; the fragment establishes no upper bound on any dimension, so num_elements() is unbounded within the shown code.
limitations: The return types of num_elements() and DataTypeSize() are not declared in the fragment; the 64-bit width of the product is implied by the direct int64_t comparison but not proven by a shown declaration.
shape_map is an internal-helper parameter (provenance unknown); attacker control of the shape magnitudes is presumed from the caller/model-input chain and is not visible in the fragment.

A potential OOB read at n->output_type(i) (L29) when a shape_map vector is longer than the node's output count is unconfirmable: the output-list capacity is not identifiable anywhere in the shown code.

The resulting memory exhaustion from constant-folding the oversized tensor happens in a downstream component outside this fragment, so it is described as the impact of the overflow rather than a separately confirmed CWE.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the shown fragment. verdict.summary: No security vulnerability is confirmed inside the fragment. Every *p read is bounded by the entry guard `if ( p == pe ) goto _test_eof;` (lines 15-16) and by each per-state `if ( ++p == pe ) goto _test_eofN;` guard preceding `case N`, with the buffer bound anchored at `pe = buffer+len` (line 8); all callback (pointer, length) pairs lie inside the buffer, and the epilogue asserts protect invariants the fragment itself maintains. Concerns that could not be confirmed as findings: an in-bounds single-byte write that casts away const on `const char *buffer` (`snake_upcase_char((char *)p)`), and the `off <= len` precondition enforced only by an assert (line 5).

assumptions: `buffer` is readable for `len` bytes and `off <= len` holds, as required by the assert at line 5 (`assert(off <= len && "offset past end of buffer");`); the fragment never dereferences index >= len.
The read bound is anchored at line 8 `pe = buffer+len;` together with the entry guard (lines 15-16) and the per-state guards, e.g. lines 40-42 `if ( ++p == pe ) goto _test_eof2;` preceding `case 2:`.

Within a single call, `MARK(mark, p)` records positions in the current buffer and `LEN`/`PTR_TO` are used at positions <= p in that same buffer, so every callback receives an in-domain (pointer, length) pair.
limitations: `snake_upcase_char((char *)p)` (tr21/tr23 actions) writes one byte through a const-cast pointer derived from `const char *buffer` (line 1); the store is in-bounds, but whether the backing object is read-only (which would turn this into a crash/DoS) is caller-determined and unconfirmable from the fragment, so it is recorded as a const-correctness/UB hardening concern without a CWE.

`off <= len` is enforced only by the assert at line 5; under NDEBUG, `off > len` would make `p = buffer+off` exceed `pe` and `case 1: switch((*p))` (line 20) would read out of bounds. `off` is an internal parameter of unknown provenance in the fragment, so this is a precondition/hardening concern rather than an attacker-directed finding.

`parser->mark`, `parser->field_start`, and `parser->query_start` persist across calls; the pointer/length arithmetic (`LEN(mark, p)`, `http_field(...)`) assumes consecutive calls reuse the same backing buffer. A caller swapping buffers between calls would make the subtraction cross-object (UB); that caller contract is not visible in the fragment.
The commented-out `assert(*pe == '\0' ...)` (line 10) documents a caller contract that `buffer[len]` is NUL; the fragment itself never dereferences `*pe`.

Higher-level HTTP parsing policy (e.g., Transfer-Encoding/Content-Length handling that underlies request-smuggling classes) lives in the callback bodies (`parser->http_field`, `parser->header_done`) and is not shown in this fragment; those classes are out of scope here.

verdict.summary: Integer overflow in the size guard at IsConstantFoldable lines 28-29: num_elements()*DataTypeSize(...) is computed in 64-bit unsigned arithmetic and wraps for fully-defined shapes with >=2^62 elements (e.g. dims [2^31,2^31], DT_FLOAT -> product 0). The wrapped size never exceeds max_constant_size_in_bytes, so the oversized-output rejection (line 30) is skipped and IsConstantFoldable returns true (line 69), admitting constant folding that materializes a ~2^64-byte tensor and causes memory exhaustion / denial of service. Root cause is CWE-190 integer overflow corrupting the security-relevant size gate.

evidence.reason: out_shape is taken from shape_map->find(n->name()) at line 23 and indexed at line 26; the only per-shape constraint in the fragment is IsFullyDefined() at line 27, which bounds neither dimensions nor element count, so out_shape.num_elements() retains its full positive range (admitted witness: 2^62 for dims [2^31,2^31]). The product at line 28, evaluated as a 64-bit unsigned size (element count * DataTypeSize), wraps: 2^62 * 4 = 2^64 mod 2^64 = 0, so the comparison at lines 28-29 is false for any non-negative int64_t cap declared at line 6, the oversized-output guard (return false at line 30) is bypassed, and the node is admitted by return true at line 69. This is CWE-190: an integer overflow corrupts the byte-size value used in the security-relevant gating comparison, defeating the resource-exhaustion protection documented at line 22 ("We can skip the node if an output is known to be oversized") and enabling oversized constant folding (OOM/DoS).

assumptions: Line 22's comment establishes that the multiplication/comparison at lines 28-29 is the size gate meant to skip nodes with oversized outputs; bypassing it admits folding of oversized nodes.

Line 27 IsFullyDefined() is the only guard applied to out_shape; it excludes unknown/partial dims but imposes no maximum on num_elements(), so values up to the full int64 positive domain remain admitted.

Line 6 declares max_constant_size_in_bytes as int64_t, fixing the byte-size comparison domain; the product uses the plain C++ '*' operator on the name-implied element-count and bytes-per-element return values with no checked arithmetic or division-based bound.

num_elements() and DataTypeSize() return name-implied count/byte-size values (int64 element count and size_t byte size in the TensorFlow API contract); the fragment itself shows no declaration or check bounding either operand.
limitations: Potential OOB read of n's output-type table via n->output_type(i) at line 28 when shape_it->second.size() exceeds n's output count: the capacity of n's output array is not identifiable in the fragment, so this is unconfirmable (no CWE).

A negative max_constant_size_in_bytes (full int64_t domain at line 6, unconstrained in the fragment) would convert to a huge unsigned value at the comparison and disable the size gate for all inputs; treated as a caller-config robustness concern, not a confirmed attacker-controlled path inside the fragment.
The line 25 loop (int64_t i < size_t) could only misbehave for vectors longer than 2^63-1 entries, which is not realizable; not a finding.

The absolute memory exhaustion occurs in the constant-folding consumer outside the fragment; the defect confirmed here is the corrupted size value in the gating comparison (lines 28-29) that lets IsConstantFoldable return true (line 69).

The early return true for n->IsConstant() at lines 9-11 bypasses the size gate entirely, but constants are already-materialized graph inputs and no independent confirmed impact is derivable from the fragment.

verdict.summary: ml_append()'s return status is discarded at line 37, and when vim_strsave() returns NULL (lines 34-35) the insert is skipped but the counter updates at lines 41-48 still advance line1/line2/cursor exactly as if one line had been inserted. On a failed or skipped insert the buffer does not grow, so the next iteration can reach ml_get(line1) (line 34) with a line1 that exceeds the line range admitted by the loop guard (line 30) and the buffer's line count, and appended_lines_mark(n, count) (line 51) still records count lines that were never inserted. This is an improper check for the exceptional (failed/skipped insertion) condition, CWE-754.

evidence.reason: The return status of ml_append() is discarded; on a FAIL (or when vim_strsave() returned NULL at line 34 and lines 36-39 skipped the append), no line is inserted, yet lines 41-48 unconditionally advance line1 by 1-2 and line2 by 0-1 and the cursor by 1, an invariant that holds only if each iteration inserts exactly one line. The loop guard at line 30 (while (line1 <= line2)) then admits the drifted counters, so a later ml_get(line1) at line 34 requests a line number beyond the non-grown buffer's line count (e.g., line1=1, line2=3, n=1 in a 3-line buffer with two skipped inserts yields ml_get(5)), and appended_lines_mark(n, count) at line 51 reports count lines inserted that were not. Primary mechanism: improper check of the exceptional condition (CWE-754); the physical out-of-bounds extent is range-based because the buffer line count is not declared in the fragment.

assumptions: linenr_T is a signed integer line-number type (per its name); line1, line2 and n are not constrained anywhere in the fragment, so each retains its full declared domain (no line1<=line2 check, no buffer-bounds check).
ml_get(line1) (line 34) and ml_append(cursor, ...) (line 37) treat their first argument as a 1-based line number; the buffer's line count is not visible in the fragment.
FAIL (line 26) and the NULL result of vim_strsave (line 35) are the fragment's failure signals; ml_append returns a status that the fragment does not capture.

The loop is correct only under the invariant that every iteration inserts exactly one line (the bookkeeping at lines 41-48 depends on it); that invariant is neither verified nor restored after a failed/skipped insert.
Termination is guaranteed for all inputs: line1 gains at least 1 per iteration (lines 43, 45) while line2 gains at most 1 (lines 46-47), so line1-line2 strictly increases; no non-termination finding.
limitations: The out-of-bounds read extent at ml_get(line1) (line 34) cannot be byte-grounded: the buffer line count and the width of linenr_T are not declared in the fragment, so CWE-125 is not independently confirmed.

count = line2 - line1 + 1 (line 6) is computed without a line1<=line2 guard, so count<=0 is in its residual range and reaches b_op_end.lnum (line 10), appended_lines_mark (line 51) and msgmore (line 55); no security-relevant sink consumes count, so no CWE is assigned.
Integer overflow of line2-line1+1, n+1 and n+count (lines 6, 9, 10, 26) cannot be demonstrated without linenr_T's range and would only affect mark/undo bookkeeping shown here.
A NULL returned by ml_get(line1) would be passed to vim_strsave (line 34) without a check, but the fragment shows no producer of a NULL ml_get result, so a CWE-476 claim is unconfirmable.

The confirmed verdict relies on the exceptional path (vim_strsave returning NULL or ml_append failing), which is permitted for this error-handling finding because operations (ml_get at line 34, appended_lines_mark at line 51) run on the failure state; the illustrative witness uses two consecutive skipped inserts in a 3-line buffer.
The (long) cast at line 55 and (colnr_T)0 at line 37 are the only representation changes; neither is shown to alter a value.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable from the fragment alone. The loop-bound field bin->ne_header->SegCount and the index into bin->segment_entries[i] (line 12) cannot be checked against any visible capacity because the segment_entries array is never declared or allocated in the shown code, so the OOB-read candidate is ungrounded. The integer-overflow candidate in bs->paddr = (ut64)se->offset * bin->alignment (line 18) and the resource-exhaustion candidate from the loop count (line 7) depend on types and ranges not shown. bin->ne_header and bin->segment_entries are framework/binary-parser-provided members with no nullable contract shown in the fragment, so they are treated as non-NULL per the framework-pointer rule.

Error-handling quirks — returning a partial list on R_NEW0 failure (lines 9-11) and unchecked r_str_newf (line 19) — have no security-relevant downstream operation on the failure state within the shown code, so they are not findings.
