verdict.summary: The brush loader computes width*height*bytes in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic (L122, L165) while the only product guard (L51) validates the product in 64-bit via G_MAXSIZE division. A crafted .gbr header (e.g., width=height=32768) passes every shown check while making the 32-bit product wrap to 0; the pattern-conversion path then writes up to ~4 GiB through brush_buf[i*4+3]=plain_brush[i] (L177) into a 0-byte g_malloc (L165), a heap buffer overflow (CWE-787) rooted in the integer wrap (CWE-190).

evidence.reason: Heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The loop bound at L167 is the 32-bit unsigned product P = ph.width*ph.height (ph.width==bh.width, ph.height==bh.height enforced at L156-157), while the allocation at L165 `g_malloc(4 * bh.width * bh.height)` is also evaluated in 32-bit unsigned and wraps to 4*(P mod 2^30) for P in [2^30, 2^32). With width=height=32768 (P=2^30) the capacity from L165 is 0 bytes, yet the index i*4+3 reaches 2^32-1, writing ~2^32 bytes out of bounds (the L169 read over brush_buf+i*4 overflows identically). The guards at L47-51 protect only the 64-bit product (G_MAXSIZE division) and leave the 32-bit multiplication at L122/L165 unwrapped; guards L85-86, L95-100, and L152-159 are all satisfiable from file bytes. Root cause is the 32-bit integer wrap (CWE-190).

Integer overflow root (CWE-190). bh.width, bh.height, bh.bytes are 32-bit unsigned (residual [1, GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE] x [1, GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE] x {1,2,4,18} per L47-50), so the product is computed in 32-bit unsigned before widening into gsize. The only product guard, L51 `G_MAXSIZE / bh.width / bh.height / bh.bytes < 1`, operates in the 64-bit domain and admits products up to 2^64-1, including values >= 2^32 whose 32-bit result wraps (e.g., 4*32768*32768 = 2^32 -> 0). The wrapped value sizes g_malloc at L123 and is relied on as the buffer extent at L262, corrupting the allocation size and driving the OOB write/read.

assumptions: BrushHeader and PatternHeader fields are 32-bit unsigned (guint32), inferred from g_ntohl usage at L38-44 and L145-150 and the unsigned long casts at L56-57; the typedefs are not shown in the fragment.

GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE is a compile-time constant whose numeric value is not shown; the concrete witnesses assume it is at least 32768, and the verdict therefore rests on residual-range analysis rather than a fully demonstrable single value.
sizeof(BrushHeader) and sizeof(PatternHeader) are compile-time constants; L95/L154 apply them as lower bounds only.
GLib g_new/g_malloc abort rather than return NULL on allocation failure.
limitations: The exact numeric bound imposed by GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE (L47-48) is not visible, so membership of the concrete witness (width=height=32768) in the admitted set cannot be fully demonstrated; the overflow is confirmed at range level because no shown statement bounds the 32-bit product below 2^32.

The OOB read at L262 (gimp_pixel_rgn_set_rect consuming the undersized brush_buf) shares the same root overflow but its reachability additionally depends on unshown GIMP behavior (image/layer creation at L242/L251 succeeding); not reported as a separate CWE.
The case-2 loop (L190-206) exhibits the same overflow family at higher thresholds (width*height >= 2^31) plus signed-overflow UB on gint i; not separately confirmed due to the same unshown bound.

bn_size (L95-99) is upper-unbounded: header_size near 2^31 yields a ~2 GiB g_new and read from a 4-byte header field (resource exhaustion / allocator abort, CWE-400/CWE-617 candidate); demoted because the worst demonstrated effect is a transient failed allocation with no memory corruption.

gimp_image_new (L242), gimp_layer_new (L251), and gimp_drawable_get (L257) returns are unchecked; NULL/invalid-ID producers and their contracts are not visible in the fragment, so the potential NULL dereference at L259 through drawable->width is unconfirmable.
gimp_any_to_utf8 (L110) could return NULL on invalid UTF-8, feeding strlen at L247; the NULL producer is not visible in the shown code.
The discarded lseek return at L67 can cause wrong-offset reads for version-1 files, but this has no demonstrated memory-safety impact.

verdict.summary: get_recurse_data_length is an internal walker over compiler-generated bytecode. The fragment contains no entry-point input (argv/network/file/config); every bytecode length, offset, and private-data value consumed at L43/L48/L49/L74/L89/L106/L179/L186/L202/L214 is internal-helper or framework data with provenance unknown from the fragment, and no buffer capacity is declared. Candidate OOB reads near ccend, a reachable debug assert after stride overshoot (L236), and possible loop non-termination via a zero/negative OP_KET stride (L49+L51) all have admitted-set witnesses but fail impact confirmation (unshown allocation capacity, no demonstrated attacker direction, debug-only asserts), so they are recorded as limitations rather than findings.

assumptions: The walked region is [cc, ccend) with exclusive end, per the loop guard `while (cc < ccend)` (L21) and the post-loop `SLJIT_ASSERT(cc == ccend)` (L236); this is the only bound on cc shown in the fragment.

`memset(common->recurse_bitset, 0, common->recurse_bitset_size)` (L13) writes exactly recurse_bitset_size units, matching its own size field; recurse_bitset/recurse_bitset_size are framework state, and no other size derivation flows into this sink.
LINK_SIZE and IMM2_SIZE are compile-time macros referenced but not defined in the fragment; they are treated as positive opcode-stride constants by their use in the shown advances.
limitations: OOB read candidates at cc[1] (L202, L214), PRIVATE_DATA(cc)/PRIVATE_DATA(cc+1) (L43, L48, L49), GET2 (L74, L89), and *alternative with alternative = cc + GET(cc,1) (L106–L107) fire when cc is within a few code units of ccend; witnesses pass L21, but the backing buffer's capacity and whether ccend is the allocation end are not identifiable from the fragment, so the exact excess is unconfirmable (CWE-125 not confirmed).

Stride overshoot past ccend from `cc += 1 + 2 + cc[1]` (L202, L214), `cc += size` where size = GET(cc,1) (L179, L187), or `cc += PRIVATE_DATA(cc+1)` (L49) can trigger the reachable assert `SLJIT_ASSERT(cc == ccend)` (L236) in assert-enabled builds; the witnesses pass every shown guard, but attacker direction for the internally generated bytecode is not demonstrated in the fragment and the assert is debug-only (CWE-617 not confirmed).

Possible loop non-termination (CWE-835): for OP_KET the net advance is PRIVATE_DATA(cc+1) + 1 + LINK_SIZE (L49+L51), which is 0 for PRIVATE_DATA(cc+1) = -(1+LINK_SIZE) (a value the L48 `!= 0` assert admits) and negative below that; the default-path advance via next_opcode (L231) is unquantified. Termination is therefore not established for the fragment's admitted value set, but the stalling values come from internal bytecode with unknown provenance, so this is not a confirmed attacker-triggerable finding.
`common->optimized_cbracket[offset]` (L80) with offset = GET2(cc, 1+LINK_SIZE) (L74, range 0–65535) could index out of bounds only if the array is smaller than 65536; its capacity is not shown.

`int length` (L4) could overflow only after about 2^31 increments; the iteration-count bound and the downstream consumption of the returned length (as an allocation/stack size) are outside the fragment, so no impact is confirmable.

`offset = PRIVATE_DATA(cc)` (L43, L113, L123, L136, L149, L156, L166, L184) narrows sljit_sw to int; any truncation consequence depends on unshown type widths and on recurse_check_bit's unshown index semantics.

Output pointers needs_control_head/has_quit/has_accept (L248–L250) are dereferenced without NULL checks; a NULL value cannot be produced inside the fragment, so such a dereference would be caller-supplied and is out of scope.

No (a)-class entry-point input (argv, environment, socket/file content, MMIO, protocol message, user config) appears in the fragment; all bytecode- and common-derived values are internal-helper/framework data whose provenance the fragment does not establish.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds write in create_cache_bins: a file-supplied depArray ut16 is masked to 15 bits at line 80 and used as an index into deps (capacity cache->hdr->imagesCount, line 19) with no bound check, so deps[dep_index]++ at line 81 writes up to ~128 KiB past the allocation; the same loop also reads depArray past its depListCount-capacity when the 0xffff sentinel is absent or the start index is out of range (CWE-125). Reachable when R_DYLDCACHE_FILTER is set and cache->accel is present.

evidence.reason: CWE-787 primary: dep_index = depArray[k] & 0x7fff (line 80) has residual range [0,32767] for every depArray[k] admitted by the line-79 guard (all ut16 except 0xffff), but deps is sized by cache->hdr->imagesCount at line 19 (valid indices [0, imagesCount-1]). Witness: imagesCount=100, depArray[0]=0x0064 -> dep_index=100 -> deps[100]++ writes bytes [400,404) beyond the 400-byte allocation. No shown statement checks dep_index < cache->hdr->imagesCount; path guards at lines 13, 40, 42, 46, 51, 58, 61, 67, 77, 79 all admit the witness.

CWE-125 secondary (independent root cause): depArray is allocated with cache->accel->depListCount ut16 elements at line 41 (capacity 2*depListCount bytes), but the loop has no k < depListCount bound; k starts from the unconstrained file value extras[j].dependentsStartArrayIndex and the condition reads before testing the sentinel. Witness: depListCount=200, start=200 -> depArray[200] reads bytes [400,402) past the allocation; if no 0xffff entry exists, reads continue unbounded. The only guard (depArray[k] != 0xffff) cannot protect the first read and never bounds the index.

assumptions: r_buf_fread_at (line 46) returns the byte count, as the comparison against cache->accel->depListCount * 2 implies, so a full read fills depArray with depListCount file-supplied ut16 values.

cache header fields (imagesCount, depListCount) and extras[j].dependentsStartArrayIndex are plain counts read from the dyld-cache file; the fragment imposes no bounds on them (no shown minimum or equality statements).
deps (line 11) is non-NULL whenever target_libs is non-NULL, because an allocation failure at line 20 returns before line 58.
depArray is ut16[depListCount] (lines 3, 41) and deps is int[imagesCount] (lines 11, 19), per the declarations shown.
limitations: deps[j] access at lines 59/65/75/103 can be OOB for i>0 if hdr[i]->imagesCount exceeds cache->hdr->imagesCount (capacity line 19), since the fragment never ties the per-header count to the first header; same CWE-787 mechanism, omitted from cwe per the single-secondary rule.
&img[dep_index] at line 83: img's allocation is inside read_cache_images (not shown), so OOB-read capacity for img is not identifiable in the fragment; unconfirmable here.

Discarded r_buf_read_at return at line 112 can leave magicbytes uninitialized for r_read_le32 at line 113, but the only in-fragment consequence is the switch default at line 151; no security-relevant operation runs on the failure state.
eprintf sinks at lines 72 and 88 format file-derived strings into stderr diagnostics; no downstream consumption is shown, so log-injection impact is unestablished.
Unchecked strdup at lines 136/138/141/144 can store NULL into bin->file, but bin->file is never dereferenced in the fragment.

Line-79 loop termination depends entirely on a file-supplied 0xffff sentinel; absent one, k advances past depListCount (OOB reads, CWE-125 above) and can wrap as a ut32, but non-termination is subsumed by the OOB-read finding.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable within the shown fragment. The only security-relevant sink pattern is the array subscript TabPageIdxs[mouse_col] (lines 264, 279, 322), indexed by the unconstrained global mouse_col: the click path bounds it only by mouse_col < Columns (line 276) and the drag paths bound it not at all, but the fragment never declares TabPageIdxs's capacity or any relationship between Columns and that capacity, so no out-of-bounds excess can be computed and no CWE-125 finding is confirmable. All other candidates (position loop termination, column arithmetic, unvalidated register name, discarded vungetc status) depend on unshown callee/framework contracts and are recorded as limitations.

assumptions: TabPageIdxs is a pointer to an integer array; it is NULL-checked at line 255, but its element capacity is not declared or derivable anywhere in the fragment.
mouse_row and mouse_col are int globals set by the mouse-input layer outside the fragment; the shown code imposes no range constraint on mouse_col (only comparisons at lines 258, 276, 542, 549).
Columns is an int global compared at line 276; the fragment states no relationship between Columns and the size of the array pointed to by TabPageIdxs.
oap may be NULL (comment, line 2); every dereference in the fragment is NULL-guarded (lines 175, 187, 472, 483, 509, 771, 773).
regname (line 176) has internal-helper provenance via oap->regname; no attacker-controlled path that sets it is visible in the fragment.
limitations: Out-of-bounds read from TabPageIdxs[mouse_col] at lines 264 and 322 (unguarded) and 279 (guarded only by mouse_col < Columns at line 276, which admits all negative int values): unconfirmable because the fragment declares no capacity for TabPageIdxs and no Columns-to-capacity relation, so no excess can be computed (capacity-grounding rule).
No lower-bound check on mouse_col exists at line 276; a negative value passes the guard, but the OOB consequence cannot be stated without the array capacity.

Termination of the for(;;) loop at lines 58–85 relies on the typeahead queue being finite and vpeekc()/safe_vgetc() semantics (lines 68, 76) not shown in the fragment; greedy continuation only when c == nc and each iteration consumes one queued character.
The whitespace-skipping loop at lines 769–770 (gchar_pos/inc) has termination and bounds that depend on unshown callee contracts; VIM_ISWHITE(NUL) semantics are not visible in the fragment.
Integer arithmetic at lines 566, 595–596, 605–606, 614–615, and the column increment at 805–806 cannot be shown to wrap (operand magnitudes unbounded in the fragment; downstream consumers not shown).

regname passed to do_put/prep_redo/AppendCharToRedobuff (lines 236–242, 652–658) is unvalidated in the fragment, but its provenance is an internal helper parameter and no callee contract or attacker path is shown.
The return value of vungetc(nc) (line 79) is discarded; on failure a single typeahead character is lost with no security-relevant operation on the failure state demonstrated.

verdict.summary: No confirmed security vulnerability in the fragment. Every status-returning call is checked before its result is used, the only printf-family sink (snprintf at L146-147) is bounded by the sizeof capacity argument with a fixed format string, the only array access (pcim_iomap_table(pdev)[0] at L95) uses constant index 0 after a checked region-reservation call and a NULL element check, and there are no input-derived sizes, memory copies, loops, or injection sinks.

assumptions: Framework/library pointers (pdev, cfg_trans, base_params, and the table returned by pcim_iomap_table at L95) are treated as non-NULL because no shown statement marks them nullable and no shown producer of NULL exists.

The snprintf size argument at L146 (sizeof(trans->hw_id_str)) is the destination's compile-time capacity, so the write is bounded to at most size-1 characters plus NUL for every admitted input; the format's output is a constant 23 bytes including NUL for any u16 argument values.
A successful pcim_iomap_regions_request_all(pdev, BIT(0), ...) at L89, whose return is checked at L90, establishes the managed-IO table before pcim_iomap_table(pdev) at L95 is called.
trans->hw_rev is read from MMIO and validated against 0xffffffff at L110 before any bit manipulation at L123-124.
limitations: Potential NULL dereference of pcim_iomap_table(pdev) at L95 is unconfirmable from the fragment: no shown statement produces a NULL table pointer, the checked pcim_iomap_regions_request_all call at L89-93 precedes it, and framework pointers are treated as non-NULL absent a visible nullable contract.

trans_pcie->msix_enabled (read at L154) has no initializer visible in this fragment; its writer (iwl_pcie_set_interrupt_capa, called at L144) is not shown, and neither branch leads to a security-relevant sink, so an uninitialized-read finding cannot be confirmed.

cfg_trans->base_params->pcie_l1_allowed (L47) dereferences base_params without a visible NULL check; cfg_trans is a framework-provided pointer with no shown nullable contract, so its NULL-ability is out of scope.

The hw_rev bit manipulation at L123-124 could in principle wrap, but the value's type is not visible in the fragment and its only downstream use is the debug print at L142, so no CWE-190 finding is confirmable.

Behavior of not-shown callees (iwl_trans_alloc zeroing, iwl_pcie_set_interrupt_capa, pcim_iomap_regions_request_all internals) is assumed standard per their names and the shown ret checks; any deviation is outside the fragment's scope.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable within the fragment. Every dereference that can be reached is NULL/ERR-guarded by the shown code: pols[0] at lines 7/12 before the deref at line 15, and pols[1] at lines 25-26 before the deref at line 31. The unconditional write pols[1] = ... at line 20 and the pols[i]->action reads in the loop at lines 35-36 are unsafe only if the caller's pols array has fewer than m elements, but the array's capacity is never declared, sized, or derived anywhere in the fragment, so any out-of-bounds claim fails the required capacity grounding and is recorded as a limitation, not a finding.

assumptions: Line 7 excludes *num_pols == 0 and pols[0] == NULL, and line 12 excludes IS_ERR(pols[0]), so the deref of pols[0] at line 15 is guarded by shown statements.
Lines 25 and 26 exclude NULL and ERR_PTR values of pols[1] before the deref at line 31; the fragment checks exactly the valid/NULL/ERR outcome set of xfrm_policy_lookup_bytype.

xfrm_nr fields (lines 15 and 31) are non-negative small integers per kernel convention, so the int accumulators at lines 15 and 31 do not overflow on any realistic path; the fragment itself does not declare these field types.
limitations: Line 20 writes pols[1] with no shown statement establishing that the caller's array has capacity >= 2; only `struct xfrm_policy **pols` (line 2) is visible, so a CWE-787 claim cannot satisfy the capacity-grounding requirement and is demoted (the same absence also prevents a safe verdict).

The loop at lines 35-36 reads pols[i] for i in [0, *num_pols); *num_pols is unconstrained above zero (any int != 0 is admitted past line 7) and the capacity/contents of pols at i >= 1 are not established by the fragment, so OOB read (CWE-125) or NULL deref (CWE-476) via pols[i] are unconfirmable.

Line 30 (*num_pols)++ wraps to INT_MIN only for an entry value of INT_MAX (which line 7 admits); the wrapped value reaches only the loop bound at line 35 and the out-parameter, with no security-relevant consumption visible in the fragment, so it is not a confirmed CWE-190.

On the lookup-error path, line 27 passes the entry *num_pols to xfrm_pols_put; if the entry count were >= 2, the ERR pointer stored at index 1 (line 20) would be included in the put count, but that requires an entry contract and callee semantics not shown in the fragment.

NULL-valued pols, num_pols, or num_xfrms parameters would fault at line 7, but such NULLs are only producible by an out-of-scope caller; the fragment contains no producer of NULL for these parameters.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable from the fragment. The main-copy loop (lines 45-73) is provably in-bounds against the line-32 capacity, but the dangerous STRCPY appends at lines 150, 157-158, and 164 can only overflow if dp->d_name's length exceeds the unshown BASENAMELEN constant, so no witness can be constructed from the shown arithmetic; all memory-safety hypotheses are recorded as limitations.

assumptions: Line 32 `buf = alloc(STRLEN(path) + BASENAMELEN + 5);` is the only declared capacity for `buf` in the fragment; `STRLEN(path)` is a byte count and `BASENAMELEN` is an unshown macro whose value is not used in any confirmed computation.

The copy loop at line 45 terminates at the NUL of `path` and writes exactly `STRLEN(path)` bytes plus the terminator at line 73, so `p` ends at `buf + STRLEN(path)`, which is strictly inside the line-32 capacity.
`mb_ptr2len` (line 64) returns at least 1 and never advances past the string's NUL because of the line-45 guard, so the copy loop always progresses and terminates.
Recursion depth is bounded by the shown `stardepth < 100` guards (lines 120 and 153) and, for the line-169 recursion, by consumption of one wildcard component per level.
The fragment's own recursive call sites (lines 125, 160, 169) pass non-negative `wildoff` values; the top-level caller's `wildoff` is not shown.
`gap->ga_data` is treated as a valid array of `ga_len` pointers when `qsort` runs at line 208, per the Vim `garray_T` invariant (not restated in the fragment).
limitations: Heap-buffer-overflow candidates at `STRCPY(s, dp->d_name)` (line 150), `STRCPY(buf + len, "/**")` (line 157), `STRCPY(buf + len + 3, path_end)` (line 158), and `STRCPY(buf + len, path_end)` (line 164): the required witness is a directory entry longer than `BASENAMELEN + 5` (plus small slack), but neither the `BASENAMELEN` value nor the `dirent`/`NAME_MAX` bound on `dp->d_name` appears in the fragment, so the capacity is not resolvable and the excess cannot be demonstrated by the shown arithmetic.

A negative top-level `wildoff` would make `path + wildoff` (lines 49, 57) undefined behavior, but the fragment's shown recursion sites always pass non-negative values; a negative caller value is out of scope.

`vim_regfree(regmatch.regprog)` (line 204) may receive NULL when `EW_NOTWILD` is set and `vim_regcomp` failed (line 112 falls through); NULL-tolerance is in the unshown callee and cannot be confirmed from the fragment.
Check-then-use race (CWE-367) between `mch_lstat`/`mch_getperm` (lines 180-181) and `addfile` (line 194): the interleaving and the concrete security impact are not demonstrable inside the fragment.

`fnamencmp(path + (s - buf), dp->d_name, e - s)` (line 148) may use a misaligned window after backslash removal at lines 78-84, which could admit a non-matching entry, but reads remain in-bounds and no security decision boundary is shown to be affected.
`len = STRLEN(buf)` (line 151) narrows `size_t` to `int`; an overflow would require a `buf` larger than INT_MAX, which is not derivable from the fragment.

Discarded return values of the recursive calls (lines 125, 160, 169) were examined as a status-handling flaw but are not one: results accumulate in the shared `gap` and the caller recomputes `matches` from `gap->ga_len` at line 206.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the line-copy helper in which the only input-derived indices are ml_get(line1) (line 33) and ml_append(cursor, ...) (line 36), and the only arithmetic is count = line2 - line1 + 1 (line 6) plus n + 1 / n + count (lines 9, 10, 25). No vulnerability is confirmable from the shown code: the loop provably terminates because line1 strictly increases every iteration (unconditional ++line1 at line 42, with the line1 == n branch at lines 40-41 pushing line1 past cursor), vim_strsave's NULL return is checked (line 34), u_save failure is handled (lines 25-26), and p is freed exactly once. Claims of OOB access or integer overflow cannot be grounded because the buffer's line capacity, ml_get/ml_append bounds contracts, and linenr_T width are not present in the fragment, so they are recorded as limitations rather than findings.

assumptions: linenr_T is a signed integer line-number type; its exact width is not declared in the fragment and no arithmetic overflow is derivable from it.

u_save, ml_get, ml_append, vim_strsave, and appended_lines_mark are standard buffer/undo/allocator routines whose parameter contracts (valid line-number range, FAIL semantics) lie outside the fragment.
FAIL, CMOD_LOCKMARKS, cmdmod, curbuf, and curwin are framework constants/objects not defined in the fragment; none supplies a trust invariant used for the verdict.

Loop termination is established by the shown bookkeeping itself: line1 strictly increases (line 42 unconditional; lines 40-41 set line1 = cursor, which is >= line1_old), line2 increases by at most 1 per iteration (lines 45-46), and the constant-gap phase is broken when line1 reaches n (line 40), after which line1 - line2 strictly grows until line 29's check fails.
limitations: OOB read at ml_get(line1) (line 33) and invalid-index insert at ml_append(curwin->w_cursor.lnum, ...) (line 36) are unconfirmable: the buffer's line-count capacity and the APIs' bounds contracts are not visible in the fragment, and no fragment arithmetic establishes them; line1 and n retain the full linenr_T domain because no shown check constrains them.

Integer overflow/underflow in count = line2 - line1 + 1 (line 6) and n + 1 / n + count (lines 9, 10, 25) cannot be demonstrated since linenr_T's width is unshown and the fragment imposes no bound on the parameters; downstream uses (marks, appended_lines_mark, msgmore) are not memory sinks in the fragment.

The ml_append return value (line 36) is discarded; on insert failure the line-shift bookkeeping (lines 40-46) desyncs from the buffer and a subsequent ml_get(line1) (line 33) reads a line of unknown validity, but the consequence cannot be bounded from the shown code.
If vim_strsave returns NULL (lines 33-34), the append is skipped while cursor/line1/line2 bookkeeping still advances, producing the same unconfirmable desync.

count <= 0 (when line2 < line1, e.g., line1=3, line2=1) reaches appended_lines_mark(n, count) (line 50) and msgmore((long)count) (line 52); the callees' handling of non-positive counts is not contractually shown.
An unconstrained n outside the buffer's line range is not rejected anywhere in the fragment, so destination-index behavior beyond the shown arithmetic is out of scope.

verdict.summary: Heap overflow in dnsc_load_local_data: the size_t length sum (strlen(provider_name) + 15 + 4*sizeof(struct SignedCert) + 2) is narrowed into uint16_t rrlen (lines 40-44, declaration line 19). When the provider name length makes the sum an exact multiple of 65536, rrlen truncates to 0, malloc(0) (line 45) allocates a 0-byte buffer, and the size argument at the snprintf sinks (lines 50/54/56/65) becomes rrlen-1 == -1, converted to SIZE_MAX as size_t, writing an unbounded (~64 KB) record past the heap chunk. Trigger requires an unconstrained provider-name length (no shown bound) and malloc(0) returning non-NULL (standard glibc behavior).

evidence.reason: Primary overflow sink. rrlen is uint16_t (line 19); for provider_name length L = 65536 - ((4*sizeof(struct SignedCert) + 34) mod 65536), the size_t sum (lines 40-44) is an exact multiple of 65536, so storing it into uint16_t rrlen truncates it to 0. malloc(rrlen) (line 45) then allocates 0 bytes (capacity 0; malloc(0) non-NULL is standard glibc behavior, admitted by the if(!rr) guard at line 46). rrlen - 1 promotes to int -1 and converts to the size_t snprintf parameter as SIZE_MAX, so this write emits strlen(provider_name)+15+1 bytes (up to ~65536) past the heap chunk: heap buffer overflow by unbounded copy (CWE-122), root-caused by the unsigned size_t-to-uint16_t narrowing (CWE-681).

Corrupted allocation-size sink of the same finding: the argument rrlen is the modulo-2^16-truncated length sum from lines 40-44. For any provider_name length L with sum ≡ 0 (mod 65536), rrlen == 0 and malloc(0) is the buffer the subsequent snprintf sinks (lines 50/54/56/65) overflow, because their size arguments derive from the same truncated rrlen (rrlen - 1 == -1 -> SIZE_MAX). Allocation size and writer size are both driven by unconstrained input length; CWE-122 primary with CWE-681 (narrowing conversion) secondary.

Additional overflow sink of the same root cause: with rrlen truncated to 0, the size_t expression rrlen - 1 - strlen(rr) evaluates to SIZE_MAX - strlen(rr) (int -1 promoted, then converted to size_t before the subtraction), so this trailing write also runs unbounded past the 0-byte heap chunk allocated at line 45, after the first overflow at line 50 already corrupted the heap (CWE-122; root cause CWE-681).

assumptions: dnscenv->provider_name length is unconstrained: the fragment contains no check, cap, or minimum between the function entry and its strlen/snprintf uses at lines 40 and 50.

sizeof(struct SignedCert) is a compile-time constant >= 1 (C object-size rule), so the congruence class L = 65536 - ((4*sizeof(struct SignedCert) + 34) mod 65536) is always a valid provider-name length in [1, 65535].

Standard C integer arithmetic is assumed: size_t is 64-bit, int is 32-bit, uint16_t promotes to int, and assigning an unsigned value to uint16_t is modulo 2^16 (C17 6.3.1.3p2); a size_t function parameter receives the int value -1 as SIZE_MAX.
malloc(0) returning a unique non-NULL pointer (as in glibc) is assumed to reach the write path; the if(!rr) guard (line 46) admits that outcome.
limitations: Out-of-bounds access to signed_certs[i] (line 21) and rotated_certs[j] (line 24) is unconfirmable because neither array's capacity/declaration appears in the fragment.
The 4-byte memcpy from cert->serial (line 29) cannot be assessed: struct SignedCert layout is not shown.

unchecked strdup results at lines 6, 7, and 66 could pass NULL into cfg_str2list_insert/cfg_strlist_insert on OOM, but callee NULL semantics are outside the fragment and no security-relevant operation on the failure state is shown.

If malloc(0) returns NULL, the function returns -2 at line 48 before the overflow; the finding depends on the allocator returning a usable pointer (brittle-boundary dependency reflected in confidence 0.6).

Discarded snprintf return values at lines 50/54/56/65 cause only truncation (no memory unsafety) when rrlen >= 1, potentially emitting a malformed local-data record; treated as robustness, not a finding.
Log writes containing provider_name/rr (lines 8-9, 59-64) perform no filtering (log-injection shape) but the data is configuration-sourced with no shown attacker control; unconfirmed.
The per-byte loop (lines 51-58) may read uninitialized struct padding into rr; initialization state of SignedCert is not shown, so unconfirmed.

For rrlen >= 1 the worst-case sizing (4*sizeof(struct SignedCert) per byte, comment line 42) makes the series of snprintf writes exactly fit or truncate by at most one byte; no overflow occurs on that path.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable within the shown fragment. The dangerous-looking operations — the indirect read at line 89 (`*alternative` from `cc + GET(cc, 1)`), bytecode-derived advances at lines 46/99/108/117/143/149/164/176, the array subscript at line 73, and the debug-only asserts at lines 26/45/64/156/180/195/199 — all depend on buffer capacities, callee contracts, or bytecode well-formedness invariants that are not established anywhere in the shown code. Every boundary claim therefore fails the capacity/provenance grounding required for confirmation and is recorded as a limitation rather than a finding.

assumptions: Line 20 (`while (cc < ccend)`) bounds the entry-byte read `switch(*cc)` at line 23 to positions strictly below `ccend`; for every listed `case` the minimum advance is >= 1 (e.g., OP_SET_SOM += 1 at line 28, OP_KET += 1+LINK_SIZE at line 48, iterators += 1 or 2 at lines 97/124/130, MARK-family += 1+2+cc[1] >= 3 at line 164, PRUNE-family += 1 at line 171).
PCRE2_SPTR is a pointer type; all advances in the fragment are shown in code-unit units with plain int offsets, with no narrowing cast visible.
limitations: OOB read at line 89 (`*alternative`, offset `GET(cc, 1)` from line 88): offset is bytecode-derived with no shown range check, but the bytecode buffer's capacity is not declared or allocated in the fragment, so no boundary witness can be grounded (CWE-125 candidate).
OOB read of `cc[1]` at lines 164 and 176 when only one byte remains before `ccend`: same missing-capacity grounding; also requires a malformed trailing opcode.
Array subscript at line 73 (`common->optimized_cbracket[GET2(cc, 1 + LINK_SIZE)]`): bytecode-derived index with no shown bound, but the array size is not visible in the fragment.

Advance overshoots at lines 46 (`PRIVATE_DATA(cc + 1)`), 99/108/117 (`GET_EXTRALEN(cc[-1])`), 143/149 (`size = GET(cc, 1)` for OP_XCLASS), and 164/176 (`1 + 2 + cc[1]`): no shown bound vs `ccend`; exploitability depends on bytecode/metadata consistency established outside the fragment.

CWE-835 non-termination: for OP_XCLASS, `size = GET(cc, 1)` at line 143 has no shown minimum, so size 0 would stall the loop at line 149; the `default:` advance via `next_opcode` (line 194) has no shown progress contract.

CWE-476/CWE-617: if `next_opcode` returns NULL (line 194), only debug-only `SLJIT_ASSERT(cc != NULL)` (line 195) reacts; in release builds NULL would reach the dereference at line 23. The callee contract and attacker control of the opcode byte are not shown.

Debug-only asserts at lines 26/45/64/156/180/199 would abort only on bytecode/flag inconsistencies the fragment neither produces nor checks; the invariants they protect are established outside the shown code.

`int length` overflow (declared line 4): max +4 per iteration with >= 1-byte progress means overflow needs a ~2^29-byte region; no bound on `(ccend - cc)` is shown and the fragment contains no security-relevant consumer of `length` beyond the return at line 216.
NULL dereference at output writes (lines 213-215) would require a caller-supplied NULL pointer; no NULL-producing path exists in the fragment.

verdict.summary: Log injection (CWE-117): raw client-controlled bytes of NBD_OPT_LIST_META_CONTEXT / NBD_OPT_SET_META_CONTEXT query strings, including newlines and control characters, are passed unescaped to debug() at lines 464-467. An attacker who enables structured replies can forge log entries, poison log-based monitoring, or cover their tracks; the only validation on the path is the length check in check_string (lines 460-462).

evidence.snippet:
debug ("newstyle negotiation: %s: %s %.*s",
                   optname,
                   option == NBD_OPT_LIST_META_CONTEXT ? "query" : "set",
                   (int) querylen, &data[opt_index]);
evidence.reason: Sink lines 464-467: client-supplied meta-context query bytes, read from the network into data at line 370 (capacity optlen+1 per line 38), reach the log sink with %.*s precision equal to attacker-controlled querylen and no escaping or filtering at any point from line 370 to the sink (the only guard, check_string at lines 460-462, is length/capacity validation per its call-site arguments; line 492 confirms arbitrary queries are admitted and only ignored). Concrete witness passing every visible guard: structured-replies enabled via NBD_OPT_STRUCTURED_REPLY (lines 355-358), then NBD_OPT_SET_META_CONTEXT with optlen=17, exportnamelen=0, nr_queries=1, querylen=5, query="a\nb\nc"; guards at 34, 50, 60, 376, 389, 403, 454, 460 all admit these values (17<=MAX_REQUEST_SIZE boundary as shown at line 34, tls!=2 for line 60, opt_index=12 <= optlen=17 for line 454, querylen=5 <= optlen-opt_index=5 for line 460), and the sink writes the 5 raw bytes including the newline into the debug log. Primary mechanism is log injection (CWE-117): attacker-controlled control characters survive to a log write, enabling log forgery and monitoring evasion.

assumptions: data buffer capacity is optlen+1 bytes from `data = malloc (optlen + 1)` at line 38, and payload recv calls (69, 106, 134, 179, 335, 370, 508) transfer exactly optlen bytes.
Guards at lines 182 (optlen>=6), 389 (optlen>=8), 424 and 454 (opt_index+4<=optlen) establish minima that prevent unsigned underflow in optlen-6, optlen-8, and optlen-opt_index.
check_export_name (72/223/403) and check_string (460) are validation helpers whose length/capacity parameters are consumed as such (name-implied semantics); their bodies are not in the fragment.
debug() is the process log sink (name-implied), and conn_recv_full returns -1 on failure (as used throughout the fragment).
name_of_nbd_opt / name_of_nbd_info return non-NULL strings (no NULL producer shown).
limitations: `data = malloc (optlen + 1)` (line 38) can wrap to 0 only when optlen == UINT32_MAX and is admitted past the line 34 guard `optlen > MAX_REQUEST_SIZE`; since MAX_REQUEST_SIZE is not defined in the fragment, admission of UINT32_MAX (and hence a heap overflow via a subsequent conn_recv_full) cannot be demonstrated, nor can safety be proven — no CWE assigned.

`(int) querylen` at line 467 becomes negative (printf precision omitted => read until NUL) only when querylen > INT_MAX, which requires optlen > INT_MAX and therefore MAX_REQUEST_SIZE > INT_MAX — invisible-constant dependent; unconfirmed.

The +1 trailing byte allocated at line 38 is never NUL-terminated anywhere in the fragment; any callee relying on it (check_export_name, finish_newstyle_options) is not visible, and all shown call sites pass explicit lengths — no confirmed over-read.

`send_newstyle_option_reply_exportnames (option, &nr_options)` (line 123) takes the outer-loop counter by address; its effect on nr_options is unshown, so the option-budget interplay is unconfirmable.
The log-injection severity is low; if debug output is not treated as a security boundary in the target deployment, this reduces to a hardening concern.

verdict.summary: singlevar resolves a global by re-running singlevaraux for ls->envn and asserts var->k != VVOID; the fragment never establishes that the environment name binds in the current scope chain, so a crafted chunk whose scope lookup for the env name yields VVOID reaches lua_assert at line 8 and aborts the process (reachable-assertion DoS).

evidence.snippet: lua_assert(var->k != VVOID);  /* this one must exist */
evidence.reason: The assert is the sink: after the branch at line 5 admits var->k == VVOID (VVOID is a demonstrated output of the line-4 singlevaraux call for any undeclared name), line 7 re-runs the identical lookup keyed on ls->envn, whose value and resolvability the fragment never constrains (no initializer, no check, no minimum guarantee; the line-8 comment is not a program statement). If that lookup yields VVOID (a member of the call's residual outcome set, identical to the line-4 call form), the assert evaluates false and aborts. Primary mechanism: reachable assertion (CWE-617); impact is a crash/denial of service.

assumptions: Line numbering: the fragment is counted starting at 'static void singlevar (LexState *ls, expdesc *var) {' = line 1.
Line 5's branch demonstrates that the singlevaraux call form at line 4 can set var->k to VVOID for admitted input (any reference to an undeclared name in the compiled chunk).
lua_assert carries standard assert semantics (abort on false) as its name states.
limitations: The concrete failure requires that ls->envn not resolve in the active scope chain; the scope-chain construction and singlevaraux body are not shown, so the witness is a residual-range witness, not a fully simulated single value — this caps confidence at 0.65.
The discarded return values of both singlevaraux calls (lines 4 and 7) cannot be confirmed to diverge from var->k because the callee's contract is not shown (CWE-703/754 class not confirmed).
varname is not NULL-checked before codestring at line 9, but no shown statement can produce NULL, so a NULL dereference is unconfirmed.
If Lua is built with assertions disabled, the abort does not fire; the standard Lua build enables assertions, but the build configuration is outside the fragment.
No memory-safety, injection, crypto, or file-access sinks exist in this fragment; no size/capacity arithmetic is present to audit.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable from the shown fragment. Every in-fragment read of the terminal-input region is bounded by shown guards (lines 127, 176/181, 223-224, 240-246, 290-292) plus the NUL sentinel written at tp[len] (line 85), and the small arrays key_name[2] are only written at indices 0-1. The one-byte-past write at tp[len] (index exactly *buflen / tb_off+tb_len) and the appends into string[MAX_KEY_CODE_LEN+1] depend on capacities (bufsize relation, tb_buflen, MAX_KEY_CODE_LEN, callee output bounds) that are not declared or constrained anywhere in the fragment, so they are recorded as limitations, not findings.

assumptions: Line 85 'tp[len] = NUL;' is itself in-bounds (i.e., buf / typebuf.tb_buf have capacity at least *buflen+1 / tb_off+tb_len+1); this is the precondition that makes the NUL a valid sentinel bounding all later reads.

termcodes[] and termleader[] are framework-owned internal tables (termleader is rebuilt by gather_termleader() at line 31); termcodes[idx].len corresponds to the code[] string length and termleader is NUL-terminated, though neither invariant is shown in the fragment.
typebuf.tb_buf/tb_off/tb_len obey Vim's internal buffer invariant with tb_off+tb_len within the allocation; not verifiable from this fragment.
limitations: Line 85 writes NUL at buf[*buflen] on the buf path (tp=buf+offset, len=*buflen-offset) and at typebuf.tb_buf[tb_off+tb_len] on the typebuf path: the index is exactly the length, one byte past the last used byte, but no allocation/capacity for buf or tb_buf is shown and bufsize is never compared with *buflen, so an off-by-one (would be CWE-787 if capacity == *buflen) is unconfirmable.

string[MAX_KEY_CODE_LEN + 1] (line 19): MAX_KEY_CODE_LEN is not defined in the fragment and the output bounds of modifiers2keycode() and mb_char2bytes() are not shown, so the writes at string[new_slen .. new_slen+2] cannot be proven in- or out-of-bounds.

GUI get_bytes_from_buf(tp+slen, …) and get_long_from_buf(tp+slen, …) read past tp+len by their fixed counts; their internal bound checks are not in the fragment, only the -1 return handling is visible.

The returned expression len + new_slen - slen + offset can wrap int for unconstrained *buflen/max_offset values, but no in-fragment consumer of the return value exists, so no security impact is confirmable.

modifiers_start is reset to NULL at line 119 and forwarded to check_termcode_mouse() when a match took the direct-match branch; a NULL dereference inside the unshown callee cannot be assessed from the fragment.

The termleader scan (lines 72-76) terminates only if termleader is NUL-terminated, an invariant not shown in the fragment; the data is framework-owned rather than attacker-derived, so it is not a finding.

The K_SPECIAL skip (lines 61-65, 'there are always 2 extra characters') is safe for the shown reads because every later iteration re-checks offset against tb_len/*buflen at lines 44/51 before dereferencing tp.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The dangerous STRCPY sinks (lines 150, 157-158, 164) write into buf allocated at line 32 with capacity STRLEN(path)+BASENAMELEN+5; byte-level accounting shows the largest single-level write totals at most STRLEN(path)+STRLEN(d_name)+1 bytes, so overflow would require STRLEN(d_name) > BASENAMELEN+4. Neither BASENAMELEN's value nor any bound on d_name length appears in the fragment, so the excess cannot be quantified and the finding is unconfirmable. All other sinks (copy loop, STRCPY at 123, backslash removal, p[1] probe) are provably in-bounds from shown arithmetic, recursion is capped by stardepth<100, and the readdir loop terminates on NULL.

assumptions: buf capacity is STRLEN(path) + BASENAMELEN + 5 bytes per line 32; BASENAMELEN is a positive named constant whose value is not shown.
path is NUL-terminated, as implicitly relied on by STRLEN(path) at line 32 and the while (*path_end != NUL) loop at line 45.
dp->d_name is a NUL-terminated string read from readdir (line 138); its maximum length is defined outside the fragment.
Recursion depth is bounded by the stardepth < 100 guards at lines 120 and 153 plus the incremented static stardepth at lines 124-126, 159-161.
limitations: Heap overflow candidate at STRCPY(s, dp->d_name) (line 150) and STRCPY(buf + len, ...) (lines 157-158, 164): the write totals STRLEN(path)+STRLEN(d_name)+1 against capacity STRLEN(path)+BASENAMELEN+5; overflow requires STRLEN(d_name) >= BASENAMELEN+5, and since neither BASENAMELEN nor the dirent d_name length bound is visible in the fragment, the excess cannot be quantified and no concrete witness is constructible. No CWE-787/CWE-122 verdict is supported.

Negative wildoff reaching buf + wildoff at line 78 and rem_backslash(p) at line 79 would be an out-of-bounds read, but no in-fragment producer of a negative value exists (recursive callers pass (int)(s - buf) at line 125 and len + 1 at lines 160/169); supply from an unshown caller is out of scope.

vim_regfree(regmatch.regprog) at line 204 can receive NULL only when EW_NOTWILD is set and vim_regcomp failed (line 112); whether vim_regfree(NULL) is safe is a callee contract not shown in the fragment.

"**" recursion into arbitrarily many/symlinked directories (lines 153-161, 165-169) can widen match sets, but depth is capped at 100 and CTRL-C is checked at entry (lines 24-28); resource exhaustion beyond the intended expansion feature is not demonstrated.
ReDoS via vim_regexec (line 145) with a path-derived pattern is not confirmable because the regex engine's behavior is not part of the fragment.
EW_NOTWILD with a failed vim_regcomp falls back to fnamencmp (lines 147-148); all reads there are in-bounds per the s-buf <= strlen(path) argument, so this is at most a correctness concern.

verdict.summary: Heap buffer overflow in GetEXIFProperty: with property="exif:*" (or "exif:!"), key is allocated as a copy of property (AcquireString at line 761, e.g. 7 bytes), then FormatLocaleString(key, MaxTextExtent, "%s", description) at lines 783-784 writes a full EXIFTag description (>= 8 bytes with NUL, e.g. "exif:Make") into it because the size argument MaxTextExtent ignores key's real capacity. A crafted EXIF profile with any one valid entry (e.g. tag 0x010F) plus any short property string whose 5th char is '*' yields a 3-byte heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

evidence.reason: key was created at line 761 by AcquireString(property); property's residual range after the only length constraint (strlen(property) > 5, lines 447-448) is >= 6 chars, so key's capacity is strlen(property)+1 (e.g. 7 bytes for "exif:*" admitted by all=1 at lines 458-459). description is taken from the visible EXIFTag[] table (lines 773-782) selected by attacker-controlled tag_value (line 615) and is at least 10 bytes with NUL (e.g. 0x010F -> "exif:Make", 10 bytes). FormatLocaleString's size argument MaxTextExtent exceeds the destination's actual capacity for the whole admitted property set, so the printf-family write at lines 783-784 writes strlen(description)+1 = 10 bytes into the 7-byte block: a 3-byte heap out-of-bounds write, confirmed by simulation where every guard on the path (441-442, 447-448, 530-531, 549-550, 553-554, 560, 566, 610-611, 617, 620, 623, 625-626, 652-653, 731, 753) admits the witness. Primary mechanism: CWE-787 (buffer overrun; write).

Same root cause with all=2 (property="exif:!", lines 464-465): for tag_value >= 0x20000 the sink writes the 8-byte string "unknown\0" into key whose capacity is again strlen(property)+1 = 7 bytes (AcquireString at line 761), overflowing by 1 byte, since no shown guard sizes key to the written string.

assumptions: AcquireString(property) follows its standard ImageMagick contract: it allocates exactly strlen(property)+1 bytes and copies the string (its body is not shown; the finding's capacity grounding and confidence rest on this).

MaxTextExtent is a fixed constant (4096 in ImageMagick) larger than every EXIFTag description, so FormatLocaleString writes are not truncated; only its role as the buffer capacity in 'char buffer[MaxTextExtent]' (line 649) is visible in the fragment.

ReadPropertyByte/Short/Long consume bytes and decrement the length argument (used at lines 535-545, 565, 595, 615-616, 621, 637, 825, 852); under this helper contract the marker-scan loop terminates and all length-derived bounds hold.
size_t is 64-bit (LP64) for the components*tag_bytes product at line 624; on this width no overflow occurs (components <= 2^31-1, factor <= 8, product <= 2^34).
limitations: On a hypothetical 32-bit size_t, components*tag_bytes[format] at line 624 can wrap for components >= ~2^29 and the overflow check at lines 625-626 is not a complete guard; the fragment does not establish the pointer width, so this is not reported as a finding.

The guard at lines 652-653 admits p == exif+length-tag_bytes[format], weaker than the actual bound needed, but the p derivations (q check at 610-611; dir_offset checks at 638-643) keep every value read in-bounds in the shown code; no OOB read is confirmed.
Misaligned dereferences *(float *)p1 / *(double *)p1 (lines 720, 725) are undefined behavior on some architectures but no concrete memory-safety failure is derivable from the fragment.

NewSplayTree (line 576) and AcquireQuantumMemory (663-664, 735-736) allocation failures are not followed by a security-relevant operation on the failure state (NULL value is skipped at line 753); only a robustness concern.
Exact line numbers were derived by counting the fragment as supplied; small offsets are possible if the original file differs in whitespace- or blank-line handling.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable from the shown fragment. The only security-relevant candidate is the array read `TabPageIdxs[mouse_col]` on the drag paths (lines 263 and 321) and the click path (line 278): the drag paths have no bound on `mouse_col` (the only guard, `mouse_col < Columns`, line 275, covers only the click path and admits negative values), but the capacity of `TabPageIdxs` is not declared anywhere in the fragment and the mouse-coordinate producer is outside the fragment, so the out-of-bounds claim cannot be quantified per the capacity-grounding rules and is demoted to a limitation. All `oap` dereferences are NULL-guarded (lines 176, 188, 470, 481, 507, 769, 771), and both loops terminate on shown progress: the `for(;;)` loop consumes one character per `continue` (line 76), and the whitespace loop depends only on the unshown `gchar_pos` end-of-line contract.

assumptions: The `for (;;)` loop at lines 58-85 consumes exactly one input character per `continue` (line 76 `nc = safe_vgetc();`), so iteration count is bounded by typeahead length; it has no fixed point.
`*ml_get_cursor() != NUL` at line 800 guards line 801; a non-NUL character's byte length cannot move `curwin->w_cursor.col` past the bytes of the current line.
`old_curwin` (line 24) and `save_cursor` (line 34) are matched: `save_cursor` is restored only when `curwin == old_curwin` (line 522).
Every dereference of the nullable `oap` is preceded by `oap != NULL` (lines 176, 188, 470, 481, 507, 769, 771).
limitations: Potential out-of-bounds read `c1 = TabPageIdxs[mouse_col];` at lines 263, 278, and 321: `mouse_col` is unconstrained by the shown code on the drag paths (line 275 guards only the click path and admits negative values), but the capacity of `TabPageIdxs` is never declared or derived in the fragment, and the producer of `mouse_col` is outside the fragment, so the excess over capacity cannot be computed. No CWE is attached per the grounding rules.

A negative `mouse_col` would pass the line-275 guard, but no shown statement establishes that the mouse layer can produce a negative column (only `mouse_row < 0` is exercised at line 547); at most a range claim.
`find_tabpage(-c1)` at line 307 would overflow if `c1 == INT_MIN`, but `TabPageIdxs` contents are not shown, so such a value cannot be demonstrated.
Termination of `while (gc = gchar_pos(&end_visual), VIM_ISWHITE(gc)) inc(&end_visual);` (lines 767-768) relies on the unshown `gchar_pos` contract of returning NUL at end of line.
`moved` (line 489) is assigned and never used; dead store without security impact.
The fragment declares no buffer or allocation, so no memory-safety finding can satisfy the capacity-grounding requirement.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable within the shown fragment. Entry-point strings (optarg into xasprintf 'LABEL="%s"'/'UUID="%s"', argv[0..1] into mnt_context_set_source/set_target, types into the fstype setters) are exactly sized, index-in-range, or handed to libmount consumers whose parsing and privilege enforcement lie outside the fragment. Demoted candidates: discarded set_source/set_target return values (CWE-754), free(srcbuf) ordering (CWE-416) pending an unshown copy contract, and LABEL/UUID quote injection whose sink is not shown.

assumptions: C runtime contract: argv[0..argc-1] are non-NULL NUL-terminated strings and argv[argc]==NULL; relied on for argv[0]/argv[1] reads at lines 279 and 287-288 under the exact guards at lines 267 and 280-281.

getopt_long (lines 86-87) terminates with -1 and returns a non-NULL NUL-terminated optarg only for options that require an argument; every optarg-consuming case (lines 137, 141, 148, 154, 163, 166, 206, 210) is such an option per the optstring at line 86 and longopts at lines 56-57.
usage(), exit_non_root(), and err() terminate the program, and xasprintf aborts on allocation failure (util-linux xalloc helpers); bodies are not shown.
mnt_new_context() is NULL-checked at lines 81-82 before any cxt use.
CHAR_MAX is 127 on the target ABI, so MOUNT_OPT_* enum values (lines 11-20) are 128-139, distinct from ASCII option characters.
limitations: CWE-754 unconfirmed: mnt_context_set_source (lines 150, 156, 210, 287) and mnt_context_set_target (lines 206, 278, 288) returns are discarded, unlike the checked calls at lines 118/129/134/138. A failure (libmount-internal allocation error) leaves the context without source/target; every trace resolves to the print_all/usage paths (lines 231-238, 241-242, 290-291) or to a mnt_context_mount call (line 304) with a partial operand set whose security effect depends on callee behavior not shown, and the triggering failure cannot be produced by the fragment's own data.

CWE-416 unconfirmable: free(srcbuf) at lines 151/157 immediately after mnt_context_set_source(cxt, srcbuf) at lines 150/156 is a use-after-free only if set_source aliases its argument; the copy contract is not visible in the fragment.

CWE-77/-78/-22-class unconfirmable: xasprintf at line 148 (and UUID at 154) embeds optarg unescaped, so optarg="a\"b" yields srcbuf="LABEL=\"a\"b\"" with the quote surviving to set_source; no downstream injection sink (mount-option parse, helper execution, fstab matching) is present in the shown code.

Restricted-mode integrity (CWE-862/287) rests on unshown bodies: exit_non_root (line 91), sanitize_paths (line 294), and libmount's own restricted checks; the fragment shows the gates but cannot prove or disprove a bypass.
mnt_context_get_cache() (line 224) / mnt_table_set_cache() (line 225): cache NULL-ness and aliasing semantics are not shown; no security-relevant state is derived from them in the fragment.

No boundary claims were possible for memory: the fragment contains no fixed-capacity buffer copied from input besides excl_st[ARRAY_SIZE(excl)] (line 71), indexed only inside the unshown err_exclusive_options.

verdict.summary: Heap buffer overflow in dnsc_load_local_data: the record length is summed in size_t and truncated to uint16_t rrlen (lines 45-49), and the guard at line 40 admits provider_name lengths up to 0xffff0000-1, so a length such as P=65439 (any P ≡ -(17+4*sizeof(struct SignedCert)) mod 65536) makes the sum exactly 65536 and rrlen wrap to 0. malloc(0) (line 50) yields a 0-byte buffer while the snprintf size argument at line 55 is rrlen-1 == (int)-1, converted to SIZE_MAX, so the provider name plus the 15-byte literal are written out of bounds; the same corrupted size feeds the escape-loop writes (lines 59/61) and the closing quote (line 70). Primary CWE-787; secondary CWE-190 for the uint16_t truncation of the security-relevant size.

evidence.reason: Sink: heap write whose size argument is out of domain. rrlen is declared uint16_t (line 19) and assigned the size_t sum strlen(provider_name)+15+4*sizeof(struct SignedCert)+2 (lines 45-49), truncating modulo 65536. The only guard, line 40, admits (unsigned)strlen(provider_name) < 0xffff0000, so P=65439 (with sizeof(struct SignedCert)=20; in general P ≡ -(17+4*sizeof(struct SignedCert)) mod 65536) is admitted and makes the sum 65536, i.e. rrlen==0. The capacity is malloc(rrlen) at line 50 = 0 bytes. rrlen-1 promotes uint16_t 0 to int -1, converted at this call to size_t SIZE_MAX, so snprintf writes strlen(provider_name)+15 = 65454 chars plus NUL beyond the 0-byte allocation: heap buffer overflow (CWE-787), root cause uint16_t truncation of a security-relevant size (CWE-190). The same corrupted size reaches the escape-loop snprintf calls (lines 59/61).

Second distinct sink consuming the same corrupted size. When provider_name length P satisfies M = P + 15 + 4*sizeof(struct SignedCert) + 2 ≡ 0 (mod 65536) — admitted by the line 40 guard, e.g. P=65439 for sizeof(struct SignedCert)=20 — rrlen (declared uint16_t at line 19, computed lines 45-49) is 0 and malloc(0) (line 50) yields a zero-byte buffer. The size argument rrlen-1-strlen(rr) evaluates to (size_t)(-1)-strlen(rr) = SIZE_MAX-strlen(rr), so this snprintf also writes out of bounds (CWE-787). assumptions: The fragment's `continue` at line 43 (missing semicolon) is treated as `continue;`, otherwise the fragment does not compile.

sizeof(struct SignedCert) = S is a positive compile-time constant whose numeric value is not shown; the witness is constructed for any S, and the walk uses S=20. For any S, P = (65536 - ((17 + 4*S) mod 65536)) mod 65536 ∈ [0, 65535] makes the sum exactly 65536.

Witness counts signed_certs_count = 1 and rotated_certs_count = 0 are used to enter the outer loop body and skip the rotation early-continue; the fragment establishes no minimum, so count = 1 (inside the declared domain) is required for reachability.
provider_name is a valid NUL-terminated string, as required by strlen/strdup at lines 6, 40, 45, 71.

limitations: The finding depends on both the exact wrap to rrlen==0 and malloc(0) returning non-NULL; confidence capped at 0.8.
memcpy(&serial, cert->serial, sizeof serial) at line 29 could read past the serial field, but the member's size is not visible in the fragment — unconfirmable.
Indexing dnscenv->signed_certs + i (line 21) and dnscenv->rotated_certs[j] (line 24) assumes array sizes ≥ the respective counts, which the fragment does not show — unconfirmable.
