In the non-wrap regime the closing quote can be dropped by line 70 (size becomes 1 at maximum content), truncating the RR; no memory impact in that regime and no config parser is shown, so no injection claim is made.
The line 40 guard also fails to exclude lengths ≥ 2^32 because (unsigned) truncates size_t modulo 2^32; noted as an additional admission of the same guard, not a separate finding.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the fragment. The two floating-point division sinks are protected by visible guards: line 15 forces numRecords >= 101 on the non-timeseries path (denominator >= 5.05 at line 63), and line 92 excludes numRecords == 0 before the timeseries division at line 125. rsRandCursor and plan_executor_factory::make statuses are checked before use. Residual robustness concerns (negative sampleSize reaching SampleFromTimeseriesBucket, unconstrained gTimeseriesBucketMaxCount producing NaN, precondition invariant) cannot be confirmed to a security impact within the shown code and are recorded as limitations.

assumptions: Line 15 gate: continuing past `if (sampleSize > numRecords * kMaxSampleRatioForRandCursor || numRecords <= 100)` implies numRecords >= 101, which makes the line 63 denominator numRecords * 0.05 >= 5.05.
Line 92 guard: continuing past `if (!(bucketUnpacker && numRecords))` implies numRecords != 0, protecting the line 125 denominator from the numRecords == 0 case.
CollectionShardingState::get (line 49), coll/expCtx/opCtx, and getOwnershipFilter are treated as non-NULL under their framework contracts; no shown statement marks them nullable.
All long long arithmetic is promoted to double before multiplication/division; no wrapping integer arithmetic or narrowing conversion exists in the fragment.
limitations: Negative sampleSize is admitted by the shown gates (e.g., sampleSize=-1, numRecords=1 with bucketUnpacker set passes lines 29 and 92) and is passed as the `sampleSize` constructor argument to SampleFromTimeseriesBucket (line 137); a negative count is out-of-domain for a sample-size parameter, but the callee body is not shown and no concrete failure mechanism (loop bound, unsigned conversion) can be demonstrated — unconfirmed, no CWE.

gTimeseriesBucketMaxCount is unconstrained in the fragment; if it were 0, the line 125 division would yield IEEE NaN/Inf and minAdvancedToWorkRatio would flow into TrialStage (line 128), but the zero value is not established by any shown statement and TrialStage's consumption of the ratio is unshown — range claim only, no CWE.

The `invariant` at line 11 aborts only on an unmet caller/framework precondition (lock state not held); the guard value is not attacker-directed through the shown checks, so it is not a confirmed CWE-617.

No buffer, copy, format-string, command, SQL, path, URL, crypto, or loop constructs exist in the fragment, so the not-vulnerable verdict for those classes rests on absence of a sink rather than a located protective check.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable from the fragment. All attacker-controlled data (optarg/argv) flows only into libmount context setters and a self-sizing xasprintf with constant format strings (lines 148, 154); every non-root use is gated by guards at lines 90-94, 262-265, 274-276, and 285-286, and there is no memory, injection, crypto, or status-handling sink whose argument can be shown out of domain. The unescaped LABEL/UUID quoting (lines 148/154) is a potential parsing ambiguity whose impact would require unshown libmount parsing, so it is recorded as a limitation, not a finding.

assumptions: argv elements are NUL-terminated C strings via the OS execve contract, relied on at lines 278, 287-288 and by getopt_long/strchr/strncmp (lines 86-87, 244-245).
getopt_long guarantees 0 <= optind <= argc and optarg points into argv, so the shift at lines 218-219 and the argc==0/1/2 branch reads at lines 278, 287-288 are in bounds.
xasprintf allocates exactly the formatted size (N+9 for LABEL, N+8 for UUID) and aborts on failure, so no overflow/truncation of srcbuf can occur at lines 148/154.
mnt_context_set_source/set_target copy their string argument, implied by the immediate free(srcbuf) at lines 151/157.
usage(), print_version(), and exit_non_root() terminate (util-linux convention), making the code after lines 241-242 and 291 unreachable on those error paths.
limitations: LABEL/UUID quoting candidate: optarg is embedded verbatim at lines 148 and 154 with no escaping of embedded '"' or '\'; e.g., `mount -L 'a" b'` produces `LABEL="a" b"` passed to mnt_context_set_source (line 150). Whether the unshown libmount parser treats the quote as a delimiter, and any resulting impact, is not established in the fragment, so no injection sink or CWE can be confirmed.

Non-root source-only flows (argc==0, lines 257-265, e.g. `mount -L label`) are admitted by the fragment; their safety depends on unshown libmount fstab 'user' permission checks, so no privilege claim can be confirmed in either direction.

Handling of attacker strings by unshown callees (mnt_context_set_fstype_pattern/set_fstype at 246/248, set_options_pattern at 141, append_fstab at 166) is outside the fragment; none is a standard-operation sink whose argument can be shown out of domain.

No memory-safety, integer, crypto, or non-termination candidate is confirmable: the fragment performs no bounded copies or input-derived size arithmetic, and the only loop (line 86) always advances and terminates on -1.

verdict.summary: No security vulnerability is confirmable within the shown fragment. The most dangerous-looking sink is the Ctrl-U rewrite at lines 486-492: ccline.cmdlen -= j (line 487) and ccline.cmdbuff[ccline.cmdlen] = NUL (line 492) can only produce a negative index if ccline.cmdpos > ccline.cmdlen, a pre-state that no statement in the fragment can establish (all visible assignments keep cmdpos in [0, cmdlen]: lines 488, 545, 567, 695, 704), and the capacity of ccline.cmdbuff is not declared anywhere in the fragment. The same externality blocks the K_RIGHT re-read (line 559) and K_LEFT head-off subtraction (lines 573-574), which depend on the unshown mb_ptr2len/mb_head_off contracts and undeclared buffer capacity. All return values visible in the fragment are checked and dispatched; there are no injection, crypto, file, or format-string sinks in the fragment. The not-vulnerable verdict rests on the absence of a demonstrable in-fragment path rather than on a visible protective check, so confidence is capped low.

assumptions: ccline.cmdpos, ccline.cmdlen, and c are int and comparisons/arithmetic use int semantics (lines 8-10, 486-489, 545, 567, 577, 704).
Every exit path of the function reaches theend (lines 69, 75, all breaks and goto returncmd fall through to line 1000), so ++depth at line 39 is always balanced by --depth at line 1004.

The for(;;) loop at line 202 consumes input at line 227 (safe_vgetc) on every iteration and has explicit exits via break (lines 318, 411, 535, 714, 727, 736, 758) and goto returncmd, so termination does not depend on the content of the command line.
firstc, count, and indent are used only as character discriminators or are forwarded unchanged to not-shown helpers; no in-fragment size/index/format derivation uses them.
limitations: Ctrl-U deletion block (lines 486-492): an OOB write would require a pre-state with ccline.cmdpos > ccline.cmdlen (e.g., cmdlen=2, cmdpos=3 -> cmdlen=-1 -> cmdbuff[-1]=NUL at line 492). No shown statement can produce that pre-state; the 0 <= cmdpos <= cmdlen invariant and the actual capacity of ccline.cmdbuff are maintained/allocated by not-shown code (init_ccline, put_on_cmdline, cmdline_erase_chars, cmdline_browse_history), so the finding cannot be confirmed (fails Phase 3 part 2).

K_RIGHT loop (lines 543-559): after the guard at line 545 admits cmdpos < cmdlen, the advance at lines 552-555 can place cmdpos at cmdlen, and the read at line 559 can reach index cmdlen; whether it can exceed cmdlen depends on the not-shown mb_ptr2len semantics and on buffer well-formedness. Without a declared cmdbuff capacity or a shown bound on mb_ptr2len, no OOB (CWE-125) is confirmable.

K_LEFT loop (lines 569-580): ccline.cmdpos -= (*mb_head_off)(...) at lines 573-574 could underflow only if mb_head_off returns more than the current position; that contract is not visible in the fragment, so no CWE-125 is confirmable.
IObuff[j] = NUL at line 876 with j = mb_char2bytes(c, IObuff) at line 875: IObuff's capacity is not declared in the fragment and mb_char2bytes is unshown; not confirmable.
vim_strsave(ccline.cmdbuff) at line 958 is not NULL-checked, but the result is never dereferenced within the fragment, so no CWE-476/754 path exists in the shown code.

The safe verdict is based on the absence of a demonstrable in-fragment failure path rather than on a located protective check establishing the cmdbuff capacity or the cmdpos<=cmdlen invariant, which keeps confidence at 0.6 and the severity at unknown.

verdict.summary: sug_filltree() walks the case-folded trie with stack arrays arridx/curi/tword/wordcount all declared with MAXWLEN elements and indexes them by depth, but depth is only ever incremented per trie byte (line 88) and is never compared against MAXWLEN by any guard in the shown code. A trie containing a word of MAXWLEN bytes drives depth to MAXWLEN, so the descent writes arridx[depth], curi[depth], wordcount[depth] (lines 89-91) and the word-end writes tword[depth] = NUL (line 60) and ++wordcount[depth] (line 71) one element past each array's declared capacity, a stack out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) reachable from the trie data consumed by the function.

evidence.reason: Taint: depth (declared int, line 5) starts at 0 (line 36) and is incremented once per non-zero trie byte at line 88; the trie bytes come from slang->sl_fbyts/sl_fidxs (lines 27-28), constrained only by the NULL checks (lines 29-30) and the byte-skip bound at line 79 — nowhere is depth capped against MAXWLEN (verified by absence of any depth<MAXWLEN check in lines 37-94). Witness: a word of exactly MAXWLEN bytes (indices 0..MAXWLEN-1 in-bounds) followed by end byte 0 makes depth==MAXWLEN, so this line writes char_u tword[MAXWLEN] at index MAXWLEN — index equals capacity of the declaration at line 8 (valid max MAXWLEN-1) — a stack OOB write, excess 1 element, CWE-787.

Same taint/witness as the primary sink: at the push of the MAXWLEN-th character (depth becomes MAXWLEN via the preceding tword[depth++] = c), this statement writes idx_T arridx[MAXWLEN] at index MAXWLEN, equal to the declared capacity (line 6, valid 0..MAXWLEN-1) — OOB stack write, CWE-787.
Same witness: with depth==MAXWLEN on the final descent, writes int curi[MAXWLEN] at index MAXWLEN, equal to the declared capacity (line 7, valid 0..MAXWLEN-1) — OOB stack write, CWE-787.
Same witness: with depth==MAXWLEN on the final descent, writes int wordcount[MAXWLEN] at index MAXWLEN, equal to the declared capacity (line 13, valid 0..MAXWLEN-1) — OOB stack write, CWE-787.

For a trie word longer than MAXWLEN (e.g. MAXWLEN+1 non-zero bytes), the extra byte executes this statement when depth==MAXWLEN, writing char_u tword[MAXWLEN] at index MAXWLEN (capacity declared at line 8, valid 0..MAXWLEN-1), then depth==MAXWLEN+1 for the subsequent sinks — OOB stack write, CWE-787.
Word end at depth==MAXWLEN (word of MAXWLEN bytes) executes this read-modify-write on int wordcount[MAXWLEN] at index MAXWLEN, equal to the declared capacity (line 13) — OOB stack write, CWE-787.

Word end at depth==MAXWLEN followed by a duplicate NUL byte (byts[n+1]==0 with n+1 < sl_fbyts_len, guard at line 79 admitted) incrementally writes int curi[MAXWLEN] at index MAXWLEN, equal to the declared capacity (line 7) — OOB stack write, CWE-787.

assumptions: MAXWLEN is a positive compile-time constant; each array declared with [MAXWLEN] at lines 6, 7, 8, 9, 13 has exactly MAXWLEN elements, so valid indices are 0..MAXWLEN-1.
char_u is an unsigned byte type and idx_T an integer trie-index type; byts/idxs contents and sl_fbyts_len arrive from outside the fragment with no shown well-formedness or word-length constraint.

The trie representation is as consumed by the shown logic: a sequence of (count byte, byte...) nodes, where a zero byte at a node marks end-of-word (per the branch at line 57) and the duplicate-NUL skip at lines 79-83 is bounded by slang->sl_fbyts_len.
limitations: Malformed-trie OOB reads (byts[n] line 56, byts[arridx[depth]] line 39, idxs[n] line 89, idxs[arridx[depth]] line 42) are demoted: byts' length sl_fbyts_len is only evidenced by its use at line 79 and is never enforced on the main traversal, idxs' capacity is not identifiable in the fragment, and no shown statement establishes sl_fbyts_len>=1 or trie well-formedness, so the boundary cannot be fully grounded.

The return value of spell_soundfold (line 61) is discarded; if that helper could fail, uninitialized local tsalword (line 9) would be passed to tree_add_word (line 65). The callee's failure semantics are not shown, so this error-handling candidate is unconfirmed.

The primary witness requires the input trie to contain a word of at least MAXWLEN bytes; the fragment shows no producer of the trie and no word-length validation, so per the role rules the residual range is unconstrained — but any caller-side guarantee capping word length below MAXWLEN (not visible here) would make the overflow unreachable.
smsg(_("Total number of words: %d"), words_done) (line 96) passes unsigned words_done for %d; benign format mismatch with no security impact.
got_int (line 37) can terminate the loop mid-build leaving a partially populated soundfold trie; no shown consumer of that partial state is present, so it is not a finding.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the fragment. This is the post-CVE-2022-0847 fixed copy_page_to_iter_pipe: every newly filled page-cache-backed pipe buffer is given buf->flags = 0 (line 36), closing the stale PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE mechanism; all pipe->bufs[] indexes are masked to [0, ring_size-1] by lines 7/21/30, so the maximum reachable index is ring_size-1; and bytes is clamped to i->count (lines 11-12) before i->count -= bytes (line 46), so the count cannot underflow. The only structurally interesting derivation is a size_t-to-u32 narrowing of buf->len (lines 25 and 40) for bytes >= 2^32, whose witness passes every shown guard but whose corrupted value has no consumer inside the fragment, so its impact is undemonstrable here and it is recorded as a limitation rather than a finding.

assumptions: pipe->bufs[] has exactly pipe->ring_size entries, implied by the mask use at lines 7/21/30 (the array declaration is not in the fragment).
i->count, i->iov_offset and i->head are the pipe-backed iterator's remaining byte count, offset and last-used buffer index, consistent with uses at lines 8, 11-12, 20, 26, 43-44, 46.
sanity(i) (lines 17-18) returns false for a inconsistent iterator, and pipe_full(i_head, p_tail, pipe->max_usage) (lines 32-33) is true when the ring occupancy has reached max_usage.
unlikely() (lines 11, 14) is a branch-prediction hint with no semantic effect.
page, i and pipe are non-NULL on entry; no statement in the fragment can produce a NULL value for them.
limitations: size_t-to-unsigned-int narrowing of buf->len at lines 40 and 25: bytes retains residual range [1, i->count] with i->count unbounded in the fragment, so bytes = 2^32 + 1 is a member of every guard's admitted set (lines 11-12, 14, 17, 22, 23, 32) and the stored length truncates; however the fragment shows no consumer of the corrupted buf->len, so the security impact is undemonstrable and no CWE is attached.
The pipe->bufs[] array capacity is not declared in the fragment; the safe index conclusion relies on the visible mask arithmetic (line 7) bounding every index below ring_size.
A NULL dereference of page/i/pipe (e.g. line 37-38) is not producible by any shown statement and would require out-of-fragment caller misuse.

The merge path (lines 23-27) never writes buf->flags; the exclusion of an external pipe_write-created CAN_MERGE buffer from matching buf->page == page relies on pipe_write internals not shown in the fragment (the fragment's own created buffers carry flags == 0 via line 36).
ring_size == 0 would underflow p_mask at line 7 to UINT_MAX, permitting an out-of-ring index at lines 21/30; no shown statement produces ring_size == 0, and pipe creation is outside the fragment.
offset + bytes (line 43) can wrap only for operands near SIZE_MAX (~2^64); no shown sink consumes the wrapped i->iov_offset within the fragment, and no shown constraint admits such magnitudes.

pipe->head = i_head + 1 (line 42) wraps only if i->head is at UINT_MAX-1/UINT_MAX from the caller; ring wraparound is the design, and no in-fragment security-relevant operation consumes the wrapped head.

verdict.summary: No security-relevant sink exists in this fragment. The parameter c is only stored into VIsual_mode and compared to Ctrl_V; all other input is global window state consumed as scalar values. There are no memory operations, injection sinks, crypto/entropy use, file/access-control logic, loops, or reachable aborts, and no discarded return status is followed by a security-relevant operation. The only position-consuming call, coladvance(curwin->w_virtcol), cannot be assessed because w_virtcol's domain and coladvance's contract are not visible in the fragment.

assumptions: Constants referred to in the fragment (Ctrl_V, VE_BLOCK, TAB, INVERTED, NUL, TRUE) and conditional-compilation macros (FEAT_CONCEAL, FEAT_FOLDING, FEAT_CLIPBOARD) are defined outside the fragment; they are used only in equality/flag tests or scalar assignments, and no capacity or boundary claim depends on their values.

curwin is a framework-provided global pointer (lines 4, 14, 19, 42, 44-45); the fragment performs no operation that can produce a NULL curwin, so NULL dereference is not assessable as a finding herein.
limitations: The validity of coladvance(curwin->w_virtcol) (line 17) is unconfirmable: the fragment neither derives nor bounds curwin->w_virtcol, and coladvance's contract is not shown, so no OOB/position claim can be made in either direction.

Return values of validate_virtcol(), coladvance(), foldAdjustVisual(), trigger_modechanged(), setmouse(), and conceal_check_cursor_line() are discarded, but no security-relevant operation in the fragment consumes a failure state, so this is not an error-handling finding.

Any potential issue requiring caller-supplied NULL curwin, an unshown invariant of gchar_cursor()/get_ve_flags()/conceal_cursor_line(), or unshown macro values would depend on code outside the fragment and is out of scope.

verdict.summary: Crafted bytecode can reach OP_JMPUW's sink `pc = irep->iseq + a;` (line 322) with a derived from the bytecode operand and no main-path bound against `irep->ilen` (the only `ilen` check is inside the break-restore path at line 308), causing an out-of-bounds read of `irep->iseq` and execution of out-of-range bytecode. Independently, OP_ARGARY (line 671) and OP_BLKPUSH (line 1171) read one `mrb_value` past `e->stack` when `kd=1` and `MRB_ENV_LEN(e)` sits exactly at the guard boundary `m1+r+m2+2` admitted by lines 638/1165.

evidence.reason: CWE-125 primary sink. Operand `a` (uint32_t, entry-point bytecode input with residual range [0, 2^32-1] from the line 302 arithmetic `(uint32_t)((pc - irep->iseq) + (int16_t)a)`) is used to index `irep->iseq`, whose capacity is `irep->ilen` elements as named by the fragment's own valid-target bound `mrb_assert(a >= 0 && a < irep->ilen)` at line 308. That check exists only on the CHECKPOINT_RESTORE path; the main path's only guard (lines 311-317) bounds `a` against a catch-handler range when `ch != NULL` and never against `irep->ilen`. Witness: `pc == irep->iseq`, operand `a=1`, `irep->ilen=1`, `ch==NULL` (admitted by `if (ch)` at line 312): line 302 yields `a=1`, and line 322 sets `pc` one element past `iseq`, so the next fetch reads `iseq[1]` (index == capacity); any `a >= irep->ilen` triggers it.

CWE-125 independent OOB read. With operand `b=0x11` (provenance (a)): `m1=0, r=0, m2=0, kd=1, lv=1`. Guard line 638 (`MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1`) admits ENV_LEN >= 2; taking ENV_LEN = 2 (the admitted minimum) the guard `2 <= 1` is false and execution proceeds; `stack = e->stack + 1` (line 640), so `stack[1]` is `e->stack[2]`, i.e. index == capacity of `e->stack` (capacity = `MRB_ENV_LEN(e)`, the bound the fragment itself uses for env accesses at lines 252/267). The guard constant `+1` protects indices up to `e->stack[m1+r+m2+1]` and is one short of the `kd==1` access at index `m1+r+m2+2`. One-element overread whose value is stored into `regs[a+2]` and later used as a Ruby object.

CWE-125 independent OOB read, same guard-boundary defect as OP_ARGARY. Guard line 1165 (`MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1`) admits ENV_LEN = m1+r+m2+2; with operand `b=0x11` (`m1=r=m2=0, kd=1, lv=1`) and an on-stack env with ENV_LEN = 2, the guard is false and `stack[1] = e->stack[2]` is read at index == capacity (`MRB_ENV_LEN(e)`), one element past `e->stack`. Line 1175 repeats the same index. The read value is tested for nil and copied to `regs[a]`.

assumptions: irep->ilen is the element count of irep->iseq; the fragment names that exact bound for a jump target in the line 308 assert.
MRB_ENV_LEN(e) is the capacity (element count) of e->stack; the fragment uses it as the access bound for e->stack at lines 252, 267, 638, 1165.
Operands a/b/c are decoded from the bytecode stream by unshown FETCH macros and are unconstrained in the fragment (provenance (a), full declared domains: uint32_t / uint16_t / uint16_t).
Sub-field ranges of `b` follow the shown masks: m1 in [0,63], r in {0,1}, m2 in [0,31], kd in {0,1}, lv in [0,15].

CHECKPOINT_RESTORE bodies execute only on the longjmp restore path; on the ordinary execution path only the CHECKPOINT_MAIN body runs, so the line 308 assert does not bound the main-path value of `a`.
limitations: regs[]-indexed operations (OP_MOVE/OP_ARRAY/OP_ARYPUSH/OP_APOST writes, OP_HASH, OP_ENTER, OP_KARG/OP_KEYEND, OP_AREF/OP_ASET, OP_SETIDX regs[a+3], OP_SEND setup, regs[irep->nlocals] at line 1811) cannot be confirmed: the capacity of `mrb->c->ci->stack` is not identifiable in the fragment.

pool[b], syms[b], irep->reps[b] indexing and OP_STRING/OP_SYMBOL/OP_ERR lengths derived from `pool[b].tt >> 2` cannot be confirmed: pool/syms/reps lengths and the string-storage capacities are not identifiable in the fragment.
The lv==0 branches of OP_ARGARY/OP_BLKPUSH read `stack = regs+1` with no shown length guard; capacity unknown, so the same one-past-end analysis cannot be grounded there.
Uninitialized `blk` use at lines 420, 443-447, 568 depends on the unshown ARGUMENT_NORMALIZE macro; producer not confirmable.
Impl-defined conversions `(int32_t)(((uint32_t)b<<16)+c)` (line 115) and `int lim = a+b*2` (line 1559) have no demonstrable security-relevant consequence in the fragment.

Reachable-assert candidates (lines 308, 339, 455, 595, 1091, 1124-1125, 1808) are debug-only or protect fragment-established invariants; the 308 assert is reachable with an out-of-range break value only when asserts are compiled in.
OP_EXT1/2/3 unknown-opcode fallthrough (`pc--; NEXT;`) and main-loop non-termination (CWE-835) are unconfirmable because the dispatch/fetch macro semantics are not shown.
Unchecked allocations (mrb_ary_new_*, mrb_hash_new_capa) have no shown security-relevant operation on the failure state; treated as mruby abort-on-OOM behavior, not a finding.

verdict.summary: One-byte out-of-bounds write in gopherToHTML: a gopher line whose length reaches TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 (either a line of exactly TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 bytes admitted unclamped, or any longer line clamped to TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 at line 77) makes line 96 write '\0' at index TEMP_BUF_SIZE, one past the TEMP_BUF_SIZE-byte buffer declared at line 6. The trigger (line length) is fully attacker-controlled through gopher data; the written value is a fixed NUL byte, giving attacker-directed memory corruption of one byte past the buffer (a NUL-byte off-by-one).

evidence.reason: Sink writes at index llen+1 into the buffer declared at line 6 with capacity TEMP_BUF_SIZE (valid indices 0..TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1). llen is derived from attacker-controlled input at lines 71/73 (memchr line length, unbounded in the fragment) and the guard at line 75 admits llen == TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 (unclamped, since TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 >= TEMP_BUF_SIZE is false) while its own clamp at line 77 maps every llen >= TEMP_BUF_SIZE to exactly TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 (and line 91 re-adds gopherState->len, still landing at TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1). For those admitted values the index llen+1 equals TEMP_BUF_SIZE, i.e. index == capacity, a one-byte OOB write of '\0' (CWE-787). Witness: inbuf = 'A'*(TEMP_BUF_SIZE-2)+'\n', len = TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1, gopherState->len == 0: memchr at line 68 finds '\n', llen = TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 at line 71, guard 75 does not clamp, memcpy at line 94 writes indices 0..TEMP_BUF_SIZE-2 (exact fit), and line 96 overwrites line[TEMP_BUF_SIZE].

assumptions: line's capacity is exactly TEMP_BUF_SIZE bytes: quoted from line 6 (LOCAL_ARRAY(char, line, TEMP_BUF_SIZE)) and line 16 (memset(line, '\0', TEMP_BUF_SIZE)); the numeric value of TEMP_BUF_SIZE is not needed.

gopherState->len stays within [0, TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1] as produced by the fragment itself: increments at line 84 are post-clamp (line 77) and line 92 resets to 0; the primary witness uses gopherState->len == 0.

inbuf/len are entry-point input: the fragment parses gopher protocol lines and TAB-separated fields, so the data is externally supplied, and no statement in the fragment constrains its length or content.
limitations: OOB write at memcpy(gopherState->buf + gopherState->len, pos, llen) (line 83) is unconfirmable because the capacity of gopherState->buf is not declared anywhere in the fragment.

Negative llen from the clamp expression TEMP_BUF_SIZE - gopherState->len - 1 (line 77) would require gopherState->len > TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1, which the shown code's own updates (lines 84, 91, 92) never produce; not a finding.
Whether the overwritten byte is in stack or heap storage depends on the unshown LOCAL_ARRAY macro; only the out-of-bounds index itself is confirmed, so CWE-787 is used rather than CWE-121/CWE-122.

HTML/URL injection via unescaped port/host in the appendf hrefs (lines 219-225, 232-233, 239-240) cannot be confirmed from the fragment alone: the adversary must hit gtype == GOPHER_TELNET/GOPHER_3270 or selector starting with 'GET /' and the numeric GOPHER_*/conversion constants and escaping-helper semantics are not visible, so no fully-shown-code witness can be constructed.

Residual stale bytes between successive lines (line is not re-zeroed per iteration and line[llen] is not set before processing) is a parsing-correctness concern, not an independent confirmed memory-safety issue.

verdict.summary: No security vulnerability is confirmable within the fragment. The fragment contains no memory-safety, injection, crypto, file, or authz sinks. Suspicious numeric paths (double-precision rounding in the sampleSize guards at lines 14 and 28, a potential 0/0 NaN at line 124 only when gTimeseriesBucketMaxCount==0, and an unvalidated-sign sampleSize forwarded at line 136) all fail the confirmation standard: the degenerate inputs are not established by any shown statement and the downstream failures would occur in unshown callees.

assumptions: expCtx is a boost::intrusive_ptr dereferenced at lines 6, 10, 13, 60 and 84 with no null check; the fragment establishes no nullable contract, so it is treated as framework-guaranteed non-null.
gTimeseriesBucketMaxCount (lines 28, 124, 137) has no declared type or positive lower bound visible in the fragment.
numRecords is an internal-helper parameter (record count); only lines 14 (numRecords > 100 on the non-timeseries path) and 91 (numRecords != 0 on the timeseries path) constrain it.
kMaxSampleRatioForRandCursor=0.05 (line 12), kCoefficient=0.01 (line 27) and 0.02 (line 121), kMinBucketFullness=0.25 (line 122), kMaxPresampleSize=100 (line 59).
limitations: A negative sampleSize (e.g., -2^62) passes line 28 and line 91 and is forwarded unchanged to SampleFromTimeseriesBucket at line 136; the callee body is not shown, and no standard/name-implied failure (loop bound, unsigned conversion, allocation size) can be confirmed within the fragment, so impact is unconfirmed.

A NaN minAdvancedToWorkRatio at line 124 requires gTimeseriesBucketMaxCount == 0 with sampleSize == 0 and numRecords > 0; degeneracy of that config datum is a range claim, not an established input, and the consumption of the NaN threshold by TrialStage (line 145) is not visible.

Floating-point precision loss in the guards at lines 14/28 can admit a sampleSize exceeding exact 5% by up to a few hundred documents for collections near 2^63 records; the only downstream effect is the plan-choice heuristic, with the TrialStage fallback compensating, so no security mechanism is corrupted.
CollectionShardingState::get(...) at line 49 is dereferenced at line 50 without a null check; a NULL producer is not shown in the fragment.
The invariant abort at line 10 fires only on lock-state conditions that are not attacker-directed data within this fragment.

verdict.summary: No exploitable vulnerability is confirmable from the fragment alone. Every `*p` read is preceded by an EOF guard (entry `if ( p == pe ) goto _test_eof;` at L16-17 and each state's `if ( ++p == pe ) goto _test_eofN;`, e.g. L42-43), so reads stay within the [buffer+off, buffer+len) segment; `off <= len` is asserted at L5, and the `tr22` header_done pointer/length (L292) is exactly in-bounds. Unresolvable concerns are recorded in limitations.

assumptions: L5 `assert(off <= len && ...)` implies p = buffer+off <= pe = buffer+len (L7-8), so the parse segment is [buffer+off, buffer+len).

The entry guard L16-17 and the per-state `if ( ++p == pe ) goto _test_eofN;` checks (e.g., L42-43, L282-284, L366-367, L433-434) establish p < pe before every `(*p)` read, both on first entry and on `switch (cs)` re-entry.
By the shown comparisons at L946-950, parser->nread/body_start/mark/field_len/field_start are integral and comparable with size_t len.
The caller supplies a buffer with at least len readable bytes; the fragment contains no statement establishing NUL termination (the *pe == '\0' assert is commented out at L10).
limitations: The macro bodies for MARK/LEN/PTR_TO and the puma_parser field/member types are not in the fragment, so the pointer/length arguments to the parser callbacks (L63, L103, L111, L117, L123, L127, L135, L139, L145, L149, L228, L236, L242, L292, L376, L382, L386, L394, L398, L404, L408, L518) cannot be traced through shown code; in particular a cross-call reuse of stale parser->mark/field_start/field_len into those callbacks (structurally possible via re-entry at `case 2`/`case 15`/`case 18` without a same-call MARK) cannot be confirmed from the fragment, because neither the macros' arithmetic nor the caller's buffer-retention contract is shown.

All bounds enforcement is assert-based (L5, L11, L945-950); whether NDEBUG is defined is not shown, so if assertions compile out, no shown runtime check enforces the invariants - this is an absence in the fragment, not a demonstrated flaw.

A len==0/off==0 call would trip `assert(parser->mark < len)` and `assert(parser->field_start < len)` (L948/L950) only if those fields start at 0; their initialization is not shown, so the witness is not derivable from the fragment.
`parser->nread += p - (buffer + off);` (L943) and the persistent marker fields accumulate across calls; repeated or buffer-compacting usage is caller-controlled and outside the fragment.
`snake_upcase_char((char *)p);` (L306, L310) mutates the const input buffer in place; it is in-bounds per the state guards, so it is a const-violation design note rather than a memory-safety finding.
Signed char comparisons (e.g., L25, L422, L491) affect which byte values the grammar accepts, not memory safety; high-bit bytes are admitted as fragment/URI characters in some states.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds read in parseDragons: b is allocated with size = r_buf_size(buf) - off, and the fragment only guarantees size >= 1 (line 8) before memcmp(..., b, 4) at line 44 and memcmp(..., b + 8, 4) at line 47 read fixed 4-byte blocks. A crafted small file (e.g., remaining size 1-3 bytes with off = 0) makes the reads exceed the size-byte allocation by up to 11 bytes (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: b's capacity is exactly `size` from `malloc (size)` at line 11; guards on the path (line 4 off<size, line 8 size>=1, line 12 b!=NULL, line 16 available==size) leave residual size in [1, INT_MAX], admitting size=1..3. memcmp with n=4 reads b[0..3], so for size=1 (witness: 1-byte file, off=0, read succeeds) offsets 1..3 are past the 1-byte heap allocation — heap OOB read (CWE-125) by up to 3 bytes.

Same taint and capacity (`malloc (size)` line 11, residual size in [1, INT_MAX]). For witness size=4 (4-byte file, off=0, line 15 read succeeds) the read at b+8..b+11 is entirely beyond the 4-byte allocation; for size in [8,11] it is partially OOB. Distinct sink statement (CWE-125).

assumptions: r_buf_size(buf) returns the full size of the RBuffer and r_buf_read_at returns the number of bytes actually read (a failed read yields available != size) — name-implied semantics; no shown statement bounds the size below 1.
malloc(size) succeeds for the witness; the failure path (line 12) returns before any dereference, so it does not affect the finding.
The fragment contains no loop constructs, so no loop-derived iteration bounds apply.
limitations: Line 65 `r_read_le32 (b + 12)` would OOB-read for size < 16, but its execution depends on the unshown `D` macro, so reachability is not established in the fragment.

Lines 18 and 55 return NULL without freeing b, leaking the size-byte allocation; severity depends on caller/framework volume outside the fragment, so it is treated as a robustness concern, not a confirmed finding.
Line 69 `off + 16` may overflow signed int for off > INT_MAX - 16, but r_coresym_cache_element_new is outside the fragment, so the security impact of the wrapped value is unconfirmable.

Line 52 `off - 8` is negative when off < 8; r_buf_read_at's offset handling is unshown and the result is only count-checked at line 53 (the write into b stays within its capacity), so no in-fragment memory-safety sink is derivable.
A negative off is essentially excluded by line 4's int-to-ut64 comparison; it could pass only for buffer sizes within a few units of UINT64_MAX, which the line-15 read path cannot reach.

verdict.summary: jetp3852_print_page overflows the stack buffer data[DATA_SIZE] with memset(end_data, 0, 7) when the scan-line size equals DATA_SIZE (the only guard, line 22, rejects only line_size > DATA_SIZE, admitting equality, and a nonzero trailing byte prevents the shrinking loop at lines 33-34), writing 7 bytes past the line-10 capacity (CWE-787). Independently, the transpose step treats full scan-line bytes dp[0..7] as indices into the 8-element spr40/spr8/spr2 tables, so any byte >= 8 causes an out-of-bounds read of those tables (CWE-125), with the value folded into the printer output.

evidence.reason: line_size (int, assigned at line 19) is bounded only above by the line-22 guard `if (line_size > DATA_SIZE)`, whose admitted set is every int value <= DATA_SIZE, including exactly DATA_SIZE. end_data = data + line_size (line 29) then equals data + DATA_SIZE, one past the last valid index (DATA_SIZE-1) of `byte data[DATA_SIZE]` (line 10, capacity DATA_SIZE = LINE_SIZE*8). With a scan line whose last byte is nonzero, the trailing-zero loop (lines 33-34) exits without decrementing and the blank-line branch (line 35) is not taken; line 45 writes zeros at offsets DATA_SIZE..DATA_SIZE+6, all 7 bytes beyond the buffer (CWE-787 stack buffer overflow; witness: line_size == DATA_SIZE, data[DATA_SIZE-1] != 0).

The lookup tables have capacity 8 (visible from `static ulong spr40[8] = spread3(0x40);` at line 53 and the 8-entry spread3 macro at lines 51-52), but they are indexed by raw scan-line bytes dp[0..7] copied at lines 30-31; no shown statement masks (`& 7`) or otherwise constrains those bytes. A byte value of 8 (in the full 8-bit index domain) reads spr40[8], one element past the table, and values up to 255 read up to ~248 elements past it; the resulting pword (line 57) is written to plane_data and emitted to the printer stream (CWE-125 out-of-bounds read of static storage).

assumptions: Capacity of data is DATA_SIZE bytes, claimed from `byte data[DATA_SIZE];` (line 10) together with `#define DATA_SIZE (LINE_SIZE * 8)` (line 3).

Capacity of plane_data is LINE_SIZE*3 bytes, claimed from `byte plane_data[LINE_SIZE * 3];` (line 11); the transpose writes (lines 66-68) are exactly in-bounds because the last odp is plane_data + LINE_SIZE - 1 (loop line 48, i <= DATA_SIZE-8).
Capacities of spr40/spr8/spr2 are 8 ulongs each, visible from the initializers (lines 53-55) and the 8-element spread3 macro (lines 51-52).
byte is an 8-bit type (unsigned in Ghostscript's typedef, which is outside the fragment); if signed, the spr-table indices would be negative and still out of the 0..7 domain.

gdev_mem_bytes_per_scan_line returns the scan-line byte length and gdev_prn_copy_scan_lines writes exactly line_size bytes, per their size arguments at lines 19, 30-31; no additional invariant for them is visible in the fragment.
LINE_SIZE is a positive integer constant; its value is not defined in the fragment.
limitations: Negative line_size would make end_data point before data and make line_size_color_plane negative, so line 45 would write before data and gp_fwrite (lines 107-108) would receive a negative count promoted to a huge size_t; this requires gdev_mem_bytes_per_scan_line to return a negative value, which is only a range claim, not a demonstrated witness.

When line_size < DATA_SIZE, the transpose loop (lines 56-65) reads data[line_size..DATA_SIZE-1], which no shown statement initializes after the line-30 copy (CWE-457-style uninitialized read emitted to the printer); confirmed in the shown code but treated as lower-impact and not listed as an extra CWE.

Return values of gdev_prn_copy_scan_lines (lines 30-31) and of the gp_* write calls (lines 14, 74, 78, 93-95, 107-108, 115) are discarded; no security-relevant operation in the fragment consumes the failure state.

Any invariant outside the fragment that constrained line_size to be at least 7 bytes below DATA_SIZE, or constrained scan-line bytes to 0..7, would neutralize the two findings; no such statement exists in the shown code and cannot be used per the analysis rules.

The CWE-787 witness requires device geometry admitting line_size == DATA_SIZE (or within 6 bytes below it), which is configurable but not shown in the fragment; this boundary dependence caps confidence at 0.8.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable from the fragment. The strongest candidate is an out-of-bounds read in onig_node_str_cat (line 51): len = enclen(reg->enc, p) (line 29) is never validated against the remaining string bytes, and a truncated multibyte tail (e.g., a lone 0xF0 byte with end-p == 1) yields len == 4, so the copy reads 3 bytes past the logical string end. However, the source buffer's allocation capacity is not declared or derivable in the fragment (only the pointers sn->s/sn->end, lines 13-14, and the non-emptiness check, line 15), so per the capacity-grounding rule the OOB claim is a limitation, not a confirmed finding. The alt_num *= (n + 1) arithmetic (line 55) cannot wrap because n is bounded by the items array contract (line 8) and the threshold break (line 56) caps the transient product at <= 32; NULL-deref producers (line 79) and non-termination (line 93 with len == 0) depend on unshown callee/library behavior.

assumptions: sn->s / sn->end are valid pointers with end > start, guaranteed by 'if (start >= end) return 0;' (line 15) which admits only end - start >= 1 byte.

ONIGENC_GET_CASE_FOLD_CODES_BY_STR (lines 22-23) writes at most ONIGENC_GET_CASE_FOLD_CODES_MAX_NUM items into the array declared at line 8 and returns that count (els n would already overrun items inside the callee).
enclen(reg->enc, p) returns the byte length of the character beginning at p (library semantics), but the fragment imposes no check linking it to end - p.
limitations: OOB read candidate (CWE-125 unconfirmed) at line 51: len (line 29) is unvalidated and can exceed end - p (witness: end = start + 1, byte 0xF0, n == 0, len == 4; the copy reads 4 bytes of which 3 lie past the string extent). This is the real-world CVE-2019-19204 style of bug, but the source object's allocation capacity is not identifiable from the fragment (no array/allocation declaration for the string data), so the boundary claim is unconfirmable and is reported only here.
The same unvalidated len feeds 'p += len' (line 93); p can overshoot end, but no shown memory operation consumes that overshoot beyond the line-51 read.
Non-termination (CWE-835) if enclen returned 0 is not established: no shown statement admits len == 0 and enclen's behavior is outside the fragment.
NULL dereference at line 79 (NODE_CAR(prev_node)) and the line-66/line-99 helpers: no shown statement produces NULL prev_node/srem on the successful return paths; producers are in unshown callees.

alt_num integer overflow (line 55) is not a finding: under the items contract the multiplier n+1 <= MAX_NUM+1 and the threshold break (line 56) caps the transient product at <= 32, so no int wrap is reachable.
Case-fold expansion resource exhaustion is mitigated by the threshold break (line 56); without it the loop would still be linear in input length, and the input size bound is not shown.
Error paths were walked: no double-free/use-after-free is confirmed; unreachable single-shot leaks on OOM paths are out of scope per the rules.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability in suggest_trie_walk() can be confirmed from the fragment alone. All writes to the fixed-capacity locals (tword[MAXWLEN] line 7, stack[MAXWLEN] line 8, preword[MAXWLEN*3] line 9, compflags[MAXWLEN] line 14) are indexed by trystate_T fields (ts_twordlen, ts_prewordlen, ts_complen) and by depth, whose values are installed by the unshown go_deeper()/TRY_DEEPER() helpers; the only visible depth bound (depth < MAXWLEN - 1, line 126) covers a single path, and no shown statement bounds the other indices, so no in-bounds or out-of-bounds index can be derived from the shown code. In-place edits of the caller buffer fword (REP/swap states, e.g. lines 1368-1371) have no declared capacity in the fragment. Every candidate fails the witness requirement: the dangerous index/size derivation is not traceable entirely within the shown code, and the carry-over of these as confirmed findings would violate the fragment-only rule.

assumptions: fword is a NUL-terminated byte string; the shown code relies on this at lines 177-180, 637, 696-697, 823, 967, 997-1002.
tword, stack, preword, compflags are declared with capacities MAXWLEN, MAXWLEN, MAXWLEN*3, MAXWLEN at lines 7, 8, 9, 14 respectively; these are the only capacities usable for boundary claims.
Node byte ranges are self-described by byts[arridx] (line 108) and the shown guards at lines 159, 652, 900 keep ts_curi in [1..len] for node-local reads.
line 126 (depth < MAXWLEN - 1) bounds the prefix-tree go_deeper path only.
limitations: tword/stack/preword/compflags out-of-bounds writes (CWE-787 candidates at lines 151/181/698/931, 143/549/695/930/1031/1119/1187/1248/1363, 238/302/305/322-323/553/576-579, 269-270/479-480/498): sink capacities are visible but the index values are installed by the unshown go_deeper() and gated by the unshown TRY_DEEPER; no witness value for ts_twordlen==MAXWLEN, ts_complen==MAXWLEN, or depth==MAXWLEN can be constructed from the shown code, so part 2 (traceable derivation) fails.
(char_u)STRLEN(preword) truncation at lines 153 and 554 would only wrap if STRLEN(preword) >= 256; reaching such a length is not derivable from the fragment.

fword in-place expansion in STATE_REP (STRMOVE line 1368, mch_memmove line 1371) and swap/rotate writes: the capacity of the buffer backing the fword parameter is not declared anywhere in the fragment, so the boundary claim is unconfirmable in either direction.

Negative sp->ts_fidx - repextra passed to add_suggestion (lines 245, 408, 423): no shown guard constrains repextra relative to ts_fidx (the line-384 guard tests only ts_fidx > 0), and add_suggestion's treatment of a negative length is not shown; the failure path cannot be demonstrated.
NULL dereference of lp->lp_slang (line 31) or lp->lp_replang (lines 1303, 1317): the fragment contains no producer of a NULL value for these pointers.

Node-walk reads of byts/idxs are safe only under an unshown spell-file layout invariant; malformed dose tree data could invalidate the self-described lengths, but the tree buffer sizes are not visible and this parsing happens outside the fragment.

DEBUG_TRIEWALK-only sprintf into changename[MAXWLEN][80] (lines 537-541, 686-692, 828-830, 925-927, 1025-1027, 1113-1115, 1181-1183, 1242-1244, 1354-1356) is compiled out unless that macro is defined and additionally depends on unshown ts_twordlen.
The scoring oddity at line 855 (comparing fword[ts_fidx] with fword[ts_fidx+1] after deletion rather than the deleted character) is a logic quirk with no security impact demonstrated.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the shown fragment. The only sink with an identifiable capacity, the stack buffer declared at lines 5-6, is fully protected by the guard at line 82 (admitted dire->size in [0, SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN-1], so the memcpy at 87-88 and the NUL store at 89 never exceed the NAME_LEN+1 name region). Plausible issues - strcpy into dir->dirs[].name (line 101), OOB reads of directory_table (lines 54/57/73-74/77-78/87-88) including reads past the size bound from the unguarded inner loop, integer wrap in bytes/size (lines 48-49) and in the realloc size (lines 94-95), and a NULL dereference of *i (lines 25-29, 32) - cannot be confirmed because the respective capacities, struct layouts, and helper contracts are not declared in the fragment.

assumptions: buffer at lines 5-6 ('char buffer[sizeof(squashfs_dir_entry_3) + SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1]') provides a name region of SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN+1 bytes at dire->name, assuming squashfs_dir_entry_3's name field is the trailing member and sizeof covers the preceding fields (struct layout not shown).

The guard at line 82 ('if(dire->size >= SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN)') admits dire->size in [0, SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN-1] because dire->size is an unsigned short-sized field; this bound is used symbolically (numeric VALUE of SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN is not shown, but the guard-relative bound is derivable from the shown comparison).
lookup_entry (line 42) returns -1 on failure (this single failure value is checked at line 44); all other return values are treated as byte offsets into directory_table.
limitations: OOB reads of directory_table (lines 54, 57, 73-74, 77-78, 87-88): the capacity/allocation of directory_table is not declared anywhere in the fragment, so no excess over a real object can be quantified; additionally, entry/name reads inside while(dir_count--) (lines 73-88) proceed after bytes has advanced past the size bound (only header reads re-check bytes < size at line 51), but that overshoot is also unquantifiable without the table capacity.

strcpy at line 101 into dir->dirs[dir->dir_count].name: source string length is at most NAME_LEN+1 bytes (NUL forced at line 89), but struct dir_ent::name capacity is not visible; a 1-byte overflow would exist only if that capacity equals NAME_LEN, which the fragment neither declares nor excludes.

Integer wrap / signedness in 'bytes += (*i)->offset' (line 48), 'size = (*i)->data + bytes - 3' (line 49), and '(dir->dir_count + DIR_ENT_SIZE) * sizeof(struct dir_ent)' (lines 94-95): the types of (*i)->offset and (*i)->data and the reachable magnitudes (entry counts, byte offsets) are not declared or bounded in the fragment; a wrapped negative bytes (line 48) would feed directory_table + bytes whose capacity is also invisible.

NULL dereference of *i at lines 25-29 and 32 after '*i = read_inode(...)' (line 17): no shown statement establishes that read_inode can return NULL on any admitted input; the NULL producer is outside the fragment.
Possible non-termination of the outer loop (line 51) via int wraparound of bytes requires unshown types and an unshown directory_table capacity.

dirh.count == UINT_MAX makes dir_count wrap to 0 at line 59, which passes the guard at line 65 and skips the inner loop; this is benign (only a 12-byte header is consumed) and is not reported as a finding.
The EXIT_UNSQUASH and goto corrupted error paths (lines 21, 45-46, 65-68, 82-85, 96-98) are intentional, guard-protected error handling and are not reachable-abort (CWE-617) findings.

verdict.summary: gopherToHTML writes the NUL terminator one byte past the end of the local line buffer whenever a gopher response line fills TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 bytes: the clamp at lines 77-80 caps the copy to TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 bytes but line[llen + 1] then indexes TEMP_BUF_SIZE, exactly one past the capacity declared at line 6 (CWE-787). The same function also emits attacker-controlled host/port fields unescaped into generated HTML HREFs (lines 236-241), enabling HTML attribute injection/XSS (CWE-79).

evidence.reason: Sink: one-byte OOB write at line[N] where N = TEMP_BUF_SIZE is the capacity of `line` declared at line 6 (LOCAL_ARRAY(char, line, TEMP_BUF_SIZE)). llen is derived from entry-point input inbuf via memchr (lines 70-75) and is clamped at line 79 to TEMP_BUF_SIZE - gopherState->len - 1 whenever line 77 fires, so the total copied into line is exactly TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1; the terminator write at llen+1 then uses index TEMP_BUF_SIZE == capacity. Witness: inbuf = "a\n" + (TEMP_BUF_SIZE-2)*'A' + "\n", len = TEMP_BUF_SIZE+1; second iteration has gopherState->len = 0, llen = TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1, guard 77 false, memcpy at 96 fills line[0..TEMP_BUF_SIZE-2], and line 98 writes past the end. The guard at line 77 fails to protect the sink because its admitted set (total >= TEMP_BUF_SIZE) always produces total == TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 after clamping, and the no-clamp boundary total == TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 also reaches index == capacity; every guard on the path (67, 71, 81, 89) is passed. Primary mechanism: stack out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

evidence.snippet: snprintf(tmpbuf, TEMP_BUF_SIZE, " %s\n", icon_url, host, rfc1738_escape_unescaped(selector + 5), html_quote(name));
evidence.reason: Sink: HTML/attribute injection (CWE-79). `host` (bytes between the 2nd and 3rd TAB of the entry-point response line, lines 124-128) is passed as a raw %s argument into the HREF attribute; the only transformations on host are TAB/CR/LF truncation (lines 134-147), which do not remove `"`, `<`, `>`, or spaces, so metacharacters survive to the generated HTML that is appended to the client response (lines 246, 331). Witness: conversion = HTML_DIR, line `0n\tGET /x\tx"><script>alert(1)</script><a href="\t70` — guards 121/126/131 pass, gtype '0' takes the else at 233, strncmp(selector, "GET /", 5) at 234 passes, and the output becomes `<A HREF="http://x"><script>alert(1)</script><a href="/x">`. Content inserted into `line` is attacker-controlled via inbuf (no content filter in the shown code).

assumptions: LOCAL_ARRAY(char, name, TEMP_BUF_SIZE) at lines 6-7 declares fixed-size local arrays with capacity TEMP_BUF_SIZE elements; the fragment's own memset/snprintf calls (lines 17-18, 219, 223+) use TEMP_BUF_SIZE as the byte capacity, consistent with that interpretation.

gopherState->len is 0 at the start of any loop iteration after a prior full-line iteration: line 94 resets it to 0, and the else branch (lines 95-97) leaves it unchanged; clamps keep gopherState->len + llen <= TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1.
inbuf/len are the gopher server response and its length (entry-point input, attacker-controlled); the fragment places no constraint on their content.

The output document built by this function is rendered as HTML by the client (gopherHTMLHeader, whose Content-Type is set outside the fragment, is assumed to emit text/html; html_quote usage throughout shows the fragment treats its output as HTML).
limitations: memcpy(gopherState->buf + gopherState->len, pos, llen) at line 85: the capacity of gopherState->buf is not visible in the fragment, so a possible overflow there is unconfirmable.
Impact of the one-byte write past `line` (which adjacent stack slot is corrupted) depends on compiler layout, not visible in the fragment; the OOB write itself is confirmed by the shown declarations.

The exact neutralization behavior of rfc1738_escape_part / rfc1738_escape_unescaped is not shown; not needed for the host-based injection (host is never escaped in the HTTP branch) but limits claims about other fields.
atoi on arbitrarily long numeric tokens (lines 271, 273, 297) may invoke undefined behavior on overflow, but no security-relevant sink consumes the wrapped value, so it is not a finding.

xstrdup and other Squid allocation results are not NULL-checked; if allocation failure were non-fatal, escaped_selector could be NULL, but the fragment shows a fatal-allocator convention and no failure-state consumer, so this is a limitation.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable within the shown fragment. The only incident-shaped pattern is that the unconstrained int parameter `size` (residual range INT_MIN..INT_MAX, no constraint visible on any line) is forwarded unchanged to the length parameters of `nc->info->receive(nc, buf, size)` (line 8) and `qemu_send_packet(nc, buf, size)` (line 10). Because the shown code performs no derivation on `size` (thin-wrapper carve-out) and the callee behavior plus `buf`'s capacity are outside the fragment, an OOB read cannot be confirmed. Other out-of-scope concerns (short-buffer read inside `inc_tx_bcast_or_mcast_count`, unchecked `nc`, discarded send return status) are recorded in limitations.

assumptions: `PTCregs` is declared `static const int PTCregs[6]` at line 3; all six entries (PTC64..PTC1522) are compile-time constants, so no input-derived value is stored in or indexed through the table in the shown code.
`qemu_get_queue(s->nic)`'s result (line 6) is framework-provided and treated as non-NULL because the fragment neither marks it nullable nor checks it (framework-data rule).
The fragment shows no return statement, so no return status is produced; the only status-like values are the discarded returns of the calls at lines 8 and 10.

verdict.summary: parseDragons never validates that the int offset `off` (or its derived value `off-8`) is non-negative. L4 only rejects `off >= size`, so negative offsets are admitted; they are passed as the address argument to r_buf_read_at at L18 and L55, which consumes the argument as a byte index into buf. With buf_size=35, off=3 and file bytes that fail both magic memcmp checks, L55 reads 32 bytes at offset -5, i.e. 5 bytes before the buffer's valid region; with off=-1, L18 reads 1 byte before it. The `available != size` checks (L19/L56) only absorb failures the callee reports, so a read that proceeds yields an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

Witness: buf_size=35, off=3 passes L4 (3<35), L8, L11 (size=32>=32) and L19 (L18 reads 32 bytes from [3,35) into b=malloc(32) at L14); attacker-chosen file bytes make both memcmp checks (L47, L50) fail, so L53 is taken. L55 then derives address off-8=-5 and passes it to r_buf_read_at, a helper whose first parameter is by name/use an index consumed as a byte offset; the requested region [-5,27) is 5 bytes outside [0,35). L56 catches the failure only if the callee reports a short count; a callee that performs the read returns 32==size and the OOB read completes. Out-of-domain address derivation at the call site: CWE-125 OOB read.

evidence.snippet: int available = r_buf_read_at (buf, off, b, size);
evidence.reason: After L4, off retains the negative sub-range [INT_MIN, -1] (no shown check establishes off>=0). Witness: buf_size=31, off=-1 passes L4 (-1<31); L7 computes size=31-(-1)=32, growing past buf_size; L8/L11 pass; b=malloc(32) at L14. L18 passes address -1 and length 32 to r_buf_read_at, whose offset parameter is consumed as a byte index into buf; the region [-1,31) exceeds the valid [0,31) by 1 byte. The length equals b's L14 capacity, so b is not overrun; the excess is in the source-address domain. L19 only converts the failure to NULL if the callee bounds-checks and reports it; otherwise the OOB read occurs: CWE-125.

assumptions: r_buf_size returns the buffer length and is non-negative on the continuing path; the fragment's own arithmetic (`size -= off`, `if (size < 32)`) treats it that way.
r_buf_read_at(buf, addr, dst, len) consumes `addr` as a byte offset/index into buf and `len` as a byte count; its body is not shown.
Valid byte offsets into buf are [0, r_buf_size(buf)); negative offsets are out of domain.
The D macro block and #if 0 region do not affect reachability; with size>=32 (L11), the b+8/b+12 accesses are in-bounds.
limitations: Whether the OOB read physically occurs depends on r_buf_read_at's negative-offset handling, which is not shown; if it strictly bounds-checks and reports a short count, L19/L56 convert the case to a benign NULL return. Confidence therefore capped below 0.8.

`off + 16` at L72 can overflow (signed-overflow UB) when off is near INT_MAX (requires buf_size > INT_MAX since L4 admits off < size) and would pass a wrapped negative offset to r_coresym_cache_element_new, whose body is not shown.

If r_buf_read_at's length parameter is a 32-bit int, `size` (st64) truncates for size > INT_MAX; any resulting error/short count still compares unequal to size via integer promotion (L19/L56), so no success-on-failure was confirmed.
Memory leak: `b` is not freed on the failure paths at L21 and L58; treated as a single-shot leak because no caller loop/volume is visible in the fragment.
eprintf calls pass `int off` to %x (L2/L63/L66/L69), a format-argument signedness mismatch with no attacker-controlled format string.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable from the fragment. The loop's only progress is p += len (line 132) with len from enclen(reg->enc, p) (line 32) and no shown check on len, but the standard char-length contract supplies len >= 1, so non-termination has no in-fragment witness. fold_len (lines 62-63) is consumed against buf whose declared capacity (line 11) is the same named maximum the callee is defined to honor. n is bounded by the items array declaration (line 10) and alt_num *= (n+1) (line 94) is capped by the break at line 95 (factors >= 2, so at most 4 expansions before break). All allocation and status returns are checked (lines 27, 39-42, 46, 48-51, 74-76, 80-84, 88, 98-102, 106, 112-115, 122-125, 139, 143-147, 154-157), empty input is rejected at line 18, and simulated ownership paths (split at lines 70-84, error frees at 40/74/100/113/123/145/155) free each node exactly once. Encoding-specific OOB reads/writes and alt-expansion bugs would occur inside callees whose bodies are not shown.

assumptions: Capacity of items is its declaration at line 10: OnigCaseFoldCodeItem items[ONIGENC_GET_CASE_FOLD_CODES_MAX_NUM]; the fill-array API ONIGENC_GET_CASE_FOLD_CODES_BY_STR (lines 25-26) returns a count n at most that large by name-implied contract.
Capacity of buf is its declaration at line 11: UChar buf[ONIGENC_MBC_CASE_FOLD_MAXLEN]; ONIGENC_MBC_CASE_FOLD (lines 62-63) writes at most that many bytes by name-implied contract.
Non-empty input minimum is established in-fragment: line 18 (start >= end) return 0, so the loop at line 24 always runs with at least one byte.
enclen (line 32) returns the byte length of the character at p; the standard contract is len >= 1, but this minimum is not stated in the fragment.
onig_node_new_str / onig_node_list_add return NULL only on allocation failure, and every return site is NULL-checked in the fragment.
limitations: CWE-835 loop non-termination if enclen returned 0 would be a finding, but a witness requires an unshown callee to violate its char-length contract; no in-fragment statement bounds len (line 32) either way.
CWE-125 OOB read for a truncated multibyte tail would occur inside enclen (line 32), which receives no end pointer; the encoding family and callee body are not shown, so it is unconfirmable.

CWE-787 overflow of buf would require fold_len > ONIGENC_MBC_CASE_FOLD_MAXLEN, which the callee contract (and the identical named constant in the declaration at line 11) excludes; the signed int ops on fold_len/len could in principle go negative, but no shown derivation produces a negative length for admitted input.

CWE-190 in alt_num *= (n + 1) (line 94): n is bounded by the items array capacity (line 10) and the break at line 95 keeps alt_num <= 8 before each multiply; no witness reaches INT_MAX, though the constant values are not visible in the fragment.

Semantic-only risks: a char whose enclen length overshoots the remaining bytes (e.g., multibyte encodings at the tail) skips trailing bytes of the compiled regex, and a 0-length fold would drop a character; both are correctness issues with no memory-safety consequence demonstrable inside the fragment.

Any heap overflow / use-after-free in expand_case_fold_string_alt (line 105), expand_case_fold_make_rem_string (line 138), or the ONIGENC_* helpers is outside the fragment; the arguments passed (n, items, p, len, end) are in-domain by the contracts cited above.
OOM-triggered paths are single-shot and each error path frees only nodes not yet attached to root; no attacker-directed double-free or NULL deref is derivable from the shown code.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the fragment. The suspicious mismatch between the NFT_OFFLOAD_F_ACTION count used for nft_flow_rule_alloc(num_actions) at line 20 and the per-expression offload calls at line 39 cannot be confirmed as an out-of-bounds write: the capacity of flow's action storage is not visible in the fragment, and whether offload callbacks append actions matching the counted set is callee-side behavior that the shown code neither states nor checks.

assumptions: kzalloc (line 26) returns zero-initialized memory, so ctx->dep.l3num (line 47) is initialized to 0 even if no offload callback sets it; this is the API contract named by the call itself.
kfree(ctx) at line 53 is reached with ctx == NULL on the line 27-29 path; kfree(NULL) being a no-op is the kernel API contract named by the call.
ERR_PTR (lines 18, 22, 56) converts a negative/0 error code into an error pointer per its name; no dereference of these values occurs in the fragment.
The guard at lines 17-18 admits num_actions in [1, INT_MAX] for the allocation at line 20; no upper bound on num_actions is derivable from the shown code.
limitations: Action-array out-of-bounds write (potential CWE-787) via nft_flow_rule_alloc(num_actions) at line 20 vs. per-expression expr->ops->offload(ctx, flow, expr) at line 39 is unconfirmed: the capacity of flow's action storage is not identifiable in the fragment (allocation body/size arithmetic not shown), and a violation requires an offload callback to append an action for an expression not flagged NFT_OFFLOAD_F_ACTION at line 11, which is a callee-side behavior absent from the fragment. No concrete witness or excess count can be simulated.

Unbounded-allocation / resource exhaustion claim on nft_flow_rule_alloc(num_actions) at line 20: the fragment derives no cap on the rule's expression count or on num_actions; any bound exists only outside the fragment.
Discarded return of nft_flow_rule_transfer_vlan(ctx, flow) at line 45: its return type/status is not shown, so a success-after-failure or status-handling flaw cannot be established.

Loop termination of the passes at lines 9-15 and 34-44 depends on the unshown nft_expr_more/nft_expr_next contract; non-termination or an overrun on attacker-chosen input cannot be derived from the fragment.
NULL expr or expr->ops (dereferenced at lines 11, 35, 39) cannot be produced by any shown path; any guarantee is a helper/rule invariant outside the fragment.
Integer overflow of num_actions (line 12) requires more than INT_MAX expressions in a rule; no shown statement makes that reachable.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the shown fragment. All strlcat() writes into mountent.mnt_opts are exactly bounded: the buffer is allocated as calloc(MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN, 1) (line 77) and every strlcat passes the identical constant as its size argument (lines 80, 82, 85, 87, 89, 91, 93, 95-97), so no admitted flags/mount_user value can write out of bounds. Error paths for setreuid, sigfillset, sigprocmask, capability raise, lock, setmntent, fileno, fstat, addmntent, and endmntent are handled. Remaining concerns (unchecked calloc failure passing NULL mnt_opts to addmntent, unproven mtab injection via getusername's return, and unshown addmntent escaping) depend on unshown callee behavior or unshown provenance and are recorded as limitations, not findings.

assumptions: MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN (lines 77, 80, 82, 85, 87, 89, 91, 93, 95, 96) is a single named constant, so the calloc byte count equals every strlcat size argument; the capacity of mnt_opts is therefore exactly the strlcat size. Its numeric value is not shown and is not needed.
devname, mountpoint, and fstype are NUL-terminated C strings by convention (stored at lines 74-76 and consumed by addmntent at line 102); the fragment derives no length from them.
getusername (line 13) returns either NULL or a NUL-terminated string, matching its only shown use under the guard at line 94.
addmntent (line 102) consumes the mntent record's string fields per its standard semantics; its internal escaping and NULL-field handling are not visible in the fragment.
MOUNTED (line 49) and the MS_* option masks are named constants whose values are not shown; no boundary claim depends on their values.
limitations: Unchecked allocation: if calloc(MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN, 1) (line 77) returns NULL, the guard at line 78 skips only the strlcat appends and addmntent(pmntfile, &mountent) (line 102) is still called with mountent.mnt_opts == NULL. Whether that dereferences (CWE-476) or prints a placeholder depends on unshown libc behavior; the failure is not attacker-directed, so this is an unchecked-allocation robustness concern, not a confirmed finding.

Potential mtab record/option injection via mount_user: line 94 admits any non-NULL string and lines 95-97 append it unescaped before addmntent writes the record (line 102). Attacker control of getusername's return value is not visible in the fragment (internal-helper provenance), and addmntent's escaping behavior is unshown, so neither taint nor neutralization can be confirmed.
devname/mountpoint/fstype are checked for nothing before addmntent (lines 74-76, 102); consequence of NULL or non-terminated values depends on unshown callee behavior.

Discarded statuses: toggle_dac_capability(1, 0) (line 116), sigprocmask restore (line 117), and unlock_mtab (line 113) return values are ignored; no shown security-relevant operation consumes their failure state, and the process already runs with real==effective uid.

atexit(unlock_mtab) (line 41) remains registered on lock_mtab failure (lines 43-47) where unlock_mtab is also called (line 52/60/69), so a later process exit may unlock an unheld lock; no security impact is shown.
No loop structures exist in the fragment, so loop iteration-bound, parser-position, and sentinel-overrun analyses are vacuous.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the shown fragment. The allocation-size computation at line 7 derives from smap->map.value_size and smap->map.max_entries, but the fragment shows no declaration of those fields' types, no value of sizeof(struct stack_map_bucket), and no caller-side bound; a u64 multiplication wrap (and any undersized-allocation overflow in pcpu_freelist_populate) cannot be demonstrated with the shown code's own types, so the overflow candidate is unconfirmable rather than confirmed. Both return statuses are properly checked (lines 9, 13) and propagated (lines 10, 22).

assumptions: elem_size is declared u64 at line 3, so the addition on lines 3-4 is performed in u64, and the explicit (u64) cast on smap->map.value_size implies a narrower integer field, though its exact width is not visible in the fragment.

The only allocation-capacity quantity computable in the fragment is symbolic: with value_size=0 and max_entries=1 the allocated size equals sizeof(struct stack_map_bucket); all larger claims require field types and sizeof values absent from the fragment.
limitations: Integer wrap of `elem_size * smap->map.max_entries` at line 7 (potential CWE-190/CWE-195) is unconfirmable: the declared types of smap->map.value_size and smap->map.max_entries, the value of sizeof(struct stack_map_bucket), and any caller-side validation are not visible, so no concrete overflow witness can be expressed in the shown code, and the wrap's downstream consumer (pcpu_freelist_populate at line 16) is an unshown callee.
The free_elems path at line 21 frees smap->elems once within this fragment; a double-free or use-after-free would require the caller's error handling or a later reuse, none of which is shown.
A NULL smap dereference at line 4 is not producible within the fragment; it would require an out-of-scope caller to pass NULL with no shown contract marking it nullable.
The bpf_map_area_alloc signature (notably size_t narrowing of the u64 size) is not visible, so a truncation-on-32-bit claim is not grounded in the shown code.
The safe verdict rests on the unconfirmability of the suspected overflow rather than on a located protective check; a caller-side bound on value_size/max_entries could exist outside the fragment.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read in the GUI scrollbar-event loops of check_termcode: the loop headers at lines 479-480 and 508-509 evaluate tp[j], tp[j+1], tp[j+2] with j advanced only inside the body (482/490/495 and 511/516) and never bounded against len (line 54) or the buffer capacity bufsize (line 4); the only terminator is a NUL byte, which the fragment never guarantees for a caller-supplied buf. An adversarial input that matches the KS_VER_SCROLLBAR/KS_HOR_SCROLLBAR key name (e.g., via the GUI CSI two-byte path at lines 95-102) and repeats a nonzero event pattern drives j past the end of buf, causing an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), e.g., with *buflen == bufsize == 8 the second header evaluation reads buf[8..10].

evidence.snippet:
for (i = 0; tp[j] == CSI && tp[j + 1] == KS_VER_SCROLLBAR
						     && tp[j + 2] != NUL; ++i)
evidence.reason: Sink is the loop-condition read itself. j is derived in the shown code (line 478 j=0; lines 482/490/495 j += 3 + num_bytes + num_bytes) and is NOT bounded by len (lines 47/54) or by the buffer capacity bufsize (declared line 4) before tp[j+1]/tp[j+2] are read; the only shown terminator is a NUL byte and the fragment never establishes a NUL terminator for the buf!=NULL path (lines 49-55). Attacker-controlled buffer contents (Phase-1 entry-point input) matching KS_VER_SCROLLBAR (admitted by every guard on the path: line 61 CSI!=K_SPECIAL, line 75 termleader filter, line 82 not-ESC, line 270/340 key_name!=NUL, line 350/377/424/444 not KS_EXTRA/mouse/menu/tabline, line 471 key_name==KS_VER_SCROLLBAR) with *buflen==bufsize==8 and all-nonzero bytes yields j=8 after one event, and the second header evaluation reads tp[8]/tp[9]/tp[10], i.e. index >= capacity 8 -> out-of-bounds read (CWE-125, excess >= 1 byte).

evidence.snippet:
for (i = 0; tp[j] == CSI && tp[j + 1] == KS_HOR_SCROLLBAR
						     && tp[j + 2] != NUL; ++i)
evidence.reason: Identical unbounded-index read for the horizontal-scrollbar loop: j (initialized line 507, advanced lines 511/516) is never checked against len (line 54) or bufsize (line 4) before tp[j+1]/tp[j+2] are read. A caller-supplied buffer (buf != NULL) of bufsize==*buflen==7 with the pattern {CSI, KS_HOR_SCROLLBAR, 0x01, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04} completes one event (j=7), and the following header evaluation reads tp[7] (index == capacity 7) -> one-byte out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

assumptions: The fragment is compiled with FEAT_GUI defined and USE_ON_FLY_SCROLL undefined so lines 471-521 are active (the #ifdef guards at lines 470/522 are visible in the fragment).

key_name[0] can equal KS_VER_SCROLLBAR/KS_HOR_SCROLLBAR for attacker-chosen input: either via the GUI CSI two-byte path (gui.in_use true, lines 95-102, key_name[0]=tp[1]) or via a termcodes[] entry whose name[0] is the constant (table contents not shown).
The first byte (CSI) is present in the gathered termleader so the filter at lines 72-76 does not continue; gather_termleader() (lines 30-31) gathers from the termcodes table (contents not shown).

For the buf != NULL path, *buflen <= bufsize and buf is a readable array of bufsize bytes, consistent with bufsize being forwarded as the buffer capacity to put_string_in_typebuf (lines 593-594) and handle_csi (lines 306-307).
get_bytes_from_buf/get_long_from_buf (lines 483, 491, 512) return positive byte counts (1 and 4) for well-formed event bytes so j advances instead of breaking at lines 484-485/492-493/513-514.

Per-iteration num_bytes values come from callees whose bodies are not shown; the witness is therefore a residual-range account (j unbounded by any shown guard) rather than a fully byte-exact simulation, capping confidence at 0.6.
limitations: OSC/DCS argp boundary: with len == 2 and 'ESC ]'/'ESC P', argp = tp + 2 == tp + len (one-past the valid window, lines 282, 320-326, 330-336); whether handle_osc/handle_dcs dereference *argp and whether tp+2 exceeds an identifiable allocation cannot be confirmed (callee bodies and allocation capacity not shown).

GUI mouse coordinates: get_bytes_from_buf(tp + slen, bytes, 4) at line 361 is reached with only len >= 3 guaranteed (lines 97-98); the callee contract and the underlying allocation size are unidentifiable from the fragment.

Writes into string[] at lines 578 and 589-591: capacity is MAX_KEY_CODE_LEN + 1 (line 19) but the constant's value is not shown, and new_slen originates from modifiers2keycode (line 567, body unshown); overflow not confirmable.

current_menu = (vimmenu_T *)val (line 431) casts buffer bytes to a pointer; the later dereference semantics are inside check_menu_pointer (line 436, unshown) and events are GUI-sourced, so no memory-safety verdict is made.

Stale slen after a mid-loop callee failure in the scrollbar branch (slen assigned only at lines 496/517 after all reads succeed, while breaks occur at 484-485/492-493/513-514) is a logic inconsistency whose effect lies inside put_string_in_typebuf (unshown).

For the typebuf path (buf == NULL, lines 42-48), the capacity of typebuf.tb_buf is not declared in the fragment, so no boundary claim is made there; the OOB finding is grounded on the buf != NULL path where bufsize (line 4) is the declared capacity.

Reachability of the KS_VER_SCROLLBAR/KS_HOR_SCROLLBAR branches depends on termcodes[]/termleader content and on gui.in_use, which are not shown; the witness uses the fully-shown GUI CSI path (lines 95-102) with gui.in_use assumed true, so exploitability is configuration-dependent.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the fragment. Directory-path construction is bounded: snprintf at line 42 passes sizeof(mfn) as the size argument for the line-34 MAXPATHLEN buffer, and the estrndup copy length at line 64 is capped at sizeof(mfn)-1 for the entire admitted mflen range [0, INT_MAX]. The realloc-growth arithmetic (maxfiles = (maxfiles+1)*2; mlen = maxfiles*sizeof(*filearr)) only wraps at a physically unconstructible iteration count (>=2^30..2^61 directory entries), and the remaining candidates (mset[j].me[i].mp deref, set_text_binary loop progress, uint32_t/size_t index mismatch) depend on callees or volumes not visible/feasible within the shown code.

limitations: Integer overflow in maxfiles/mlen (lines 54-55) would need >= 2^30 (32-bit) to 2^61 (64-bit) regular directory entries in one directory to wrap size_t before the erealloc at line 57; no concrete witness is constructible, so the heap-OOB-write candidate at line 64 is demoted with no CWE.

Potential NULL dereference of mset[j].me[i].mp at line 81 cannot be confirmed: me/count/mp are produced by load_1 (lines 69, 74) whose body is not shown; no NULL-capable producer is visible in the fragment.
Possible non-termination of the loop at lines 80-86 depends on set_text_binary (line 85) returning an unchanged index, which is unconfirmable from the shown code.

Early goto-out paths (lines 39, 47, 61) leak filearr and its strings once; single-shot leaks with no attacker-controlled volume compounding are not reported as findings.

TOCTOU between stat (line 32) and opendir (line 36) on fn is not treated as a finding: fn is the caller-selected magic path and no attacker model for a competing change is derivable from the fragment.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable within the shown fragment. The objects whose capacities are declared here, the local `buffer` (line 5: `char buffer[sizeof(struct squashfs_dir_entry) + SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1]`) and the `dir->dirs` array grown by realloc (lines 89-96), are kept in-bounds by shown guards: line 71 admits `dire->size` in [0, SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN-1] so the memcpy/NUL at lines 76-78 fit exactly, and the realloc pattern keeps every store index below capacity. The prominent candidate, reads at `directory_table + bytes` (lines 52, 66, 76) that can advance far past the logical `size` bound, cannot be confirmed as an out-of-bounds access because `directory_table`'s allocation/capacity is not declared anywhere in the fragment; it is recorded as a limitation along with the other ungroundable candidates.

assumptions: `buffer` at lines 5-6 is sized `sizeof(struct squashfs_dir_entry) + SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1`, and `dire->name` (line 7) is treated as the trailing member at byte offset `sizeof(struct squashfs_dir_entry)` with capacity `SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1`.
The guard at line 71 uses the same identifier `SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN` as the capacity expression at line 5, so both refer to the same value.

`DIR_ENT_SIZE` is a positive constant, so the realloc pattern at lines 89-96 (`dir->dir_count % DIR_ENT_SIZE == 0` → allocate `dir->dir_count + DIR_ENT_SIZE` elements) always leaves the next store index, `dir->dir_count`, below the allocated element count.
`lookup_entry`'s `-1` sentinel is fully handled at lines 44-46 (EXIT_UNSQUASH).
limitations: Out-of-bounds read candidate on `directory_table` (sinks at lines 52, 66, 76): `bytes` can exceed the logical bound `size` (line 49) because the inner loop (line 65) is never checked against remaining data; simulation: with `bytes = 100`, `(*i)->data = 10` (size = 107), `dirh.count = 255` (dir_count = 256, admitted by line 60) and all entry sizes 0, the 256 iterations advance `bytes` to 1128 and read source offsets 104..1127, far past `size`. Whether any of these is an actual out-of-bounds access cannot be determined because `directory_table`'s allocation/capacity is not declared in the fragment (both the dangerous and the safe verdict are unprovable).

Negative non-`-1` returns from `lookup_entry` (admitted by lines 44-46 as written) would flow through `bytes += (*i)->offset` (line 48) into `directory_table + bytes`; `lookup_entry`'s return domain and `directory_table`'s base/capacity are outside the fragment.
