verdict.summary: File-controlled width/height reach size = bytes_per_line * hh (line 87), whose 32-bit int product overflows for admitted values (e.g. #define width -8 and #define height 5 make size = -1610612736). At line 88 the negative int sign-extends into a ~2^64-byte g_malloc request; GLib g_malloc aborts the process on allocation failure, giving a tiny-file denial of service. The fill loops themselves are write-bounded (<= size bytes) and cannot overflow the allocation.

evidence.reason: Allocation-size sink: size derives solely from attacker-controlled ww/hh (sscanf %d at line 33 into value, assigned at lines 41/43; only guard is !ww||!hh at line 77, excluding 0), via bytes_per_line = (ww+7)/8 + padding (line 85) and size = bytes_per_line * hh (line 87). For the admitted witness ww=0xFFFFFFF8 (from '#define width -8'), hh=5, version10p=1: padding=1, bytes_per_line=536870912, product=2684354560 fits in 32-bit unsigned but exceeds INT_MAX, so size becomes -1610612736 (CWE-190 overflow in the size computation). g_malloc converts this negative int to gsize by sign-extension to 0xFFFFFFFFA0000000 (~1.845e19 bytes), an unsatisfiable allocation; GLib g_malloc terminates the process on failure. The witness passes every guard on the path (lines 31, 33, 40, 42, 56, 74, 77, 80).

assumptions: guint/int are 32-bit and gsize is 64-bit (standard GLib types), so int->gsize sign-extension of the negative size yields a ~2^64 request; on a 32-bit platform the request is 2.5 GiB and fails for the same reason.

GLib g_malloc returns NULL only for a 0 request and terminates the program on allocation failure; the shown if (!bits) at line 114 therefore corresponds only to the size-0 case and does not mitigate the huge-size path.

char line[MAX_SIZE] / char name_and_type[MAX_SIZE] (lines 9, 11) are the only array capacities in the fragment; the line-31 strlen guard leaves processed lines at most MAX_SIZE-2 chars, so %s tokens (lines 33, 56-64) never reach name_and_type's capacity.
bytes_per_line is always even for guard-admitted ww (padding+floor((ww+7)/8) parity), so size is even and the line-94 loop writes at most size bytes; the line-105 loop writes exactly size bytes.
limitations: A classic 'undersized allocation + heap overflow' is not confirmable in this fragment: both fill loops are bounded by size and write <= size bytes into the g_malloc(size) buffer (parity argument above), so no in-fragment OOB write is demonstrated.

When size wraps to 0/small-positive or negative and the fill loops are skipped, the fragment still returns bits with full ww/hh (lines 117-119), but the resulting uninitialized-data / caller-side OOB read occurs in an unshown caller and is out of scope.
The hotspot parsing (lines 44-52) performs type-- before the buffer start only in cases that hit continue before any dereference; no out-of-bounds read is reachable with the shown guards.

No computational, injection, crypto, or file/access-control vulnerability exists in this fragment beyond the confirmed allocation-size overflow; all sscanf formats are literals and next_int results are checked before use.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable from the fragment alone. Multiple suspects (1-byte label off-by-one where guard at line 22 admits label_length == entry_length while 1 + label_length bytes must fit in entry_length; unconstrained helper-return label_length reaching malloc/strncpy at lines 33/38; discarded setpos/seek statuses at lines 8/42; ungrounded index uses of idxt.offsets and indx->entries) each fail the three-part confirmation because the fragment shows neither the physical capacity of buf->data/offsets/entries nor the write/return contracts of the unseen label- and buffer-helper functions. All legitimately id'd in-bounds paths (ptagx vs tags_count allocation, tagvalues vs INDX_TAGVALUES_MAX, loop termination) are correct in the shown code.

assumptions: Size-t arithmetic is modulo 2^64 (size_t); uint8_t read at line 21 yields 0..255; uint32_t fields are 0..2^32-1.
buf->maxlen is the authoritative end of the readable buffer region as the fragment uses it at lines 15, 16, 20, 145.
The fragment's derived sub-capacity is the region [buf->offset, buf->offset + entry_length) created at line 20.
char text[INDX_LABEL_SIZEMAX] (line 26) and uint32_t tagvalues[INDX_TAGVALUES_MAX] (line 108) are fixed-size arrays whose capacities are the shown named constants.
limitations: Potential OOB read of idxt.offsets[curr_number + 1] (line 7): no declaration of the offsets array capacity exists in the fragment, and curr_number is unbounded there, so the excess cannot be quantified.

Potential OOB access to indx->entries[entry_number] (lines 33, 38, 43-44, 97, 127, 133, 137-139): guarded only against total_entries_count (line 10), not against a declared array capacity, which the fragment does not show.

One-byte label off-by-one: the line-22 guard 'label_length > entry_length' admits equality, yet 1 (length field, line 21) + label_length data bytes exceeds the entry_length-byte region, leaving buf->offset at or past the line-20 maxlen when the unseen label helpers consume their length argument; control_bytes[0] at line 66 then reads past the fragment-derived sub-capacity. Not confirmed as a physical OOB read because the size of the buf->data allocation and the helpers' exact boundary behavior are not shown.

label_length is reassigned at lines 29/31 from helper returns that the fragment never constrains; if either helper returns a length >= INDX_LABEL_SIZEMAX, strncpy at line 38 reads past text[INDX_LABEL_SIZEMAX] (and the helper would have overflowed text). Depends on callee semantics and the unshown numeric value of INDX_LABEL_SIZEMAX.

Return values of mobi_buffer_setpos (line 8) and mobi_buffer_seek (line 42) are discarded; on failure the parse continues with a stale buf->offset, producing corrupted entries only, since subsequent reads remain bounded by a maxlen no larger than the original.
ordt->ordt2 dereference at line 28 has no NULL guard; a NULL ordt can only be supplied by the caller (out-of-scope premise).
tagx->tags[i] accesses (lines 61, 66, 72, 74, 82, 89, 90) and malloc(tagx->tags_count * ...) (lines 52, 97) assume tags_count equals the tags array length, which is not shown.
(int) tagx->control_byte_count (line 42) is a narrowing cast whose source type is not shown, so a negative/implementation-defined seek value cannot be grounded.
buf->maxlen is not restored on the early returns at lines 24, 36, 55, 101, 131; this only narrows the buffer for subsequent use (no overflow derivable), a state-consistency flaw only.

entry_number = curr_number + entry_offset (line 9) can wrap, but any wrapped value still passes through the line-10 guard before use, so no out-of-domain index is derivable without the unseen entries capacity.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable within the fragment. The buffer operations at lines 57, 58, 61, 67, 72-73 are safe only under an unshown caller contract: the fragment declares no minimum for p->size and no capacity/extent for rp, so the negative-offset access (rp + n - 4) reachable when p->size < 4 at line 57 cannot be confirmed as an out-of-bounds write, and no protective statement exists that would make it safe either. The assert(q2 < 2) at line 42 has no constructed input making q2 >= 2 through the shown arithmetic. All candidates are recorded in limitations without CWE.

assumptions: p->m is treated as having at least 2 readable limbs because mpn_submul_1/cnd_add_n are invoked with count 2 (lines 57, 67) and the comment at lines 54-55 describes multiplication by the two low limbs of p; this is not a declared size.
mp_limb_t is assumed to be at least 64 bits wide, consistent with the 32-bit shifts and 0xffffffff masks used at lines 29, 31, 36, 38, 59, 70; the width is not declared in the fragment.

The constants rp[2] and rp[3] at lines 72-73 and the 4-limb diagram at lines 44-52 suggest the intended configuration is p->size = 4 with a working buffer of at least 2*p->size limbs, but the fragment does not establish this.
limitations: Out-of-bounds write candidate (CWE-787): at the last loop iteration n = p->size (line 11 admits it), lines 57 and 67 address rp + n - 4, which for p->size < 4 is a negative offset (e.g., p->size = 2 gives rp - 2 at line 57); the witness passes the shown loop guard, but rp's capacity/extent is not declared or derivable in the fragment and no shown statement establishes a minimum for p->size, so the claim is unconfirmable per the missing-capacity rule.

Reachable abort candidate (CWE-617) at assert (q2 < 2) (line 42): q2 is a deterministic function of rp contents via lines 27-40; no concrete value sequence shown in the fragment produces q2 >= 2, so no witness exists.

Signed-overflow / negative-derivation candidates: n = 2*p->size (line 6) can overflow or go negative for extreme/degenerate p->size, and lines 7-8 would then read negative indices; no security-relevant bound or capacity is shown to measure the effect, so this stays unconfirmed.

Uninitialized use candidate (CWE-457): if p->size <= 0, the loop body never runs and u0/u1 are written to rp[2]/rp[3] (lines 72-73) without being set; the degenerate caller value is not excluded by the fragment, but no capacity or caller provenance is shown, so it is not a confirmed finding.

Cross-configuration concern: u1 << 32 (lines 29, 36) is undefined for 32-bit mp_limb_t; the fragment implies a 64-bit limb but does not declare it, so this is a robustness note, not a confirmed vulnerability.

verdict.summary: In kssl_keytab_is_available, a KRB5_KT_NOTFOUND return from krb5_kt_get_entry (lines 37-41) is converted into the success value rc=1 (lines 42-44) and returned to the caller via return(rc) (line 55), so the availability check reports the Kerberos keytab as available when the looked-up host-key entry is absent — an improper check/handling of an exceptional condition (CWE-754).

evidence.reason: krb5rc from krb5_kt_get_entry (lines 37-41) retains the full krb5_error_code domain; the branch at line 42 admits exactly KRB5_KT_NOTFOUND (a nonzero error code meaning the keytab holds no matching entry), and line 43 converts that failure into the success value rc=1, which then reaches return(rc) at line 55 — returning success after the lookup failed. Witness (all prior guards, lines 10/25/35, are excluded with return 0; line 42 admitted): keytab_file=NULL, service_name=NULL, default keytab resolves, krb5_kt_get_entry returns KRB5_KT_NOTFOUND. The fragment contains no statement establishing that a keytab entry always exists, so NOTFOUND is producible by the shown flow. Primary mechanism: improper check of an exceptional condition treated as success (CWE-754).

This is the sink that publishes the corrupted status: on the line 42-44 path, rc was set to 1 after krb5_kt_get_entry reported KRB5_KT_NOTFOUND, so the accessibility probe returns a false 'available' signal for the absent entry, delivering the CWE-754 status-handling flaw to the caller.

assumptions: krb5 library contract implied by the shown usage: krb5_kt_get_entry populates `entry` only on success (return 0), so krb5_kt_free_entry at line 48 is reached only for the success case; krb5_kt_resolve/krb5_kt_default set `krb5keytab` only on success, making the single krb5_kt_close at line 52 correct on every path.

KRB5_KT_NOTFOUND (special-cased at line 42) is a nonzero krb5 error code for 'no matching keytab entry'; the fragment's dedicated branch and the line 29 comment ('the host key we are looking for') show it is treated as a distinct, expected outcome of the entry probe.
No buffer or array capacity is declared anywhere in the fragment; byte-level capacity claims are not derivable by construction.
limitations: kssl_ctx may be NULL at the line 15 dereference, but the fragment contains no producer of NULL; the value is caller-supplied, so CWE-476 is not confirmed.

Content, length, and NUL-termination of kssl_ctx->keytab_file and kssl_ctx->service_name are not established in the fragment; any over-read inside krb5_kt_resolve or krb5_sname_to_principal would depend on library buffer contracts not shown.

The line 42-44 behavior can alternatively be read as intentionally reporting 'keytab mechanism reachable' (NOTFOUND included in the success set); the caller's interpretation of the return value is not visible in the fragment, which caps confidence at 0.65 and severity at low.
Return values of cleanup calls (lines 48, 52, 53, 54) are ignored, but no security-relevant operation runs on their failure states, so they are not findings.
No memory-safety claim is confirmable: there are no arrays, allocations, indices, or pointer arithmetic in the fragment whose capacities could be quoted.

verdict.summary: No confirmed exploitable vulnerability within the shown fragment. All attacker-derived sizes that reach memory sinks are bounded by visible guards and capacities: width>0 (L331-332), height!=0 (L333-334), bpp whitelist {1,4,8,16,24,32} (L337-340), compression/bpp pairing (L344-349), colormap capacity 4*colors (L412-413) >= read size packet_size*colors (L426), and pixel capacity rows*max(bytes_per_line, columns+256) (L462-463) >= ReadBlob length (L456/470). On the declared 64-bit size_t arithmetic, rows*bpl <= 2^64-2^33 does not wrap. Residual concerns (32-bit size_t overflow; attacker-mask shift-count UB at mask<<32) are recorded in limitations because the platform width and callee behavior needed for a witness are not derivable from the fragment.

assumptions: pixels capacity is rows*MagickMax(bytes_per_line, image->columns+256UL) bytes per the allocation at L462-463 (and L483-484), and max(bpl, cols+256) >= bpl by construction, so ReadBlob(image,length,pixels) at L470 never writes past capacity because length = bpl*rows (L456).

bmp_colormap capacity is 4*image->colors bytes (L412-413) and colors <= 2^bits_per_pixel <= 256 for bpp<16 (L341-343, L378-382), so ReadBlob(packet_size*colors) at L426 and the fill loop L434-441 stay in bounds.
DecodeImage's destination size is its 4th argument image->columns*image->rows (L488-489), matching the per-row column reads in case 8 (L708-724) and the allocation (L483-484).

QueueAuthenticPixels returns a row of image->columns writable pixels or NULL (NULL is checked, L624/L667/L714/L761), and GetAuthenticIndexQueue returns a queue with at least image->columns writable entries per row.
ReadBlobLSB* return values on EOF are zeros, which the shown validations (L331-349, L447) reject on every security-relevant path.

The per-case recomputed bytes_per_line values (case 1: ceil(cols/8); case 4: ceil(cols/2); case 8: cols; case 16: 2*(cols+cols%2); case 24: 4*((24*cols+31)/32); case 32: 4*cols; alpha scan: 4*cols) are all <= max(bytes_per_line, cols+256), keeping every row pointer p=pixels+(image->rows-y-1)*bytes_per_line in bounds.
limitations: 32-bit size_t integer overflow: on a platform where size_t is 32 bits, bytes_per_line=4*((columns*bits_per_pixel+31)/32) (L455) and length=bytes_per_line*rows (L456) can wrap (e.g., columns~2^29, bpp=32) and desynchronize the allocation (L462-463) from the conversion strides recomputed in the switch (e.g., case 32 bytes_per_line=4*columns). The size_t width is not derivable from the fragment, and the witness additionally requires SetImageExtent(L390) to accept a ~2^29 x 2^31 image, so this is a platform-contingent hypothesis, not a confirmed finding (no CWE attached).

Undefined shift count: with compression=BI_BITFIELDS, bpp=32, red_mask=0x00000001, the sample loop (L579-585) reaches sample=32 and evaluates bmp_info.red_mask<<32 (shift count == width of unsigned int). The only consumer of the result is quantum_bits (L586) used for color scaling, with no memory/control-flow/authorization impact, so this is a robustness defect, not a security finding.

Allocation/DoS amplification for tiny widths (e.g., columns=1, bpp=1 doubling file-size ratio ~514x) is gated by the length/8 <= GetBlobSize check (L457), the hard ReadBlob count check (L471), and SetImageExtent behavior not shown in the fragment; bounding the amplification depends on external callee behavior, so it is not confirmed.
Unchecked AcquireImage(image_info) (L64) NULL and other allocation-failure paths have no security-relevant operation running on the failure state within the fragment.
magick[1] can be stale after a short 2-byte read (L100-102); it is only used in comparisons and the acceptance guard requires count==2 (L107), so no security impact is demonstrable.
GetBlobSize (L323/L327/L457) and SetImageExtent (L390) behavior is not shown; any verdict fully resting on their limits would be unconfirmable, which is why confidence is capped below 0.8.

The per-row index queue base (GetAuthenticIndexQueue) semantics and the identical base each row could cause a row-0 index overwrite correctness bug, but all writes stay within the indexed columns span, so no memory-safety or security impact is confirmed.

verdict.summary: In pax_decode_header, the PAX sparse-map count is decoded from attacker-controlled archive bytes by decode_num (line 42), which admits the full size_t domain [0, TYPE_MAXIMUM(size_t)], then stored as sparse_map_size (line 48) and passed unvalidated as the element count to xcalloc (lines 49-50). A header value such as 2^63 forces an out-of-domain allocation (2^63 * sizeof(struct sp_array) ~ 2^67 bytes), which fails and terminates the process, giving an attacker deterministic denial of service via a crafted archive (CWE-770).

evidence.reason: sparse_map_size is assigned from u at line 48, where decode_num at line 42 admits the entire size_t domain [0, TYPE_MAXIMUM(size_t)] for attacker-controlled PAX header text copied into nbuf; no shown statement after line 42 caps the count. A header line encoding u = TYPE_MAXIMUM(size_t) (e.g., 2^63 on 64-bit size_t) passes every guard (line 3 gate, line 42 decode) and reaches the xcalloc element-count argument at lines 49-50 with product ~2^67 bytes, which is out of domain for any real allocator; standard checked xcalloc aborts on the overflow/failure, terminating the process. This is allocation of resources without limits (CWE-770) with an exact, guard-admitted witness; the buffer capacity relevant here is the allocation itself, which is derived from input rather than a constant.

assumptions: nbuf capacity is UINTMAX_STRSIZE_BOUND as declared at line 6; the COPY_BUF guard at line 18 fires when dst == buf + UINTMAX_STRSIZE_BOUND - 1, so writes stay within indices 0..UINTMAX_STRSIZE_BOUND-2 and the NUL at line 34 lands at index <= UINTMAX_STRSIZE_BOUND-2.
decode_num returning true produces u with 0 <= u <= the passed maximum (lines 42, 57, 65); the fragment applies no other numeric constraint to u.
sizeof(struct sp_array) = 2 * sizeof(off_t); the xcalloc product (count * element size) exceeds size_t for both 32-bit and 64-bit off_t with the confirmed witness value.
limitations: find_next_block() could return NULL at end-of-archive, and lines 27-28 and 39-40 dereference its result immediately; however, the fragment shows no contract marking it nullable, so per the analysis rules the NULL-producing path is not expressible in the shown code (CWE-476 demoted).

xcalloc's exact failure behavior (abort via xalloc_die vs. NULL return) is not visible in the fragment; both outcomes still produce the confirmed DoS for the admitted count, but any further impact would depend on unshown callee internals.
dumped_size += BLOCKSIZE * (current_block_ordinal() - start) at line 76 could theoretically overflow off_t, but requires an impractically large consumed archive; not confirmable from the fragment.
sparse_add_map (line 72) is not shown; the visible loop count equals the allocated element count, so no out-of-bounds write into sparse_map is demonstrated by the fragment.

COPY_BUF is bounds-safe for nbuf: the guard at line 18 returns false rather than overrunning, and the ERROR format strings are literal with orig_file_name passed as a %s argument, so no format-string injection was found.

verdict.summary: Heap buffer overflow write in qtm_decompress: when match_offset > window_posn (window-wrap branch, entered at line 95), the match copy writes match_length bytes starting at window[window_posn] (lines 92-108) without the clamp to window_size - window_posn that the else branch applies at lines 112-113. With the window nearly full (window_posn = window_size-1, reachable at the last slot before the line 135 wrap) an attacker-chosen match (selector 6, match_length >= 5, match_offset > window_posn with j <= window_size passing line 98) writes several bytes past the qtm->window_size-byte heap window buffer, e.g., indices window_size..window_size+3 for match_length=5.

evidence.reason: CWE-787 heap OOB write. i = match_length (line 93) is unclamped in the wrap branch (match_offset > window_posn, line 95); the else branch clamps i to window_size - window_posn at lines 112-113 but this branch does not, so match_length (>= 5 via line 80, attacker-controlled sym/extra from the bitstream, no shown bound) bytes are written from window[window_posn]. window has capacity W = qtm->window_size per the fragment's own uses at lines 98, 102, 112-113, 135. Witness: window_posn = W-1, match_offset = W+1 (admitted by line 95; j = 2 at line 97 passes line 98 because 2 <= W), match_length = 5 (passes line 103 since j < i): line 108 writes indices W+1..W+3 (plus index W already written by line 105), i.e. 4 bytes past the W-byte heap buffer. The frame-alignment checks at lines 123-126 execute only after the inner loop and cannot protect the sink.

CWE-787 heap OOB write, same root cause as the primary finding. In the wrap branch the first copy run writes j bytes from window[window_posn]; j = match_offset - window_posn is only bounded by the offset check at line 98 (j <= window_size) and is not bounded by the remaining window space window_size - window_posn. For window_posn = W-1 and j >= 2 (admitted: match_offset = W+1 gives j = 2 <= W) this run already writes index W, one byte past the W-byte window whose capacity is established by lines 98, 102, 112-113, 135.

assumptions: qtm->window points to a buffer of qtm->window_size bytes; the fragment itself uses qtm->window_size as that byte capacity at lines 98, 102, 112-113, and 135.

QTM_GET_SYMBOL and QTM_READ_BITS (lines 41, 52, 58, 64-65, 71-72, 78-79, 82-83, 131) consume the attacker-supplied compressed bitstream through i_ptr/i_end (line 3); their bodies are outside the fragment.

window_posn = qtm->window_posn and frame_start = qtm->frame_start (lines 30-31) are stored decoder state; the fragment assigns frame_start = window_posn at line 147 and advances it in exact QTM_FRAME_SIZE steps (lines 123-126), so frame_start = window_size - QTM_FRAME_SIZE is an admitted value yielding frame_end = window_size at line 48.
limitations: The exact magnitudes of qtm->length_base[]/position_base[]/length_extra[]/extra_bits[] (lines 65-66, 72-73, 79-80, 83-84) are not visible, so the witness (match_length = 5, match_offset = window_size+1) is expressed via residual ranges admitted by the shown guards rather than an enumerated decoder-table value; this caps confidence at 0.7.

The else-branch copy is clamped (lines 112-113) but still advances window_posn by the full match_length at line 116; a subsequent out-of-bounds write after exact frame alignment (line 124 equality) is a same-root-cause derivation that is not independently confirmed.
If window_posn exceeds window_size, line 120 forms an out-of-bounds pointer and lines 123-126 typically error only after the write; not counted as a separate finding.
Line 46 converts out_bytes (off_t, up to OFF_MAX at line 12) into unsigned int frame_end arithmetic, which can wrap; the resulting behavioral impact is not demonstrated within the fragment.

Line 131 (do { QTM_READ_BITS(i, 8); } while (i != 0xFF);) termination and the inner decode loops depend on the unbounded/unseen macro handling of input exhaustion; non-termination and resource-exhaustion claims are unconfirmable.
i_ptr/i_end, range, symf, bits_needed, and bit_run are declared but unused in the shown code; no finding.

verdict.summary: In gst_flxdec_chain, flxfh.size is copied from the stream (line 98) and checked only against avail (lines 105, 151), with no lower bound. In the FLX_FRAME_TYPE branch, flxfh.size - FlxFrameChunkSize (lines 111-112) underflows/wraps to ~2^32 for any size < FlxFrameChunkSize (e.g., size=0), passing the admitted set and handing gst_adapter_take an out-of-domain length (~4 GB request with no data available), causing an OOB heap read, a ~4 GB allocation, or a NULL result dereferenced at line 113 (CWE-190). Independently, in the default branch a size=0 chunk makes gst_adapter_flush consume 0 bytes while avail stays >= FlxFrameChunkSize, so the loop at line 90 never terminates on attacker-chosen input (CWE-835).

evidence.reason: flxfh.size is entry-point input copied at line 98; the only shown constraint is the upper bound avail >= flxfh.size (line 105), which admits 0..avail and imposes no minimum. With flxfh.size = 0 and avail >= FlxFrameChunkSize (line 90), the guard at line 105 admits the value and 0 - FlxFrameChunkSize wraps to 0xFFFFFFFA (or -6 converted to the same huge guint), so gst_adapter_take requests ~4,294,967,290 bytes from an adapter holding 0 bytes (after the flush at line 109), i.e., an out-of-domain length for the take's 'nbytes <= available' contract, causing an OOB heap read / huge allocation / NULL result dereferenced at line 113. Primary CWE-190 (integer wraparound corrupting a length argument).

With an admitted chunk (id != FLX_FRAME_TYPE, flxfh.size = 0, avail >= FlxFrameChunkSize), the guard at line 151 admits the value, gst_adapter_flush at line 154 consumes 0 bytes, and avail recomputed at line 160 stays >= FlxFrameChunkSize with res == GST_FLOW_OK, so the loop at line 90 repeatedly maps and re-reads the same unchanged 6 bytes and never terminates on attacker-chosen input. No shown statement establishes a minimum flxfh.size or any other progress guarantee. CWE-835.

assumptions: FlxFrameChunkSize and FlxHeaderSize are positive byte-size compile-time constants used as memcpy lengths at lines 22 and 98.
gst_adapter_take consumes exactly nbytes and requires that many bytes available; the shown guard at line 105 only bounds flxfh.size by avail, not the subtracted expression.
The adapter accumulates pushed buffers (line 14), so the PLAYING loop at line 90 is reachable with avail >= FlxFrameChunkSize after the header is consumed (lines 18, 25).
limitations: Declared types of FlxHeader fields (width, height, frames, speed, size) and FlxFrameChunk.size are not visible in the fragment; the exact wrapped value at lines 111-112 depends on that type, though both signed and unsigned interpretations yield an out-of-domain length.

Integer overflow in flxdec->size = width * height (line 78) and flxdec->size * 4 passed to gst_buffer_new_and_alloc (line 124), which could produce an undersized output buffer overflowed by flx_colorspace_convert (lines 140-141), is unconfirmable because the fragment does not establish the width/height value domain.
flxdec->converter is only created when flxh->depth <= 8 (lines 67-69); a NULL converter for depth > 8 used at line 140 cannot be confirmed because the element's initial converter value is not shown.
chunk == NULL after a zero-length gst_adapter_take (flxfh.size == FlxFrameChunkSize) dereferenced at line 113 depends on the unshown empty-request contract of gst_adapter_take.
Bounds enforcement inside flx_decode_chunks (lines 127-129) and flx_colorspace_convert (lines 140-141) is outside the shown code and was not analyzed.
Unchecked gst_buffer_map return (line 138) and the g_free(chunk) leak on the error return at line 132 are robustness/leak concerns without attacker-directed failure state or volume compounding.

verdict.summary: No security vulnerability is demonstrable from the fragment. The function contains no memory-copy/index/length sink, no injection/crypto/file/auth sink, and every dereference is guarded by a visible NULL test (L5/L11/L46/L60/L89) or by a checked non-zero error return (L76). The only structural hazard is the outer-loop update `un= next_unit ? next_unit : un->next_unit()` (L6) combined with caching the successor at L19 before calling the unshown `un->exclude_level()` (L20); whether that call invalidates the cached pointer cannot be established from the shown code, so the use-after-free candidate is recorded as a limitation, not a finding.

assumptions: The inner-unit and select chains traversed at L4-L6 and L46 are NULL-terminated (the loop conditions `un` / `sl` are the only shown terminators), so iteration is finite for any chain admitted by the shown NULL tests.
`const_item()`, `empty_result()`, and the `fixed`/`substype()`/`is_jtbm_merged` classifiers are read-only boolean/enum queries consumed only in guards.
`first_inner_unit()` (L4) may return NULL for an empty list; the loop condition L5 handles it, and L11 handles a NULL `un->item` before any predicate dereference.
limitations: Unconfirmed use-after-free pattern: at L19 `next_unit= un->next_unit()` is cached before `un->exclude_level()` (L20), and the loop update L6 resumes iteration from that cached pointer (dereferenced at L8). A two-element chain {A,B} with `A->item` non-NULL and `A->item->fixed==false` (admitted by L11/L13) passes L21 and re-enters the loop with `un==B`; the claim that B is then dangling requires `exclude_level()` to free/detach the unit, and the fragment contains no statement establishing that invalidation. No CWE is assigned because the failure cannot be traced entirely through the shown code.

Robustness-only: on the early `return TRUE` at L76-L77, the mutations at L66-L75 (`current_select`, `select_options`, `SELECT_DESCRIBE` flags) are not restored (restore happens only at L82-L83). This is state leakage on an error-exit path with no security-relevant operation consuming the failure state, so it is not a confirmed security finding.
Dead code: `if (res) return TRUE;` at L104-L105 is unreachable because L76-L77 already returns for every non-zero `res`; no security impact.

The safety of `inner_join->optimize()`, `save_union_explain()`, `set_limit()`, and `exclude_level()` depends on their unshown implementations; the fragment shows no argument derivation that is out of domain for any of them (no sizes, indices, or buffers are computed or passed).

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. All attacker-derived lengths are range-checked before use (lines 39, 45, 56, 65, 71); the TLS1_AAD decryption subtraction is guarded against underflow by line 82, and the only fully identifiable destination capacity (actx->tls_aad, >= POLY1305_BLOCK_SIZE per the line-22 memset) covers the fixed EVP_AEAD_TLS1_AAD_LEN-byte copy at line 77. The memcpy candidates involving actx->tag (line 59) and the caller's GET_TAG buffer (line 67) cannot be confirmed because those capacities are not declared in the fragment, and NULL-payload claims have no in-fragment producer.

assumptions: memset(actx->tls_aad, 0, POLY1305_BLOCK_SIZE) at line 22 is a valid write, so actx->tls_aad has capacity >= POLY1305_BLOCK_SIZE; this is the in-fragment capacity evidence used to bound the 13-byte memcpy at line 77 and the index writes at lines 85-86.

For dl->length < so_ext_len the difference wraps to 2^N - (so_ext_len - dl->length), so the pointer argument addresses dl->str - (so_ext_len - dl->length), i.e. before the string object whose extent is dl->length bytes (the same extent memcpy consumes at line 8). my_strcasecmp then reads at least one byte out of bounds (exact excess so_ext_len - dl->length >= 1 for a non-empty SO_EXT), the OOB read at CWE-125. No guard exists between the parameter and the sink: the only conditional (line 4) is the sink statement itself, and no dl->length >= so_ext_len check appears anywhere in the fragment.

assumptions: so_ext_len is declared size_t at line 3 and dl->length is used in the same unsigned arithmetic (lines 4, 7, 8, 11), so the line-4 subtraction wraps modulo 2^N for dl->length < so_ext_len.

verdict.summary: NULL pointer dereference in the gzip-header EXTRA handling (fragment line 144): when the gzip FLG field sets FEXTRA (0x04) and the 16-bit XLEN field is >= 1, the statement `len = state->head->extra_len - state->length;` dereferences state->head before the `state->head != Z_NULL` check at line 145. The fragment never establishes head as non-NULL and NULL-checks it in every other access, so with head == Z_NULL (no application header buffer installed) an attacker-supplied gzip header makes inflate() read from address 0 and crash (denial of service).

evidence.reason: Sink is a NULL-pointer read of state->head. Taint: gzip FLG FEXTRA bit (0x0400) flows from input into state->flags at line 87, admitted by guards 88 ((flags&0xff)==8) and 93 ((flags&0xe000)==0); XLEN (>=1) flows into state->length at line 128. Path: line 43 magic check admits 1f 8b; line 126 gates on flags&0x0400; line 141 copy=state->length; line 142 caps copy to have (>=1); line 143 admits copy=1. state->head is never assigned in the fragment and is NULL-checked at lines 52, 98, 107, 116, 129, 135, 145, 169, 180, 191, 202, 216, so head==Z_NULL is within the residual range of the fragment's own contract; the only head guard on this path (line 145, state->head != Z_NULL) is evaluated after line 144 and does not protect it. Primary CWE-476 (NULL dereference) with DoS impact. Witness: header 1f 8b 08 04 | MTIME | XFL | OS | XLEN=01 00 | one extra byte, with head==Z_NULL.

assumptions: GUNZIP build with gzip wrapping active (state->wrap & 2) so the FLAGS/EXLEN/EXTRA chain at lines 85-158 executes; these cases are compiled into the fragment (lines 42, 84, 223).
state->flags is the 16-bit CM/FLG header word: mask 0xff => CM (line 88), 0xe000 => reserved FLG bits (line 93), 0x0400 => FEXTRA (line 126), 0x0200 => FHCRC, 0x0800 => FNAME, 0x1000 => FCOMMENT.

state->length and head->extra_len receive the same attacker value from hold at lines 128/130; state->length only decreases afterward (line 156), so extra_len - state->length cannot underflow on the fragment's own path, and the zmemcpy at lines 148-150 writes at most extra_max - len bytes while len < extra_max (line 147) — the line 147 cap excludes the historical wrap-driven overflow.

NEEDBITS/BITS/DROPBITS/PULLBYTE/LOAD/RESTORE macro bodies are not shown; their standard zlib semantics (bit accumulation, bounded by avail_in) are assumed for the trace, and no independent sink is derived from them.

krb5rc = krb5_kt_get_entry(krb5context, krb5keytab, 
                                princ,
                                0 /* IGNORE_VNO */,
                                0 /* IGNORE_ENCTYPE */,
                                &entry);
evidence.reason: princ is NULL whenever krb5_sname_to_principal (lines 30-32) fails: princ is initialized NULL at line 6 and the call's error status is discarded (krb5rc is unconditionally overwritten at line 34 without any intervening test). The only constraint on the service_name input is the NULL-excluding ternary at line 31, so non-NULL inputs on which principal construction fails remain admitted and drive princ=NULL into this sink. krb5_kt_get_entry consumes the principal argument as the required lookup key with name-implied dereference semantics, yielding a CWE-476 NULL pointer dereference; the unchecked return at lines 30-32 is the independent CWE-754 root cause.

assumptions: princ is declared NULL at line 6 and remains NULL when krb5_sname_to_principal fails, per the krb5 out-parameter contract combined with the shown initializer.
KRB5_KT_NOTFOUND at line 39 denotes the 'entry absent' outcome of krb5_kt_get_entry, as the shown branch compares against it.
kssl_ctx->service_name is admitted as any non-NULL C string; the ternary at line 31 is the only shown constraint on it.
limitations: A specific service_name value guaranteed to fail krb5_sname_to_principal cannot be named from the fragment (krb5 internals not shown); the witness is range-based over the admitted non-NULL string domain, capping confidence at 0.7.

The NULL dereference itself executes inside the callee krb5_kt_get_entry (body not shown); if that library tolerates a NULL principal, the residual confirmed defect is the unchecked return (CWE-754) alone.

The KRB5_KT_NOTFOUND branch (lines 39-41) maps a missing keytab entry to rc=1, identical to the success result at line 46, so return(rc) at line 52 reports 'available' for an absent entry; the security impact depends on the unshown caller's interpretation, so it is not reported as a confirmed finding.
A NULL kssl_ctx would fault at line 15, but the fragment contains no NULL producer for it (caller contract not shown).

KRB5SVC is a constant not defined in the fragment; its value and validity cannot be verified.
If krb5_kt_get_entry fails after partially populating entry, entry is not freed; no shown producer confirms that state.

Several memory-safety-relevant derivations exist (the second vim_strncpy into wcopy at lines 135-137, the alloc size arithmetic at line 215, and the AppendToRedobuffLit length at lines 225-226), but every overflow/underflow witness depends on bounds that are not visible in the shown code: the numeric value of MAXWLEN, the declared types/domains of suginfo_T/suggest_T fields (st_wordlen, st_orglen, su_badlen), and the spell_find_suggest contract. The only directly guarded index use (selected at line 196) is fully covered by the guard at line 190.

wcopy has capacity MAXWLEN+2 bytes per its declaration at line 5; the numeric value of MAXWLEN is not visible in the fragment.
SUG(sug.su_ga, i) indexes the growarray by element index consistent with ga_len, used identically at lines 129 and 196.
ml_get_curline() returns a NUL-terminated line; the fragment relies on this at lines 61, 221, and in the strlen-based allocation at line 215.
alloc() returns NULL on failure, which is why the fragment NULL-checks it at line 216.
limitations: Candidate stack overflow into wcopy at lines 135-137 (potential CWE-787): dest offset stp->st_wordlen plus length su_badlen - st_orglen would exceed the MAXWLEN+2 capacity only for field values whose domains and signedness are not visible in the fragment; guard at line 134 only ensures the length argument is positive. No concrete witness is expressible from the shown code, so this is unconfirmed.

Candidate huge/negative length to AppendToRedobuffLit at lines 225-226: the expression stp->st_wordlen + sug.su_badlen - stp->st_orglen can be negative only if st_wordlen < st_orglen - su_badlen, and the callee parameter type is not visible; the fragment does admit su_badlen < st_orglen as a normal case (line 149), but no failure can be demonstrated from visible types/values.

Candidate out-of-bounds reads via precision-controlled %.*s at lines 111-112, 118-119, 151-152, and 202-204: requires su_badlen or st_orglen to exceed the bytes remaining at sug.su_badptr, not derivable from the fragment.

badlen is bounded only to >= 1 on the visual path (lines 40-45) with no shown relation to line length; any consequence would occur inside the unshown spell_find_suggest body (lines 88-89), so no sink can be anchored.
limit can be negative (lines 84-87, Rows < 2); the effect is inside the unshown spell_find_suggest and no capacity or guard in the fragment is violated by it.
The backing array length behind SUG(sug.su_ga, i) is not visible; indexing is nonetheless consistently bounded by ga_len at lines 127-129 and 190/196.

verdict.summary: In the XBM version-1.0 fill path with padding (ww%16 in 1..8), the loop at lines 102-108 skips the second byte at each scanline boundary via the condition `((bytes+2) % bytes_per_line)` on line 106, leaving one byte per scanline of the g_malloc(size) buffer (line 96) never written. The fully populated-looking buffer is then returned to the caller at line 125 (`*data = bits;`), exposing indeterminate heap bytes as image data (uninitialized-value exposure, CWE-457). All classic-looking flaws in the fragment are guarded: the signed-division overflow check at line 94 rejects both wrapped and negative `int` sizes (largest admitted allocation size is 2147483520, well within INT_MAX), and both fill loops are bounded so no index can reach `size`.

evidence.reason: Sink for the uninitialized-value exposure (CWE-457). With file-derived `ww=17`, `hh=1` (both admitted by the guards at lines 41/46 giving residual range [1, INT_MAX]) and a `static short ... = {` line matching line 62, `version10p=1` and `padding=1` (lines 86-87), so `bytes_per_line = (17+7)/8 + 1 = 4` (line 91), `size = 4` (line 93), and the guard at line 94 (`4/4 == 1 == hh`) admits the value 4 for `g_malloc(size)` (line 96). The v1.0 loop (lines 102-108) writes indices 0,1 at `bytes=0` and index 2 at `bytes=2`, then skips the second byte because `(2+2)%4 == 0` (line 106), so index 3 of the 4-byte buffer allocated at line 96 is never written; `hh` such pad bytes are left unwritten per image. Line 125 then passes the whole buffer, including indeterminate bytes from the non-zeroing allocation at line 96, back to the caller as valid image data.

assumptions: `line` and `name_and_type` capacities are `MAX_SIZE` per their declarations at lines 9 and 11; the `fgets` bound plus the check at line 31 guarantee `strlen(line) <= MAX_SIZE-2` for lines reaching the sscanf calls.
`g_malloc`/`g_free` are GLib malloc/free; name-implied malloc semantics (non-zeroing allocation, abort on failure) are relied on for the CWE-457 mechanism.
`bytes_per_line` is always even in the version-1.0 path (case analysis over `ww%16` in {0}, {1..8}, {9..15}), which the OOB and padding-byte accounting depends on.
`next_int(fstream)` returns negative on parse failure and non-negative byte values otherwise, per the checks at lines 103-104 and 114-115.
limitations: Loop OOB write hypotheses (CWE-787) are refuted: total writes are `size` (padding=0) or `size - hh` (padding=1), max index `size-1`, verified by an exhaustive sweep over ww<=1024, hh<=64 for both versions (0 OOB cases); larger domains follow from the even-`bytes_per_line` argument.

Integer-overflow/negative-size DoS candidates are refuted by the guard at lines 94-95: signed division of a negative `size` can never equal the positive `hh`, and a wrapped product can never yield quotient `hh`; the largest size admitted by the guard is 2147483520 (simulated).

The `if (!bits)` check at line 122 occurs after the loops at lines 102-118 that dereference `bits`; a NULL-deref (CWE-476/CWE-754) would require `g_malloc` to fail, which per the GLib contract aborts instead, so this is recorded only as a defensive-hardening concern.

The unbounded `%s` conversions into `name_and_type` (lines 33, 62-70) are safe only because the line-length cap at line 31 bounds the token; if `MAX_SIZE` semantics were different this would need re-auditing.
`sscanf` `%d` on out-of-range numerals is undefined behavior but has no confirmed downstream security impact (the `value <= 0` guards and byte truncation absorb it).
`next_int`'s body is not shown; if it failed to advance its read position on malformed hex, the parsing could stall — unconfirmable from the fragment.
The `hot` branch's double post-decrement (lines 51-53) is a logic quirk (hotspot values are often not set as expected) with no demonstrated memory-safety impact.

The CWE-457 impact presupposes the consumer of `*data` actually reads the unwritten pad bytes; the exposure itself (capacity `g_malloc(size)` at line 96, unwritten index `size-hh .. size-1`) is fully derived from the shown code.

verdict.summary: Unsigned integer overflow in the allocation-size arithmetic at line 15: *count + auth_count is computed in unsigned int before the size_t multiply, so *count == 4294967295 wraps the sum (mod 2^32) to auth_count-1 and t_malloc allocates far fewer elements than the subsequent memset (line 16) and memcpy (lines 20-21) write, producing a heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787, root cause CWE-190).

evidence.reason: CWE-190 root-cause sink: *count (unsigned int, parameter line 3) is unconstrained by any shown check, so its residual range is [0, UINT_MAX]. Both operands of *count + auth_count are unsigned int, so with *count == 4294967295 and any auth_count >= 1 the addition wraps mod 2^32 to auth_count-1 before the size_t multiply, and t_malloc allocates only (auth_count-1) elements. The overflowed value is consumed here as the allocation size.

CWE-787 primary sink: for the same witness (*count == 4294967295, auth_count == 1), the allocation from line 15 holds 0 elements, but this statement writes *count == 4294967295 elements (4294967295 * sizeof(*tab) bytes) from tab, an immediate heap out-of-bounds write overshooting the allocation by ~2^32 elements. No guard in the fragment bounds *count before this sink.

CWE-787 second sink: after tab += *count (line 17) advances tab by the un-wrapped 4294967295 elements, this memcpy writes auth_count elements at that far offset, which is 2^32 elements past the (auth_count-1)-element allocation from line 15, confirming the corrupted-size chain 15 -> 16 -> 20-21. *count's residual range is the full unsigned int domain because the shown code imposes no constraint on it.

assumptions: Line numbers are 1-based positions in the fragment as presented; no repository file is attached (file: null).
*count (unsigned int) retains the full declared domain [0, UINT_MAX] because the fragment imposes no constraint before its first use at line 15.
auth_count = N_ELEMENTS(auth_request_var_expand_static_tab) at line 6 is an unshown constant; the analysis relies only on auth_count >= 1.
sizeof(*tab) is the element size used consistently by the shown allocation and write statements; the wrap analysis holds for any element size.
limitations: Index writes tab[0..33] at lines 23-107 (e.g., tab[33] at lines 105/107) cannot be checked against the capacity of the copied static region because the static table size is not visible (only N_ELEMENTS(...) at line 6); an out-of-bounds write would require fewer than 34 entries, which the fragment neither confirms nor refutes (comment at lines 13-14 indicates the table ends with NULL fields).
NULL dereference of auth_request->user (lines 23, 24, 26, 74, 79, 88) or auth_request->service (line 29) is not confirmed: no shown statement produces a NULL for these fields.

Second-level dereferences auth_request->userdb->userdb->id (line 42) and auth_request->passdb->passdb->id (line 45) are guarded only one level; a NULL second-level pointer would crash, but the fragment contains no producer of it.
An unterminated auth_request->user string would let strchr/strrchr read out of bounds, but NUL-termination is a caller contract not visible in the fragment.
t_malloc failure at line 15 is not handled, but the fragment shows no contract that it can return NULL; treating it as nullable would depend on out-of-fragment semantics.
If an unshown caller invariant guaranteed *count to be small, the overflow would be unreachable; such an invariant is not present in the fragment and cannot be used to demote the finding.

The *count += auth_count wrap at line 18 (which would return a smaller count to the caller on the overflow path) is not reported separately: no security-relevant downstream use of the wrapped count is visible in the fragment.

verdict.summary: No security vulnerability is confirmable from the fragment. Every in-fragment write into the command buffer (lines 338, 339, 343, 345) is provably confined to indices strictly below the string's own NUL position: the parser advances eap->cmd only forward and the empty-command guards (lines 63-72) and Ex-mode plus path (lines 38-46) force k <= |T|, so the maximal write index k+4 or |T|+3 is always < 5+|T|. No NULL dereference, injection, crypto, or auth sink is confirmable with in-fragment anchors. Candidates (unchecked skip_range() return, vim_regcomp() failure leaving the pattern NUL unrestored and returning OK, atoi()+1 wrap) are demoted to limitations because their security-relevant consequence or producing contract is outside the shown code.

assumptions: eap->cmd points to a writable, NUL-terminated byte buffer; the fragment itself presupposes this via STRNCMP (line 17), the NUL tests (lines 38, 63), STRLEN (line 332), and the in-place rewrites (lines 338-345).
The parser advances eap->cmd only forward: the whitespace loop stops at NUL (lines 30-35), and each modifier branch consumes at least one byte before continue (lines 99-317).
getline_equal, exmode_active, curwin/curbuf, tabpage_index, MAXLNUM and LAST_TAB_NR are framework values used only in branches; none sizes a buffer.

Commented-out/incomplete modifier cases and the behaviors of helpers (skip_range, checkforcmd_*, comment_start, skip_vimgrep_pat_ext, ends_excmd*) are taken only at their name-implied semantics as used at the call sites shown.

verdict.summary: Reachable CHECK-fail in SafeToRemoveIdentity: the only guard on node inputs (input_size() >= 1 at line 14) makes input(0) a valid index but never verifies that NodeName(node.input(0)) exists in node_map_; node_map_->GetNode(...) at line 19 can therefore return nullptr and the CHECK at lines 20-21 aborts the process. A synthetic Identity/IdentityN node whose input names a node absent from the map is admitted by every guard and triggers a crash (DoS).

evidence.reason: node.input(0) retains its full string domain after the only input guard (line 14, input_size() < 1, which merely makes index 0 valid). GetNode(NodeName(node.input(0))) at line 19 returns nullptr whenever the referenced name is absent from node_map_, and the fragment establishes no map-membership invariant before the lookup. Witness: Identity node with inputs=["ghost"], input_size()==1, name not in nodes_to_preserve_, fetch_nodes_known_==true — all guards at lines 2, 6, 9, and 14 admit it; GetNode("ghost") == nullptr, so the CHECK fails and aborts. Primary mechanism CWE-617 reachable assertion; CWE-476 is not the mechanism because the CHECK prevents a NULL dereference and the abort is the impact.

assumptions: node_map_->GetNode returns nullptr for a name absent from the map — implied by the CHECK's explicit null test at line 20 and the lookup name 'GetNode'; no shown statement guarantees presence.
node.input(i) is valid for i < node.input_size() (protobuf repeated-field contract), so line 14's guard makes input(0) valid.
node_map_ itself is non-null and GetOutputs' consumer pointers are non-null (framework state; no null producer is shown).
limitations: Provenance of the `node` parameter (attacker-supplied GraphDef vs. internally validated graph) is not visible in the fragment; attacker-directedness is inferred from the absence of any shown validation, capping confidence at 0.6.
If every caller guarantees that input names exist in node_map_, the CHECK would be defensive; that invariant is not present in the fragment and cannot support a high-confidence safe verdict.

No memory-safety, injection, crypto, integer-overflow, or error-handling finding is confirmed; the consumer loops are bounded by the returned collections and contain no input-derived indices or sizes.

verdict.summary: In fix_dl_name, the size_t expression dl->length + so_ext_len + 1 (line 8) wraps to 0 for dl->length = SIZE_MAX - so_ext_len, which passes the line 4 minimum-length guard and a non-matching tail. alloc_root then returns an allocation whose requested capacity is 0, and memcpy (line 9) writes dl->length bytes into it, causing a heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) whose root cause is the unsigned size_t overflow (CWE-190); the strcpy at line 10 writes past the same wrapped allocation.

evidence.reason: CWE-787 (heap OOB write): dl->length retains the full size_t domain [0, SIZE_MAX] because no shown statement bounds it; with dl->length = SIZE_MAX - so_ext_len (admitted by guard line 4 since SIZE_MAX-so_ext_len >= so_ext_len, and by guard lines 5-6 when the tail differs from SO_EXT), the allocation argument at line 8 wraps: (SIZE_MAX-so_ext_len) + so_ext_len + 1 == 0. memcpy at line 9 then writes dl->length = SIZE_MAX-so_ext_len bytes into that 0-capacity allocation, exceeding the capacity quoted at line 8 by SIZE_MAX-so_ext_len bytes.

CWE-190 (unsigned size_t integer overflow corrupting the allocation size): the operands are dl->length (unconstrained size_t, residual range [0, SIZE_MAX]) and so_ext_len (size_t). For dl->length = SIZE_MAX - so_ext_len, the sum wraps to 0 in the shown types, and the wrapped value is consumed as the capacity for the line 9 memcpy sink, making it the independent root cause of the CWE-787 write.

CWE-787 (heap OOB write): with the same witness dl->length = SIZE_MAX - so_ext_len, the write offset s + dl->length lies beyond the wrapped 0-capacity allocation from line 8; strcpy writes so_ext_len+1 bytes (extension plus NUL) at that offset, again exceeding the line-8 capacity.

assumptions: LEX_STRING.length is treated in the shown code as an unsigned size participating in size_t arithmetic (compared with size_t so_ext_len at line 4, added to it at line 8, used as a memcpy length at line 9); the analysis takes its domain as [0, SIZE_MAX].

SO_EXT is a NUL-terminated string literal consumed at lines 6 and 10, so so_ext_len = sizeof(SO_EXT)-1 is a compile-time constant >= 1; the overflow witness is parametric (dl->length = SIZE_MAX - so_ext_len) and holds for any so_ext_len in [1, SIZE_MAX/2].
dl->str is assumed to point to a readable buffer of dl->length bytes, since the fragment itself relies on that contract at lines 5 and 9 without any shown cap.
limitations: Potential one-byte overread inside my_strcasecmp at line 5 when the tail equals SO_EXT and dl->str is not NUL-terminated: the backing-buffer capacity of dl->str and its NUL-termination are not identifiable from the fragment, so no CWE is assigned.

alloc_root (line 8) returning NULL would make memcpy (line 9) and strcpy (line 10) dereference NULL, but a NULL-on-failure contract for alloc_root is not visible in the fragment, so this is not confirmed.
End-to-end attacker control of dl->length depends on callers not shown in the fragment; the verified failure is established from the unconstrained residual range of dl->length inside the shown code.

verdict.summary: The fragment contains one index sink (ctx->set_output(output_port, shape)) whose argument output_port is unconstrained in the shown code, but no capacity for the indexed collection is declared or derivable in the fragment, so no out-of-bounds claim can be confirmed. The only dereference of ctx is protected by an explicit null check (lines 5-7). No injection, crypto, file, auth, or error-handling flaw is present in the shown code.

assumptions: On the executed path to ctx->set_output(...), ctx is non-null; this is established by the visible check at lines 5-7 (ctx == nullptr returns early at line 6).
output_port has the full int domain (INT_MIN..INT_MAX); the fragment applies no constraint, cast, or bound to it before use at line 8.
limitations: An out-of-range output_port index into ctx->set_output (potential CWE-787/CWE-125) is unconfirmable: the capacity of the output collection is neither declared nor derived anywhere in the shown code, and the callee's index-domain contract is not visible, so no boundary claim can be grounded.
A negative output_port converted to a huge unsigned index would be out of range only relative to that unshown capacity; for the same reason it is a limitation, not a finding.
Whether GetUnknownOutputShape can return an invalid/empty ShapeHandle and whether set_output misbehaves on such a handle is not determinable from the fragment; no sink-side memory operation is shown.
No vulnerability is confirmed; the safe verdict for the index sink rests on absence of a demonstrable capacity overflow, not on a positive protective check for output_port.

verdict.summary: xla::Compiler::GetForPlatform (line 18) can fail with an error code other than NOT_FOUND; the only failure handling is the NOT_FOUND-specific return at lines 31-35, so such errors fall through unhandled and the function creates the cache and returns Status::OK() at line 61, masking a failed compiler lookup as success (CWE-754, error/status-handling flaw).

evidence.reason: compiler_for_platform (assigned line 18) has residual range 'non-OK with code != error::NOT_FOUND' after the shown checks: the guard at line 19 admits all non-OK statuses, and the only failure handler, the status.code() == error::NOT_FOUND check at line 31, returns only for NOT_FOUND. No statement in lines 36-61 re-checks compiler_for_platform, so for any other error the function still executes *cache = new XlaCompilationCache(...) (lines 59-60) and returns Status::OK() at line 61, i.e. success is returned after the failed GetForPlatform step (lines 17-18), masking the error (CWE-754 mechanism: return status compared for only part of its outcomes and failure treated as success).

assumptions: platform.ValueOrDie() at line 33 is safe because line 13-15 established platform.ok(); likewise client.ValueOrDie() at line 60 is preceded by the client.ok() check at lines 50-52, and registration (line 60) is only dereferenced after GetCompilationDevice returned true at line 54.

device, flr, and flr->config_proto() are framework-provided pointers with no nullable contract visible in the fragment, so they are treated as non-NULL per the analysis rules; no NULL producer is shown.
limitations: CWE-476 hypothesis for flr->config_proto() (line 44) and device->tensorflow_cpu_worker_threads() (line 41) is not confirmable: NULL would have to be produced by framework contracts not visible in the fragment.

The metadata early-return path (lines 4-8) does not verify that xla_device_metadata()->client() is usable; XlaCompilationCache constructor semantics are outside the fragment, so this is unconfirmable.
A nullopt gpu_ids from ParseVisibleDeviceList (line 46) flowing into set_allowed_devices (line 47) has semantics defined outside the fragment; empty visibility-list handling is not assessable here.

The confirmed CWE-754 finding has indirect impact (error masking / unintended success status) rather than direct memory-safety or injection impact, which is reflected in the low severity and 0.6 confidence.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds heap read in Node::RunForwardTypeInference: `int ix = input_idx[i]` (line 40) is copied from `edge->src_output()` (line 17) and used as an unchecked element index into the source node's experimental-type repeated field at `node_t.args(ix)` (line 45). The only guard, `DCHECK(ix < node_t.args_size())` (line 41), is debug-only (inert in release builds) and checks no lower bound, so a graph edge whose `src_output` is >= the source node's recorded output count (or negative) reads past the `args_size()`-element array, disclosing or crashing on adjacent heap memory.

evidence.reason: `ix` derives from `input_idx[i]` (line 40) which is written from `edge->src_output()` (line 17) with no runtime bound imposed by the fragment; its residual range is any `int` except the control slot. The repeated field's capacity is `node_t.args_size()` (element count read at line 41): for a node with `args_size()==2`, valid indices are 0..1. The only bound, `DCHECK(ix < node_t.args_size())` (line 41), is a debug-only assertion (absent in release builds) and never checks `ix >= 0`. Witness: `ix == 2` with `args_size()==2` (or `ix == -1`) passes every runtime guard on the path (lines 4, 11, 16-17 via `.at()`, 24-30, 37, 39) and reaches `node_t.args(2)` / `node_t.args(-1)` — the standard protobuf repeated-field accessor is unchecked in release — producing an out-of-bounds heap read (CWE-125: OOB read past/ before the element array) whose referenced object is subsequently passed to `fwd_type_fn(input_types)` at line 56.

assumptions: `DCHECK` is a debug-only assertion compiled out in release/opt builds, per its standard name-implied semantics.
`node_t.args(int)` is the standard protobuf repeated-field element accessor, which performs no runtime bounds check in release builds; `args_size()` returns the element count of the field.
`std::vector::at` performs runtime bounds checking (lines 16-17), so the index `i` cannot corrupt memory even when out of range.
The null-check loop at lines 24-30 guarantees `node != nullptr` before `node->def()` is used at line 37; a null dereference is excluded by a shown guard.
limitations: The witness for the line-45 OOB read requires a runtime graph state in which a non-control edge's `src_output` is not aligned with the source node's `experimental_type().args_size()`; that mismatch is not constructed or refuted by statements in this fragment, so the confirmation rests on the residual-range analysis of `edge->src_output()` and `input_idx` (lines 10-17, 40-45).

A second robustness concern: `edge->dst_input()` used with `input_nodes.at(i)` / `input_idx.at(i)` (lines 16-17) throws `std::out_of_range` if an edge references a port index >= `input_nodes.size()` (a graph-state inconsistency the fragment does not establish), which could abort the process; `.at()` prevents memory corruption, and the L14 DCHECK flags the same inconsistency only in debug builds — not confirmed as an attacker-reachable flaw from the shown code.

`infer_type.ValueOrDie()` (line 57) aborts on an error status from `props_->fwd_type_fn`; the callee body is not shown, so no shown statement demonstrates a failure for any admitted input — the abort-on-error path is the intended handling, not a confirmed CWE-617.

The reachable-abort reading of the DCHECKs at lines 14 and 41 applies only to debug builds and is the intended invariant-assertion behavior on inconsistent graph metadata; not confirmed as a separate vulnerability.
Line numbers are assigned sequentially from the fragment, since the original source was not numbered.

verdict.summary: In Node::RunForwardTypeInference, edge->src_output() is stored into input_idx without any sign constraint (line 17). The guard at line 41 ('if (ix >= node_t.args_size())') only rejects indexes at or above args_size(), so a negative index passes and is used at line 51 as node_t.args(ix), an out-of-bounds read of the protobuf repeated field 'args' (read one element before the array start when ix == -1, e.g. args_size() == 0).

evidence.reason: Sink CWE-125 OOB read: the index ix is derived from edge->src_output() (int, full int domain; line 17 stores it with no shown lower-bound check) via input_idx[i] at line 40. The only guard, line 41 'ix >= node_t.args_size()', admits every negative ix (e.g. -1 with args_size() == 0, since -1 >= 0 is false), but the protobuf repeated-field accessor node_t.args(ix) requires ix in [0, args_size()). Witness: src_output() == -1, args_size() == 0 passes lines 11, 24-30, 37, 39, and 41, then reads one FullTypeDef element before the array storage.

assumptions: node_t.args(ix) is the standard protobuf repeated-field accessor whose index domain is [0, args_size()); it performs no runtime bounds check in release builds.
node_t.args_size() returns a non-negative int per the protobuf repeated-field contract.
limitations: ValueOrDie() at line 63 may abort on a non-OK status from fwd_type_fn, but the callee is not shown and the failure cannot be tied to a specific admitted value in the fragment.
An out-of-range dst_input() at lines 16-17 causes std::out_of_range from at(), a robustness/exception concern, not memory unsafety.
The loop at line 35 could theoretically wrap if input_nodes.size() exceeded INT_MAX; not confirmable within the fragment.
The negative src_output() witness is a range claim from framework-provided data whose sign minimum is not established in the shown code; confidence capped at 0.7.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. All attacker-influenced index flows (tagstackidx, cur_match) are clamped and bounded by guards visible in the fragment (empty-stack check at lines 166-175, tagstackidx range guards at lines 182-199 and 260-276, MAXCOL/num_matches clamps at lines 313-321 and 545-560, TAGSTACKSIZE cap at line 140-147); the strongest remaining candidate, consumption of possibly-uninitialized find_tags() outputs after a FAIL return (lines 435-437 -> 447/479-481), cannot be confirmed because find_tags's out-parameter contract on failure is not shown in the fragment.

assumptions: TAGSTACKSIZE (line 140) is the tag-stack capacity: the fragment itself clamps tagstacklen to TAGSTACKSIZE and shifts entries, so accesses with tagstackidx < tagstacklen <= TAGSTACKSIZE are treated as in-domain.
IObuff is a fixed buffer whose capacity is IOSIZE, inferred from the sibling call vim_snprintf((char *)IObuff, IOSIZE, ...) at line 630.
MAXCOL (lines 309, 313-314, 410, 607) is the clamp ceiling used by the fragment for cur_match.
The static pairing num_matches/matches is maintained within the fragment: both are reassigned together (lines 479-481) and reset together (lines 53/57, 234/238).
The empty-stack guard at lines 166-175 establishes tagstacklen >= 1 (non-preview mode) before any DT_POP/DT_TAG/other-stack path indexes tagstack.
limitations: find_tags() FAIL path: new_num_matches/new_matches (declared lines 26-27) are only written by the call at line 435; on a non-OK return the fragment still consumes them at FreeWild (447) and at num_matches = new_num_matches; matches = new_matches (479-481), feeding matches[cur_match] (595/637). Unconfirmed (CWE-457/CWE-754 potential) because find_tags's out-parameter behavior on FAIL is callee-side and not visible in the fragment, so no concrete witness value can be expressed.

Signed integer overflow (UB) in user-controlled count arithmetic at lines 182, 260, 303, 310-311: exhaustive simulation of INT_MIN/INT_MAX outcomes shows every wrapped result either lands in-domain, is clamped, or exits via an error; no out-of-bounds index was found, but the wrap itself is undefined behavior.

tagstack[tagstackidx] accesses (e.g., lines 277-278, 298-299, 340, 384) depend on the unseen window invariant 0 <= w_tagstackidx <= w_tagstacklen at entry; an OOB would require that invariant to be broken by out-of-scope state.

NULL-dereference of name from the unchecked vim_strsave at line 384 via STRCMP at line 394, and of a negative tagp.user_data_end - tagp.user_data length at line 574, require allocation failure or a callee contract violation; robustness-only.
Regexp ReDoS (lines 417-420 -> find_tags) executes in a callee (Vim regex engine) and the pattern comes from the same user; no confirmed cross-boundary impact.
semsg at line 665 (and 592) can receive a NULL nofile_fname, but the fragment itself sets nofile_fname = NULL at line 71 and never reassigns it, so the value is fragment-produced and benign.

verdict.summary: IsSimplifiableReshape dereferences the result of node_map_->GetNode(node.input(1)) without a null check; a crafted Reshape node whose second input is not present in the node map causes a NULL pointer dereference at the IsReallyConstant(*new_shape) call (denial of service).

evidence.reason: new_shape is the unchecked return of node_map_->GetNode(node.input(1)) at line 11; the fragment imposes no constraint on it (no null check) before it is dereferenced as *new_shape here. The witness is a Reshape node with input_size()==2, admitted by the line 6 guard (2 > 2 is false), whose input(1) names a node absent from node_map_, so GetNode returns nullptr; the dereference is evaluated as the call argument before the branch can test anything. Primary mechanism: NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476) leading to a crash; confidence is capped at 0.7 because GetNode's nullable contract is not visible in the fragment.

assumptions: Line 6 guard admits input_size() >= 2, so node.input(1) at line 11 is in bounds for every admitted size; no off-by-one applies to the input indexing.
props[0] at line 39 is safe because props.empty() is checked at line 36.
limitations: The null-producing contract of node_map_->GetNode (lookup miss returns nullptr) is not visible in the fragment, so the NULL deref witness is a residual-range claim; this caps confidence at 0.7 and would be fully demonstrated only with the callee contract.

The else branch (lines 60-68) treats every non-DT_INT32 dtype as int64_t; an OOB read or internal CHECK abort for a mismatched dtype is unconfirmable because the tensor capacity and flat<> contract are not visible in the fragment.
A possible int overflow of the loop counters at lines 54 and 62 relative to NumElements() is unconfirmable: NumElements()'s return type and any element-count bound are not shown.
The error message at lines 7-9 says 'at most 2 inputs' but the guard enforces at least 2; this is cosmetic and has no security impact.
Log/error-message injection through node.name() into errors::Internal(...) is unconfirmed: no log write or printf-style sink appears in the fragment.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable from this fragment. The input-derived indices cnt (L26, uint, unconstrained) and table->tablenr reach pointer/array sinks (L43, L88, L111, L122, L136, L140, L142), but the capacities of tmp_table_param, fields_for_table, tmp_tables, and join->map2table are never declared in the shown code, so no out-of-domain derivation can be demonstrated. The remaining candidates (cast of fields->head() to Item_field at L20, empty-fields NULL deref, discarded fix_fields/extra statuses) are unconfirmable or lack a concrete security-relevant operation on the failure state.

assumptions: The fragment's shown minimum-length statement at lines 12-13 (comment 'Any update has at least one pair (field, value)' plus DBUG_ASSERT(fields->elements)) establishes that fields is non-empty, which excludes the empty-list NULL-deref path at line 20.

List structures traversed in the fragment (update_tables at L23, select_lex units/selects at L55-59, leaves at L77, unupdated_check_opt_tables at L100-120) are NULL-terminated, so the sentinel loops terminate and progress each iteration.

Framework pointers thd, table->file, and thd->mem_root are treated as non-NULL because the fragment contains no nullable contract for them.
limitations: Potential OOB access via cnt at L88 (tmp_table_param+cnt), L122 (fields_for_table[cnt]), L136/L140/L142 (tmp_tables[cnt]) is unconfirmable: cnt retains the full uint domain [0,UINT_MAX] with no shown guard, but the capacities of the indexed arrays are not identifiable from the fragment, so the exact excess (index >= capacity) cannot be computed (would-be CWE-787/125).
Potential narrowing at L26 (uint cnt= table_ref->shared) is unconfirmable because TABLE_LIST::shared's declared type is not shown.
Potential OOB/NULL deref at L43 and L111 (join->map2table[...]) is unconfirmable: the array's capacity and any NULL-producing path are outside the fragment.
Type-confusion cast at L20 ((Item_field*) fields->head()) is unconfirmable: the fragment gives no shown guarantee of the head element's dynamic type; validity depends on a caller-side invariant.

In release builds DBUG_ASSERT(fields->elements) at L13 compiles out, so the non-empty guarantee for the L20 dereference rests on the comment/caller contract; a release-build NULL-deref is a robustness concern, not demonstrable from the fragment.

Discarded return statuses: item->fix_fields(thd, 0) at L117 and table->file->extra(...) at L32/L142 — failure would require an internal framework error not producible from the fragment's own data, and no concrete security-relevant operation on the failure state is demonstrable (would-be CWE-754/703).
func_count= temp_fields.elements - 1 at L131 cannot underflow: the do-while at L100-120 guarantees at least one successful push_back before this line.

verdict.summary: No attacker-triggerable vulnerability is confirmable within the fragment. The sanity checks at lines 26-29 bound count*typesize to at most 2^31-1, so the uint32 multiplication and assert at lines 30-33 cannot overflow or abort; the data=NULL branch (lines 38-42) is mutually exclusive with the memcpy branches (lines 50-53, 71-74), so no NULL-source copy occurs; destination capacity equals datasize exactly (line 44). The division by desttypesize at line 28 is reachable for the residual value 0 of that internal-helper parameter (no shown guard excludes it), but the fragment shows no caller or attacker path supplying 0, so it is a robustness concern rather than a confirmed attacker-triggerable finding.

assumptions: direntry->tdir_offset is a union containing both toff_long (uint32, line 57) and toff_long8 (uint64, line 78) because the fragment accesses both members on the same struct type, giving the union a byte extent of at least 8; this underlies the source-in-bounds inference for the <=4-byte (line 53) and <=8-byte (line 74) memcpys.

TIFFDataWidth returns a non-negative width for recognized types; the fragment itself only establishes typesize != 0 (line 14), and line 26's cast/division additionally rejects negative typesize on the continuing path (error return).

isMapped(tif) and tif->tif_size on line 35 denote mmap state and mapped-file size, so that check bounds the mapped-path read length (datasize <= tif_size); the offset addend is not validated in the fragment.
limitations: Division by zero at line 28 when the internal-helper parameter desttypesize == 0 (declared uint32 domain [0, 2^32-1]; line 19's '(void) desttypesize;' is not a constraint). A concrete witness (typesize=1, target_count64=1, desttypesize=0) passes lines 14 and 26 and then executes 2147483647/0, but attacker control of desttypesize is not demonstrated in the fragment, so no CWE is assigned.

Attacker-controlled file offsets (lines 57, 78) reach TIFFReadDirEntryData/TIFFReadDirEntryDataAndRealloc (lines 61/63, 82/84) without a shown offset+datasize-vs-file-size check; line 35 validates only datasize. OOB behavior therefore depends on bounds checks inside the unshown callees.

The exact TIFFDirEntry/tdir_offset struct layout is not declared in the fragment, so the memcpy source-capacity inference (>= 8 bytes) is not a byte-exact declared capacity, and a capacity-anchored OOB read claim is unconfirmable.
The empty-count path returning ErrOk with *value=0 (lines 16-17) and *value=data (line 92) leave NULL-pointer handling and NULL-ness of count/value to unseen callers.
_TIFFfree(data) on error (lines 66, 87) after TIFFReadDirEntryDataAndRealloc cannot be audited for double-free because the callee's out-pointer state on failure is unshown.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the fragment. The octet-counting content copy (memcpy at line 111) is provably bounded: octatesToCopy is clamped to buffLen (lines 103-105) and to iMaxLine - iMsg (lines 106-108), the total consumed equals min(iOctetsRemain, buffLen), so the size is non-negative, the source read is within buffLen, and iOctetsRemain never underflows. The octet-count accumulator cannot overflow 32-bit int (line 29 caps the multiply-add at 2,000,000,009). The digit-accumulation write at line 38 lacks the iMsg < iMaxLine cap enforced on sibling paths and can reach index iMaxLine+9, but pMsg's allocation size and iMaxLine's value are not declared in the fragment, so an out-of-bounds write cannot be confirmed; it is recorded in limitations along with the stuffing-mode saturation behavior and isdigit(-char) UB.

assumptions: pThis->iMsg and pThis->iOctetsRemain are int-like state mutated only at the shown lines (16, 30, 38, 60, 96, 108, 112, 113).

buffLen (line 3) is the number of valid bytes at *buff for the current call, per the parameter's name-implied contract; the caller advances *buff by one per call, which the -1 at line 114 accommodates.
The fragment's own caps treat iMaxLine as the maximum message size (guards at lines 66, 95, 106 and log text at lines 56-57, 75-76), but its value and pMsg's allocation are not shown.
limitations: Line 38 writes one byte per octet-count digit with no iMsg bound; when a stuffing message has saturated iMsg to iMaxLine (lines 95-96) and the next frame starts with up to 10 digits, indices iMaxLine..iMaxLine+9 are written, exceeding the code's own iMaxLine cap by up to 10 bytes. An OOB verdict (CWE-787) is not confirmable because pMsg's capacity and iMaxLine's value are not declared in the fragment.

Stuffing-mode saturation: after iMsg >= iMaxLine (line 66) the code submits a message per byte (lines 77-78), drops new content (line 95 false), and submits the same content again on the next delimiter (lines 86-87) without resetting iMsg (line 88); the resource/security impact depends on doSubmitMsg, whose body is not shown and which may itself reset iMsg.
isdigit((int)c) at lines 14 and 28 with c negative (bytes >= 0x80 under signed char) is undefined behavior per C11 7.4, but no memory-safety consequence is demonstrable in the fragment.

Across-call validity of the memcpy source at line 111 and the **buff read at line 10 depends on the unshown caller contract (buffLen as remaining length); the special case buffLen == 0 would make line 114 advance *buff by -1.
A wrap of the addition octatesToCopy + iMsg at line 106 would require operand magnitudes (>= 2^31) not derivable from the fragment.

verdict.summary: Attacker-controlled Tensor sizes are accumulated into the unsigned `size_t` `total_inputs_size` with no bound on per-tensor byte count or iteration count (lines 18-53); the `+=` at line 52 wraps for sufficiently large sums (e.g., 2 inputs of 2^63 bytes on 64-bit), and the wrapped value is passed as the size argument of `CreateNodeDef` at lines 67-68, corrupting the size-based growth decision used to reject oversized folded constants and enabling resource exhaustion (DoS).

evidence.reason: CWE-190 primary mechanism. `value->TotalBytes()` derives from the entry-point TensorProto (`raw_val` at line 31, `new Tensor(raw_val.dtype(), raw_val.tensor_shape())` at line 44); the guards at lines 20/25/30/32/39/45 admit only const, non-ref, valid-dtype tensors and impose no bound on byte count or on the number of `node.input()` iterations, so each term and the final sum retain the full unsigned `size_t` domain. The unsigned `+=` wraps modulo the type width: on 64-bit, two admitted inputs with `TotalBytes()==2^63` yield `2^63` then `0` (true total 2^64 bytes). The wrapped value is then consumed as a size argument at the CreateNodeDef call (lines 67-68), so the overflow corrupts a security-relevant size value rather than a dead variable.

Sink-consuming the corrupted value: `total_inputs_size` (wrapped down from the true input-byte total by the arithmetic at line 52) is passed as the size argument of `CreateNodeDef`. By its name and use in the shown code it is the input-size figure on which the folding path bases its output-size rejection (line 69 routes any failure to `*result_too_large = true` at line 70). For the full admitted set no shown guard bounds the sum, so an under-counted argument defeats the growth limit for attacker-crafted graphs and permits oversized folded constant nodes to be retained and materialized downstream, causing memory/resource exhaustion.

`value->TotalBytes()` returns the byte length of the materialized Tensor as `size_t`, per the shown usage at line 52; the internal formula is not part of the fragment.
