verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The equality guard at line 10 (tuple.size() == (size_t)ctx->num_outputs()) ties the data-derived tuple size exactly to the output count, and the strict loop bound at line 14 (i < tuple.size()) keeps every index in range for both tuple[i] and ctx->set_output(i, ...) at line 15.

assumptions: ctx->num_outputs() is non-negative and ctx->set_output(i, ...) requires 0 <= i < num_outputs(); this is the OpKernelContext API contract whose bound the fragment itself uses at line 10.
OP_REQUIRES_OK (line 3) returns control from Compute on failure per its standard macro semantics, so buf is valid at lines 4 and 7 after it.
Buffer::Tuple is a size-consistent container: tuple[i] is valid for i < tuple.size(), and tuple.size() is the element count (the fragment both queries size() and subscripts the same object).
buf->Get(&tuple) (line 7) fills the local tuple once; the same object is read by the guard and the loop with no intervening mutation.
limitations: The behavior of buf->Get (e.g., blocking when the buffer is empty) is callee-side and not visible in the fragment; the call site derives no attacker-controlled size or index argument, so no out-of-domain derivation is demonstrated.
Element types, possibly-NULL tensor contents inside the tuple, and any validation ctx->set_output performs beyond its index bound are not visible in the fragment.

If ctx->num_outputs() could be negative (contrary to the framework contract), the (size_t) cast at line 10 would change the value domain; no analysis conclusion depends on that case and it is not producible by the shown code.

verdict.summary: CreateNgrams at line 104 is called with ngram_width = data_length + 2*pad_width_ (line 101) after the early-exit only for data_length == 0 (line 95). pad_width_ is never validated in the shown code, so with preserve_short_ true and a short non-empty sequence whose ngram_widths_ all exceed its length, an unvalidated pad_width_ >= 1 makes the derived width exceed the item's data length; for the last batch item this reads 2*pad_width_ tstring elements past the end of the input data buffer (capacity via data->flat<tstring>().size(), line 18), a heap out-of-bounds read reachable with data=['a'], splits=[0,1], ngram_widths=[5], preserve_short_=true, pad_width_=1.

evidence.reason: CWE-125: the sink derives ngram_width at line 101 as data_length + 2*pad_width_ with pad_width_ unconstrained anywhere in the shown code (no guard on pad_width_ exists between its entry and this call). For the witness data size 1 (capacity anchor line 18: const int input_data_size = data->flat<tstring>().size()), splits=[0,1] (admitted by lines 22, 26, 27, 34), ngram_widths_=[5] (guard line 4 admits 5), preserve_short_=true, pad_width_=1: lines 63-64 admit (length=1>0, num_ngrams=0) so ngrams_splits_data[1]=1; the per-width loop (lines 79-85) adds 0 ngrams leaving output_start_idx==ngrams_splits_data[0] (line 91 admitted); data_length=1 passes line 95; line 101 yields ngram_width=3; ngram_width as the elements-per-ngram argument consumed by CreateNgrams reads input_data[0..2] while the buffer holds 1 tstring element, an over-read of 2 tstring objects immediately past the input tensor buffer on the last batch item (splits_vec(i+1)==input_data_size).

assumptions: Line 43 allocates ngrams_splits with splits->shape(), giving ngrams_splits_data a capacity of splits_vec_size elements (splits_vec.size(), line 19) - uses at lines 52, 57, 66, 73, 78, 91 stay within it for all inputs admitted by the shown guards.

Line 73 allocates ngrams with TensorShape({ngrams_splits_data[num_batch_items]}) so its element count equals the cumulative ngram count, which is consistent with CreateNgrams emitting one output element per ngram and consuming ngram_width input elements per ngram (also consistent with output_start_idx advancing by num_ngrams, line 84).
get_num_ngrams returns 0 when length < ngram_width; the fragment's own short-sequence logic at lines 63-64 and 86-94 depends on this.
SPLITS_TYPE is a signed integer type used in split arithmetic and TensorShape.
limitations: Callee bodies (CreateNgrams, get_num_ngrams) are not shown; semantics are inferred from parameter names and the fragment's own sizing logic. If CreateNgrams instead copied element-wise, the same trigger would produce an OOB write, but that variant is unconfirmable from the fragment.

Integer-truncation paths: input_data_size, splits_vec_size (lines 18-19) and num_batch_items (line 40) are declared int while the tensor sizes are int64; an OOB read of ngrams_splits_data[num_batch_items] at line 73 would require tensors with >2^31 split elements plus data size divisible by 2^32 to pass line 34, and the int counter at line 25 would invoke signed-overflow UB - treated as a multi-GiB-input robustness concern, not a confirmed finding.

Accumulation overflow at line 66 (ngrams_splits_data[i-1] + num_ngrams) would require sums beyond SPLITS_TYPE range that the shown guards do not rule out, but no realistic input reaches it; no confirmable impact.
Negative pad_width_ can make ngram_width negative at line 101; the callee's behavior on a negative width is unshown, so no finding is derived from that case.
The early-return path (lines 47-55) allocates output 0 with data->shape() and leaves it unwritten; potential uninitialized-data exposure is not confirmable as a security issue from this fragment.
No error/status-handling flaw was found: every OP_REQUIRES/OP_REQUIRES_OK return status is honored and leads to error return rather than continued execution.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable within the shown fragment. The code validates input shapes (dense_shape vector, indices matrix, values vector, default_value scalar, dense_shape non-empty) at lines 19-41, normalizes the done callback at lines 5-7, and forwards the four Tensor references unchanged to functor::SparseFillEmptyRows at lines 44-47 via OP_REQUIRES_OK_ASYNC. The fragment derives no index, size, length, capacity, or pointer argument at any sink, so no out-of-domain value or missing-check consequence can be proven to reach a dangerous operation in the shown code; the risk is confined to the unshown functor body.

assumptions: TensorShapeUtils::IsVector/IsMatrix/IsScalar implement their standard semantics (rank 1 / rank 2 / rank 0), which is the role implied by their names and by the checks' placement at lines 20, 24, 28, 33.
OP_REQUIRES_ASYNC and OP_REQUIRES_OK_ASYNC return from the function on failed conditions (lines 19-41, 44), so their guards establish the stated postconditions.
context->input(int) returns a valid, non-null Tensor reference per the OpKernelContext API; nothing in the fragment marks it nullable (lines 14-17).
FunctorType()(...) returns a Status, consumed by OP_REQUIRES_OK_ASYNC at line 44.
limitations: Missing consistency checks acknowledged at lines 37-38 (indices column count vs dense rank, values length vs indices row count, element-wise index bounds, and dtype equality with T/Tindex) could allow out-of-bounds or type-confusion inside functor::SparseFillEmptyRows for mismatched inputs such as indices_t.dim_size(1)==0 with a non-empty dense_shape_t; however, the consuming callee body is not shown and the fragment derives no index/size/length argument at the call site (lines 45-46), so no witness or out-of-domain value can be expressed using only the shown code.
Whether indices_t or values_t can be zero-length (dim_size 0 / NumElements 0) is left unconstrained by the shown checks; this matters only for the unshown functor, so it is not confirmable here.
A NULL context pointer would dereference at lines 14-17, but the framework contract supplies non-NULL, and no shown statement produces NULL, so this is a limitation, not a finding.

The stale TODO at lines 37-38 requesting a dense-rank>0 check is already satisfied by the NumElements()!=0 check at line 39 for the fragment's own logic; it only remains relevant for the unshown callee.

verdict.summary: pps_id is read into a signed 32-bit variable from the attacker-controlled bitstream and only checked against an upper bound (pps_id > 255), which admits all negative values. A crafted ue(v) value of 0xFFFFFFFF wraps pps_id to -1 and passes the guard, so `avc->pps[-1]` is computed and `si->pps->id = pps_id` performs an out-of-bounds heap write (CWE-787) before the pps array.

evidence.reason: Entry-point input pps_id (s32, line 3) is assigned from gf_bs_read_ue_log at line 10 (ue(v) domain [0, 2^32-1], wrapped to s32 range [-2^31, 2^31-1]). The only guard, `if (pps_id > 255)` at line 11, admits every negative value; no lower-bound check exists on the path. Witness: bitstream ue(v) = 0xFFFFFFFF -> pps_id == -1, passing line 11 (-1 > 255 is false), so line 13 computes &avc->pps[-1] and line 14 writes the `id` member one element before the array base. A negative index is outside the valid index domain [0, N-1] of any array, so the derived pointer is out-of-domain regardless of the unshown capacity of avc->pps. This is a confirmed out-of-bounds heap write: primary CWE-787.

Same negative index from the same witness (pps_id == -1, admitted by the line 11 guard) is dereferenced again: si->pps->slice_group_count reads memory before the avc->pps array. OOB read sharing the exact root cause of the line 14 write (CWE-787 primary; not an independent CWE).

assumptions: pps_id is declared `s32` (line 3) and the assignment at line 10 wraps an unsigned ue(v) value 0xFFFFFFFF to -1 (two's-complement semantics).
gf_bs_read_ue_log performs a standard Exp-Golomb ue(v) read returning the unsigned codeNum domain [0, 2^32-1].
avc->pps is an array of structs (from the `avc->pps[pps_id]` subscript and `->id` member use at lines 13-14); any array's valid index domain is [0, N-1], so -1 is out of bounds for every possible N.
The guard at line 11 is the only statement on the path from the pps_id read to the line 13/14 sink; no lower-bound check exists (lines 3-16).
limitations: The exact element count/capacity of avc->pps[] and avc->sps[] is not declared in the shown fragment; the negative-index claim does not depend on it (index -1 is out of domain for any capacity), but the precise affected memory extent is unquantifiable here.

The index `si->pps->sps_id + GF_SVC_SSPS_ID_SHIFT` (line 17) into avc->sps is not validated in the fragment, but sps_id's provenance, the value of GF_SVC_SSPS_ID_SHIFT, and the sps array capacity are all outside the shown code; demoted to limitation with no CWE.

Line 21 passes si->sps->log2_max_frame_num as a bit count to gf_bs_read_int_log; only a nonzero check (lines 18-19) is shown, no upper bound, and the callee's behavior on oversized counts is outside the fragment; demoted to limitation with no CWE.
slice_type (line 7) is only stored and guarded by `> 9` (line 8) with no sink in the fragment, so its signedness is not analyzed further.
The discarded return of gf_bs_read_ue_log at line 6 has no downstream use, so it is not a status-handling flaw in the shown code.

verdict.summary: Attacker-controlled int64 num_streams is read at line 15 and passed unvalidated as the stream-count parameter to the QuantileStreamResource constructor at lines 17-18. A negative value such as -1 (or an unbounded value like INT64_MAX) is admitted by every guard on the path and is out of domain for a size/count parameter, enabling uncontrolled allocation/resource exhaustion (DoS) when the resource consumes the count as a size.

evidence.snippet:
auto result =
        new QuantileStreamResource(epsilon, max_elements_, num_streams);
evidence.reason: num_streams is read at line 15 (int64_t num_streams = num_streams_t->scalar<int64>()();) from an entry-point tensor, and no shown statement constrains it, leaving the full int64 domain. The only guards in the fragment (epsilon > 0 at lines 9-11 and the status check at line 20) do not touch num_streams. Witness num_streams = -1 passes every guard and reaches this call site, where the third parameter is, by name and constructor semantics, a non-negative stream count/capacity; the shown code derives this size-like argument from input without a bound, so it is out of domain for the whole admitted set, permitting uncontrolled allocation/resource exhaustion (primary CWE-770; no CWE-195 secondary because the signed-to-unsigned conversion would occur only inside the unshown callee).

assumptions: kEpsilonName/kNumStreamsName denote graph inputs whose tensor values are attacker-controlled (entry-point provenance).
int64 and int64_t are the same 64-bit signed type, so the read at line 15 involves no representation change.
The QuantileStreamResource constructor's third parameter is a stream count/capacity consumed as a size (name-implied; callee body not shown).
limitations: QuantileStreamResource's body is not shown, so the exact downstream failure (huge allocation, bad_alloc, CHECK failure, or benign handling) cannot be anchored to a concrete line; confidence is capped accordingly.
max_elements_ is passed to the constructor without validation, but its provenance and type are not visible in the fragment, so no finding is asserted for it.
The safety of epsilon_t->scalar<float>()() and num_streams_t->scalar<int64>()() (dtype/shape) relies on TF op-registration invariants that are not shown.
On ALREADY_EXISTS, ownership of `result` is unref'd inside CreateResource per the comment at lines 2-3; that contract is not visible as code.
No buffer/string/crypto/file operations exist in the fragment, so byte-level and injection analyses do not apply.

verdict.summary: The fragment only validates tensor shapes (dense_shape vector, indices matrix, values vector, equal row counts, scalar default, non-empty dense_shape) and forwards the tensors to functor::SparseFillEmptyRows whose body is not shown. It performs no memory, string, crypto, or I/O operations itself, and the functor's return status is consumed via OP_REQUIRES_OK_ASYNC. Missing validations (dense rank > 0, indices column count vs dense rank, dense dimension positivity/bounds — acknowledged by the TODO on lines 43-44) could matter only inside the unshown functor, so no in-fragment sink confirms a vulnerability.

assumptions: context and the tensors returned by context->input(k) (lines 14-17) are framework-provided; the fragment contains no statement establishing NULL/invalid values for them.
After the guard on line 45 (dense_shape_t.NumElements() != 0) and line 20 (IsVector), dense_shape is a rank-1 tensor with at least one element; its element values remain unconstrained.
done is guaranteed to be a callable after lines 5-7, so its uses in the OP_REQUIRES_* macros (lines 23, 27, 31, 37, 42, 47) and the functor call (line 52) are safe on that axis.
limitations: The fragment never checks dense rank > 0, indices_t.dim_size(1) against dense_shape_t.NumElements(), positivity/bounds of dense_shape entries, or bounds of indices coordinates (the TODO at lines 43-44 acknowledges missing checks). Any memory-safety consequence of such malformed inputs would occur inside functor::SparseFillEmptyRows<Device, T, Tindex>, whose body is not shown (call at lines 50-53); no out-of-domain index/size/length argument is derived by the shown code at that call site, so no CWE can be confirmed.
No capacity is declared, allocated, or indexed in the fragment, so no boundary or off-by-one claim is groundable in the shown code.

The fragment's own shape guards (lines 20-47) do not protect the unshown callee's internal invariants; the not-vulnerable verdict applies only to operations visible in this fragment and is capped accordingly.

verdict.summary: arg_index is derived from the size_t node count by an implicit size_t-to-int conversion (L12) with no upper-bound check anywhere in the fragment, and ++arg_index (L46) overflows once the counter reaches INT_MAX. For any result_.nodes.size() >= 2^31 (or dtypes.size() large enough to drive the counter to INT_MAX), the index truncates/overflows and the corrupted value is stored into the built graph's argument-index metadata by AddItem at L14 and L17-18 before the equality guard at L19 aborts the function. This is an integer overflow corrupting a security-relevant index/position value (CWE-190); no in-fragment memory-safety sink is confirmed, hence low severity.

evidence.reason: Implicit narrowing size_t-to-int of result_.nodes.size(). The fragment (L9, L16, L19, L25, L29, L37, L40) imposes no upper bound on result_.nodes.size(), whose residual range is the full size_t domain [0, SIZE_MAX], so any value >= 2^31 truncates (implementation-defined; e.g. 2^32 -> 0). The corrupted int is then consumed as argument/node index metadata at AddItem (L14, L17-18) before the only relevant guard at L19 fires, and the same counter overflows at ++arg_index (L46) once it reaches INT_MAX. Primary CWE-190 (integer overflow of a security-relevant count/index).

First sink of the truncated arg_index: with witness result_.nodes.size() = 2^32 and dtypes.size() = 1 (both admitted by the L9 guard, which excludes only 0), L12 yields arg_index = 0 and this call stores the wrong argument index into result_ metadata. No guard exists between L12 and this consumption; the L19 check runs only afterward and returns an error without undoing the write.

Second pre-guard sink of the corrupted index: for the same witness (nodes.size() = 2^32), the per-dtype AddItem at i = 0 stores arg_index = 0 instead of the true node position 2^32; the loop condition L16 admits i = 0 and the L19 guard has not yet executed. Consumes the value derived at L12 before any protective check.

Signed overflow site: with dtypes.size() = 2^31 (admitted by L9, which sets only a lower bound of 1) and entry nodes.size() = 0, arg_index tracks result_.nodes.size() (AddNode adds one node per call per the L15 comment and the L19 invariant), so the increment at iteration i = 2^31 - 2 evaluates INT_MAX + 1, which is signed integer overflow (UB, CWE-190). The next iteration then stores the wrapped value via AddItem at L17-18 before L19 returns an error.

assumptions: LP64 target: size_t is 64-bit unsigned and int is 32-bit signed two's complement, so the L12 conversion truncates values >= 2^31 (implementation-defined modulo-2^32 wrap) and L46 overflows at INT_MAX.

AddNode(name) adds exactly one node per call (implied by its name and the L15 comment 'Creates dtypes.size() nodes in the graph'), so arg_index and result_.nodes.size() advance in lockstep and the L19 invariant holds until the overflow; if AddNode added a different count, L19 would abort even earlier.
DataTypeVector::size() and result_.nodes.size() both return size_t; DataTypeVector (L6) is the accessed object whose size the L16 loop condition bounds.
The L19 comparison promotes the int operand to size_t, so a negative/truncated arg_index can never equal a large real node count.
limitations: Reachability of a nodes.size()/dtypes.size() value at or above 2^31 is not demonstrated inside the fragment: no shown statement produces 2^31 nodes or dtypes elements, so the witness magnitude rests on domain-range analysis and the finding is rated low severity with confidence 0.6.

The L19-L23 guard aborts the function before the truncated arg_index reaches AddAttr("index", arg_index, gnode) at L36; the corrupt value is consumed only by AddItem (L14, L17-18), stores into result_ on an error path, and the fragment performs no further security-relevant operation after the error return.
AddNode's return value (L28) is dereferenced at L29-L42 without a NULL check; the fragment contains no statement that can make AddNode return NULL, so a NULL-dereference (CWE-476) is unconfirmed.
CWE-681 is the root conversion mechanism (size_t-to-int narrowing) but is folded into the single CWE-190 finding rather than reported as an independent secondary CWE.

arg_def.name() is unconstrained, and node names built by StrCat/StrAppend (L17, L26) could collide or be arbitrarily large; no injection/log/query sink or fragment-visible security decision consumes these names, so this is not a finding.
Resource-exhaustion volume (a 2^31-element dtypes vector or 2^31 AddNode allocations, CWE-400) is not attacker-triggerable within the shown code and is not reported.
dtypes[i] accesses at L18, L29, L34, L45 are in-bounds for every i admitted by L16 (max i = dtypes.size()-1 < dtypes.size()); no OOB read/write (CWE-125/CWE-787) is present.

verdict.summary: Heap buffer overflow in DecodePngV2's DT_FLOAT decode path: decode.channels (populated at line 5 from attacker-controlled PNG data) is never validated by any shown check, so for a crafted PNG with decode.channels = 17, width = 2^27-1 and height = 4 (both admitted by the guard at lines 18-20), the 32-bit expressions at lines 77 and 81 overflow: new uint16[...] wraps to a ~1.07 GB buffer while CommonFinishDecode's per-row write is ~4.56 GB, corrupting the heap on the first row. Same wrapped-stride derivation reaches the UINT8/UINT16 sinks at lines 63 and 70 (CWE-190 -> CWE-787).

evidence.reason: Primary CWE-787 sink. The row-pitch argument `decode.channels * width * sizeof(uint16)` is derived from unvalidated `decode.channels` (taken from CommonInitDecode at line 5; no shown check constrains it) and the int `width` admitted by the guard at lines 18-20 (admitted set [1, 2^27-1], w*h < 2^29). Witness: channels=17, width=2^27-1, height=4 passes every guard condition (lines 18-20 verify numerically); then 17*134217727 overflows 32-bit int to -2013265937 and promotes to ~1.84e19, and the decoder's real row bytes 134217727*17*2 = 4,563,402,718 exceed the buffer capacity `new uint16[height * width * decode.channels]` (line 77), which wraps to 536,870,844 elements (1,073,741,688 bytes). OOB write of ~3.5 GB on the first row.

evidence.snippet:
std::unique_ptr<uint16[]> buffer(
          new uint16[height * width * decode.channels]);
evidence.reason: Secondary CWE-190 root cause. The allocation size `height * width * decode.channels` is computed entirely in 32-bit int arithmetic: for the guard-admitted witness (width=134217727, height=4, decode.channels=17 admitted since lines 18-20 never test channels), 4*134217727*17 = 9,126,805,436 wraps to 536,870,844 elements, so the buffer is undersized relative to the write at the line 80-82 sink by a factor of ~17, corrupting a security-relevant allocation size consumed by the subsequent decode write.

Same confirmed mechanism on the DT_UINT16 branch: the row-pitch argument derives from the unvalidated `decode.channels` residual range, and for channels >= 16 with guard-admitted width (lines 18-20) the 32-bit product wraps (e.g. channels=17, width=2^27-1 gives 17*134217727 > INT_MAX -> wraps to -2013265937, then ~1.84e19 after promotion), which is an out-of-domain capacity argument for the destination write at this call site; execution reaches here only if the allocate_output at lines 35-38 succeeds, otherwise OP_REQUIRES_OK returns before the sink.

Same confirmed mechanism on the DT_UINT8 branch: the per-row byte count `decode.channels * width * sizeof(uint8)` uses the unvalidated `decode.channels` residual range; for channels >= 16 and guard-admitted width (lines 18-20), the 32-bit multiplication `decode.channels * width` overflows (e.g. 17*134217727 = 2,281,701,359 > INT_MAX), producing a wrapped value out of the domain of the destination-capacity argument at this call site, so the decoder write can overrun the tensor allocated at lines 32-38.

assumptions: Guard at lines 18-20 admits exactly width,height in [1, 2^27-1] with width*height <= 2^29-1; verified by the fragment's own arithmetic (int64 total_size at lines 16-17, equality probes at 18-19).
Output tensor element count is height*width*decode.channels per TensorShape({...}) at lines 33 and 38; intended FLOAT buffer capacity is the new-expression at line 77.
OP_REQUIRES_OK at lines 30-33/35-38 guarantees `output` is non-null before use at lines 61-63, 68-70, 80-82, 92.

Standard C++ semantics: `sizeof(uint8)`/`sizeof(uint16)` are size_t (64-bit) and are promoted only after the first `decode.channels * width` multiplication completes in the operand type; `int` is 32-bit two's complement on the target platform.
data_type_ branches are mutually exclusive; DT_FLOAT path is the primary witness path, DT_UINT8/DT_UINT16 share the same derivation.
limitations: The declared type of png::DecodeContext::channels and the internal contract of png::CommonInitDecode are not shown; the overflow arithmetic assumes a 32-bit-or-narrower channel field. If the unshown decoder provably bounded decode.channels to <= 4, the overflow would be unreachable, but no such shown statement exists, and per the analysis rules that unseen invariant cannot justify a safe verdict either.

The concrete FLOAT-path witness requires the wrapped ~1.07 GB allocation at line 77 to succeed; UINT8/UINT16 witnesses require the fully-sized (9-18 GB) output tensor allocation to succeed, otherwise OP_REQUIRES_OK returns before the sink.

Exact callee write behavior of png::CommonFinishDecode (that the row-pitch argument is used as the destination per-row capacity) is inferred from the parameter name and its use as a length/capacity; the callee body is not shown.
A huge allocation failing with uncaught std::bad_alloc from line 77, and allocation-volume DoS generally, are environment-dependent, single-shot robustness concerns, not confirmed findings.
All loop/parser-position analysis is out of scope: the fragment contains no loops; iteration occurs only inside unshown callees.

verdict.summary: xQueueGenericCreate computes the queue storage size as ( size_t )( uxQueueLength * uxItemSize ) at line 14, performing the multiplication in UBaseType_t before widening, so the product can wrap for in-domain inputs (e.g., 65536*65536 -> 0 on 32-bit UBaseType_t). The only overflow guard is a configASSERT (line 17) whose runtime enforcement is not visible in the fragment; when vacuous, the wrapped size reaches pvPortMalloc at line 28, producing a heap allocation undersized by up to 2^32 bytes, and the undersized storage is then handed to prvInitialiseNewQueue at line 46 with the full nominal length/item size, enabling heap corruption.

evidence.snippet: pxNewQueue = ( Queue_t * ) pvPortMalloc( sizeof( Queue_t ) + xQueueSizeInBytes ); /*lint !e9087 !e9079 see comment above. */
evidence.reason: CWE-190: xQueueSizeInBytes is produced at line 14 as ( size_t )( uxQueueLength * uxItemSize ) — the wrap happens in UBaseType_t before the widening cast, so for uxQueueLength = uxItemSize = 65536 (both in the full residual domain [0, 2^W-1], no enforced constraint in the shown code; line 9's assert admits 65536) the product wraps to 0 and xQueueSizeInBytes becomes 0. The only overflow check, configASSERT at line 17, is a macro whose enforcement is not visible in the fragment — when compiled out the wrapped value passes to this allocation-size sink, so pvPortMalloc allocates sizeof( Queue_t ) instead of sizeof( Queue_t ) + 2^32, undersized by exactly 2^32 bytes (witness B on 16-bit UBaseType_t: 400*400 wraps to 28928, shortfall 131072). The resulting undersized storage region is then passed with the full uxQueueLength/uxItemSize to prvInitialiseNewQueue at line 46, so queue storage is consumed beyond the allocation, causing heap corruption.

assumptions: UBaseType_t is an unsigned integer type of width W (and size_t of width S); neither width is defined in the fragment. Witnesses are given for the standard W=32 and W=16 FreeRTOS port widths; the overflow mechanism exists for any width for which in-domain input pairs satisfy uxQueueLength*uxItemSize >= 2^W.

prvInitialiseNewQueue is, by name and by the roles of its arguments (uxQueueLength, uxItemSize, pucQueueStorage), the initializer that lays out uxQueueLength items of uxItemSize bytes in the storage region; its body is not shown.
The undersized-allocation path requires pvPortMalloc to succeed; the shown NULL branch (lines 48-52) is handled correctly and is irrelevant to this witness.
limitations: configASSERT's definition/enforcement is not shown. If the platform compiles it as an enforcing assertion, the line 17 check catches the wrapping witness and the undersized allocation is not reached — instead the same attacker-supplied values produce a reachable assertion abort (CWE-617 candidate), which is also not confirmable from the fragment. The overflow-to-allocation path is confirmed for builds in which configASSERT is vacuous (the common production configuration), but the fragment itself does not establish either behavior.

The actual out-of-bounds WRITE occurs inside prvInitialiseNewQueue (line 46), whose body is not shown; the storage capacity it receives (xQueueSizeInBytes == 0 for the witness) is undersized by the full nominal product, but the write itself is not observable in the fragment, so CWE-787 is not independently confirmed and is not included in the cwe array.
A zero uxQueueLength is rejected only if line 9's configASSERT is enforced; a degenerate zero-length queue otherwise follows, which is not separately confirmed as a vulnerability.
A second-order overflow of sizeof( Queue_t ) + xQueueSizeInBytes is subsumed by the primary UBaseType_t product wrap and is not analyzed separately.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable from the fragment alone. The visible guards (lines 18-20) bound width and height to [1, 2^27-1] and width*height to < 2^29, which keeps the int arithmetic in lines 63/70/77/81 in-range for the channel counts those guards are intended to cover. However, decode.channels is never validated in the shown code and its declared type/signedness is not visible, so the integer-overflow/OOB candidates at lines 63/70/77/81/88-92 cannot be completed: the wrap cannot be shown to occur in the shown types, and the sink semantics of png::CommonFinishDecode and feasibility of the preceding multi-GB output allocations are outside the fragment. All allocation and decoder return statuses are checked before use; error paths return gracefully, with only a single-shot decoder-context leak on the failing-op_type_ paths (lines 38-53 vs 55) that does not compound.

assumptions: OP_REQUIRES/OP_REQUIRES_OK abort the Compute call and return on a false condition; continuation past line 56 therefore implies status.ok() and a valid non-null output, which is the visible guarantee for the dereferences at lines 62, 69, and 92.
allocate_output success implies the returned Tensor is valid for the requested shape; the fragment checks the status at lines 55-56 before any use of output.

decode.width and decode.height are integer fields whose casts to int and comparisons against their int64 form (lines 14-18) imply the truncation check at line 18 is meaningful only for 32-bit unsigned-style values; the exact declared types are not shown.
sizeof(uint8) == 1 and sizeof(uint16) == 2 throughout lines 63/70/81.

TensorShape dimension arithmetic is int64, so the output tensor sizes at lines 32/35 do not itself overflow int32; the int arithmetic of concern is at lines 63/70/77/81 where operands are int (width, height) and decode.channels of unshown type.
data_type_ and op_type_ are internal member state; exactly one data_type_ branch (58/65/72) executes per call.
limitations: decode.channels is never constrained between line 5 and its sinks (lines 32, 35, 63, 70, 77, 81, 88, 92), and its declared type/signedness is not shown: the integer-overflow candidates (e.g., width=2^27-1, height=2, channels=17 passing the guard at 18-20) cannot be confirmed because the wrap cannot be shown to occur in the shown types, and a signed vs unsigned field flips the result (unsigned yields in-range arguments and no OOB). Demoted CWE-190/CWE-787/CWE-125 candidates.

png::CommonFinishDecode behavior (how the size argument at 63/70/81 is consumed and how many bytes per row are actually written) is callee-internal and not visible; byte-account exactness of lines 63/70 rests on the decode-to-buffer contract rather than shown code.

The DT_FLOAT branch OOB-read candidate (lines 77, 88-92) additionally requires the preceding output-tensor allocation (lines 34-35, height*width*channels floats) to succeed at sizes that would make the int product at line 77 wrap; that feasibility is not established in the fragment.

Attainability of decode.channels values beyond the PNG channel range is provided by png::CommonInitDecode internals, which are outside the fragment; no shown statement bounds channels positively or negatively.
A negative decode.channels producing a TensorShape dim CHECK failure (CWE-617) has no shown producer and is unconfirmed.

The DecodeGif + DT_FLOAT path (4-D output at line 32 vs output->tensor<float,3>() at line 92) is unconfirmed: the op_type_/data_type_ combination reachability and Tensor::tensor rank-check semantics are not visible.

On failing op_type_ paths (DecodeBmp/DecodeAndCropJpeg, lines 38-53), png::CommonFreeDecode at line 55 is skipped, leaking the decoder context on an already-failing path; a single-shot leak with no attacker-controlled volume, not a finding.
No loops exist in the fragment, so no loop termination, parser-position, or ReDoS/algorithmic-complexity claims apply.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds write via out_mat.col(out_offset): the batch loop (line 85) iterates over input_size[0] while the output tensor has only output_size[0] batches (lines 41-42), so with unvalidated pooling_ratio_[0] > 1 (line 23) b >= output_size[0] yields col indices at or beyond the output tensor's column count (lines 60-61). DCHECK_GT at line 24 is debug-only and admits the trigger values.

evidence.reason: out_offset (lines 96-97) = (b*output_size[1]+hs)*output_size[2]+ws with b drawn from [0, input_size[0]) by line 85, but the output tensor's column capacity is output_size[2]*output_size[1]*output_size[0] (Map at lines 60-61; allocation shape at lines 41-42). pooling_ratio_[0] (line 23) is unvalidated in the fragment, so ratio > 1 makes output_size[0] < input_size[0] and b = output_size[0] is admitted; witness dims [4,4,4,1], ratio [2,2,2,1], seqs [0,4]/[0,4] give b=2, hs=0, ws=0, out_offset = 8 = cols, so col(8) writes one element past the 8-element output buffer (read-modify-write via cwiseMax), an out-of-domain column index at the CWE-787 sink.

assumptions: tensor_in dims originate from externally supplied op input (entry-point), guarded only by dims()==4 at line 10.
allocate_output results are success-checked by OP_REQUIRES_OK (lines 39-43, 45-49, 51-55), so output tensors are valid when reached.

Eigen column-major Map col(j) accesses flat offsets j*rows..j*rows+rows-1, so a col index equal to or above the map's column count reads/writes past the mapped buffer (capacity grounded at lines 41-42 and 60-61).
GeneratePoolingSequence returns size-2 vectors [0,4] on the witness path; the fragment imposes no shown constraint on the returned size beyond the loop use at lines 87/95.
limitations: If the op's constructor (not shown) validates pooling_ratio_[0]==1 and pooling_ratio_[3]==1 as stock TensorFlow does, the batch-mismatch OOB cannot trigger; that invariant is outside the fragment and cannot be used in either direction.

int64-to-int truncation of dim_size at line 16 and signed int overflow in the Map column products (lines 58, 61) can corrupt logical shapes, but no downstream out-of-domain access was demonstrated in the fragment (col arithmetic with correct rows stays inside the flat buffer when columns wrap).
Debug-only DCHECK_GT abort at line 24 (output_size==0 via ratio >= dim or ratio 0/inf) is a candidate CWE-617 only in debug builds; build flags are not shown, so it is demoted.

If GeneratePoolingSequence returned an empty vector, height_cum_seq.size()-1 at lines 87/95 would underflow (size_t) and lines 89/91/99/101 would index out of bounds; the helper's contract is not shown, so this is unconfirmable.
pooling_ratio_ indexed at line 23 assumes a >=4-element member vector, which the fragment does not establish.
PRNG seeding (line 31) uses internal seeds for pooling-sequence generation and is not a security-sensitive entropy sink.

verdict.summary: gf_text_get_utf8_line converts the fgets line into the fixed 2048-byte stack buffer szLineConv with an unbounded write cursor j: for unicode_type=0, a line of bytes >=0xC0 doubles the output (1 input byte -> 2 writes via the branch at line 17 plus the fall-through write at line 53), so lengths >=1025 write at indices 2048-2050 against the 2048-byte capacity declared at line 5; the subsequent strcpy(szLine, szLineConv) at line 57 can additionally overflow the caller's lineSize-byte buffer (capacity established by memset/fgets at lines 8-9). A separate UTF-16 byte-swap loop (lines 68-75) reads past szLine when a line ends with its NUL at lineSize-1 without a two-NUL terminator inside the buffer.

evidence.reason: Primary finding, CWE-787. szLineConv's capacity is 2048 bytes (char szLineConv[2048]; at line 5, valid indices 0..2047). File bytes entering via gf_fgets (lines 9-10) retain len in [0, lineSize-1] with lineSize an unconstrained u32 (line 1, no cap anywhere). Witness: unicode_type=0 (admitted by line 11), lineSize=1026, line of 1025 x 0xFF: every byte passes line 15 (0xFF&0x80!=0) and line 17 (0xFF&0xC0=0xC0!=0x80; final byte's successor is NUL, 0x00&0xC0=0!=0x80), so each byte writes twice (lines 18-20 then this statement); j reaches 2048 at i=1024 and this statement writes szLineConv[2048] and szLineConv[2049], past the 2047 max index. No guard in lines 11-58 compares j against 2047.

Same root cause, CWE-787. With the Witness A path (unicode_type=0, lineSize=1026, 1025 x 0xFF) j=2050 at loop exit, so this terminator write hits index 2050, and even Witness B (unicode_type=1 admitted by line 11, lineSize=2049, 2048-byte ASCII line) leaves j=2048, writing index 2048 -- both beyond capacity 2048 declared at line 5. No length guard precedes this statement.

CWE-787 over the caller's buffer: szLine's capacity is lineSize, established by memset(szLine, 0, sizeof(char)*lineSize) at line 8 and gf_fgets(szLine, lineSize, txt_in) at line 9. Witness A' (unicode_type=0, lineSize=1024, 600 x 0xFF): every byte passes line 17 so the conversion emits 1200 bytes plus the NUL at line 56 = 1201 bytes (still within szLineConv), and this strcpy writes 1201 bytes into the 1024-byte szLine, a 177-byte overrun; no size check exists between the conversion loop and this copy.

CWE-125 OOB read. szLine's capacity is lineSize per lines 8-9. Witness C: unicode_type=2 (little-endian #else path, line 64), lineSize=4, file 'a\0b' (3 bytes, no newline) so gf_fgets leaves NUL at index 3. After swaps at i=0 (szLine[0]=0x61!=0) and i=2 (szLine[2]=0x62!=0), both admitted by this guard's failure path, i=4, and this statement reads szLine[4] and szLine[5], both beyond capacity 4; if the OOB bytes are nonzero the loop continues with OOB reads/writes at lines 71-74. Nothing in the fragment guarantees zeros past index lineSize-1 (line 8 zeroes exactly lineSize bytes).

assumptions: gf_fgets behaves like standard fgets: it writes at most lineSize-1 characters plus NUL into szLine (consistent with the memset at line 8, the NULL check at line 10, and strlen at line 13).
szLine's buffer capacity is exactly lineSize bytes, as used by memset (line 8) and gf_fgets (line 9) in the shown code.
szLineConv's capacity is exactly 2048 bytes per its declaration at line 5.
The analysis takes the little-endian preprocessor path (#else at line 64) for the byte-swap branch; the big-endian path (line 62) would instead swap for unicode_type==3.
limitations: The terminator write at line 79 (szLineConv[i] = 0) and the copy at line 80 could be OOB if gf_utf8_wcstombs returns a byte count of 2048, but that depends on the callee's exact return/termination contract, which is not visible in the fragment.
The swap-loop OOB write at lines 71-73 requires non-zero stack garbage beyond the buffer; the OOB read at line 70 is unconditional for the stated witness.
j (u32) would wrap for lineSize >= 2^31, but the szLineConv overflow already occurs at len=1025, so the wrap is not a separate root cause.
unicode_type values outside {0..3} are not validated by the fragment, but no separately confirmed sink was derivable for them.

verdict.summary: The only memory-read sinks (pj_memcpy at lines 30 and 35) are fully protected by the bounds guard at line 26, which admits only p + 4 <= max and excludes p + 4 > max; the two 2-byte reads consume exactly the 4 admitted bytes (max index p+3). Both get_name_len and get_name statuses are checked. Remaining concerns (unchecked pj_pool_alloc result, name_len+4 arithmetic, name_part_len-driven pointer arithmetic, and the int cast of p-start) cannot be confirmed from the fragment's own statements and are recorded as limitations.

assumptions: max (line 3) is the one-past-the-end pointer of the packet, as used by the comparison `p + 4 > max` at line 26.

get_name_len/get_name (lines 10/19) return consistent, non-negative lengths on success and write at most the allocated `name_len + 4` bytes into `q->name.ptr`; this contract is not visible in the fragment.
pj_pool_alloc (line 15) returns a valid non-NULL pointer; the fragment does not mark it nullable.
limitations: Unchecked pj_pool_alloc result at line 15: a NULL dereference inside the unshown get_name (line 19) is not producible from any statement in the fragment (library pointer treated as non-NULL), so CWE-476 is unconfirmed.

Integer overflow of `name_len + 4` (line 15) and out-of-range `start + name_part_len` pointer arithmetic (line 23) cannot be witnessed: the fragment neither caps `name_len`/`name_part_len` nor shows a path to INT_MAX or to a negative value.
Truncation at `*parsed_len = (int)(p - start)` (line 39) requires a packet span greater than INT_MAX, which no shown statement establishes.
UB in evaluating `p + 4` (line 26) when `p` is already beyond the object is theoretical here: the guard still prevents the reads, and no concrete guard-passing witness leads to a memory error.
Loop termination, read-position invariants, and write bounds inside the unshown callees get_name_len/get_name are out of scope for this fragment.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable from the fragment. The one allocation is exactly sized: length = strlen(argv[4]) + 1 + strlen(argv[5]) + 1 (line 42) equals the bytes written by the size-bounded snprintf at line 46 for every finite input, and malloc's result is NULL-checked (line 44). Every argv/argv_eol index access (lines 20, 21, 24, 25, 29, 30, 31, 35, 37, 87, 89, 90, 93, 94) is guarded by visible strict-inequality argc checks that keep the index in [0, argc-1]. Two residual concerns are unconfirmable under the evidence rules and are recorded in limitations: (1) line 30's argv[arg_start+1] + 1 points one byte past the NUL if that token is empty and is printed via %s at line 99, but neither the production of empty tokens nor the backing buffer capacity is visible in the fragment, so an OOB read cannot be demonstrated; (2) length is int while the strlen sum is size_t (lines 42-43), but any truncation either makes malloc fail (NULL-checked) or only truncates snprintf output, with no security-relevant downstream corruption in the fragment.

assumptions: argv[i] and argv_eol[i] are non-NULL, NUL-terminated strings for every 0 <= i < argc (IRC protocol callback framework contract); the fragment's own guards only constrain i < argc via argc comparisons.
irc_nick_set_host(ptr_nick, str_host) duplicates str_host before the free at line 48, as implied by the shown free immediately after the call.
IRC_PROTOCOL_MIN_ARGS(5) (line 8, macro body not shown) guarantees at least 5 arguments; it is moot because line 11 already requires argc >= 8 before argv[3..7] are used.

weechat_printf_date_tags is a bounded formatter driven by the literal format at line 83; all 18 input-derived arguments (lines 87-101) are %s values, so no format-string content can reach the format grammar.
limitations: Empty-token hopcount pointer (CWE-125, unconfirmed): with argc >= arg_start+2, argv[arg_start][0] != ':' and argv[arg_start+1] == "", line 30 computes argv[arg_start+1] + 1, a pointer one byte past the token's NUL, which is then read as %s at line 99. This is not a confirmed OOB read because (a) no shown statement establishes that the parser can produce an empty argv entry (a degenerate framework value is at most a range claim), and (b) the capacity/layout of the token's backing buffer is not identifiable from the fragment, which the OOB standard requires.

Int truncation (CWE-190/CWE-681, unconfirmed): length (int, line 4) receives the size_t sum at line 42; reaching a sum > INT_MAX needs ~2 GiB strings, a magnitude no shown statement establishes as reachable, and every wrap outcome is safe in-fragment (malloc(size_t from negative int) fails and is caught at line 44; a small-positive wrap only truncates snprintf output at line 46). No corrupted security-relevant value is consumed downstream.
Unchecked strdup at line 67: on allocation failure ptr_nick->realname becomes NULL, but no code in the fragment dereferences it afterward, so no security-relevant operation runs on the failure state.

NULL-dereference hypotheses for server/argv/argv_eol are not confirmable: the fragment contains no NULL producer for them, and framework-provided pointers are treated as non-NULL absent a shown nullable contract.
Discarded return values of snprintf (line 46) and weechat_printf_date_tags (line 78): neither outcome affects a decision; snprintf is size-bounded regardless.

verdict.summary: The ELF parser maps the untrusted file with capacity st.st_size (mmap, line 23) and then dereferences header-derived offsets, counts, and string pointers with only a start-pointer check (validated_offset, line 183): shdr[e_shstrndx] (line 177), shdr[i]/phdr[i] loops (lines 182, 269), the strlen scan (line 257) and the dyn loop with an unbounded count (lines 349-357) all read beyond the mapped capacity on crafted input (CWE-125), and the .dynamic/.dynstr search leaves the dynstr/dynamic indices uninitialized when no matching section exists, using them as array indices (line 349) (CWE-457).

evidence.reason: CWE-125: name is derived at line 182 as elf_map + shstrtab.sh_offset + shdr[i].sh_name, both file-controlled 32-bit values with full residual domain. The only guard, validated_offset at line 183, admits any start pointer in [elf_map, elf_map+st.st_size) but constrains neither NUL termination nor the scan end. With capacity st.st_size = 52 (mmap, line 23), shstrtab.sh_offset = 0, sh_name = 51, byte 51 = 'A', the guard admits name = elf_map+51 (51 < 52); strlen then reads byte 51 and byte 52, i.e., index == capacity, producing an out-of-bounds read of at least 1 byte (unbounded if no NUL follows).

CWE-125: e_shoff (line 175) and e_shstrndx are entry-point values with no shown bound against st.st_size. Witness: 52-byte ELFCLASS32 file with e_shoff = 52 and e_shstrndx = 0; the struct read shdr[0] begins at byte offset 52, i.e., index == capacity (capacity = st.st_size from mmap, line 23), so the read is out of bounds (at least 40 bytes for the aggregate copy).

CWE-125: phdr = elf_map + ehdr->e_phoff (line 176) and e_phnum are unvalidated against st.st_size. The loop guard at line 268 (i < e_phnum) admits i = 0. Witness: 52-byte file with e_phoff = 52, e_phnum = 1; phdr[0].p_type is read at byte 52, i.e., index == capacity (capacity from mmap, line 23) — out-of-bounds read.

CWE-457: dynamic is declared at line 335 and assigned only at line 343 when a section named ".dynamic" is found (dynstr likewise at line 340). For any ELFCLASS32 file with e_shnum = 0 or without a ".dynamic"-named section, the loop at lines 337-345 never assigns, leaving dynamic indeterminate, and line 349 uses it as an index into shdr — uninitialized-use UB whose result is then used as a file offset (lines 349-350, 366), with undefined out-of-bounds consequences.

evidence.snippet:
name = elf_map + shdr[dynstr].sh_offset + dyn[i].d_un.d_val;
                    snprintf(value, 50, "Shared library: [%s]", name);
evidence.reason: CWE-125: dyn[i].d_un.d_val is a file-controlled 32-bit value (read at 357/358) and shdr[dynstr].sh_offset is unvalidated; neither is bounded against st.st_size. Witness: .dynstr with sh_offset = 0, a DT_NEEDED entry (d_tag attacker-set) with d_val = 0xFFFFFFF0, count = 1 (sh_size = 8, line 350); the loop guard at 354 admits i = 0; line 366 yields name = elf_map + 0xFFFFFFF0, far beyond the map, and the %s at line 367 reads from it — out-of-bounds read.

CWE-125: count = shdr[dynamic].sh_size / sizeof(Elf32_Dyn) (line 350) is unvalidated, up to 0xFFFFFFFF/8 ≈ 536,870,911, and the dyn base (line 349) is unvalidated. The loop guard i < count (line 354) admits indexes i whose byte offset shdr[dynamic].sh_offset + i*8 exceeds capacity st.st_size (mmap, line 23); e.g., sh_offset = 96, sh_size = 16, capacity 100 → i = 1 reads bytes 104-111 out of bounds.

assumptions: Line numbers are 1-based relative to the fragment as presented, starting at 'int parse(char *elf) {'.

Elf32_Ehdr/Shdr/Phdr/Dyn layouts and field widths follow the ELF ABI (e_shnum, e_phnum, e_shstrndx are 16-bit; offsets/sizes are 32-bit; sh_name is the first member of Elf32_Shdr; sizeof(Elf32_Shdr)=40; sizeof(Elf32_Dyn)=8), since the fragment references these library types without defining them.

validated_offset(name, elf_map, elf_map+st.st_size) semantics are inferred from its call-site arguments: nonzero marks the start pointer invalid; it admits start pointers inside the mapped range and does not, per any shown statement, validate NUL termination or the full string extent.
MODE = get_elf_class(elf) (line 10) is treated as entry-derived with no fragment-visible constraint beyond use at line 30; the witnesses assume it returns ELFCLASS32 for the crafted files.
The mmap'd object's capacity is st.st_size bytes per line 23; page-rounding/zero-fill behavior of mmap is not part of the fragment and is not used to justify any verdict.
limitations: The strcpy truncation write at line 258 goes out of bounds only when strlen(name) > 15 depends on bytes beyond the mapped file (which the attacker cannot set inside the fragment); it was therefore not reported as a confirmed CWE-787 write, though it accompanies the confirmed CWE-125 strlen read at line 257.

Reads of ehdr fields (lines 36-169) for files smaller than the ELF header share the same missing-minimum-size root cause but are not separately evidenced; reachability requires get_elf_class (unshown) to return ELFCLASS32 for a short file.

Integer wraparound of shstrtab.sh_offset + sh_name (32-bit) can point name inside the map while the intended string is out of bounds; the resulting start pointer still passes validated_offset, so no independently confirmed sink is derived.
flag2str_sh/flag2str (lines 262, 314) and the INFO/PRINT_* macros have unshown bodies; any overflow or format behavior inside them is not confirmable from the fragment.
The 64-bit branch mirrors all reported 32-bit findings; it is not separately evidenced.

Real mmap rounds the mapping to page granularity, so several of the OOB reads above may land in zero-filled page slack and not fault; per the fragment-only rule, capacity is st.st_size (line 23), and the out-of-bounds accesses are counted relative to that capacity.
stale/unset 'tmp' for unrecognized sh_type/p_type (default: break with no assignment) can print misleading values but has no confirmed security impact.
No munmap/close is performed; this is a single-shot resource leak with no attacker-controlled volume, not a finding.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability can be confirmed from the fragment alone. The only security-relevant operations are codegen stack/register bookkeeping (push/pop/pop_n at lines 17-18, 66-77, 87-150; gen_move at 47/66/73/100/135/138; bytecode emission at 144/153/156) whose indices/sizes (sp, idx, n, cursp()) have no capacity declaration or callee contract visible in the shown code, so every memory-safety hypothesis is unconfirmable and belongs in limitations. Argument count n is clamped to at most 15 by the shown guards (lines 107-110, 113-128, 140-150); the only reachable abort-style calls are the standard codegen_error paths (29/33/174) with no shown failure consequence. No injection, crypto, file, authz, or error-status-handling flaw is derivable from the shown statements.

assumptions: s->sp is an integer stack pointer shared by cursp()/push()/pop()/pop_n(); the fragment itself writes it at lines 151 and 161.
tree->car / tree->cdr are the AST node links used by nint(), nsym(), and codegen(); tree->cdr->cdr->car (line 103) may be NULL and is guarded by the if (tree) at line 104.

The called helpers (codegen, gen_move, gen_values, gen_hash, genop_1/2/3, genjmp2_0, dispatch, gen_setupvar, gen_setxv, gen_massignment, lv_idx, new_sym, attrsym, codegen_error) have no bodies in the fragment; they are treated only with name-implied semantics and as consuming the shown arguments.

n is bounded to 0..15 on every path whose arithmetic is visible: gen_values is called with an explicit limit of 13 or 14 (line 106), negative returns are clamped to 15 (line 108), and lines 113-128 and 140-150 keep n at or below 15.
The safe-call branch (lines 98-102) is only reachable after a shown push (line 93 for noself or line 96 for a receiver), so cursp()-1 at line 99 cannot underflow on any shown path.
limitations: Stack/register capacities (codegen stack size, register-file size, symbol-pool size) are not declared anywhere in the fragment, so any out-of-bounds claim against pop_n(14) (line 143), gen_move with idx (line 47), or the OP_ARRAY/OP_SEND operands (lines 144, 156) is unconfirmable (no capacity line to quote).
The VM semantics of OP_ARRAY's operand (how many slots it consumes) are outside the fragment; whether the 15th slot read at line 144 is in-bounds is a callee/VM invariant, not a shown-code fact.

Whether gen_values (line 106) can return values outside its name-implied count contract [0,13/14] (or negative) is not shown; a hypothetical huge n reaching genop_3 at line 156 was considered and demoted because the witness contradicts the name-implied limit contract of the call site.

lv_idx (line 44) returning a value outside the scope's local-variable table is not established in the fragment, and treating idx == 0 as an upvar (lines 45-52) is at most a correctness concern with no demonstrated security impact.

Reachability of codegen_error (lines 29, 33, 174) for unexpected/attacker-directed AST node types is possible, but its behavior (exception vs. abort, any memory impact) is not shown, so no CWE-617 or DoS verdict can be grounded.

All observed pop_n/pop/push sequences balance against pushes visible in the fragment (e.g., lines 68-70 vs 75, lines 87-96 vs 151/161); residual risk depends entirely on unshown helper behavior and is therefore out of scope for a confirmed verdict.

verdict.summary: In Compute(), nnz = indices_t->dim_size(0) (line 64) is an int64_t with no upper cap, but the gather loop at line 90 iterates with an int counter (for (int i = 0; i < nnz; ++i)). For any nnz >= 2^31 the counter overflows at i == INT_MAX (CWE-190), wraps to -2^31, and the next iteration executes indices_mat(i, d) at line 92 with a negative row index, deterministically reading out of bounds from the nnz x NDIM indices buffer (CWE-125); the wrapped loop also cannot terminate normally, and dense_gathered_flat(i) at line 101 becomes an OOB write when the OOB-read index value happens to satisfy the line-93 bounds check.

evidence.reason: OOB read (CWE-125) rooted in signed int counter overflow (CWE-190). nnz = indices_t->dim_size(0) (line 64) is int64_t and, per the shown code, only constrained to be >= 0 and equal to values_t->dim_size(0) (line 26); no statement caps it. The loop condition at line 90 (for (int i = 0; i < nnz; ++i)) promotes int i to int64_t for the comparison, but ++i overflows when nnz >= 2^31: witness nnz = 2^31 (indices shape [2^31, 1], values shape [2^31], sp_shape = [2^31], dense shape [1]) passes every shown guard (lines 9, 14-15, 26, 31, 36, 55); after i = 2^31-1 == INT_MAX the counter wraps to -2^31 and the condition -2^31 < 2^31 holds. indices_t matrix has capacity nnz x NDIM = 2^31 elements (dim_size(0) at line 64, IsMatrix at line 9), and indices_mat(-2^31, d) reads flat index -2^31 — 16 GiB before the buffer for NDIM=1 — a negative element index outside [0, 2^31). The FastBoundsCheck guard at line 93 and the OP_REQUIRES at line 98 execute only after this read and cannot protect it.

assumptions: OP_REQUIRES_OK at lines 3-6 returns on failure, so indices_t, values_t, shape_t, dense_t are valid non-NULL Tensors when the checks proceed (TensorFlow kernel contract visible through the macro use).
The allocator returns success on lines 65-69 for the witness-sized tensors; on allocation failure OP_REQUIRES_OK returns before the vulnerable loop (environmental precondition, not a shown bound).

b.y_reshape() and b.y_bcast() have length ndims when the branch executes, as asserted by the comment at lines 78-79 and consistent with the VecGreaterEq rank check at line 49; this keeps shaped<T,NDIM>/ToIndexArray in-domain and is not a confirmed flaw.
rhs_ref.dimension(d) (line 93) is the dense side's extent after broadcasting, i.e., the same extent against which coeff(idx) at line 101 is indexed.
Practical two's-complement wraparound of the signed int ++i at line 90 is assumed; in strict C++ it is undefined behavior.
limitations: The OOB write at line 101 (dense_gathered_flat(i) with wrapped negative i) is not reported as confirmed: it executes only if the garbage read at line 92 passes FastBoundsCheck at line 93 for every dimension d, which is not guaranteed within the shown code.

Non-termination (CWE-835) and allocation-volume DoS (CWE-400) from nnz >= 2^31 are consequences of the same root issue and are not counted as separate CWEs; they only occur when the line-98 error does not abort first.

shape_t vector entries (line 41) are not validated to be non-negative; TensorShape(shape_vec) at line 42 and BCast behavior for negative dims are not derivable from the shown fragment, so any crash/CHECK from negative shape entries is unconfirmed.

The finding requires the fragment's allocations (lines 66-68) and the attacker-supplied tensors to be materializable at ~2^31 elements (tens of GiB); if the allocator fails, OP_REQUIRES_OK returns an error and no memory violation occurs.
ndims > 5 is properly rejected by the default branch (lines 117-122), and ndims = 0 is excluded by NumElements() > 0 (line 36); neither is a finding.

verdict.summary: Confirmed OOB read and a huge-length copy in mpgviddmx_process. (1) Line 139 copies 8 - ctx->bytes_in_header bytes from `start`; the only preceding size guard (line 128) ensures remain >= 5 but never ties the copy length to remain, so bytes_in_header == 1 (set from a prior 1-byte tail at lines 129-130) with a 5-byte packet reads 2 bytes past the pck_size-byte packet buffer (CWE-125). (2) pck_size (u32, line 31) is narrowed to signed s32 at line 35 without validation; for pck_size >= 2^31, remain is negative, still enters while(remain) (line 111), passes if(remain<5) (line 128), and memcpy(ctx->hdr_store, start, remain) at line 129 converts the negative length to a ~2^63-byte size_t, an unbounded heap overwrite (CWE-195).

evidence.reason: CWE-125 OOB read. Source region capacity is the packet buffer of pck_size bytes returned at line 31 (gf_filter_pck_get_data). ctx->bytes_in_header has residual {1,2,3,4} (set to remain in 1..4 at line 130, to 3 at lines 199/433); guard at line 128 only admits remain >= 5, and no check relates the copy length 8 - bytes_in_header to remain. Witness: prior 1-byte packet sets bytes_in_header = 1 (lines 129-131); next packet pck_size = 5 gives remain = 5 (lines 31,35), both guards 128 (5<5 false) and 137 (nonzero) admit, and line 139 reads 7 bytes from start, i.e., 2 bytes (start[5], start[6]) past the 5-byte buffer.

CWE-195: signed-to-unsigned conversion of a negative value into a huge length at a memory sink. remain = pck_size (line 35) narrows the u32 pck_size residual [0, 2^32-1] (unconstrained in the fragment) to s32; for pck_size = 0x80000000, remain = -2147483648, which is admitted by while(remain) (line 111, nonzero) and if(remain<5) (line 128). The memcpy length argument, negative s32, converts to size_t 0xFFFFFFFF80000000 (~2^63 bytes), an OOB write of ~1.8e19 bytes against any destination allocation the shown code computes (largest visible size sizeof(char)*hdr_store_alloc with u32 hdr_store_alloc at line 70).

assumptions: gf_filter_pck_get_data (line 31) returns a pointer with exactly pck_size readable bytes (the API contract visible at the call site); reading past it is out of bounds.
u32-to-s32 conversion at line 35 wraps (two's-complement), producing negative remain for pck_size >= 2^31.
ctx->bytes_in_header residual is {0,1,2,3,4} per lines 130, 163, 170, 199, 433.
limitations: ctx->hdr_store's initial allocation and exact capacity are not declared in the fragment, so the write-side overflow of line 139 (destination hdr_store+bytes_in_header needs >= 8 bytes) and the precise destination excess of the line 129 huge copy cannot be quantified against a quoted capacity; only the copy lengths are fully derivable.

Reachable-abort candidates at lines 360, 500-502, 528 and size inflation at line 420 depend on unshown parser behavior (gf_m4v_parse_config/parse_frame/get_object_start), so they were not confirmed.
