Sink: subscript into x_cur, declared with XFRM_MAX_DEPTH elements at line 9, so valid indices are 0..XFRM_MAX_DEPTH-1. nx_cur is incremented at line 32 once per iteration where xfrm_migrate_state_find (line 30) returns non-NULL, so nx_cur equals the number of prior successful finds; it is bounded only by the loop iteration count i < num_migrate (line 29), never by the array capacity. num_migrate (int, line 2) is gated only by the opaque call at line 14 whose body is not shown; no bound <= XFRM_MAX_DEPTH is derivable in the fragment, so its residual range is the full int domain (entry-point count). Witness: num_migrate = XFRM_MAX_DEPTH+1 with all line-30 finds and line-34 migrations non-NULL; at i = XFRM_MAX_DEPTH, nx_cur == XFRM_MAX_DEPTH and this write lands at index == capacity, one sizeof(struct xfrm_state *) past the line-9 array.

CWE-787 stack OOB write, same root cause and witness as the line-31 sink. x_new is declared with XFRM_MAX_DEPTH elements at line 10; nx_new is incremented at line 36 once per iteration where xfrm_state_migrate (line 33) returns non-NULL and is bounded only by the loop bound i < num_migrate (line 29). For num_migrate = XFRM_MAX_DEPTH+1 with every migration succeeding, the write at i = XFRM_MAX_DEPTH targets x_new[XFRM_MAX_DEPTH] (index == capacity), one element past the line-10 array.

assumptions: XFRM_MAX_DEPTH is a positive integer constant, so the declarations at lines 9 and 10 give x_cur and x_new exactly XFRM_MAX_DEPTH elements each, with valid subscripts 0..XFRM_MAX_DEPTH-1 (derived from the declarations themselves).
Non-NULL returns from xfrm_migrate_state_find (line 30) and xfrm_state_migrate (line 34) are values the shown branches explicitly handle and therefore admit.
sizeof(struct xfrm_state *) is at least 1 byte, so the excess write is at least one element in size.
limitations: The body of xfrm_migrate_check (line 14) is not shown; a callee that rejects num_migrate > XFRM_MAX_DEPTH would make the overflow unreachable in the full kernel, but no such bound can be cited in the fragment. Confidence capped at 0.8 per the fragile-boundary rule.
The numeric value of the macro XFRM_MAX_DEPTH is not shown; all boundary claims are stated relative to the named constant in the declarations at lines 9-10.

The read side of the loop (mp / m[i], line 29) relies on the caller supplying at least num_migrate valid elements; that caller guarantee is not shown and affects reads, not the confirmed write overflow.

No other vulnerability class (injection, crypto, file/access control, error-handling, non-termination) is present in the fragment; err is assigned before every goto out/restore_state, and NULL results are guarded before use.

verdict.summary: No security vulnerability is confirmable from the fragment. Every client-controlled length is bounded by a visible guard before reaching the reads it protects: optlen is capped at L34 and must satisfy optlen>=6 (L185) or optlen>=8 (L392); exportnamelen must satisfy exportnamelen <= optlen-6 (L203) before memcpy at L210, and optlen == 4+exportnamelen+2+2*nrinfos (L212) before the info loop at L267; meta-context reads are gated by opt_index+4 > optlen (L427/L457) under the name-implied maxlen contracts of check_export_name (L406) and check_string (L463). All fragment-visible reads stay inside the malloc(optlen+1) allocation (L38). The remaining candidates (optlen+1 uint32 wrap, (int) querylen in %.*s, helper-contract-dependent bounds) require invisible values (MAX_REQUEST_SIZE) or unseen helper behavior and are recorded in limitations, not as findings.

assumptions: data capacity is optlen+1 bytes from `data = malloc (optlen + 1)` (L38); every shown read of data targets indices < optlen, leaving the +1 byte unused by any shown operation.
conn_recv_full is treated, by its name and the fragment's exclusive use of its -1 return, as reading exactly len bytes or failing.
check_export_name and check_string take (len, maxlen) arguments and are treated as enforcing len <= maxlen by name and use; their bodies are not shown.
MAX_REQUEST_SIZE (L34) and MAX_NR_OPTIONS (L15) are macro guards whose values are not visible; optlen's residual range is symbolic [0, MAX_REQUEST_SIZE] only.
Backend default-export/description getters may return NULL and are explicitly NULL-checked at L278-282 and L296-301.
limitations: malloc(optlen+1) uint32 wraparound (heap overflow via conn_recv_full of optlen bytes into a zero/small buffer) would require optlen == UINT32_MAX to pass the L34 guard `optlen > MAX_REQUEST_SIZE`; MAX_REQUEST_SIZE's value is not shown, so admission is unconfirmable in either direction.

debug '%.*s' with (int) querylen (L467-470) would read past data if querylen > INT_MAX (negative precision), which requires optlen - opt_index > INT_MAX under check_string's maxlen (L463-465) and hence an unshown MAX_REQUEST_SIZE > 2^31; unconfirmable.

In NBD_OPT_LIST/SET_META_CONTEXT, exportnamelen (L403) and querylen (L459) are bounded only by the unseen helpers check_export_name (L406-408) and check_string (L463-465); an OOB read at L415-416/L429/L459/L467 would follow only if those helpers failed to enforce their maxlen parameter, which contradicts their name-implied semantics — not confirmed.

send_newstyle_option_reply_exportnames(option, &nr_options) (L123) receives the loop counter's address; whether the unseen callee writes through it is unknown, and no out-of-domain call-site argument is derivable from the fragment.
The comment at L38 promises a trailing NUL but malloc does not zero-initialize and no shown statement writes data[optlen]; however, no shown statement reads data[optlen], so no impact is confirmable.
debug at L436 passes uint32_t nr_queries for %d (formal varargs type mismatch, cosmetic-only in practice); no attacker-controlled string content reaches any log format, so no log-injection impact.
conn->default_exportname[b->i] (L173-176) indexes an invisible array with framework-provided backend indices; no attacker-derived value reaches that index in the shown code.
EXPORT_NAME / NBD_OPT_GO handshake_finish send path (L81-88) reads only memset-initialized bytes (offsetof/sizeof variants), so no uninitialized-struct disclosure is present.

verdict.summary: MqttClient_WaitType can loop forever. MqttPacket_Read's return value 0 (EOF/zero-length read) is admitted by the failure branch 'if (rc <= 0) { break; }' (lines 94-95) but the only failure exit 'if (rc < 0) return rc;' (line 227) excludes 0, so control reaches 'if (!waitMatchFound) { goto wait_again; }' (lines 235-237) with waitMatchFound still 0 (line 30) and re-enters the switch with the state reset to MQTT_MSG_BEGIN. No shown statement exits the loop for persistent rc == 0, so a broker closing the connection (persistent EOF) wedges the client thread in an unbounded busy loop (CWE-835); the same unreachable-exit loop is also sustainable by a peer streaming well-formed non-matching packets.

evidence.reason: Non-termination (CWE-835). MqttPacket_Read (line 91) can return 0, which line 94 ('if (rc <= 0)') treats as failure; the failure return only fires for rc < 0 (line 227), so rc == 0 passes the guard and reaches line 235 ('if (!waitMatchFound)') — waitMatchFound is initialized to 0 (line 30) and only set to 1 on a match (line 139), unreachable for rc == 0 — and executes this goto. The loop re-enters through MqttPacket_Read (91) and repeats indefinitely with no counter, cap, or overall deadline in the shown code; the only exits (rc < 0 at 227-232, waitMatchFound == 1) are unreachable for persistent zero-length reads/EOF, so an attacker-controlled broker close causes a permanent client-thread busy loop.

assumptions: Line 18's comment establishes the fragment-visible contract that every packet_obj passed in begins with an MqttMsgStat member; used for the line 19 cast and the *mms_stat reads/writes.

MqttPacket_Read is treated as a bounded stream read respecting its len argument (client->rx_buf_len, line 91); its failure domain is defined by the shown guard at line 94, which admits rc <= 0 including rc == 0.
Line 136's 'wait_packet_id == 0' is the wildcard case; a nonzero wait_packet_id requires an exact packet-id match for waitMatchFound.
limitations: Type-punning cast at line 19 and the *mms_stat writes (88, 113, 219) rely on the line 18 caller contract (leading MqttMsgStat, enum-sized); no attacker path through the fragment violates it, so no CWE-843/125 finding is confirmed.

MQTT_MSG_AUTH (line 58) or preserved MQTT_MSG_READ entry could set readLocked = 1 (line 124) without the MQTT_MSG_BEGIN lock (line 44), causing a double unlock at lines 223-224; 'MQTT_MSG_AUTH' has no shown producer in the fragment, so no witness derivable from shown code — demoted.

MqttClient_HandlePacket receiving &client->msg (line 143) or pendResp->packet_obj (line 156) with a decoded type could be a type/length mismatch, but the size of client->msg and the callee body are not shown — no capacity anchor, demoted.
pendResp use-after-free/race requires unshown RespList_Remove/free behavior and an interleaving not producible from the fragment's own statements — demoted.

Positive wm_SemLock error codes (lines 83-85, 163-165) would also fall into the same loop because line 227 only returns rc < 0; if lock errors are negative this is moot, and the rc == 0 witness already confirms the loop — not a separate CWE.
Buffer-capacity claims on client->rx_buf or client->msg cannot be grounded: no declaration/allocation of those objects exists in the fragment.
The sustained non-matching-packet flood variant (rc > 0 each iteration) reaches the same line 237 sink; it is part of the same CWE-835 finding, not an independent CWE.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the fragment. The buffer layout is internally consistent: calloc(hash_len * 2) at line 22 provides two hash_len-byte regions (passwd1_sum at [0, hash_len), passwd2_sum at [hash_len, 2*hash_len) via line 26), and every write/read (lines 29/31, 43-44, 48, 51, 56) stays within those regions given the shown equality keylen = PBKDF2_LENGTH - PBKDF2_SALT_LEN (line 41). Error paths are checked (lines 13-16, 23-24, 35-36, 45-46, 53-54). Remaining concerns depend on constants or caller-side capacities not visible in the fragment and are unconfirmable (see limitations).

assumptions: hash_len has a single source per configuration (lines 10/19) and is reused consistently for allocation (line 22), region split (line 26), stored-hash read (lines 29/31), digest output (line 51), and comparison (line 56), so digest-branch regions are exactly hash_len bytes inside a 2*hash_len allocation.

Line 41 defines keylen = PBKDF2_LENGTH - PBKDF2_SALT_LEN, so PBKDF2_SALT_LEN + keylen == PBKDF2_LENGTH; hence the key read at line 48 ends exactly at the 2*PBKDF2_LENGTH capacity when 0 <= PBKDF2_SALT_LEN <= PBKDF2_LENGTH.
Passing the NULL check at lines 23-24 implies calloc's requested size 2*hash_len was representable and non-huge, so hash_len cannot be a large negative value on the success path.
read_env_passwd/read_default_passwd consume argument 2 as a destination capacity and write at most that many bytes, per their name-implied buffer+size contract.
limitations: If PBKDF2_SALT_LEN > PBKDF2_LENGTH, keylen (line 41) is negative and converts to a huge size_t at lines 43-44 and 48, enabling an OOB write to passwd1_sum / OOB read of key; the constant relationship is not shown in the fragment, so no witness can be constructed and this cannot be confirmed either way.

OOB read of passwd is unconfirmable: `length` (size_t, unconstrained in the fragment, lines 43/51) bounds the read, but the capacity of the caller's password buffer is not identifiable from the shown code.

Integer overflow of hash_len * 2 (line 22) or negative hash_len pointer arithmetic (line 26) would require digest_length/PBKDF2_LENGTH magnitudes near INT_MAX/2, which no shown statement establishes; the producer is a fixed internal algorithm, not attacker data.

Empty/zero-state behavior (e.g., digest_length returning 0 at line 19 leading to a 0-byte comparison at line 56, or read_* returning 0 non-error at lines 29/31) depends on unshown helper contracts and has no demonstrated exploit.

The return convention is caller-side: mismatch leaves ret = 0 (lines 48-49, 56-57) and read_*'s 0-return semantics are unshown, so any authentication-bypass-by-status-return claim is unconfirmable from the fragment.
digest_free(d) with d == NULL on the PBKDF2-config path (lines 60-62) relies on an unshown callee contract; at most a robustness concern.
No loop, allocation-sized-by-input, or format-string sink exists in the fragment, so ReDoS/resource-exhaustion and format-string classes are out of scope here.

verdict.summary: pjstun_parse_msg reads the STUN header (lines 11 and 26) and the per-attribute length field (line 42) before any check guarantees the buffer actually holds those bytes: buf_len is never verified to be >= the header size before the header dereference (the equality check at line 27 runs after the reads and underflows for short buffers), and the attribute loop admits 1-3 remaining bytes (line 36) while the attribute-header read needs 4, with the length guard at line 45 executing only after the read. This causes bounded (1-4 byte) out-of-bounds reads on short, attacker-controlled messages (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: Entry-point buf_len (pj_size_t, residual [0, SIZE_MAX], unconstrained by any shown statement before this line) is the declared buffer capacity per the function's own model (line 27 treats buf_len as the message extent). With buf_len=1, this 2-byte read exceeds the declared capacity by 1 byte. The only length guard (line 27) executes after this read. Primary CWE-125 out-of-bounds read.

Witness: buf_len=2 with bytes 0x00 0x01 (type 0x0001, admitted by the switch at lines 13-24). Line 26 then reads bytes 2-3, 2 bytes past the declared capacity buf_len=2. Line 27's check (msg_len != buf_len - sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr)) runs after this read and underflows to a huge value for buf_len < 20, so it cannot protect the read. Primary CWE-125 out-of-bounds read.

The loop condition at line 36 (msg_len > 0) admits msg_len=1,2,3, but this read requires 4 bytes of attribute header. Witness: header (type 0x0001, length 0x0005) + attribute (length 0x0000) + 1 tail byte, buf_len=25; iteration 1 consumes 4 bytes leaving msg_len=1; iteration 2 is admitted by line 36, and this 2-byte read of (*attr)->length falls at least 1 byte past buf+buf_len. The guard at line 45 (msg_len < len) executes after this read, so it cannot prevent the overread. Primary CWE-125 out-of-bounds read.

assumptions: buf_len is the byte length of the message buffer; the code itself uses it that way at line 27 (buf_len - sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr) compared against the 16-bit payload length).
PJ_ARRAY_SIZE(msg->attr) at line 6 yields the element count of the msg->attr array member, so writes to msg->attr[attr_count] under the line 36 guard stay in-bounds (no out-of-bounds write finding).
pj_ntohs reads exactly 2 bytes and returns a host-order pj_uint16_t.
pj_size_t is an unsigned size type, so buf_len - sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr) at line 27 underflows for short buffers instead of rejecting before the reads.
limitations: The actual allocation size behind buf is not visible in the fragment; the overreads are measured against the declared length buf_len and may land inside a larger caller allocation, which caps practical impact (bounded 1-4 byte overreads, low severity).

sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr) and the field offsets of pjstun_attr_hdr are not visible in the fragment; the header-overread claim does not depend on those values, but the exact byte excess of the attribute overread (1-3 bytes) depends on the length-field offset within the attribute header.
The declaration of msg->attr is not shown; its capacity is inferred only from PJ_ARRAY_SIZE semantics, so no out-of-bounds write to msg->attr is claimed.

No other vulnerability classes were confirmed: PJ_LOG format strings are compile-time constants with numeric arguments (no format-string/log injection); len arithmetic cannot overflow uint32; the loop strictly consumes >= 4 bytes per iteration (no non-termination); no unchecked return status gates a security-relevant operation.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable within the shown fragment. All NULL/error statuses are checked by visible guards (lines 12, 17, 20, 35, 46, 64, 74, 84, 88), and the suspicious arithmetic and silence-fill sinks (lines 30, 31-33, 41, 42-44, 53-59) depend on struct-field ranges, buffer capacity, and callee contracts that are not present in the fragment, so no concrete witness passes the three-part confirmation.

assumptions: substream is NULL-guarded at lines 12 and 82 before any dereference of its fields in the playback and capture blocks.
runtime is assigned at line 13 before every use in the playback block, including the goto __direct path (line 15), and at line 86 before use in the capture block.
Return statuses from snd_pcm_oss_make_ready (16/83), mutex_lock_interruptible (20), snd_pcm_oss_sync1 (34/45), and snd_pcm_kernel_ioctl (72/87) are all checked before any continuation.
Framework-provided pointers substream->runtime and runtime->control are treated as non-NULL because the fragment contains no statement marking them nullable.
limitations: Divide-by-zero candidates at lines 30 and 44 require width == 0, but the range of snd_pcm_format_physical_width() is a callee contract not shown in the fragment and runtime->oss.format is unconstrained by shown code; no witness is constructible.

Subtraction underflow at lines 30 (period_bytes - buffer_used) and 41 (period_bytes - period_ptr) requires buffer_used or period_ptr to exceed period_bytes; the guards at lines 26 and 37 do not exclude it, but the fragment shows no producer or bound establishing such a state.

An out-of-bounds fill at lines 31-33 and 42-44 cannot be assessed because the capacity of runtime->oss.buffer is not identifiable from the fragment (no declaration/allocation line), and the byte/count semantics of the state fields are not shown.
Modulo-by-zero at line 53 depends on runtime->period_size == 0, which no shown statement establishes or refutes.

snd_pcm_lib_write/writev(substream, NULL, size) at lines 57/59: callee bodies are not shown; the NULL buffer and the discarded return status could not be confirmed to cause any security-relevant failure-state operation.
The parameter pcm_oss_file and the framework pointers are assumed non-NULL from an out-of-fragment caller/framework contract; the fragment itself shows no NULL check for pcm_oss_file.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable from the shown fragment. Every segment id is range-checked to [0, num_segments) at lines 40-47 before the write loop, and the write/read indexes at lines 57-58 are linear combinations of values admitted by shown guards. Claims of out-of-bounds access (output_flat, flat_input, flat_segment_id cross-indexing) and of integer-overflow-corrupted indexes all depend on capacities and arithmetic inside unshown helpers (GetOutputShape, allocate_output, GetStrides, GetFlattenedRelativeOffsets) or on allocation succeeding at infeasible magnitudes, so they are recorded as limitations without CWE.

assumptions: Tensor/OpKernelContext framework objects returned by context->input() and dim_size() are valid non-NULL objects with non-negative dim sizes (framework contract; no counter-evidence in the fragment).
OP_REQUIRES / OP_REQUIRES_OK abort Compute and return an error on false status/value, so failure states do not reach the write loop.
Validation loop at lines 40-47 covers every element of flat_segment_id; the write loop at line 57 re-reads flat_segment_id(i) from the same read-only tensor with no intervening mutation (no TOCTOU).
INDICES_TYPE and NUM_SEGMENTS_TYPE are assumed signed as in the standard int32/int64 instantiations; unsigned instantiations would weaken the >= 0 conjunct but the fragment does not fix the types.
limitations: OOB write via output_flat(output_index) (lines 57-61) is unconfirmed: the output buffer capacity is fixed by GetOutputShape/allocate_output (lines 30-33), whose bodies and layout are not shown; the guard at line 43 bounds ids to [0, num_segments), and no in-fragment arithmetic demonstrably leaves the buffer domain.

Integer overflow in flat_segment_id(i) * big_stride (line 57) is unconfirmed: reaching the write loop at extreme magnitudes requires allocate_output success (line 32) with matching huge output element counts, an unshown allocation/shape computation; no traceable witness exists entirely in the shown code.
OOB read of flat_input(offset) (line 61) is unconfirmed: flat_input.size() is not stated in the fragment.
Potential OOB read of flat_segment_id(i) at line 57 if relative_offset_set.size() (line 56) exceeded flat_segment_id.size(); the relationship is fixed by unshown helper bodies.
int loop counter start_offset (line 55) would signed-overflow for big_stride > INT_MAX; physically unreachable given the output allocation gate; not a confirmed termination flaw.

DoS via huge output allocation requested before segment-id validation (lines 30-33 vs 40-47) is handled by OP_REQUIRES_OK; single-shot resource exhaustion with no shown amplification is not a confirmed finding.
separator_ contents are unknown; it is appended into tensor output (line 60), and no injection sink (log/command/SQL/header/URL) exists in the fragment.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability is confirmable within the shown fragment. The buffer arithmetic is internally consistent: calloc(hash_len * 2, ...) at line 22 gives a 2*hash_len-byte object, passwd2_sum at line 26 gives a hash_len-byte second half, and every sink window (lines 29/31, 43-44, 48, 51, 56) fits those capacities exactly, provided the unshown callees honor their length-argument contracts and PBKDF2_SALT_LEN lies in [0, PBKDF2_LENGTH]. Every candidate flaw (unvalidated digest_length at line 19, PBKDF2 constant relations at lines 39-48, strncmp truncation of binary digests at lines 48/56, read-helper return semantics at lines 29-35) depends on values, contracts, or framework degenerate states not present in the shown code, so none meets the three-part confirmation standard.

assumptions: Line 22 'passwd1_sum = calloc(hash_len * 2, sizeof(unsigned char));' yields exactly 2*hash_len bytes when it succeeds, so the first half has capacity hash_len bytes.
Line 26 'passwd2_sum = passwd1_sum + hash_len;' makes the second half a contiguous object of exactly hash_len bytes (indices [hash_len, 2*hash_len-1]).
Line 10 sets hash_len == PBKDF2_LENGTH in the PBKDF2 branch, so total capacity there is 2*PBKDF2_LENGTH bytes.

Lines 29/31 pass hash_len as a destination-capacity argument for passwd2_sum; the shown code relies on the name-implied contract that read_env_passwd/read_default_passwd write at most that many bytes.
IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PASSWD_CRYPTO_PBKDF2) at lines 9 and 38 is a compile-time constant, making the two branches disjoint; both are analyzed.
strncmp, pkcs5_pbkdf2_hmac_sha1, and digest_digest are standard library/crypto operations whose length/documentation semantics (dkLen output bytes, n-byte comparison) are name-implied.
limitations: digest_length(d) (line 19) is not validated: no shown statement excludes negative or zero results. A negative value only forces calloc (line 22) to fail and return -ENOMEM (line 24); a zero-length digest chain (calloc(0) non-NULL, read success, digest_digest success) would make line 56 'strncmp(..., 0) == 0' succeed and set ret=1, but that depends on framework-degenerate values with no visible producer or minimum — unconfirmed.

The values of PBKDF2_LENGTH, PBKDF2_SALT_LEN, and PBKDF2_COUNT are not visible. If PBKDF2_SALT_LEN > PBKDF2_LENGTH, keylen (line 41) is negative and key (line 39) points past the second half before strncmp (line 48); if PBKDF2_SALT_LEN == PBKDF2_LENGTH, keylen == 0 makes strncmp(...) == 0 unconditionally. Neither constant relation can be confirmed from the fragment.

strncmp on binary digest material at lines 48 and 56 stops comparing at the first NUL byte; a stored key/digest beginning with 0x00 could admit a wrong password whose derived digest shares that leading byte. The witness cannot be constructed from the shown code because the stored blob is produced by unshown helpers and NUL producibility of the hash output is not shown.

Return semantics of read_env_passwd/read_default_passwd (lines 29/31) are unknown; only ret < 0 (line 35) is rejected, so a non-negative short/partial read proceeds with partially zero-filled data. No security impact is demonstrable within the fragment.

passwd and length are forwarded unchanged to pkcs5_pbkdf2_hmac_sha1 (lines 43-44) and digest_digest (line 51); no capacity for the passwd buffer is declared in the fragment, so any out-of-bounds read there would be in unshown callees and is unconfirmable.
int arithmetic hash_len * 2 (line 22) can wrap only into a negative/huge size_t, which makes calloc fail; no undersized allocation or corrupted security-relevant value results, so no CWE-190 finding.
Single-shot leaks of digest d on the early returns at lines 16 and 24 do not compound with attacker-controlled volume.
The comparison at lines 48/56 is not constant-time; timing side channels are outside the listed classes and the fragment offers no protection statement.

verdict.summary: Attacker-supplied row_remapping values (e.g., {0, INT64_MAX}, with only the size checked at L9) flow into max_old_row/row_start (L23/L27/L107) and overflow `max_old_row - row_start + 1` at L116-117: the int64_t result wraps to INT64_MIN and then to 0, so `row_start += slice_length` (L121) stops advancing and the while loop at L112 never terminates while `tensor_slices.push_back` (L120) grows without bound - a CPU/memory DoS (CWE-835, root cause signed overflow CWE-190).

evidence.reason: row_remapping element values are entry-point input whose only shown constraint is the size check at L9; no value-domain check exists, so max_old_row (L27) can be INT64_MAX and row_start (L107) can be 0, both admitted by the L106 guard. `max_old_row - row_start + 1` (L116-117), an int64_t computation, wraps: with max_old_row=INT64_MAX, row_start=0 it becomes INT64_MIN, and on the next iteration INT64_MAX - INT64_MIN + 1 = 0. slice_length therefore becomes 0, `row_start += slice_length` (L121) makes no progress, and the L112 condition `row_start <= max_old_row` remains true forever, so the loop never terminates while L120 appends TensorSlice objects without bound: attacker-controlled CPU/memory DoS (primary CWE-835 non-termination; the signed overflow corrupting the loop-progress value is the confirmed root cause CWE-190).

assumptions: row_remapping/col_remapping element values are unconstrained beyond the size checks at L9 and L43; the raw min/max extraction at L20-29 uses them directly.

num_rows_, num_cols_, and max_rows_in_memory_ are attribute/member values with no shown bounds; the witness uses num_rows_=2, num_cols_=1, and any max_rows_in_memory_ value (positive or non-positive both reach slice_length=0 via overflow).
Signed int64_t overflow is treated as two's-complement wrap-around, the practical runtime behavior for this platform/compiler.
A crafted checkpoint providing a DT_FLOAT rank-2 tensor satisfies L70, L76, and L83; with col_remapping non-empty, L93 is bypassed.
limitations: The witness requires RemapVectorToMap (L13) to return OK for {0, INT64_MAX}; its body is not shown, so its accept/reject set cannot be audited. The fragment itself contains no rejection of large old IDs, and no unshown invariant can be credited as making the operation safe.

The first loop iteration passes the wrapped negative length INT64_MIN to TensorSlice::set_length (L119); whether that callee aborts, errors, or accepts is not visible in the fragment, so that outcome (e.g., a possible CWE-617 abort) is unpinned. The stall from slice_length=0 in iteration 2 is a pure fragment-visible consequence.

old_tensor_name is read via scalar<tstring>()() at L66 with no shown NumElements()==1 check (contrast ckpt_path at L57-58); a 0-element tensor could cause an OOB read (CWE-125) or a callee CHECK failure, but the callee contract is not in the fragment, so this is not reported as a confirmed finding.
row_id_present[i] and col_id_present[j] at L213 could be OOB reads if RemapVectorToMap (unshown) produced vectors shorter than num_rows_/num_cols_; not confirmable from the fragment.
int loop counters at L20/L152/L170 versus int64_t bounds only wrap for sizes >= 2^31, which would first fail the very large allocations at L129/L146; not reported.
ckpt_path is logged verbatim at L68; no terminal-control escalation is established, so log injection (CWE-117) is not reported.

verdict.summary: In the delete branch (mod == 'd'), `pos--` at line 41 can move pos to -1 on admitted input (*decoded_size == 0 with dir == '<'); the guard at line 45 only checks `l < 0` and the upper end `d + l > decoded + INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX`, both of which pass, so the mismatch check at line 49 dereferences decoded[-1], an out-of-bounds read 1 byte before the decoded buffer. The subsequent memmove at line 53 can then write decoded[-1] if the adjacent heap byte equals the rule byte.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds read at decoded[-1]. Entry-point input c=0x05 and *decoded_size=0 (helper param with full int domain; no statement in the fragment establishes a minimum of 1) flow through lines 7-9 (mod='d'), 11-12 (dir='<', no reset), to line 41 where `if (dir == '<') { pos--; }` sets pos = -1. The guard at line 45 admits the path: l = 0-(-1) = 1 >= 0, and d + l = (decoded-1)+1 = decoded is not > decoded + INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX for the non-negative capacity the fragment's own end-pointer use implies. With pos = -1 the subscript decoded[pos] at line 49 accesses 1 byte below the buffer start (capacity low bound = decoded[0]), a confirmed CWE-125 OOB read; a matching adjacent byte would additionally let line 53 write decoded[-1].

assumptions: INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX is a non-negative named constant used as the exclusive upper end of decoded at lines 32 and 45; its numeric value is not shown in the fragment.
decoded[0] is the first valid byte of the buffer, so index -1 is below the buffer start.
rule is NUL-terminated (the sentinel loop at line 7 exits on c == 0).
limitations: The OOB write via memmove at line 53 (destination decoded[-1], length 1) requires the adjacent heap byte to equal the rule byte c; that condition is not constructible from the fragment, so it is not reported as a separate CWE-787 finding.

An entry *decoded_size = -1 yields an unconditional OOB write at line 37 (pos = -1, l = 0 passes the line 32 guard); valid only by the unconstrained int residual domain, noted but not reported as primary.

debug_print with '%s' on decoded (lines 23, 33, 46, 50) can read past the buffer because stored bytes are never 0 (0 terminates the loop at line 7); the allocation size of decoded is not shown, so the over-read is unconfirmable.
Termination of the line 7 loop requires a caller-supplied NUL in rule; an unterminated attacker buffer could over-read, but rule's size/termination contract is outside the fragment.
Upper-bound safety of insert/delete is enforced only relative to the fragment's own end constant (lines 32/45); no claim is made that the actual allocation matches INDX_INFLBUF_SIZEMAX.

verdict.summary: pjstun_parse_msg performs out-of-bounds reads of the message buffer: the attribute loop enters with only 1-3 payload bytes remaining (loop condition is msg_len > 0) and reads the 4-byte attribute header at line 41 before the length guard at line 44 can reject it, reading up to 3 bytes past buf+buf_len; header fields are also dereferenced at lines 10 and 25 before any check that buf_len covers the STUN header.

evidence.reason: OOB read (CWE-125): the 16-bit *attr->length field is read from p_attr (set at line 40) while only msg_len bytes remain, with msg_len in {1,2,3} admitted by the loop condition at line 35 and the equality at line 26 (buf_len = msg_len + sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr), capacity = buf_len declared in the signature lines 1-2). Reading offsets 2-3 of the attribute header requires >= 4 bytes; e.g. msg_len=3, buf_len=S+3 reads buf[S+3], 1 byte past buf[buf_len-1] (msg_len=1 reads up to 3 bytes past). The guard at line 44 executes after this read and cannot protect it (it also fires, since len >= 4 > msg_len, returning at line 47).

OOB read (CWE-125): buf_len (entry-point packet size, full unsigned domain [0, 2^32-1] since no shown statement constrains it) can be less than the 4 bytes needed to read the 16-bit length field at header offsets 2-3; e.g. buf_len=3 reads buf[3], 1 byte past capacity, before the length-equality check at line 26 (which executes after this dereference). No minimum-size check precedes this read or the type read at line 10.

OOB read (CWE-125): msg->hdr is set to buf at line 9 and the 16-bit type field at offsets 0-1 is read with no shown check that buf_len >= 2; for buf_len in {0,1} (full parameter domain, attacker-influenced datagram size) up to 2 bytes are read past capacity. The only length validation (line 26) runs after this dereference.

assumptions: pj_ntohs is a standard 16-bit network-to-host conversion that reads exactly the 2 bytes of the 16-bit field passed to it.

pjstun_msg_hdr and pjstun_attr_hdr each contain a 16-bit 'type' followed by a 16-bit 'length' at offsets 0 and 2 (the fragment reads both members via pj_ntohs), so each structure spans at least 4 bytes and reading 'length' requires >= 4 bytes.

pj_size_t is unsigned; on the success path line 26 forces buf_len = msg_len + sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr), so bytes remaining from p_attr equal msg_len at every loop entry.

The OOB reads are unreachable only under unshown caller-side contracts (e.g., callers guarantee buf_len >= sizeof(pjstun_msg_hdr) and msg_len >= 4 before calling); such external invariants are out of scope and cannot be used.
Line 50's type read is not a finding: it is only reached when line 44 admits (msg_len >= len >= 4), so at least 4 bytes remain and the 2-byte read is in-bounds.
Integer arithmetic in lines 41-42 and 59 stays within pj_uint32_t/pj_uint16_t ranges for all admitted inputs; no overflow or truncation was confirmed.
NULL buf/msg dereferences have no producer inside the fragment (caller-provided only) and are not findings.

The OOB bytes read at line 41 influence only the len comparison and the forced error return; there is no confirmed subsequent use for further memory access, so severity is rated low rather than medium despite the memory-safety nature of the bug.

A scalar (rank-0) first splits tensor would make line 12's dim_size(0) an out-of-domain read of the TensorShape dims array; that array's capacity is not identifiable from the fragment (API contract not quoted in the shown code).

If SPLITS_TYPE is int32, lines 12 and 17 narrow int64 dimensions; truncation would require a dimension at least 2^31+1, whose reachability cannot be demonstrated from the shown code (resource/allocation bounds not shown).

The framework-array indexing at lines 7 and 9 (context->input(n) / input(n+1)) is only safe under the op-registration invariant (total inputs == n+2), which is not stated in the shown code.
The fragment contains no loops, so loop-bound, parser-position, and termination analysis applies only to unshown callees and cannot be performed here.

verdict.summary: NULL pointer dereference at the beach: cleanup label. obj is initialized to NULL (line 11) and reaches `obj->cache_buf = NULL;` (line 67) with no intervening assignment whenever get_prelink_info_range_from_mach0 returns NULL (NULL is the admitted set of the guard at line 14, which jumps to beach) or R_NEW0 fails (guard at line 19). A crafted Mach-O that fails prelink-range lookup crashes the loader (denial of service), CWE-476.

evidence.reason: Sink is a store through pointer obj when obj is provably NULL. Line 11 (`RKernelCacheObj *obj = NULL;`) initializes obj to NULL; on the path where get_prelink_info_range_from_mach0 returns NULL (line 13), the guard at line 14 (`if (!prelink_range)`) admits NULL, `goto beach` (line 15) transfers control before the only other assignment to obj at line 18 executes, and line 67 dereferences it, crashing the loader on attacker-supplied input (CWE-476). The secondary witness via line 18 R_NEW0 failure also yields obj == NULL at this sink (guard line 19 admits NULL, jump at line 21). No guard or reassignment exists between line 11 and line 67 on either path.

assumptions: Line 11 (`RKernelCacheObj *obj = NULL;`) guarantees obj is NULL before any error jump on the paths originating at line 15 and line 21, because line 18 is either not reached or returned NULL.

The guard at line 14 (`if (!prelink_range)`) makes NULL an admitted return value of get_prelink_info_range_from_mach0 within the shown code; constraining it to be always non-NULL would render that check dead.

On the prelink_info/list failure paths (lines 30 and 39), R_FREE (obj) precedes the dereference at line 67; because the R_FREE macro is not shown, those paths are either a NULL deref (if R_FREE nulls its argument) or a use-after-free (if it does not) — the confirmed witness uses the unambiguous line 15/21 paths where obj is still NULL.

A potential out-of-bounds read inside r_cf_value_dict_parse (lines 26–27) from attacker-controlled range.offset/range.size is unconfirmable: both values are produced by the unshown helper, the fragment imposes only a truthiness check (range.size != 0, line 25), and no capacity of fbuf is declared in the shown code.
The early return at lines 6–8 leaks the fbuf reference; it is a single-shot leak without attacker-controlled compounding volume.

verdict.summary: The fragment is a test harness with no confirmed vulnerability. All fprintf format strings are literals (lines 15, 23-24, 30, 35-38), so tainted values reaching %s/%d arguments cannot inject format syntax. The STRNEQ at line 34 is only reachable when both xml and data->expect are non-NULL: xml is NULL-checked at line 29, and a NULL data->expect forces erc=-1 at line 12 followed by early returns at lines 16, 20, or 25 before line 34. Return statuses from the parse and format calls are fully checked (lines 14, 28-29). Remaining concerns (NULL args at line 8, NULL data->backing passed to %s) are caller-suppliable only and have no in-fragment producer, so they are not confirmable findings.

assumptions: data->expect is provably non-NULL on any path reaching line 34: a NULL value sets erc=-1 at line 12 and every continuation requires rc==-1 at line 14, after which either src==NULL returns at line 20 or src!=NULL returns -1 at line 25.

The format strings at lines 15, 23-24, 30, and 35-38 are compile-time literals; data values are only varargs arguments.
Return values of virStorageSourceNewFromBackingAbsolute (line 14), virDomainDiskSourceFormat (line 28), and virBufferContentAndReset (line 29) are fully checked before any downstream use.

data->backing may be NULL when passed to fprintf %s at lines 24 and 38 and to virStorageSourceNewFromBackingAbsolute at line 14; the fragment neither establishes nor excludes NULL, and a NULL would be caller-supplied rather than derived by the shown code.
The definition of struct testBackingParseData is not shown; field types (rv as int, expect/backing as pointers) are inferred from their uses.

Behavior of virStorageSourceNewFromBackingAbsolute, virDomainDiskSourceFormat, and virBufferContentAndReset is outside the fragment and was not analyzed; only the call sites' arguments and status handling were audited.
fprintf(stderr, "%s", NULL) would be undefined behavior, but no in-fragment path derives data->backing == NULL, and the failure cannot be tied to a security mechanism in the shown code.

verdict.summary: fiber_switch passes the unchecked signed parameter `len` into stack capacity arithmetic: on the first-resume (MRB_FIBER_CREATED) path, the only guard on `len` is `len >= 15` (line 38), leaving all negative values admitted to the else branch, where `len+2` is passed to `mrb_stack_extend` (line 44) as a stack-room size. A witness such as `len = -3` yields `mrb_stack_extend(mrb, -1)`, an out-of-domain negative size consumed as capacity, corrupting the fiber stack bookkeeping that the subsequent stack stores (lines 51-52) and the VM entry (line 63) depend on. No shown statement establishes a lower bound on `len`.

evidence.snippet: mrb_stack_extend(mrb, len+2); /* for receiver and (optional) block */
evidence.reason: Sink line 44 consumes `len+2` as a non-negative stack-room/capacity increment. `len` is declared `mrb_int` (line 1) with full signed domain; the sole guard on it, `if (len >= 15)` (line 38), excludes only `len >= 15` and admits `len <= 14`, including every negative value. Concrete witness `len = -3`: status MRB_FIBER_CREATED falls through the switch (lines 23-24), line 32 passes with a non-NULL proc, `-3 >= 15` is false (line 38), and line 44 executes `mrb_stack_extend(mrb, -1)` with a negative size argument — out of the domain the operation requires. The resulting undersized/corrupted stack region is then written by `c->cibase->n = len` and `c->stbase[0] = ...` (lines 51-52) and consumed by `mrb_vm_exec` (line 63), yielding an out-of-bounds write on the heap-backed fiber stack (CWE-787). The capacity on this path is established only by this very call, and the argument supplied to it is provably out of domain for the whole admitted set of `len`.

assumptions: `mrb_int` is a signed integer type, so `len`'s declared domain is [MRB_INT_MIN, MRB_INT_MAX]; the fragment constrains only its upper end (`len >= 15`, line 38).
`a` is the argument array paired with `len` (the caller contract; read at lines 40, 48, 55).
`mrb_stack_extend(mrb, room)` consumes its second argument as a non-negative stack-room count per its name and call-site use (lines 39, 44).
`MRB_FIBER_CREATED` is an admitted status: the switch's `default` case (lines 23-24) lets it reach line 29.
A valid fresh fiber has `c->ci->proc != NULL`, so line 32's raise is not taken on the witness path.
limitations: The exact arithmetic inside `mrb_stack_extend` (how a negative room folds into its size computation) is not visible in the fragment; the confirmed defect is the out-of-domain negative size argument at line 44 (call-site confirmation).

Huge positive `len` (>= 15) at line 40 can drive an unbounded allocation/copy in `mrb_ary_new_from_values`; attacker control of `len` and input volume is not established in the fragment, so this resource-exhaustion concern is demoted.

The negative `n` stored at line 51 and the unguarded `fiber_result(mrb, a, len)` at line 55 have consumers (VM/callinfo) outside the fragment; they share the same negative-`len` root cause and are not counted as separate CWEs.
`c->ci--` (line 36) and `c->ci[1].stack[0]` (line 57) depend on callinfo-layout invariants not shown in the fragment; no separate finding.

`e = b + len` (line 46) is UB pointer arithmetic for negative `len` but is never dereferenced on that path (loop at lines 47-49 runs zero iterations); folded into the root-cause finding, not counted independently.
The `c->stbase[0]` write at line 52 for degenerate `len = -2` (which makes line 44 request room 0) relies on a minimum stack size not established in the fragment; not a separate finding.

verdict.summary: fiber_switch uses the unvalidated mrb_int parameter `len` to compute `len+2` as the size argument to the stack-reservation call mrb_stack_extend at line 35. Nothing in the fragment constrains `len` (no range check, cap, or minimum), so its residual range includes negative values (e.g., -3 gives len+2 = -1) and values whose len+2 overflows in the shown signed arithmetic (e.g., 2147483646 wraps to -2147483648 for a 32-bit mrb_int); either way a negative size reaches a call whose parameter is a non-negative stack-space count. The copy loop at lines 36-40 then writes `len` elements starting at c->stbase+1 using the unwrapped value, yielding a reservation/write-volume mismatch, and line 44 stores the unvalidated value into c->cibase->n. Primary mechanism: integer overflow / missing range check corrupting an input-derived size (CWE-190).

evidence.snippet: mrb_stack_extend(mrb, len+2); /* for receiver and (optional) block */
evidence.reason: Parameter `len` (line 1, mrb_int) is never checked in the fragment, so its residual range is the full signed integer domain. `len+2` is therefore negative for every len <= -3 (witness len = -3 gives -1) and wraps to a negative value for len near the type maximum (e.g., 2147483646 -> -2147483648) in the same signed mrb_int arithmetic. Both forms violate the non-negative size/room domain of mrb_stack_extend implied by its name and the comment "for receiver and (optional) block"; the shown code derives an out-of-domain capacity argument at the call site. The damage path is completed in the fragment: the loop `e = b + len; while (b<e) { *b++ = *a++; }` (lines 36-40) writes `len` elements to stbase[1..len] using the unwrapped value, without any shown bound tying it to the actually-reserved stack space, and line 44 stores the unvalidated value into c->cibase->n. Mechanism: integer overflow / unvalidated input-derived size used as a capacity (primary CWE-190).

assumptions: mrb_int is a signed fixed-width integer; `len+2` (line 35) and `e = b + len` (line 37) are computed in that type.
mrb_stack_extend's second parameter is a non-negative stack-space/room size: by its name and the comment "for receiver and (optional) block".
mrb_raise does not return, so the raising guards at lines 12-22 and 32-34 terminate their branches.
fiber_check (line 3) returns a valid context pointer because the fragment dereferences it at lines 5 and 8 without a NULL check and no shown statement produces NULL.
MRB_FIBER_CREATED is distinct from the four status values handled explicitly in lines 11-22, so it is admitted by the `default` case at lines 23-24.
limitations: The backing capacity of the fiber value stack (the object behind c->stbase) and the valid length of `a` are not identifiable from the shown code, so the numeric OOB-write/read excess of the copy loop at lines 36-40 cannot be grounded; CWE-787/CWE-125 are therefore not confirmed.
The wrap case of `len+2` depends on the unshown width of mrb_int (e.g., 32-bit); the negative-len case (len <= -3) does not.

Storing a negative arity into c->cibase->n (line 44) and passing a negative length to fiber_result (line 48) have downstream consumers outside the fragment, so their individual impact is not confirmed here.

A NULL dereference at line 45 via MRB_PROC_ENV(c->cibase->proc)->stack[0] would require a shown producer of NULL for c->cibase->proc or its REnv; the only proc guard (line 32) checks c->ci->proc, a different field, and no NULL source is visible.
Bounds of c->ci[1] (line 50) and of the c->ci-- pop (line 42) are not derivable from the fragment.

Return values of fiber_check_cfunc (line 8), fiber_switch_context (line 28), and mrb_stack_extend (line 35) are discarded; no failure state is visibly consumed as a size/index/pointer, so no CWE-754/CWE-390 finding is confirmed.

The copy loop advances b by one element per iteration, so it terminates for every input; its iteration volume equals the input length with no shown amplification, so non-termination/resource-amplification is not a finding.

verdict.summary: No vulnerability meeting the confirmation standard is present in the fragment. The only concrete defect is that the error path (lines 14-17) returns -EINVAL without freeing the kzalloc'd attachment 'a' from line 8, a single-shot memory leak not shown to compound with attacker-controlled volume; no security-relevant operation runs on the failure state. No loops, no input-derived indexes or copy sizes, no format-string/command/SQL/crypto sinks exist in the fragment to analyze further.

verdict.summary: ljpeg_start computes len from the JPEG segment length field without validation (line 14): a craftable value of 0x0000 or 0x0001 yields len=-1/-2, which fread (line 16) converts to a huge size_t (CWE-195), copying up to the remaining file length into the 64 KiB stack buffer data (capacity 65536, line 4) — a stack out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) with fully attacker-chosen bytes. A truncated file whose last segment payload starts with a marker such as 0xffc0 additionally causes the do-while loop (lines 11-39) to hang forever because the discarded fread statuses leave stale, attacker-chosen bytes to be re-parsed at EOF.

evidence.reason: len is derived entirely from file bytes at line 14: len = (data[2]<<8 | data[3]) - 2, residual range -2..65533 with file bytes domain 0..255 and no shown constraint; the line-15 guard checks only tag (admitted set 0xff01..0xffff) and admits the witness tag=0xffc0. For file bytes FF D8 | FF C0 00 00 | <65,537+ bytes, len=-2 is passed as fread's size_t nmemb, converting to 2^64-2 (CWE-195 signed-to-unsigned), and fread writes up to the stream length into data, whose capacity is 65536 bytes per the declaration 'uchar data[0x10000];' at line 4 — the write reaches index 65536 == capacity, an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) of at least one attacker-chosen byte, with the fread return status discarded so the overrun is not detected.

assumptions: data capacity 65536 bytes is visible in the shown code at line 4: 'uchar data[0x10000];'
fread's standard library contract: size_t nmemb, reads up to nmemb items and returns a short count at EOF; the fragment discards all fread return values (lines 9, 12, 16).
ifp is a stream over externally supplied file bytes; the fragment itself consumes that stream, so its contents are entry-point input with no shown constraint.
limitations: Confirmed secondary concern (not added to cwe): with a truncated file such as FF D8 FF C0 00 08 FF C0 00 00 00 00, the do-while loop (lines 11-39) never terminates: at EOF the discarded fread returns leave data unchanged, tag stays 0xffc0 (admitted by line 15, != 0xffda), and line 16 copies 0 bytes — an attacker-controlled hang (CWE-835 / unchecked return CWE-754).

make_decoder_ref (line 30) is not shown; the shown loop bound keeps dp <= data+65533 between iterations, but the helper's own reads cannot be bounded from the fragment, so any over-read beyond data+65536 is unconfirmable.
struct jhead layout is not shown, so the capacity of jh->huff for the FORC assignments (lines 42-45) cannot be verified; no finding is based on it.
Stale in-bounds reads beyond a segment's len (lines 19, 21-24, 33-34) stay within the 65536-byte buffer and are treated as a robustness concern, not a confirmed vulnerability.
merror at line 48 is reachable only if calloc fails (line 47) and is not attacker-directable within the fragment; no security operation runs on that failure state.

verdict.summary: The header length check at line 8 uses sizeof(bh), the size of a pointer, instead of sizeof(blobheader). An attacker-controlled NVRAM blob whose length lies between the pointer size and the struct size passes the guard and the function reads blobheader fields past the end of the buffer (CWE-125), leaking over-read bytes into caller outputs (*hdrversion/*hdrflags) and logs.

evidence.reason: Sink read of bh->flags: `length` is the only capacity certificate for `data` (lines 8/11) and its residual range after the line 8 guard is [sizeof(bh), 2^32-1] with sizeof(bh) = pointer size (bh declared at line 5), while the struct-field reads span sizeof(blobheader) bytes (lines 33, 36). Witness (LP64): length=8 and an 8-byte buffer with totlen=htonl(8), min_version=0, hdrsize=htons(sizeof(blobheader)) passes guards at lines 8, 15, 23, 33, then line 42 reads bh->flags at byte offsets >= 8, i.e. OOB read (CWE-125) of at least 2 bytes; the over-read bytes are propagated to *hdrflags.

Sink read of bh->hdrsize under the same insufficient guard: line 8 admits length >= sizeof(bh) (pointer size), not length >= sizeof(blobheader). On ILP32 builds length=4 is admitted and this read (or the min_version read at line 23) already falls outside the guarded 4-byte region; on LP64 the read is in-bounds only if hdrsize lies within the first 8 bytes, which the guard itself never establishes. CWE-125.

assumptions: `length` is the byte capacity of `data`; the parameter is used as a byte count at lines 8 and 11 ("not enough bytes for header: %u\n", length).
`sizeof(bh)` is the pointer size (8 bytes on LP64, 4 on ILP32) because `bh` is declared `blobheader *bh` at line 5 — distinct from `sizeof(blobheader)` used at lines 33 and 36.
The header is treated by the function itself as `sizeof(blobheader)` bytes (lines 33, 36), which is the byte span of the field reads.
limitations: The `blobheader` definition, member types/offsets, and padding are not in the fragment, so the exact over-read byte count cannot be numerated; the confirmed claim is that the line 8 minimum (pointer size) does not guarantee the struct-spanning reads. If a degenerate struct had sizeof(blobheader) <= sizeof(bh), no OOB would occur, but that contradicts the multi-field header contract implied by lines 15/23/32/40/42.
Caller output pointers `dataoffset`, `hdrflags`, `hdrversion` are dereferenced at lines 40-42 without NULL checks; NULL could only be supplied by the caller (out of scope).
The cast `(blobheader *)data` at line 5 can be misaligned, which is UB, but the buffer's alignment is a caller-side provenance not shown in the fragment.
`logprintf` return values are discarded, but all format strings are constants with numeric arguments, so no log/format-string injection was confirmed.
32-bit vs 64-bit pointer size shifts which field read first crosses the buffer boundary (line 23 on ILP32 vs line 42 on LP64).

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. Every write into buffer[256] (line 4) goes through g_strlcat with sizeof(buffer) (lines 29, 37, 38), so the CAP REQ buffer cannot overflow, and the content reaching the tcp_sendf sink (line 52) consists only of fixed whitelisted literals admitted by exact-match comparisons (lines 23, 35), which removes attacker-controlled CR/LF or non-whitelist bytes. Unconfirmed concerns are recorded as limitations: a possible NULL extensions_str dereference of the g_strsplit result (lines 13, 17), an unchecked strlen(serv->password) (line 24), and silent CAP REQ truncation with no security impact.

assumptions: char buffer[256] at line 4 is the capacity object; g_strlcat is used with sizeof(buffer) at lines 29, 37, 38, giving a 256-byte bound including the NUL terminator.
G_N_ELEMENTS(supported_caps) at line 33 is the element count of supported_caps, so the inner loop index x stays in [0, N-1] and supported_caps[x] at line 35 is in-bounds.
g_strsplit (line 13) returns a NUL-terminated token vector for non-NULL input, which makes the sentinel loop at line 17 terminate and stay in-bounds.
The only byte sequences admitted to the buffer are the literal 'sasl ' (line 29), the supported_caps literals (line 37) and spaces (line 38), all internal constants.
tcp_sendf at line 52 is treated as a standard '%s' formatter applied to a NUL-terminated buffer; EMIT_SIGNAL_TIMESTAMP and tcp_send_len are pass-through/constant sinks.
limitations: If the caller can invoke inbound_cap_ls with extensions_str == NULL, g_strsplit returns NULL and the loop test at line 17 dereferences NULL (potential CWE-476); the fragment contains no NULL-producing statement, so this is caller-dependent and unconfirmed.
strlen(serv->password) at line 24 lacks a visible NULL check; serv->password is a framework field whose nullability is not established in the fragment, so a NULL-deref is not confirmable here.

A long whitelisted extension list silently truncates the emitted CAP REQ (lines 29/37/38), producing a partial capability request; this is a robustness/protocol-correctness defect with no demonstrated memory-safety or injection impact within the fragment.
Resource-use analysis: tokenization and the per-token whitelist scan (lines 13, 33) do work proportional to input size with no shown amplification, so a resource-exhaustion finding was not confirmed.
Callee bodies (tcp_sendf, tcp_send_len, EMIT_SIGNAL_TIMESTAMP, g_strlcat implementation) are not shown; safety conclusions for these rely on standard/name-implied semantics.

verdict.summary: gopherToHTML writes the line NUL terminator at line[llen + 1] (line 99); when the buffered+gathered line length reaches TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1 (admitted by the guard at line 77, which clamps only when the sum is >= TEMP_BUF_SIZE), the write lands at index TEMP_BUF_SIZE, one byte past the TEMP_BUF_SIZE-byte 'line' array declared at line 6 — a reachable off-by-one stack/heap write driven by attacker-controlled Gopher server data (CWE-787). Separately, the standard menu-link builder (lines 248-249) embeds the raw 'host' field from the network line into an HTML attribute without escaping, allowing attribute injection that executes script in the client browser (CWE-79).

evidence.reason: Attacker-controlled inbuf/len flow into llen (lines 73/75). The guard at line 77 admits gopherState->len + llen <= TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1 (it clamps only when the sum is >= TEMP_BUF_SIZE); with gopherState->len == 0 and a newline at offset TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 2 of a TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1 byte input, llen == TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1 passes the guard, memcpy(line, pos, llen) (line 97) fills indices 0..TEMP_BUF_SIZE-2, and the sink writes NUL at index TEMP_BUF_SIZE, exactly one byte past the capacity TEMP_BUF_SIZE declared at line 6 (LOCAL_ARRAY(char, line, TEMP_BUF_SIZE)) and confirmed by memset(line, '\0', TEMP_BUF_SIZE) at line 18. Primary mechanism: CWE-787 out-of-bounds write (off-by-one).

evidence.snippet: snprintf(tmpbuf, TEMP_BUF_SIZE, " %s\n", icon_url, host, gtype, escaped_selector, html_quote(name));
evidence.reason: The 'host' field of the network-supplied gopher line (extracted at lines 126-130, mutated only by NUL-insertion at TAB/CR/LF and the colon substitution at line 134, none of which remove '"') is passed as a raw %s into an HTML attribute at line 249; html_quote is applied only to 'name'. A line '1Name<TAB>/sel<TAB>a" onmouseover="alert(1)/*<TAB>10' produces <A HREF="gopher://a" onmouseover="alert(1)/*:10/1/sel">, executing alert(1) in the client browser (comment swallows the trailing port/selector text). The resulting HTML is appended to the StoreEntry response (lines 254, 339) after the fragment emitted an HTML page (lines 55-60). CWE-79 (XSS / HTML attribute injection).

inbuf/len are supplied by the caller from a Gopher network response; the fragment imposes no content or upper-length constraint on them, and no minimum beyond the loop condition pos < inbuf + len (line 67).

The generated output is an HTML page sent to the client browser (the fragment itself emits <PRE>/<H2>/<ISINDEX> markup, lines 55-60 and 22-29), so the unescaped host attribute is rendered as HTML; the header emission in gopherHTMLHeader is not shown.

limitations: memcpy into gopherState->buf (line 86) and the read of gopherState->buf (line 92): the capacity of gopherState->buf is not declared or derivable from the fragment, so any overflow/under-read there is unconfirmable and no CWE is attached.

atoi(s_code)/atoi(s_recno) with a NULL argument (lines 279/281/305) is not reported: a NULL s_code forces a NULL result from the same strtok chain, which is caught by if (!result) break; (lines 276-277, 302-303) before atoi; only a residual C-standard strtok state ambiguity remains, which is a robustness concern, not a confirmed finding.
